The following are the highlights from regional administrationowned RGVK Dagestan TV news RIA Dagestan and RIA Derbent news agencies and Mdgazetaru run by the Molodezh Dagestana weekly and Ndeloru run by the Novoye Delo newspaper websites for the period    November 
Covid Updates
By  November  people in Dagestan were infected with the Covid coronavirus according to official data In the preceding  hours  new cases were identified and  people convalesced Six people died bringing the regions official Covid death toll to  Ndeloru website Makhachkala  gmt  Nov 
Acting Dagestan head Sergei Melikov ordered that the elderly and people with chronic diseases selfisolate from  November until  December The same decree issued on  November banned any entertainment or catering industry enterprises from operating between  and  for the same period Ndeloru website Makhachkala  gmt  Nov 
Dagestan PM to head Mordovia
On  November President Vladimir Putin signed a decree appointing Dagestan prime minister Artyom Zdunov as acting head of the Republic of Mordovia Mdgazetaru website reported Prior to issuing the decree Putin accepted Mordovia head Vladimir Volkovs resignation and held a working meeting with Zdunov to inform him about plans to appoint him as Mordovia head
Despite Zdunovs appointment as acting Mordovia head the Dagestan regional government he lead remains in place Ndeloru website noted There is no mention of its resignation on the websites of Dagestan head regional government and regional ministries
Moreover although the decree on Zdunovs new appointment was published at  Moscow time  gmt on  November the website of the Peoples Assembly of Dagestan regional legislature reported after  Moscow time  gmt on  November on the meeting of the legislatures committee on budget finances and taxes held earlier the same day
Two regional ministers Yunus Saaduyev finance and Gadzhi Sultanov economy attended Neither of them was described as acting minister which Novoye Delo newspaper said was evidence that the regional government did not officially resign Mdgazetaru website Makhachkala  Nov  Ndeloru website Makhachkala  gmt  Nov 
Nephew of exhead of region sentenced for bribery
Moscows Babushkinsky court has found the former head of the state enterprise Avtokhozyaystvo Askhabali Abdulatipov who is the nephew of former Dagestan head Ramazan Abdulatipov guilty of major bribery facilitation He was sentenced to six years in a maximum security penal colony and a fine of m roubles about m dollars at the current exchange rate
Abdulatipovs codefendant former Dokuzparinsky District head Abduragim Aliskerov was sentenced to seven years in a maximum security penal colony and a fine of m roubles He was found guilty of major bribery
According to the investigators Aliskerov passed Askhabali Abdulatipov m roubles to be appointed district head The bribe according to media reports was intended for regional legislature member Radzhab Abdulatipov Ramazan Abdulatipovs brother An anonymous source cited by the RIA Derbent news agency claimed that Aliskerov was asked to pay m roubles for the appointment RIA Derbent news agency Derbent  gmt  Nov 
Federal financial support
Acting Dagestan head Sergei Melikov has submitted a bill on approval of an additional agreement with the federal Finance Ministry to the regional legislature The agreement was signed in August
According to the agreement the debt of m roubles about m dollars at the current exchange rate due as  interest payments on the  budget credit would not be paid but instead remain in the regions budget to help reduce the impact of the Covid coronavirus epidemic
The remainder of the debt  roubles will be paid back between  and  in equal instalments of  per cent of the sum owed in  m roubles Ndeloru website Makhachkala  gmt  Nov 
Dagestan will get bn roubles about m dollars at the current exchange rate from the federal budget to be paid as benefits for parents of children between three and seven years of age Federal administration has put payment of child benefits under special control allocating a total of bn roubles to the regions RGVK Dagestan TV Vremya Novostey news Makhachkala  Nov 
Effects of storm
Due to heavy wind and extensive rain parts of Dagestan were affected by a power blackout Mdgazetaru website reported On  November over  people lost access to electricity Later the same day networks authority Rosseti reported that it fully restored access to electricity
However on  November over  people in nine locations across the region were without access to electricity A total of  transformer substations in Derbentsky and Kizlyarsky districts and in the city of Makhachkala were cut Local blackouts also occurred in Kaytagsky Karabudakhkentsky Kayakentsky Magaramkentsky and Tabasaransky districts and in the city of Derbent
Part of the southern wall of Derbents historical Narynkala fortress collapsed as a result of the rain Ndeloru website reported Director of the Derbent reserve museum Viktor Chesnokov said that all relevant bodies have been informed and urgent efforts to allocate funding for repairs were under way
Earlier locals alerted the museum workers about growing cracks in the Narynkala wall It turned out that the cracks appeared immediately after restoration works were completed ahead of the  celebration of Derbents th anniversary Chesnokov said Checks indicated there is a need for urgent repairs and relevant paperwork was submitted to the Ministry of Cultures oversight bodies he added Mdgazetaru website Makhachkala  Nov  Ndeloru website Makhachkala  gmt  Nov 
Islamist criminal cases
The Investigations Committees investigating directorate for the Republic of Dagestan has started a criminal case against a yearold resident of the region who is suspected of organising the activities of an extremist organisation According to the investigators in  he initiated activities of the Takfir walHijra group in Dagestan banned in Russia since  He recruited new members called for rejecting secular laws and civil society institutions and sought to set up a theocratic state
Law enforcers are now trying to locate and apprehend the suspect The investigation continues RIA Dagestan news agency Makhachkala  gmt  Nov 
A criminal case against a yearold Derbentsky District resident was sent to court He faces up to  years in prison on charges of participation in activities of a terrorist organisation and organising funding for terrorism
According to the investigators in  the suspect took part in the activities of the Islamic State IS group collecting and transferring at least  roubles about  dollars at the current exchange rate to a member of an illegal armed group The latter allegedly used the funds to commit terroristrelated crimes RIA Dagestan news agency Makhachkala  gmt  Nov 
Four jailed for planning IS attack
The Southern Precinct Military Court has found four Dagestan residents guilty of preparing a terror attack in Makhachkala in  Khidirnebi Kazuyev was sentenced to  years in a maximum security penal colony Gabibula Khalduzov to  years Samir Ibragimov to  years and Shamil Magomedov to  years The sentence can be appealed the courts press service said
According to the prosecution the four men formed a cell of the Islamic State IS group in Makhachkala In May  Kazuyev Khalduzov and Ibragimov allegedly decided to commit a terror attack deploying improvised explosive devices IEDs at a Makhachkala gig of Russian pop singer Filipp Kirkorov However they were unable to carry out the attack as the concert hall was guarded by the police and the alleged wouldbe attackers failed to get into the concert hall
In Autumn  they were arrested and taken to custody RIA Dagestan news agency Makhachkala  gmt  Nov 
Source BBC Monitoring  Nov

Text of report by DR Congos UNsponsored Radio Okapi on  December
Presenter At least  people have been killed in a double attack attributed to elements of Codeco Cooperative for the Development of the Congo and Mai Mai rebel combatants in the territories of Djugu and Mambasa in Ituri Province northeastern DR Congo
Women and children were among the victims Other civilians were made to ferry the plundered goods
Jean Claude Loki Dile files this report
Dile Nine people were savagely killed by armed men in an attack carried out in Djugu Witnesses say the attackers were Codeco combatants
The killings took place last night at around h local time in Mblemble Bambo and Tsa three villages in the same chieftaincy
The victims were riddled with bullets before being chopped into pieces says the chairperson of a civil society organisation in Bahema Badjere
Three seriously wounded persons were taken by Monuscos United Nations Stabilisation Mission in the DR Congo Bangladeshi contingent to the hospital in Bule Desire Malodra adds
Residents who had started returning to their villages following a lull returned to an internally displaced people camp in Bule
Meanwhile in Mambasa three people were killed on Monday in an attack perpetrated by Mai Mai rebel combatants The latter raided a goldmine managed by Chinese nationals
During the clash with soldiers of the FARDC DR Congo Armed Forces two assailants were killed and a civilian succumbed to his injuries after being hit by a stray bullet witnesses say
They add that seven other people including five women were forced to ferry the loot
Source Radio Okapi Goma in French  gmt  Dec

Stories being covered today by BBC Monitoring from African broadcast press and social media sources
   
ETHIOPIAS TIGRAY CRISIS
TPLF forces claim victory over Ethiopian army 
Forces loyal to the Tigray Peoples Liberation Front TPLF have said they are scoring significant victories in the battle for the control of Tigray region against federal government troops a local TV channel has reported
The mechanised units of the Tigray Defence Forces are playing a great role in destroying the onrushing infantry and mechanised units of the enemy  Tigray TV said in a report read by a man dressed in military fatigues
They are scoring victories over the enemies in their attacks to liberate Tigray from the invaders
Tigray TV was based in Mekele the capital of Tigray region before the federal army captured the city from TPLF forces on  November It is not clear where it is located now
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said no civilians were killed in the fight for Mekele He also said no women and children are among the tens of thousands of people who fled the conflict to Sudan
Ethiopias statemanaged rights commission has called for the lifting of a communications blackout in Tigray which has made it difficult to verify claims from the warring sides
See Ethiopia communications shutdown stifles reporting on Tigray crisis
Ethiopia cannot be lectured on diplomacy amid crisis
Prime Minister Abiy has told other countries which have been calling for negotiations between his government and the northern Tigray region that Ethiopia cannot be lectured on diplomacy state media reported
Ethiopia is a country that established the UN Ethiopia is a country that established the African Union AU It cannot be lectured on diplomacy Abiy told parliament in a special session on  November
They told us to negotiate because we are poor The message I have for our friends is that we know diplomacy
His comments came amid calls by US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo for dialogue and an end to the fighting in Tigray region
The Ethiopian government has persistently rejected calls including by the African Union for negotiation with TPLF leaders
The conflict has sparked a humanitarian crisis in the region with local hospitals struggling to care for the wounded and at least  people fleeing to neighbouring Sudan
See Explainer Ethiopias Tigray conflict threatens regional stability
Ethiopia PM accuses Tigray leaders of poisoning general
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has accused the leaders of the northern Tigray regional state of poisoning a military general stationed in the region who is still unable to recover and return to work
He told parliament that  days before the war started Tigray regional leaders poisoned Gen Diriba Mekonnen during lunch with them
The prime minister also announced the end of the military operation in Tigray and said federal police will proceed with the next phase of apprehending dissident TPLF officials pending their prosecution
See Explainer How strident talk defines Ethiopias Tigray conflict
Sudan appeals for help amid refugee influx from Ethiopia
Sudanese Prime Minister Abdalla Hamdok has said his country needs UN assistance to cope with the flood of refugees fleeing fighting in Ethiopias Tigray region
Hamdok made the appeal after meeting UN refugee chief Filippo Grandi in Khartoum
Grandi said Sudan has kept the border open in the best tradition of African and Sudanese hospitality but needed at least  m over the next six months to manage the refugee crisis
Khartoum is expected to host an international conference on the issue at the beginning of next year
The arrival of nearly  of Ethiopian refugees in Sudans eastern border states of Gedaref and Kassala has put a huge strain on Sudan which was already suffering from deteriorating economic conditions political instability and recurrent ethnic conflicts
The UN said Sudan has identified a more secure site some  km away from the border to accommodate the refugees
OTHER DEVELOPMENTS
Nigeria Borno state raid was revenge attack
A website has said that the killing of dozens of rice farmers in Nigerias northeastern Borno state was a revenge attack by suspected militants loyal to Boko Haram citing residents
The Royal Times website said the militants carried out the killings after residents facilitated the arrest of one of the terrorists
Sources told the website that the attackers killed the more productive members of the community
Residents in the region have warned that a famine might be looming following the attack
A UN official said as many as  people may have been killed in the attack the most violent assault on civilians this year Others put the death toll at about 
The army has come under heavy criticism following the massacre but blamed lack of equipment for its inability to tackle the insurgency
It also accused residents of working as informants for the militants The presidency also said that the farmers had not received clearance from the military to go to the rice fields
Coordinated attacks hit military bases in Mali
Malian and foreign military bases in three towns in the north came under fire from mortars and rockets within the space of a few hours on  November
No deaths or injuries were immediately reported in the attacks on Gao Menaka and Kidal
Frances Barkhane military force has  troops deployed in the Sahel as part of antimilitant operations and there are also thousands of UN peacekeepers in Mali as well as a smaller Takuba force of European troops
Takuba and UN representatives said the attackers fired mortars into the camps causing no casualties or significant damage
The raids came days after French forces killed Bah Ag Moussa a top commander of an al Qaedalinked militant group in northeastern Mali 
See Explainer Who are the forces struggling to end Sahel violence
Niger plans to double size of army to fight militants
Nigers army should double in size to at least  soldiers in the next five years in order to tackle an insurgency ravaging parts of the country Defence Minister Issoufou Katambe has said
He told parliament that President Mahamadou Issoufou had pledged to achieve this as part of a longterm strategy against terrorism and told reporters that arrangements were being made to achieve this objective 
The countrys parliament has also passed a new law raising the retirement age for soldiers from  to 
Niger is currently facing militant threats on six of its seven international borders most of which are poorly policed
See Explainer Niger attack underscores Sahel security crisis
Uganda says no regrets after deporting Canadian journalists
A Ugandan government spokesman has said the east African nation has no regrets after it deported two Canadian media workers as it faces accusations of trying to avoid scrutiny during Januarys general election the private Chimp Reports website has reported
Awardwinning correspondent Margaret Evans of the stateowned Canada Broadcasting Cooperation CBC said she was shocked by her colleagues deportation from Uganda the website said
We were deported Friday  November even though we had official media credentials she added
Government spokesperson Ofwono Opondo said his country reserves the right to admit foreign persons including journalists Good stay where you are
The privatelyowned Daily Monitor newspaper reported last week that Uganda also deported two people working with foreign NGOs for supporting regime change
President Yoweri Museveni in power since  and seeking a sixth term has accused foreign interests of supporting opposition presidential candidate Bobi Wine
Kenya denies accusations of interference in Somali affairs
The Kenyan ministry of foreign affairs has denied allegations of meddling in Somalias internal and political affairs terming the accusations unsubstantiated
Somalia on Sunday asked Kenyan ambassador Lucas Tumbo to leave and recalled its envoy in Nairobi over what it called continuous interference in the internal and political affairs of Somalia
Kenya said it received no official notice from Mogadishu
Somalia said the Kenyan government is interfering in the electoral process in the semiautonomous Jubbaland state
Relations between the two east African neighbours have been strained in recent years mainly due to a maritime rights dispute
Tensions are also rising high over the presence of Kenyan troops and the Somali National Army in Jubbaland which is backed by Nairobi but has strained ties with Mogadishu
Meanwhile Somalias weekslong parliamentary elections are set to start today ahead of Februarys presidential vote
There are however still disagreements among Somali politicians over the composition of the teams overseeing the elections
French president wishes Guineas Conde success after reelection
French President Emmanuel Macron has wished success to his Guinean counterpart Alpha Conde following his victory in Octobers election the private Africa Guinee website has reported
Following the confirmation of your election by the constitutional council and your reelection as president of the republic of Guinea I wish success to you and the Guinean people Macron said
I am aware of the expectations of the Guinean people as well as the challenges your country is facing be it the recovery of the economic and social situation with the global health crisis or reconciliation among all Guineans after the violence divisions and questions that marked these elections
Macron recently accused Conde of having changed the constitution to stay in power
Guineas main opposition leader Cellou Dalein Diallo rejected the results of the presidential election
According to his Union of Democratic Forces of Guinea UFDG party  people were killed  wounded and  arrested during postelection violence
Tanzanian police tortured Burundi refugees says rights group
Tanzanian police and intelligence agents have arbitrarily arrested forcibly disappeared tortured and extorted Burundian refugees and asylum seekers and forcibly returned at least eight to Burundi since October  Human Rights Watch has said
It said most cases followed a similar pattern Tanzanian police entered refugee camps in Kigoma region in the middle of the night and took people away In some cases Burundians disappeared without a trace
It said some returnees continued to face hostility from local officials and the governing partys youth wing the Imbonerakure after returning from Tanzania
The UN has said the environment in Burundi is not conducive for mass returns as refugees are likely to face political persecution
Burundi has repeatedly been accused of widespread human rights abuses claims it always denies
Interpol investigates Cape Verde cyberattack
Interpol has launched a probe into a cyberattack on the Cape Verdean government by a ransomware virus privatelyowned Expresso das Ilhas newspaper has reported
The paper quoted the chairman of NOSi which manages the Cape Verdes egovernment project as saying that the network responsible for the attack had been identified
I cant provide any details on the origin of the attack as the matter is being investigated and the experts are working with us to collect evidence which will be shared with the office of the attorney general said Carlos Pina
I can however assure you that the network has been identified I cannot give any additional details as they have cells in other countries
He spoke to the press five days after a malicious software attack led to the suspension of some services of the stateowned technological network RTPE

Zimbabwe to reopen land borders
Zimbabwe has said it will reopen its borders with South Africa and other neighbours from today and ease some of the rules it put in place to contain Covid
Health Minister Constantino Chiwenga who is also the vicepresident said the government will only allow in people with certificates showing they do not have the disease
The staterun Herald newspaper said adequate protective clothing and equipment for immigration officers to cover the anticipated traffic has been acquired
Zimbabwe has recorded  Covid cases according to the government
Kenya to purchase vaccines from China
President Uhuru Kenyatta has ordered the ministry of health to begin the process of acquiring Covid vaccines from China a local newspaper has reported
The Star newspaper said there is growing frustration because most of the western manufacturers have already sold billions of doses to rich countries in advance
This means Kenya will not gain full access to affordable vaccines until after the rich world has vaccinated its people probably past  it added
In June Chinese President Xi Jinping pledged that once the development and deployment of a Covid vaccine is completed in China African countries will be among the first to benefit
Kenya has registered  Covid cases since the first infection was reported in March Health Minister Mutahi Kagwe warned yesterday that Covid seems  to be making a comeback with a vengeance in the country

Uganda Opposition presidential candidate Robert Kyagulanyi alias Bobi Wine will be campaigning in the eastern city of Jinja Officials have warned the politician and his supporters against fomenting chaos
Security forces frequently break up Bobi Wines events He was arrested during campaigns nearly two weeks ago and more than  people were killed in the protests that ensued afterwards

THE FOLLOWING IS COMPILED FROM A SELECTION OF REPORTS AND HEADLINES IN AFGHAN NEWSPAPERS AND LUNCHTIME BULLETINS ON  DECEMBER  
Afghan peace talks in Doha
The Afghan Presidential Palace has confirmed that the government and Taliban negotiating teams have reached an agreement on the code of conduct comprising  articles for the intraAfghan peace negotiations and that the work on finalising the introduction of the agreement is underway private Channel One TV TV has reported on  December
The Presidential Palace has also clarified that President Mohammad Ashraf Ghani is not obstructing the peace process the report added
It comes just a day after the Presidential Palace rejected the reports of agreement on the code of conduct of the negotiations yesterday the TV channel said
On the other hand the Jamiate Islami Party which is led by Salahuddin Rabbani has called for the formation of an interim government in the current situation the report added
Meanwhile an Afghan analyst has criticised government leaders for lacking consensus in the peace talks  
Before entering into any peace negotiations a domestic consensus should have been formed Unfortunately the leadership of the government has not held sufficient consultations with the people Mohammad Ishaq Atmar told TV
I think the agreement on the code of conduct of the negotiations is a kind of progress I call it a positive step he further said
Some newspapers have also discussed the reported progress in the peace talks
But the question is what kind of progress is it Can it be called progress when the Taliban have stepped up their attacks and aggression staterun Hewad asked
Independent daily Hashe Sobh has said that informed sources in Doha have said that discussions on start talks on the main agenda of the negotiations have begun
It added though the two negotiating teams did not have any meeting over the past several days Qatar has made efforts to play the role of a mediator the paper said
NATO stand on troops pullout
Foreign ministers of the NATO member countries will take decision regarding the future of the blocs mission in Afghanistan in their coming meeting in the month of February  TV and Ariana News TV channels have reported
The meeting will be held in virtual format for two days
NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg has said that the upcoming meeting will make the final decision whether NATO troops would continue their mission or should be withdrawn from Afghanistan TV added 
He also called on the Taliban to fulfil its part of commitments in the USTaliban peace agreement signed in Doha on  February 
We face a difficult dilemma Whether to leave and risk that Afghanistan becomes once again a safe haven for international terrorists or stay and risk a longer mission with renewed violence the channel showed Stoltenberg as saying
Whatever path we choose it is important that we do so together in a coordinated and deliberated way he further said
Stoltenberg also denounced the Talibans escalating violence while requesting the group to reduce violence and sever its relations with the alQaeda
He added that there are about  NATO forces including US troops in Afghanistan
Probe into targeted killing
Afghanistans First VicePresident Amrullah Saleh has said that some clues have been found about the assassination of Yama Siawash a former journalist and an employee of the Central Bank the Ariana News reported on  December
Chairing a security meeting today Saleh added that he cannot give an affirmative reply to media outlets requests for sharing CCTV cameras recording with them as investigation into the incident was still underway
He also said that Afghan security forces have arrested a key Taliban militants who has admitted his involvement in the killing of  government employees
Meanwhile the Ministry of Defence has said that four Taliban members have been arrested for assassinations and targeted killings in Kabul independent Tolo News TV channel reported
A statement released by the Media Office of the Ministry of Defence has said that security personnel arrested the militants in Paghman district of Kabul province last night
In press private Armane Melli daily newspaper has criticised the Talibans violence 
The Taliban and other terrorist groups ongoing war against the people of Afghanistan and the Afghan government does not have any logic and justification in Shariah as the Afghan government and its constitution are completely based on Islamic values and principles the paper said
Multiple mine blasts in Kabul
An explosion has taken place in the Afghan capital of Kabul city this morning Ariana News reported The police has said that the blast was caused by a mine hidden inside garbage in the citys Alauddin Park adding that it did not result in any casualty
In another incident unidentified gunmen have shot dead a religious scholar in Kabul city Tolo News reported on  December
A police spokesman has said that the incident took place in the Kotale Khairkhana area of Precinct No  of the city this morning adding that an investigation has been launched into the incident the report added
In the meantime the Office of First VicePresident Amrullah Saleh has said that a woman has been killed in Shakardara district of the Kabul province Police have launched an investigation into the killing the channel added
Two civilians were injured in an explosion in Kabul yesterday evening the channel reported separately
The spokesman for Kabul police Ferdows Framerz has said that the explosion happened when a roadside mine went off in the Company area of Precinct No  of the city
About another incident the police said that a mine was defused before it could explode in Kabul provinces Bagrami district Kabul Police Headquarters has said that the mine was planted in front of Rana Bahir School in the district
 Vote of confidence for nominated ministers
Today the ministersdesignate for public health border affairs rural development education economy and the acting head of the Central Bank have presented their programmes and plans to Wolesi Jerga the lower house of the parliament while seeking its vote of confidence Ariana News has reported
Today was the last day of the parliaments session on vote of confidence for the ministersdesignate
Source BBC Monitoring in Dari and Pashto  gmt  Dec

By BBC Monitoring
Rival Yemeni leaders have vowed to prevail over their competitors in speeches celebrating Independence Day as their forces continued to face off on the ground
On  November Yemeni President Abdrabbuh Mansour Hadi vowed to end the theocratic putschist Houthi project and all plans to divide and partition Yemen by all means necessary His speech was carried by the government controlled Saba news agency
On  December the head of the rebel government Abdulaziz bin Habtour expressed equal resolve in a speech vowing not to rest while a Yemeni grain of sand is still under occupation according to rebelrun AlMasirah TV
Hadi accused the rebels of carrying out Irans agenda while Bin Habtour said his rivals were currently under the occupiers feet in Riyadh Abu Dhabi and Istanbul
The Saudiled coalition has sent a new batch of weapons systems and ammunition to Yemeni forces fighting the Houthis in Maarib province Saudiowned Londonbased AlSharq alAwsat reported on  December
Battles recently escalated in Maarib which is home to hundreds of thousands of Yemenis displaced by the conflict since 
Meanwhile infighting between progovernment forces and the UAEbacked Southern Transitional Council STC continued in Abyan province 
The rival forces exchanged artillery shelling near the town of Zinjibar and a drone reportedly struck STC positions causing several casualties according to AlMasdar Online news website
In Hudaydah province where a stalled UNbrokered deescalation process is in place a string of attacks in which civilians were killed have drawn condemnation from the UN 
Commenting on the latest such attack which targeted a village in the Durayhimi district Humanitarian Coordinator for Yemen Altaf Musani was quoted as saying This attack on women and children is unacceptable and unjustifiable This is a shocking attack and a clear breach of international humanitarian law

Foreign military camps in the northern Malian towns of Kidal Gao and Mnaka were attacked simultaneously by rocket fire and shelling on  November No casualties were reported but there was some material damage according to Malian military officials Kidal residents said they heard at least  explosions at the base jointly housing United Nations forces and French Operation Barkhane counterterrorism troops At the time of writing there has been no claim of responsibility 
Significance The attacks are likely to have been perpetrated by the AlQaedalinked front Jamaat Nusrat alIslam walMuslimin JNIM for several reasons The attacks were likely carried out in retaliation for recent successes claimed by France in which its troops have killed tens of jihadists including a key JNIM commander Bah ag Moussa near Mnaka in November France also claimed the killing in June of Abdelmalek Droukdel the leader of AlQaeda in the Islamic Maghreb AQIM and JNIMs main component The attacks are also likely an attempt by AQIMs new leader Abu Obaida Yusuf alAnnabi appointed on  November to assert his authority aimed at forcing out foreign troops but also mounting major attacks to obtain leverage in potential peace talks with state authorities Malian components of JNIM have already indicated a willingness for dialogue on condition that French troops depart JNIM will want to approach talks from a position of strength and has already indicated its negotiating strength after the government freed  jailed jihadists in October in exchange for four hostages held by the group Coordinated assaults on similar targets in towns several hundred kilometres apart are unusual and indicate the jihadists increased capability with the extra resources gained from the jihadists release very likely contributing to this enhancement Further attacks targeting UN and French military bases would indicate continued exploitation of jihadists greater capacity given the momentum for dialogue within Mali and a likely attempt to delay deployment of the new counterterrorism Operation Takuba comprising European special forces units under French command Kidnapforransom risks to foreigners as further leverage are also likely to increase

Municipality IBB Mayor Ekrem Imamolu In a statement the General Directorate of Security ruled out any such attempt against the mayor dismissing recent claims by some media outlets The statement noted that similar speculations and warnings are made about state officials and politicians on a regular basis and that the relevant individuals are informed and the necessary precautions are taken It is out of the question that an assassination attempt was thwarted or an assassin was caught as claimed by the news report the police said adding that security forces continue to ensure public safety through their dedicated work against terrorist organizations such as Daesh the PKK and DHKPC IBB sources told Szc daily that they were informed of a potential assassination attempt by Daesh militants two weeks ago Imamolus security detail was also informed about the attack and took extra measures to prevent it according to the report which cited an anonymous Interior Ministry official The official reportedly said they received intelligence about an attempt which would target other figures besides Imamolu Meanwhile IBB Spokesperson Murat Ongun said they received intelligence about a potential terrorist assassination on Nov   and the mayors security has ramped up safety precautions in line with the tipoff We do not have any information about an attacker being caught Our mayors routine program has been taking place as planned since the day of the tipoff Ongun said on Twitter on Tuesday The terrorist group has been trying to establish itself in Turkey after receiving heavy blows in Iraq and Syria According to testimony by terrorists detained in previous operations in Adana province Daesh had been trying to kidnap judges prosecutors and tourist groups for ransom in return for Daesh fighters held in Iraq and Syria Turkey detained the socalled Turkish emir of Daesh Mahmut zden in August zden was planning to carry out an attack on the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque and target politicians nongovernmental organization NGO heads and other prominent figures in Turkey according to the official investigation In November Turkish police detained Daeshlinked suspects in Istanbul and Adana provinces who were planning to kidnap politicians and attack the US Incirlik Air Base Turkey recognized Daesh as a terrorist group in  and since then the country has been attacked numerous times including  suicide bombings seven bombings and four armed assaults which have killed  people and injured hundreds more In response Turkey launched military and police operations both inside and outside the country capturing top Daesh members in counterterrorism efforts at home and in Syria

AlterMidya to pursue legal action against redtaggers Philstarcom  December    am MANILA Philippines  Alternative media network AlterMidya said it will pursue legal action against those who have been redtagging them after the executive director of the governments anticommunist task force accused them without providing proof of being part of the propaganda machinery of the Communist Party of the Philippines AlterMidya said in a statement released late Tuesday night that they will exhaust all means to fight back against the malicious smear campaign on their members Showing only a presentation to a Senate hearing on redtagging National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict executive director Allen Capuyan alleged that AlterMidya and its member organizations are part of the CPPs National Propaganda Bureau under its institutional wing Capuyan said again without providing much proof that there is a wave of connection in the release of supposed propaganda against the government by these alleged members of the CPPs propaganda arm The retired colonel listed several media organizations under AlterMidya as part of the alleged communist propaganda machinery but the alternative media network pointed out that this was just merely copied from the publiclyavailable list of their members and placed under an incredible heading We can clearly see through these tactics of smearing and intimidating truthtellers and critics into silence especially in the middle of a growing discontent among the public AlterMidya said Vital role This is not the first time that AlterMidya and its members have been redtagged or accused of being part of the communist rebellion by government officials Baguio City police for one tagged Northern Dispatch managing editor Sherwin De Vera as a personality of a communist front organization AlterMidya host Inday EspinaVarona has also been accused of being part of a communist front In Senate hearings the anticommunist task force has also tagged alternative journalist Deo Montesclaros as a member of the CPP and its armed wing the New Peoples Army Aside from redtagging AlterMidya said that their members have been subjected to death threats cyberattacks harassment physical harassment physical assault detention and even attempted murder But this has not stopped it from continuing on with their work Its member outfits have a consistent record of covering underreported issues in communities  some for more than two decades while other communitybased media outfits in provinces join and continually expand the network it said It added Journalists from the alternative media relentlessly report on the situation in various communities across the country on environment issues corruption human rights abuses on the situation of farmers and workers among others The National Union of Journalists of the Philippines in a statement in solidarity with AlterMidya recognized the networks vital role in serving the peoples right to know through reportage and analysis that provide fresh perspectives to often underreported social issues The union said the rampant redtagging directed at alternative media outlets is no different than the shutdown of ABSCBN and the continued attacks on Rappler adding that this is proof that the government and security forces are bent on silencing contrary views and voices

AlQaedas Maghreb branch has revealed its weakness with new leadership AQIMs continued decline of influence and power likely to increase with Annabi a flawed replacement for the slain Droukdel Armed violence in the Sahel has led to more than m people being displaced and driven many to join armed groups AFP Published date  December   UTC  Last update  sec ago The death of its leader is a severe blow to any militant group But in succession alQaeda in the Islamic Maghreb AQIM may have revealed its true weakness In a video posted online on  November AQIM confirmed senior Algerian commander Abu Ubayda Yusuf alAnnabi would take leadership following the death of Abdelmalek Droukdel who was killed in June by a Frenchled operation in Mali Annabis lack of operational and combat experience compared with Droudkel who rose to the head of AQIM in  as an experienced battalion leader has led observers to believe he may struggle to deal with the militant groups problems Chief among them is its weakening regional dominance as AQIM suffers from a decline in influence in the face of competition between militant groups in the volatile Sahel region   This handout photo released by the French Army General Staff shows an aerial view of a vehicle during a French military operation that led to the killing of Abdelmalek Droukdel AFP Formed in  from militant groups that emerged from the s civil war in Algeria AQIM has staged several deadly attacks in the Sahel since  In response France has deployed over  troops as part of its Barkhane force working with the G Sahel states of Burkina Faso Chad Mali Mauritania and Niger to rid the region of the militants The conflict has taken  lives and among other issues like food security has spurred  million people to flee their homes It has also encouraged the rise of several groups competing with AQIM for influence which often draw fighters along tribal lines The AQIM threat is becoming marginal the group is struggling for survival Akram Kharief Algerian security expert tells Middle East Eye  Annabis Ascent  Born in the eastern Algerian city of Annaba in  Annabi  became a militant at the start of the civil war in  after finishing his degree in economics at around the same time as Droudkel  Since  Annabi has headed AQIMs Council of Notables which has been led by two previous AQIM leaders including Droudkel The Algerian has appeared several times in the groups propaganda videos for example urging Muslims in  to retaliate against Frances intervention in Mali causing him to be  blacklisted by the US in  and by the UN in   The selfstyled cleric is likely to prioritise unity between militant movements in the Sahel region  To offset the presence of its greatest rival the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara ISGS which has siphoned off AQIMs pool of potential recruits and is in  open war with the group Annabi is likely to ensure his militants are better rooted in local dynamics particularly in northern Mali Burkina Faso and Niger  MEEMohamad Elaasar That looks like a tall order Annabi at least from what is publicly known lacks the resume of any previous AQIM emir particularly in the operational domain Alexander Thurston assistant professor of political science at the University of Cincinnati told MEE Annabis appointment may not be sufficient to reverse what seems like AQIMs gradual decline   Alexander Thurston analyst His appointment may not be sufficient to reverse what seems like AQIMs gradual decline  Amid the growing influence of offshoots like alQaedas affiliate in Mali and West Africa the Group for Supporting Islam and Muslims JNIM and the shift of militant activities to the Sahara and Sahel region AQIMs desire for dominance in local dynamics isnt likely to be aided by maintaining its traditional Algerian leadership which risks reducing its influence throughout the Sahel further  The terrorist organisation has scarce human resources in Algeria and is unable to recruit The actual strategy is to maintain surveillance in rural areas and in the Sahara Kharief says Competition between militant groups According to Hannah Armstrong a senior consulting analyst with Crisis Group the militant insurgency of northern Mali and French intervention has transformed militant activity in the region since  Instead of being defeated the militants went underground and resurfaced as rural insurgencies she told MEE Clashes in central Mali and on the border with Burkina Faso between militant groups linked to AlQaeda and those loyal to the Islamic State have defined the presence of the insurgency in the Sahel over the last few years Both JNIM and ISGC have been the main focus of recent Frenchled combat operations particularly in northern parts of Burkina Faso and in northcentral Mali  In comparison AQIM are more of an afterthought There has been a stronger push by Sahelian states and their external partners to defeat these jihadist militants but in many cases military pushes into precarious rural border zones have actually led to more violence  Hannah Armstrong analyst Thurston told MEE AQIM had extraordinary success in the early s in terms of raising money through kidnappings for ransom and in terms of its overt participation in controlling northern Mali during the latter phase of the  crisis However due to the ongoing military pressure militant groups are finding it more difficult to launch the type of largescale attacks on military bases that marked the end of  and are becoming more reliant on recruiting fighters and supporters from local ethnic groups as opposed to crossborder strategies As a result greater prominence has been gained by groups like JNIM through the leadership of local figures In many ways JNIM has eclipsed AQIM Thurston said   Northern Algerian AQIM leaders including Annabi have a kind of rhetorical influence and may exercise some operational influence over JNIM But JNIMs Malian leaders also have their own priorities that appear to be rooted in local politics rather than in dictates coming from Annabi or his predecessors Though seen as important symbolic victories operations targeting the leaders of militant groups often fail to reduce the overall influence and operational capacities of groups in general  For their survival rather than relying on the charisma of its leaders militant groups exert influence by manipulating domestic grievances and using anger during popular uprisings to act as an authority in lieu of the state The impact of Droukdels assassination remains to be seen But either way corruption limited state resources and state security forces abuses has made it difficult to break the cycle of violence for Sahel states Armstrong told MEE There has been a stronger push by Sahelian states and their external partners to defeat these jihadist militants but in many cases military pushes into precarious rural border zones have actually led to more violence and higher recruitment levels from JNIM and IS instead of calming things down The trend has really been to throw more military operations at the problem and I think that is relatively unsustainable heading into the Covid era where GDPs of countries are being squeezed We should see more of an emphasis on political settlements he added Algeria weighs in On a state level AQIMs greatest threat may be the country it singled out as its primary enemy As the organisation continued to expand its operations elsewhere in the Sahel it has been struggling in Algeria since  AQIMs original target the Algerian state no longer appears threatened by AQIM or by jihadists generally AQIM also appears to have little ability to recruit or even stage major attacks in Algeria especially in northern Algeria Thurston told MEE  was the first year in more than two decades that Algeria reported no terrorist bombings and despite the organisations regular communiques urging action AQIM has not conducted a significant attack in Algeria since targeting the Krechba gas facility at In Salah in March   With more coherent counterterrorism policies and coordination of the Department of Intelligence and Security and the Directorate General for National Security Algeria has managed to control militant activities of groups like AQIM which has conducted  attacks in Algeria since  and ISaffiliated Jund alKhilafah within and along its borders where it has deployed longrange surveillance optronics  AQIMs original target the Algerian state no longer appears threatened by AQIM or by jihadists generally   Alexander Thurston analyst However despite its counterinsurgency experience Algiers has failed to dominate proceedings when it comes to dealing with the Sahel conflict and in directing how operations are conducted near its borders despite its intelligence leading to the capture and killing of a number of militants including Droudkel   According to Kharief France has denied leadership on antiterrorism in the Sahel mainly because of a lack of trust They havent involved Algeria in the G Sahel nor used the Joint Military Staff Committee of the Sahel Region based in Algeria to tackle jihadism in the Sahel Algerias dissatisfaction was heightened last month when French charity worker Sophie Petronin held since  was freed after being exchanged for over  mostly AQIMlinked militants which prompted Algiers to release a statement deploring the payment of a large ransom for the benefit of terrorist groups  A few weeks later a number of those released were arrested by the Algerian army after they were intercepted at its borders  Algerias security has vastly improved in recent years as militant groups have been pushed towards rural areas of the Sahel AFP Algiers preoccupation with the security situation in Libya ongoing domestic issues since Abdelaziz Bouteflikas presidency and the onset of the Hirak protest movement in  has prevented the Sahel from being its top priority Andrew Lebovich a policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations told MEE The Algerian government at different times has placed more or less emphasis publicly on the peace process For instance after Ramtane Lamamra was removed as foreign minister in  Abdelkader Messahel for a certain amount of time was really more focused on Libya than Mali  As Algeria looks to relaunch its diplomatic credibility and to direct some of its focus away from Libya it is likely to push for a more dominating role in solving the conflict aside from its repeated calls for the  peace accords signed in Algiers be respected The recently proposed constitutional changes  on the role of the Algerian military which could see it deployed outside Algerias borders for the first time may spell a change in Algerias foreign policy principles and how it responds to security threats in future

Knifeman stabs two people in a shop before fleeing in the Netherlands  Two people have been injured in a knife attack at a Dutch shop in The Hague on Wednesday A manhunt is underway to find the suspect who fled the scene   The citys police force tweeted that there also was a fire at the store that was quickly extinguished The two injured people were being taken to a hospital by ambulance One of the two victims is conscious the police said The attack occurred at around noon in the citys Grote Marktstraat a shopping district in the centre of The Hague on the coast of the western Netherlands  Omroep West a Dutch radio station reported that a local entrepreneur said the attack happened inside an Albert Heijn a supermarket chain in the country  People were running out of the supermarket I heard someone would have thrown alcohol on the floor and lit it said the owner of a clothes store next to the supermarket told the radio station   I heard someone inside has stabbed people he told the station that reported the people who ran out of the supermarket took refuge in a restaurant across the street  Police have launched an investigation and are appealing for witnesses and a police helicopter was seen searching for the suspect Officials have said they are looking for a tall darkskinned man believed to be in his thirties wearing a black jacket tracksuit and grey Sulawesi terror group on the run splits up to evade special forces A group of terrorists who killed four Christians last week in Central Sulawesi province have split up into two or three smaller groups in the jungle as they are being pursued by the Indonesian authorities including military special forces according to a senior field military officer He told The Straits Times on Tuesday that the group of  men split up to avoid detection as they were cornered He said they had descended from the higher mountain areas and were near the borders of Poso and Sigi regencies in Central Sulawesi We used to do our tracking work relying on IT information technology but today they do not use a single mobile phone said the senior field military officer based in Poso who spoke on condition of anonymity That incident is a blow to us Police believe the extremist Eastern Indonesia Mujahideen MIT group killed the Christian family of four and torched six homes including one frequently used to hold mass prayers in a remote village of Lemban Tongoa in the province Two of the victims were beheaded The killings last Friday in a remote location where transport is difficult have prompted Jakarta to deploy special forces from the military to beef up the manhunt The MIT led by Ali Kalora had pledged allegiance to the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria Ali Kalora took over the leadership of MIT from Santoso who was once Indonesias mostwanted terrorist Santoso was killed in July  after a massive manhunt The authorities have been hunting for the Kaloraled MIT for the last few months On Tuesday and yesterday special forces units from both the Marines and the armys Strategic Reserve Command Kostrad joined the manhunt The MIT militants descended from the mountaintop areas after Indonesian officers intensively combed Central Sulawesis deeply forested area We have been relying on human intelligence information We have to do quick followup actions after any report from villagers who incident on Saturday Nigeria and its hapless citizens have been thrown into deep grief and sorrow over the unwarranted destruction of lives and properties Slaughtering human beings as if they are animals is quite provocative and totally unacceptable The massacre has triggered widespread condemnation against the bloodthirsty pillagers as well as the nations leadership for its ineptitude over the rampage It is preposterous for this administration to continue to watch idly while people are hounded to untimely and violent deaths Beheading and all forms of decapitation of innocent citizens as well as foreigners are certainly incomprehensible and unjustifiable The audacity and frenzy exhibited in killing people by Boko Haram terrorists just as their brethren in Afghanistan Pakistan Iraq and other Arab states is driven by a deepseated philosophy In Nigeria for instance this militant squad allegedly born and bred for bizarre political and religious expansionism has metamorphosed into a Frankenstein monster as depicted in the horror novel by English writer Mary Shelley The primeval and pernicious ideology upheld by these insurgents and their cohorts is at the root of this savagery To worsen matters the current leadership and security operatives have been widely accused of lack of will to defeat these murderous group due to cultural and religious affinity This is quite glaring because for over a decade state forces have been unable to rein in the dastardly group despite their superior weapons Therefore the heavy dependence on conventional armament and tactics to this guerilla warfare is not working and cannot work This is clearly evident from their modus operandi  focusing on soft targets raping women kidnapping residents arming children and bombarding worship centers houses in rural communities in the north The  government state authorities army and the good people of the region as well as  other actors in the entire Sahel region who understand these bizarre doctrines more than other people with a different orientation must find the good will to expunge all forms of radicalism and negative notions often cited by these insurgents as reasons for their nefarious activities The escalating violence in these areas is not only sad for Northern Nigeria but also for the country which has spent incalculable funds on trying to tame these rabid killers In the latest onslaught in Koshebe village near Zabarmari in Jere Local Government Area LGA the militants allegedly slew innocent rice farmers The United Nations UN Humanitarian Coordinator in Nigeria Mr Edward Kallon in a statement on Sunday described the attack as horrifying saying it is one the deadliest attacks by the terrorist group who have been raiding the Northeast region for over a decade I am outraged and horrified by the gruesome attack against civilians carried out by nonstate armed groups in villages near Borno State capital Maiduguri Recall that in early afternoon of  November armed men on motorcycles led a brutal attack on civilian men and women who were harvesting their fields in Koshobe and other rural communities in Jere LGA Reports we are receiving are indicating these innocent farmers were the victims of this callous violence Kallon also lamented that several women may have been kidnapped in the attack We have also received reports that several women may have been kidnapped I call for their immediate release and return to safety His words The entire UN system and the humanitarian community working to provide lifesaving and development assistance to the most vulnerable in Borno State is outraged by the incident Such direct attacks against innocent civilians jeopardize the ability for the most vulnerable people to survive the adversity they are facing and which we are striving to alleviate The incident he noted is the most violent direct attack against innocent civilians this year while emphasizing the urgency  for the perpetrators of this heinous and senseless act to be brought to justice It is unfortunately one of too many such attacks targeting farmers fishermen and families who are trying to recover some livelihood opportunity after over a decade of conflict I strongly condemn this attack and any act of violence against innocent civilians and I firmly urge all actors on the ground to respect international laws and humanity He further noted that rural communities in Borno State are facing untold hardships Helping them to farm land and rebuild livelihoods are amongst our priorities and the only way to avoid the looming food crisis in Borno State They and all other civilians need to be protected and spared from any kind of violence Innocent women children and men desperately need food and other support and assistance particularly at a time when we are recording some of the highest levels of food insecurity in Borno State We owe to do our utmost to help them survive these difficult times he added The dastardly act has sparked outrage across the country with most Nigerians blaming the Federal Government for its refusal or perhaps inability to halt the mindless killings The reactions have been massive with many respondents on social media lambasting the current administration for colossal failure to secure the lives and properties Sadly the only respite from the presidency was the usual lameduck statement condemning the criminals I condemn the killing of our hardworking farmers by terrorists in Borno State The entire country is hurt by these senseless killings My thoughts are with their families in this time of grief Meanwhile Nigerians have lambasted the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Publicity Malam Garba Shehu over his comments on the issue In a series of tweets posted on Monday he said the question I tried to answer on BBC was Did the security sign off on the area as being free of mines and terrorists The honest answer is no Governor Babagana Zulum said President Muhammadu Buhari should listen to the calls of our people to end the madness of insurgents He also urged the Federal Government to collaborate with Chad Niger Cameroun and neighbouring countries to dislodge the terrorists from their dens particularly in Sambisa Forest Lake Chad region and Mandara hills in Borno and Adamawa states Peoples Democratic Party PDP described the slaughter as extremely wicked and devilish  in a statement issued by its National Publicity Secretary Kola Ologbondiyan This horrific killing of compatriots comes as yet another of the recurring horrid testament and badge of failure of the President Muhammadu Buhariled APC administration to secure our nation and guarantee safety of life and property in our country Similarly the Coalition of Northern Groups CNG in its reaction blamed  the current administration for this untoward development Its spokesperson AbdulAzeez Suleiman called for an immediate overhaul of Nigerias security architecture arguing that the north had been abandoned to the mercy of insurgents bandits and rustlers As usual several prominent citizens namely Senate President Ahmad Lawan and Speaker of the House of Representatives Femi Gbajabiamila called for more military offensive against these bombers and merchants of death These wanton killings have become an odious national emblem reflecting a systemic rot that requires serious The killer mines of Libya How they work what they do After a decade of upheaval Libya is awash with arms But mines found since Haftars assault on Tripoli are of a new type likely brought in by the Wagner Group A diagram in a Tripoli military base of a OZM found in situ by GNA forces MEEDaniel Hilton Published date  December   UTC  Last update  sec ago Fourteen months of fighting in Tripoli has turned the Libyan capitals neighbourhoods into death traps Tonnes of ordnance remain from clashes between the Libyan National Army LNA and the UNrecognised Government of National Accord GNA which controls the city Most dangerous however are the mines laid by LNA forces and now being extricated by GNA military engineers More than  civilians including children have been killed by blasts with at least  people wounded Injuries include loss of limbs Middle East Eye showed photographs of mines recovered by the GNA to Mark Hiznay  associate director of Human Rights Watchs Arms Division  Much of the weaponry and ammunition left over from the clashes between the LNA and GNA dates from the rule of Muammar Gaddafi Libyas leader until  But Hiznay said the mines laid in Tripolis streets and houses were not seen in Libya until Haftars offensive on the capital They were provided he suggests by the Wagner Group a Kremlinlinked military contractor hired by Haftar This is not Gaddafi stuff this is Wagner stuff from Russia he tells MEE I cant say Wagner had these on the aeroplane when they flew in But they got their weapons from somewhere and this wasnt the LNA PMN Some of the more common mines found in Tripoli are PMNs Russianmade devices that come in two colours green and brown PMN blast mines recovered from Tripoli MEEDaniel Hilton The top of the PMN has a black circle with a cross on which is the pressure plate These are designed to either detonate when stepped on or with a weight release These are your classic blast mines Hiznay says the ones people step on and go boom PMNs have a fairly large explosive content for its size so these are the types that blow the bottoms of legs off MON and MON The MON and MON found in Libya come in a standard Soviet green and dark brown varieties In the United States they are known as claymore mines Eight MON mines displayed on shelves at a Tripoli military base MEEDaniel Hilton The MON is stood vertically on its on legs If you are stood in front of the mine then you would be faced by a slightly curved rectangle The device is triggered either electronically or by a tripwire The MON explodes directionally sending out a degree blast radius and shards of metal sheet backed by plastic towards its target These are particularly nasty I mean theyre common but theyre nasty says Hiznay MONs are infantry mines usually found on battlefields Hiznay says Regular soldiers would carry these put in front of their defensive position and ignite if theyre under attack And this would be a lastditch thing to use before they get overrun OZM Some of the deadliest traps laid in Tripoli are the antipersonnel mines known as OZMs OZM mines in front of photographs of one of their model found in situ in Tripoli MEEDaniel Hilton The device which is usually olive green is buried in the ground When activated it leaps a metre into the air before detonating sending shards of its cast iron body and steel fragments out in a degree blast radius Like the MON the OZM can be triggered by command or through a trip wire Victimactivated detonation through tripwires is banned under international law  but manual electronic detonation is legal in the belief that the mine operator can distinguish between a civilian and a combatant The Americans called them Bouncing Bettys when they encountered the German version of this in World War Two Hiznay says Somewhere out in the Libyan desert theres going to be the German grandfather of this device But we didnt see these OZMs in the other parts of the civil war PAM The fourth kind of Russian mine MEE saw was the PAM These are antipersonnel mines that were originally designed to be scattered from helicopters rockets and launchers PAM antipersonnel mines recovered from the Tripoli battlefield MEEDaniel Hilton When deployed the PAM falls on the ground rights itself on its six legs and shoots out springloaded tripwires If anyone touches the tripwire a cylinder launches one metre into the air before detonating Silver containers used to deploy PAMs from trucks have been recovered from battlefields across Libya But bomb disposal experts have also recovered green cylinders that are used to hand place PAMs like a grenade  a tactic employed by Wagner in a previous conflict We first started seeing that in Ukraine in Donetsk Hiznay says and now its popped up here again in Libya

Just in Businessman kidnapped in Zimpeto Maputo on Friday  Lusa Just in Businessman kidnapped in Zimpeto Maputo on Friday  Lusa  CAT   Dec   Comments Print Share A businessman was kidnapped on Friday afternoon in Maputo the Mozambican capital a police source told Lusa today Wednesday The businessman reportedly of Indian origina  is said to have been kidnapped by three armed men on his way home from the house of a family member said Leonel Muchina a spokesman for the Police of the Republic of Mozambique PRM They fired some shots to persuade the victim to give in dragged him into a vehicle and fled he said The yearold commercial entrepreneur was on his way home and was reportedly kidnapped in the Zimpeto neighbourhood on the outskirts of Maputo The PRM said that investigations are underway coordinated with the National Criminal Investigation Service Sernic to clarify the crime Figures so far put forward by the Mozambican authorities indicate that  kidnappings have occurred in the country including the last one on Friday since the beginning of the year whose victims are always businessmen or family members In October a group of businesspeople in the city of Beira Sofala province central Mozambique stopped their activities for three days in protest against the wave of abductions in the country The Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique CTA the largest employer association in the country has also demanded on several occasions a severe fight against this type of crime and even the Mozambican President Filipe Nyusi has already called for more measures In November the Mozambican Government promised an energetic fight against kidnappings describing this type of crime as horrendous revealing that it is investing on strengthening the capacity of the police endowing the corporation with more modern means to combat kidnappings

How Irans Nuclear Chief Fakhrizadeh was assassinated Sharjah   Reuters Iranian journalist Mohamad Ahwaze claims to have received leaked information from the countrys government about the assassination of Irans leading nuclear scientist on Friday Ahwaze says the attack was carried out by  gunmen who were supported by a team of  operatives providing them with information and logistics He says the hit squad knew Mohsen Fakhrizadehs security convoy was on its way to his holiday home and were waiting in ambush at a traffic circle marking the entrance to the town of Absard As the convoy entered the traffic circle a car bomb exploded hitting the rear security car The  attackers then opened fire on the middle car with machine guns and  sniper rifles According to Ahwaze one of the attackers then dragged the scientist out of his car and executed him The attackers then disappeared and so far not one attacker has been caught The Iranian Fars News Agency gave a conflicting report saying that there were no gunmen and that the attack was done by firing a remotecontrolled machine gun mounted on the truck that later exploded

MINNA  Suspected armed bandits have continued their onslaught and incursion into parts of Niger state as they lately launched an attack on two local markets Daja and Mangun villages killing at least four persons and also losing one of their own members to the villagers
The advancing suspected terrorist group from NigerNorth senatorial district riding on motorcycles and wielding AK  rifles our correspondent learnt invaded the local market late Monday afternoon when most of the traders were about rounding up for the days business
It was further gathered that the gun men acting on a tip off had stormed the village market and went straight to the resident of a local produce merchant simply identified as Baira but unfortunately for them met his absence
Angered by missing their target the bandits were said to have made their way into the busy market as it was the local market day and started shooting indiscriminately to scare away traders including visiting traders before embarking on a looting spree
While many of the traders scampered for safety two people hit by the bullets died as a result of injuries sustained from gun shots before help could come their way a resident of the area told daily Independent
The bandits were said to have in a commando like manner fled towards to Mangun village but unfortunately were waylaid by the vigilantes at Daja who on getting wind of the attack in their neighbourhood quickly mobilized and in the confrontation one of the bandits was killed
Local vigilantes confronted the bandits as they made their way to escape through Daja but unfortunately lost two of their fighters while the bandits also lost one of their own to the villagers before disappearing into the nearby forest
Chairman of the Niger State Emergency Management Agency NSEMA Alhaji Ibrahim Tanko Inga who confirmed the attack to journalists said his agency was informed of the attack yesterday Tuesday
Meanwhile efforts to confirm the attack from the state Police Public Relations Officer PPRO ASP Abiodun Waisu as at the time of filing this report failed to yield desired results as he refused to pick repeated calls

Brutal Attack on Indonesian Christians Stirs Renewed Fears of Persecution On Friday November  a jihadi attack took place against Christians in Sulawesi one of Indonesias largest islands This vicious attack resulted in the mutilation and death of four members of the local Salvation Army including at least one beheading along with the torching of several homes and a Christian house of worship Asia News reported  Four members of the same Christian family have been found murdered some of them beheaded All four belonged to the Protestant Church of Salvation Salvation Army Their dismembered bodies were found yesterday Central Sulawesi police reported today The murder took place in the village of Lenowu Lemban Tongoa district Sigi This attackwhich was preceded by a period of relative calmhas stirred up horrifying memories of similar brutalities in the same region beginning more than a decade ago On New Years Eve   a bomb exploded at a Christianarea market in Palu Central Sulawesi killing eight people and injuring  That May another bombing in the predominantly Christian village of Tentena Sulawesi left  dead and at least  injured Months later the Associated Press reported the beheadings of three Christian teenagers in October Six men attacked four girls Theresia Morangke  Alfita  Poliwo  Yarni Sambue  and Noviana Malewa early in the morning as they walked to a Christian school in the Poso district The first three girls were beheaded Noviana Malewa received serious injuries to her face and neck but survived the attack The murdered girls heads were wrapped in black plastic bags One was found on the steps of a Kasiguncu village church The other two were left at a nearby police station One of the bags contained a note some of which read We will murder  more Christian teenagers and their heads will be presented as presents In  three Indonesian Catholics were executed by firing squad in Palu Sulawesi having been found guilty of incitement to murder during rioting At the time Amnesty International responded Such murders approved by the State are even more unacceptable when there are as in this case serious doubts about the fairness of the trials Indonesias population is  percent Muslim But in recent years there have been largely successful efforts by Indonesias government to enforce religious freedom Other attacks have happened in various Indonesian cities over the years but the region of Sulawesi has been a particular hotspot of Islamist terror Sadly this recent attack on Christians has renewed countrywide concerns Central Sulawesi police have affirmed finding the four victims dismembered bodies but so far the identity of the killers remains in question According to BBC  The Salvation Army confirmed the killing of its members in a savage attack in a statement last week Our hearts go out to our people who have been victims of evil and to the families of those whose faith have caused such harm In a report from Reuters  Indonesian President Joko Widodo condemned the brutal murder by suspected Islamist militants as beyond the limits of humanity as the military chief prepared to deploy special forces to join the hunt for the killers In a video address the president said the attack on Friday in a region riven by bloody sectarian conflict in the past was designed to drive a wedge among the population in the worlds biggest majorityMuslim nation That gross act had the purpose of provoking and terrorizing the people They wanted to destroy the unity and brotherhood of our people he said We need to stay united in the fight against terrorism I spoke to my friend and colleague Paul Marshall a Senior Fellow in Religious Freedom at the Hudson Institute and a scholar who focuses on Indonesia He has spent much time there over many decades I asked him about these recent concerns regarding religious freedom and the situation specifically in Sulawesi He explained The dominant forms of Islam in Indonesia continue to be moderate and tolerant But there are threats from more radical groups Only one of Indonesias  provinces states Aceh is governed by Sharia law but some other counties and villages are restrictive according to Islamic standards In Indonesia there are also outright terrorist groups some affiliated with ISIS that have carried out sporadic violent attacks throughout the country although they tend to be scattered and weak Perhaps more ominous is the return from Saudi Arabia on November  of   Muhammad Rizieq Shihab  the founder of the Islamic Defenders Front a radical militia His reappearance has now emboldened more radical elements According to current reports on the recent violence the Indonesia government has indeed pulled in military special forces to supplement police antiterrorism units in the hunt for the Sulawesi terrorists who are believed to be hiding in a remote area Some locals have claimed to have seen and recognized the killers Thus far however there have been no arrests

was aimed to hit an Afghan Security Force military pickup that was driving in front of the Russian Embassys vehicle There is however a possibility that the Russian diplomatic staff was targeted forces were also being frequently targeted Currently the only faction that targets all parties indiscriminately are ISIS militants cells that carry out attacks in various regions The situation remains tense in Afghanistan even after the US and the Taliban signed a truce earlier in  Under the conditions of the agreement the Taliban has vowed to stop attacks on American forces in the country prevent it from turning into a safe haven for terrorist organizations and to engage in dialogue with the government in Kabul In return the US promised to withdraw its forces from the country after  years of war Earlier in November Washington announced a partial withdrawal of its forces from the country even though occasional attacks continue to take place some of them purportedly carried out by the Taliban itself In addition the group and the Afghan government have still not engaged in the expected dialogue to reach a political solution to the conflict which has been ravaging the country for UN envoy insists killers of Bornos farmers must be brought to justice From Timothy Olanrewaju Maiduguri United Nations Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Nigeria Mr Edward Kallon has called for the prosecution of Boko Haram insurgents that beheaded over  farmers in a Borno town last weekend  Kallon made the call in a statement on Wednesday after visiting Zabarmari a remote community near the farmland almost every day since the attack clearly show that the terror act as sheer inhumanity and abject cruelty He said the UN was committed to doing their utmost to support the people of Borno State especially the the most vulnerable people many of whom live in such remote areas This attack on Saturday is unfortunately one of too many such attacks targeting farmers fishermen and families RIO DE JANEIRO  The assailants arrived in the sleepy city in southern Brazil ready for battle They wore head coverings and body armor and they were armed with powerful rifles and loads of explosives                       Shortly before midnight on Monday explosions and volleys of gunfire shattered the calm and jolted the residents awake                       Over nearly two hours the gunmen held the city of Cricima hostage using people as human shields while they detonated explosives at a local branch of the Bank of Brazil sending a plume of bills flying into the air and shot at an overwhelmed police force                       It was a surreal scene said Clsio Salvaro mayor of the city of about  said in a televised interview Tuesday morning The city was left in a state of panic                       Brazil has among the highest crime and homicide rates in the world and bank robberies are hardly uncommon In recent years gangs have attempted to dig their way to millions through tunnels have detonated dynamite to rob banks and have blown up cash machines                       The audacious attack on Cricima was the latest in Brazil to target a relatively small city with poor defenses where security analysts say they have good odds of overpowering and dodging security forces that deal mainly with petty crime Criminals have carried out a handful of similar attacks in such places this year                       In this latest assault analysts said a team of roughly  gunmen arrived in a convoy of  vehicles from outside the state Santa Catarina and had planned the operation meticulously Officials have not said how much money they made off with                       The operation was successful for the criminals thats the truth Santa Catarina GovCarlos Moiss da Silva said They pulled off what they set out to do                       Police officials in Santa Catarina said the gunmen opened fire outside the th battalion of the military police which oversees security in the city before heading downtown and taking aim at the bank                       The gunfire left a security guard and a police officer wounded Police officials said the officer underwent surgery and described his condition on Tuesday morning as serious                       There are several drug trafficking gangs in Brazil that have carried out sophisticated robberies but authorities did not point to any of them as suspects
