By BBC Monitoring

So far there has been very limited jihadist reaction to the arrival of  British troops in Mali announced by the UK government on  December to bolster the UN peacekeeping mission in the country
While jihadists are not always quick to respond to or show interest in developments that are reported in mainstream media the muted reaction is nevertheless interesting
It may suggest that many have not yet registered the news  and may comment in coming days  or that the number of deployed British troops  is not seen as a big deal in the context of the thousands of foreign troops already present in the country 
Jihadists usually show an interest in new foreign deployments focused on counterterrorism especially in a country like Mali where the stakes are high for jihadists and where rivals alQaeda and Islamic State group IS are both active
Among the few reactions observed by BBC Monitoring was that of Islamist writer Majid alAhmad MajedAmed on Twitter In a comment on  December he said the UK deployment is evidence of the failure of French troops in Mali before adding and by the way these are all occupying forces hiding behind the cloak of peace in our modern time 
On  December Telegram user Dr alNasiri Comecai who focuses on Iraq news and is clearly sympathetic to IS factually shared details of the deployment as reported in the media without giving his own opinion
Mali where the fight against jihadists is spearheaded by France through its Operation Barkhane is among the most discussed conflict zones by jihadists The militants seek to replicate their  territorial gains that allowed alQaedaaffiliated groups to temporarily run the northern part of Mali
Currently alQaedas Sahel affiliate Jamaat Nusrat alIslam walMuslimin JNIM is the most active militant group in the country sporadically claiming attacks on French local and UN forces
AntiFrance messaging and attacks have increased in recent weeks over the countrys position in defending free speech on the subject of the Prophet Muhammad cartoons
In November proalQaeda media outlets reported attacks allegedly carried out by locals in Kidal in northern Mali targeting French convoys over the Prophet cartoons 
Meanwhile IS activity against local and foreign troops in the country has seen a notable drop this year apparently as a result of its infighting with the more capable alQaeda
Source BBC Monitoring in Arabic  gmt  Dec

Arab states hail reports of imminent Gulf reconciliation 
Several Arab countries have hailed reports of an imminent USbrokered Gulf reconciliation that if it materialises will see an end to a yearslong rift between Qatar and some of its Gulf neighbours
On  December Kuwaiti Emir Nawaf alAhmed sent three separate messages to Saudi King Salman bin Abdulaziz Qatari Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani and US President Donald Trump in which he praised the three leaders efforts to realise a historic achievement in solving the crisis
Kuwaiti AlRai newspaper quoted a senior diplomatic source as saying that reconciliation would take place at the upcoming Gulf summit scheduled to be held in Bahrain this month

Yemeni official urges US to designate Houthi rebels a terror group
Yemeni Vice President Lt Gen Ali Mohsen Saleh has told visiting US officials that the Houthi rebel group is escalating its attacks calling for the movement to be designated as a terrorist organisation
The rebels actions put the international community before a great responsibility to rescue UN agreements exert pressure on the movement and its financial backers in Tehran and preserve global security staterun Saba news agency reported Saleh as telling US diplomat David Schenker yesterday evening
More importantly the international community must respond to popular political and legal demands to criminalise this group and promptly include it on terror lists the vice president said
The Houthis have dismissed the threat of a terror listing by the US as laughable
Kuwait election results show allmale new parliament
The Kuwaiti National Assembly parliament election has resulted in an allmale legislature and several former MPs losing their seats
The incoming parliament will have  new members and  MPs who were reelected the website of AlQabas daily reported yesterday
More than  candidates competed for the  seats of the National Assembly
None of the  women candidates were elected including the only female member of the outgoing chamber  firebrand lawmaker Safaa alHashem
The election was held on  December despite the Covid pandemic with voter turnout reaching  per cent

GNA condemns failed attack on Tindi base
The GNA has issued stinging condemnation of a breach of the ceasefire by forces backed by Field Marshall Khalifa Haftars Libyan National Army LNA following a failed attack on the GNAcontrolled Tindi military base in Ubari in southwest Libya on  December
We consider this breach to be part of an external agenda aimed at thwarting the peaceful solution to Libyas crisis through dialogue the statement said criticising Haftars lack of sincerity in abiding by signed agreements
It added that the GNA was also surprised by the silence of United Nations Support Mission in Libya UNSMIL on the attack given the missions vocal support for the ceasefire
ProGNA media reported earlier that day that dozens of LNA vehicles arrived in Ubari and launched attacks on GNA soldiers stationed at the base However GNA forces were able to repel the attack and force LNA fighters to withdraw to the towns outskirts
LNA commits to ceasefire criticises GNAbacked armed militias
Haftars LNA hit back at the GNAs criticism issuing its own statement in the early hours of  December condemning the increasing number of GNAbacked armed militias in Tripoli Misrata and the transfer of weapons to the frontlines at Sirte and alJufrah
The statement published on the Facebook page of the LNA spokesperson also reaffirmed the groups commitment to the UN ceasefire agreement and the ongoing talks
The LNA command has ordered all of its units to be on a high alert and not to be drawn into any provocations that could lead to an escalation of the military situation the statement added
Doctor kidnapping suspect admits charges claims GNA
GNA Interior Minister Fathi Bashaga has said a man arrested over the fourday abduction of prominent surgeon Siddiq Khalfallah Ben Della has admitted to his involvement in the attack
In his first statement since Ben Dellas release on  December Bashagha said that an intensive investigation into the kidnapping had resulted in the doctors safe return home and the arrest of a suspect
Meanwhile UNSMIL has welcomed Ben Dellas release issuing a statement in English calling for a full and independent inquiry into all incidents of arbitrarily detention kidnapping perpetrated by armed groups who continue to undermine the rule of law across Libya
Domestic media had reported on  December that two people had been arrested following Ben Dellas release earlier that day
Unity talks in Ghadames postponed
The official unified session of Libyas parliament scheduled for  December in the town of Ghadames has been postponed by at least one day an MP has told proGNA channel AlAhrar TV
Representative Ismahan Balaoun said the session would take place on  or  December adding that over  MPs  from both the Tobrukbased House of Representatives HoR and its rival High Council of State HCS  had arrived in Ghadames meeting and exceeding the legal quorum for an official meeting
Preliminary talks in the oasis town which was selected due to its distance from Libyas two rival centres of power had begun on  December discussing rules of procedure and the division of representatives into committees according to privately owned website AlWasat
However a group of MPs from Libyas eastern administration have voiced their opposition to the Ghadames talks insisting that all official parliamentary sessions must be held in Benghazi proeastern news agency Lana reported
The Ghadames talks had been thrown into uncertainty when Aguila Saleh the Speaker of Libyas easternbased House of Representatives HoR invited all  Libyan MPs to attend an official session in Benghazi on the same day as the planned meeting in Ghadames
Saleh complained on  December that last months meeting of Libyan MPs in Tangiers had been coordinated without him according to a tweet by Saudi broadcaster AlArabiya
The Ghadames session had been agreed upon during the Tangiers talks which were attended by representatives from Libyas rival administrations
GNA defence minister discusses arms embargo with UK envoys
The GNA Defence Minister Salahedin alNamroush met with the UK Ambassador to Libya Nicholas Hopton and UK Defence Attach Mark Bavin on  December to discuss enhanced cooperation between the UK and Libyan defence ministries
AlNamroush expressed the ministrys current challenges in relation to the arms embargo on Libya which has been an obstacle to its humanitarian duties including monitoring illicit migration and clearing landmines according to a GNA Defence Ministry statement on Facebook
AlNamroush also voiced his concern over the United Nations lack of seriousness in solving the Libyan crisis
According to the statement Hopton in turn offered the UKs support for the GNA including providing aid for mine clearance operations as well as support for using DNA evidence to identity victims of violent crimes

Fighting erupted over the weekend among Ethiopian forces at a base in central Somalia after an attempt to disarm ethnic Tigrayan Ethiopian soldiers Somali media sources say
Somalias privatelyowned Radio Risala reported that the infighting occurred after Tigrayan commanders and soldiers resisted attempts to disarm them
The proShabab Somali Memo website said it is not known why the Ethiopian troops are disarming their fellow soldiers but the move was believed to be linked to the ongoing fighting in Tigray in northern Ethiopia
Another private Somali website Garowe Online said that the Tigray conflict divides Ethiopian troops under AU mission in Somalia into ethnic lines and that there was an exchange of fire at the Ethiopian base camp in Halgan area in Hiiraan region
It quoted residents as saying that they heard gunshots at the Ethiopian base in central Somalia but could not confirm casualties
Ethiopia which is battling alShabab militants in neighbouring Somalia launched a military operation in Tigray on  November after the regions forces reportedly attacked a federal army base

IntraAfghan peace talks
A Joint Working Committee of the Afghan government and Taliban negotiating teams met on  and  December to finalise the agenda of the intraAfghan peace talks private Ariana News and independent Tolo News TV channels have reported
The Joint Working Committee is scheduled to meet today also as the two sides could not reach an agreement on the components of the agenda during their meeting held on previous two days Ariana News added
The spokesman for the Talibans political office in Doha Mohammad Naeem has said that these were preliminary meetings adding that defining the agenda of the intraAfghan peace negotiations would take time the channel said  
Although the details of the meeting have not been made public both sides expressed optimism about moving ahead to finalise the agenda Tolo News channel and its website have added
The Taliban have not yet said anything about their priorities in the next phase of the talks but US charge daffaires to Kabul Ross Wilson told journalists the group wants  remaining fighters freed from jail Tolo News TV and private Channel One TV TV channel reported on  December

In an opinion piece published by Svenska Dagbladet representatives of the World Jewish Congress the Jewish Central Council of Sweden and the Central Council of the Jewish Congregations in Finland called on Sweden to act tough on racists who pose a dangerous threat to both Jews and refugees
In recent years racist and Nazi organisations have become increasingly active The number of reported hate crimes is increasing more activities are carried out by these organisations throughout Sweden and racist propaganda is becoming more common on the internet the Jewish representatives wrote
The authors insist that the groups must be banned because they pose a threat to democracy and seek to prevent them from organising disseminating information or demonstrating on the countrys streets
When a group seriously threatens democracy it is of the utmost importance that the democratic society acts vigorously they wrote referring to the UN International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination ICERD which requires the signatories to prohibit such organisations
The Jewish representatives called on Sweden to follow Finlands example and specifically ban the panScandinavian Nordic Resistance Movement NMR Finland outlawed the organisation in  and upheld the ban in  while many questioned its efficacy as its members may choose to organise under a different banner
In the appeal the NMR was accused of disseminating classic antiSemitic myths that blamed the Jews for genocide plans for world domination sexual perversion and being bloodthirsty The same kind of antiSemitic ideas that more than  years ago led to the Holocaust and the murder of six million Jews the letter said
The NMR was also described as being dangerous to refugees and members of the LGBT community as both allegedly suffered attacks based on hatred
The NMR is a Nazi racist and proviolence organisation that poses a threat to our open democracy The groups mere presence in the public space leads to concerns about incidents and psychological and physical violence against individuals the letter concluded
The NMR is a panNordic movement with roots in Sweden that seeks to create a unified nondemocratic Nordic State Since its foundation in the late s it has mushroomed into neighbouring Finland Norway Denmark and even Iceland Its members have reportedly served prison terms for crimes such as robberies assault manslaughter and paramilitary activity that includes the illegal possession of firearms Justifying the ban the Finnish Interior Ministry branded the organisation a revolutionary and militant movement whose goal is to create a National Socialist state

Irans changing tactics The Arab coalition to restore legitimacy in Yemen reported last month that it had thwarted a Houthi terrorist operation targeting a Greek oil tanker in the vicinity of the Bab AlMandab strait According to the coalition sources an explosive laden speedboat was used in the attack On Saturday the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations UKMTO naval authority reported that it was aware of an attack on a vessel off the coast of Yemen The authority later updated the advisory notice on its website to say the incident is now complete Vessel and crew are safe UKMTO gave no further details The two attacks mark a dangerous precedent that indicate that Houthi militias with Iranian support have begun to escalate hostile activities targeting international commercial navigation in the Red Sea Previous attacks carried out by the Houthis were restricted to vessels belonging to coalition members or its main allies The Saudiled Coalition also reported that the Houthis planted  mines in the Red Sea near Bab AlMandab  an additional sign that the Houthis are bent on increasing the risks to international maritime traffic The escalation comes at a time of a growing Iranian footprint in Yemen following the arrival of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps IRGC commanders under diplomatic cover In October Tehran announced that it had appointed Hassan Eyrlou an IRGC leader as its plenipotentiary and extraordinary ambassador to Sanaa According to coalition reports since  the Houthis have staged numerous terrorist attacks against coalition ships starting with the UAE auxiliary ship HSV Swift using a Chinese made C missile In October  the Houthis fired several missiles against the USS Mason but missed In January  three mined dinghies struck a Saudi frigate west of Hodeida port as the ship was patrolling within the coalitions zone of operations The attack killed two crew members and injured three others Two months later Arab coalition forces intercepted three speedboats converging on several ships near the Yemeni port of Midi In April of the same year the Houthis struck a Saudi oil tanker near Hodeida In July  the Houthis struck two more Saudi tankers but inflicted only minor damage As the foregoing tells us there is an upward trajectory in the Iranianbacked Houthi terrorist threat in the Red Sea When we compare the recent operations to the abovementioned ones we notice a number of significant trends One is the salient qualitative shift towards a lack of discrimination between vessels belonging to coalition membersallies and those belonging to other nationalities The tanker struck two weeks ago was Greek It follows that there is a strong possibility that the Houthis and Iran have shifted to a strategy of threatening maritime traffic in the Red Sea in general Also significant is the diversity in means maritime mines missiles made in China and modified in Iran and with greater frequency explosive laden boats The latter means might be favoured because it is easier to use and may cause more damage The preference may also be influenced on the one hand by the lack of precision in striking targets at long range as was the case with the USS Mason and on the other hand by the fact that speedboats can pack a bigger explosive charge than a single mine and also pursue their targets Another possible reason behind this development is that Iran wants to shift the thrust of its threat from the Gulf to the Red Sea by way of the Arabian Sea which is less of a sign of a decision to reduce the level of threat to the Straits of Hormuz as it is a sign of a strategy of augmenting the threat to maritime routes As for the use of a proxy for this purpose Iran realises that if it undertook such an attack itself it would invite an American response which President Donald Trump had said he was ready to deliver The types of ships attacked offer further insight into HouthiIranian strategy That most of the attacks target oil tankers is clearly meant to deliver a message that says that imposing sanctions against the Iranian petroleum sector will elicit a response in kind The Houthis would be motivated by similar reasons The coalition has a chokehold on oil supplies through Hodeida Port which helps explain Houthi attacks against Aramco facilities and the petroleum derivatives facility in Jeddah Such factors confirm that the Houthis strategic aim is to use the terrorism weapon against the movement of oil as a pressure tactic and bartering card  In light of the foregoing it appears important to assess the efficacy of maritime safety measures in the coalitions theatre of operations According to figures available in Arab coalition reports  per cent of attacks were intercepted and one the attempted missile attack on the USS Mason failed due to poor targeting although the missile targeting the HSV Swift hit its mark As for the mined speedboat attacks many were intercepted before reaching their target In the recent cases when the payload struck the damage was limited In general there were no preemptive operations to thwart Houthi attacks The coalition has also been successful at mine clearing operations along Yemens western coast However it should be stressed here that the Houthis ability to strike in the vicinities of Bab AlMandab to the south and Muhra governorate to the southwest means they have a reach that extends well beyond their areas of control and influence This is too large of an area for the coalition to safeguard on its own given the limited size and capacities of the Yemeni coast guard In addition the two recent incidents ie the strike against the Greek tanker and the one reported by UKMTO reflect a lack of international support for the coalitions operations in this region at a time when Iran and its Houthi proxy are increasing threat tactics in the region and when there is a greater need for intelligence and technical cooperation to deal with qualitatively different types of risks and the new directions they are taking Coalition leaders clearly expected more as in the aftermath of the attacks against AlFujairah and Aramco last year the US and other world powers said that they would work to safeguard maritime traffic in this region A version of this article appears in print in the  December  edition of AlAhram Weekly Search Its a European and global issue EU Commission VP Margaritis Schinas JPost  Its sometimes hard for American progressives to understand Jewish support for Israel One reason is that the United States is relatively free of antiSemitism compared to other democratic nations although its on the rise here Thats one reason my grandparents and father moved here from Paris before WWII  A recent report found that in  there were over  reported antiSemitic attacks in the EU Another European Union survey of European Jews found that in the prior  years  personally experienced an antiSemitic act Just as importantly only  said they reported it the rest said reporting it was useless  Harretz  Nowhere is antiSemitic terrorism more evident than in France which has the third largest number of Jews in the world As immigration of Muslims to Europe has increased and the ultranationalist right movement has risen European Jews have been under increasing attack In the wake of these attacks in  Prime Minister Netanyahu of Israel called for French Jews to move to Israel To some this may sound like a radical response to the crisis But lets put this call into context  Many on both the French right and left have ignored or rationalized antiSemitism On the right its the familiar charge of shylock or Christ killer The left has often cited violence in the West Bank and Gaza as an excuse for Muslims attacking French Jews who have never even been to Israel and may not be Zionists at all   Charlie Hebo a French publication which ran a cartoon making fun of Islam was attacked several years ago Afterwards over  million people came out to decry efforts by Islamic religious radicals to stifle a free press via violence But only secondarilyas an afterthought did that rally also mention the simultaneous murdering of French Jews at a Paris kosher supermarket  The most heinous antiSemitic act in France in recent years was the  kidnapping and killing of Ilan Halimi as detailed in the Tablet newsletter and French papers Halimi was a yearold Parisian who was kidnapped specifically because he was a Jew The key players were primarily Muslims or Muslim converts Although his captors believed all Jews to be rich Halimi was a cell phone salesman from a poor immigrant family  The kidnappers asked for  Euros in ransom which the family could not pay   He was held for three weeks duct taped from head to feet with a straw for feeding Occasionally he was unwrapped solely for the purpose of being burned and horribly tortured especially in his sexual organs After three weeks Halimi naked handcuffed bleeding and with severe burns covering  of his body was finally set free by his captors Tied to a tree he died within minutes of being found  No less than  people were either directly involved or knew details of the abduction which they kept to themselves In   people were convicted with the leader receiving a life term but the others getting ridiculously lenient sentences some as little as  months Some were just acquitted   The Halimi murder is the most gruesome individual case but there have been numerous recent incidents of violence against French Jews both by Muslims and by ultranationalists once again using Jews as a scapegoat   Several years ago a Jewish school in Toulouse was attacked killing a Rabbi and several children The Synagogue of La Roquette was attacked by  protesters trying to get inside and harm Jews trapped inside They were initially driven off by young Jewish men and then eventually by police  In recent years Jewish businesses were firebombed and burned  Innocent French Jews were attacked with stun guns and Tasers sprayed with tear gas and beaten One even had a swastika cut into his chest Swastikas were painted on graves in Jewish cemeteries But there were no massive millionperson rallies by the French to protest these outrages  Moreover it is impossible to forget the negative climate regarding Jews that has existed in both Europe and France long before the relatively recent Muslim immigration  Frances long history of antiSemitism is exemplified by the infamous Dreyfus Affair in  Captain Dreyfus a Jewish artillery officer was falsely convicted of treason based on trumped up evidence The real culprit a wellconnected Christian went free   Collaboration with the Nazis was widespread something that the French and Europeans would rather forget With the help of French collaborators many Jewish French citizens men women and children were rounded up They were then deported in cattle cars and murdered by the Nazis   France between  and   Unless France tackles its longstanding problem of antiSemitism including hate crime attacks by Muslim immigrants Jews emigrating to Israel and America will increase After all who would individual travelled extensively and always alone except for his travel to North Korea as part of a tour group  The longest visit the individual made to any one country was to India where he stayed early age and was also an avid internet user it said  In February  he booked flights to New Zealand to arrive in Auckland on August   and then on to Dunedin on August   We see these activities as the Houthi spy confessions reveal infiltration of Yemeni army ADENConfessions of a Houthi spy cell broadcast by the internationally recognised Yemeni governments official television station revealed the extent of militia infiltration into some institutions of the internationallyrecognised government considered Yemens legitimate authority  and the escalation of the Houthis intelligence activity The Houthi spy cell was reportedly operating within the Yemeni National Army and the defence ministrys headquarters in Marib The report which was broadcast Saturday evening under the title Threads of Labour includes confessions of Houthi cell members in Marib that they infiltrated army institutions in what is the first official recognition by the legitimate government of such an occurrence The report features confessions by senior officers in the Yemeni defence ministry in Marib including a brigadier Khaled AlAmir who served as director of the warehouse department in the armys logistical support authority and one of his relatives a lieutenant called Basem Ali Abdo alSamit who was in charge of surveillance photography sending coordinates and communicating with senior intelligence officers of the Iranbacked Houthis in Sanaa According to military sources the Houthi cell played a key role in determining the locations of the meetings of leaders of the National Army in Marib among them Defense Minister Mohammad Ali alMaqdashi and Chief of Staff Sagheer bin Aziz Those meetings were targeted by direct Houthi missile strikes that killed some of their companions The cell was also in charge of locating weapons caches and some tribal and military leaders residences The confessions obtained from a member of the cell who made multiple visits to Sanaa during which he met with prominent Houthi military and security leaders including Abdul Hakim alKhawani who runs the Houthi National Security Agency revealed that Iran played a direct role in directing missiles and drones Speaking of operations including drones and missiles the cell member explained that Tehran was deeply involved in the activity even mentioning a meeting that was held in the presence of Iranian and Iraqi figures Yemeni Information Minister Muammar alEryani said that the recordings revealed dangerous information according to the confessions of the Houthi militias spy cell official Eryani added These confessions confirm the presence of experts from Iran and Iraqi militias in the Houthi operation rooms and their participation in preparing missile attacks targeting the National Army and residential neighbourhoods in liberated areas and civilian sites in neighbouring countries Political sources described the Yemeni defence ministrys announcement that the Houthi cell had been dismantled as the first official recognition of militia infiltration  a file that had so far been kept quiet except for some reports by Yemeni activists and journalists Informed sources who spoke on condition of anonymity indicated to The Arab Weekly that the Houthi intelligence breach is much greater than what is being declared Since the Houthi coup in September  the Iranbacked group has invested significant resources to enhance its intelligence and recruitment activities taking advantage of its control over security institutions in the capital Sanaa such as the National Security Agency and other political security agencies in addition to capturing the states intelligence database and archives The sources pointed out that Houthis intelligence manoeuvres were more sophisticated than the legitimate governments which failed to form alternative bodies and did not invest many resources in the intelligence file The issue of the Houthi cell may have brought down the curtain on a big file that the National Army has been suffering from and that is untrustworthy people assuming sensitive positions within the army said Yemeni journalist AbdulWahab Buhaibeh who specialises in military affairs  Appointments  In a statement to The Arab Weekly Buhaibeh indicated that Officers  such as Khalid alAmir the leader of the dismantled cell and his likes assumed sensitive positions in the army in the absence of reliable criteria for appointments These appointments are subject to personal loyalties kinship or narrow interests This made the National Army a hive for agents and suspects he added The Yemeni journalist pointed out that if the leadership of the National Army wants to immunise the military institution from infiltration it must review all appointments in all sensitive departments and state institutions and empower the leaders who have proven their worth on the ground over the past six years He called on the National Army Command to strengthen the role of the Military Intelligence Service by supporting it with the needed capabilities effectively linking it with its branches in various regions and other brigades and military units and improving coordination between the different bodies In recent years Yemeni press reports have highlighted the Houthi militias use of soft cells that include women to recruit transmit information and even plant bombs One of those cells was known as Sonia Abdo in Aden which infiltrated the ranks of the armys leadership planted explosive devices aimed at assassinating top figures and destabilised security in liberated areas before it was dismantled in June  Its members eventually escaped from the Criminal Investigation Prison in Aden in still unknown circumstances In addition to conducting espionage operations and transferring information in Yemen media reports indicate the female Houthi agents were active in other Arab countries where political and military leaders hostile to the Iranbacked militia are based The role of these cells in other countries according to media sources was limited to approaching some of these leaders and recruiting or silencing them through threats or extortion Yemeni and international media outlets previously highlighted the alleged role of Houthi leader Sultan Zaben director of research in Houthicontrolled areas in recruiting extorting and forcing women to work with the militiass soft cells Yemeni sources told The Arab Weekly that the Houthis focus on intelligence and infiltration of Yemeni security services gave them an advantage in their war with the Yemeni government and helped them gain knowledge of many plans and movements of the Yemeni army in addition to enabling them to penetrate some of the governments political military and security institutions The sources indicated that the Houthis not only controlled the Yemeni states intelligence institutions after the coup but also worked to establish their own parallel bodies such as the Preventive Security Service which received direct logistical support from Irans Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps IRGC and the Lebanese Hezbollah movement to carry out internal and external tasks In January  about four months after the coup the Houthis leaked a phone call between Yemeni President Abd Rabbo Mansour Hadi and his office manager at the time Ahmed Awad bin Mubarak in an attempt to put pressure on Hadi It is believed that they also succeeded in taking control of both the national security apparatus and the political security apparatus after leaking a number of secret documents and recordings

 Indian sailors held by Houthis thank UAE community for Yemen rescue
Supplied

Help from the UAE community poured in for  Indian sailors who were reportedly held captive by Houthi rebels in Yemen for nearly  months With the support of Indian missions social workers and philanthropists the seafarers finally flew home last Sunday via Dubai

The  Indian sailors had travelled from Mumbai India to Muscat last January to work for an Omanbased shipping company There they were accompanied by six others  five Bangladeshis and one Egyptian

The seafarers were reportedly kidnapped in February after their ship capsized off Yemens coast

The Indian Embassy in Yemen the Ministry of External Affairs MEA India and Sudheer Thirunilath who heads the Pravasi Legal Cell in Bahrain ensured the safe release of  abducted Indian nationals social worker Sreedharan Prasad told Khaleej Times

The embassy in Yemen had arranged the safe repatriation of the Indian nationals he added

Dr Dhananjay Datar an Indian businessman in the UAE also helped facilitate the rescue by maintaining contact with the Indian Embassy in Djibouti

When the crew arrived at Dubai International Airport last Saturday they didnt have a penny in their pockets Dr Aman Puri ConsulGeneral of India to Dubai and Harjeet Singh Consul Labour I promptly looked into the matter The officials from the Indian Consulate in Dubai reached the airport in an hour and extended all support to ensure their safe return back home Prasad said

Dr Datar CMD Al Adil Trading LLC also donated a sum of Rs each as emergency help to the rescued workers

The sailors were able to fly to Mumbai at am on Sunday by Air India Express

Stuck in a war zone

The crew started their first voyage on two ships on February  to the Yanbu port On February  the sea turned turbulent and one ship sank Al Adil Trading said in a statement

Fortunately the crew members of the sunken ship were rescued in time and their journey continued via another ship Soon after the weather turned rough and cyclonic which forced the ship to anchor on the spot

The sailors didnt know that the point at which they anchored was a war zone As a result the entire crew was reportedly arrested and confined for further enquiry

Their passports documents cell phones and cash were seized the company added

By Rina ChadijahIndonesian police said they shot dead six supporters of hardline Muslim cleric Muhammad Rizieq Shihab during a confrontation on a highway outside Jakarta in the first bloodshed since tensions rose after he came home last month from selfexile abroadThe early morning shooting occurred when police officers riding in a car trailing the preachers motorcade were attacked by a group of his supporters from the Muslim Defenders Front FPI the organization which Rizieq leads police said But an FPI official claimed it was the police who attacked the motorcade and that its six slain members were unarmed victims of an extrajudicial killingThe officers were following Rizieqs motorcade because they had received information that his supporters were planning a protest at police headquarters in Jakarta during the day on Monday the chief of police in the nations capital said The preacher had been called in for questioning then over allegations that FPI violated COVID restrictions at rallies held last month Jakarta police chief Muhammad Fadil Imran saidIt started with information from various sources that there would be a mobilization of people during the questioning of MRS Muhammad Rizieq Shihab at the Jakarta police headquarters Fadil said at a press conference explaining why a police car was following the motorcadeOur officers whose lives were in danger took firm and measured action resulting in the death of six of  followers of MRS who attacked themNo officers were injured in the incident Fadil said adding that police were looking for the four other alleged attackersMunarman general secretary for FPI an antivice group that Rizieq founded disputed the polices account He accused officers of kidnapping the men and killing themIt was Indonesians goes by one name told reportersFPIs statement said the unidentified people intended to harm Rizieq who had been under surveillanceThe organizations initial statement after the nighttime incident said that six of its members were kidnapped FPI found out they have been killed after police held a press conference on Monday afternoonFor their part police said that a car carrying FPI  a singleedged Japanese weapon  two sickles and two handguns allegedly used by the slain menFPIs Munarman said Rizieq was on his way out of Jakarta to a private religious study session in West Java Islamic insurgency in the northern part of the Sinai Peninsula in clashes that also left at least six casualties among its troops The military said in a statement that forces destroyed around  hideouts and weapons depots and dismantled around  explosive devices The statement said the military destroyed six fourwheel drive vehicles and  motorcycles used by militants since Sept  The military said forces also arrested two dozen suspected militants and seized weapons in the raids It did not specify whether the soldiers were killed or wounded In February  Egypt launched an operation against militants in the Sinai and the Western Desert along the border with Libya It has also built a buffer zone along the border with the Gaza Strip to curb the flow of militants and weapons through a vast underground tunnel network The military periodically releases figures on the operation and is believed to have killed hundreds of militants since it began The details provided by the military could Islamic State leader in the border town of Rafah security officials said Forces Monday killed Sweilam along with two of his associates in a raid on his hideout east of the Mediterranean city of elArish An official said Sweilam  was one of the masterminds of an attack on a mosque in Sinais AlRawdah village in November  that killed over  worshippers in the deadliest such killing in Egypts modern history The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to brief the media about the ongoing operation In Egypts Western Desert the military said airstrikes Peninsula for years but the insurgency became far more deadly after the  military ouster of Mohammed Morsi an elected but divisive Islamist president amid nationwide protests against his brief rule An Islamic State affiliate based in the Sinai has carried out highprofile attacks in recent years mainly targeting security forces and Egypts Christian minority

The New Zealand government will introduce a raft of initiatives in response to an independent investigation into the March  terror attacks on two mosques in Christchurch in which  people were killed Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern said Tuesday The almost page Royal Commission report released the same day investigated what public sector agencies knew in the lead up to the terror attack whether agencies failed to anticipate such an incident and their response to the worst mass shooting in New Zealands history With the exception of the manifesto that shooter Brenton Tarrant a white supremacist from Australia emailed to multiple organizations and government offices minutes before opening fire on two mosques in central Christchurch the report found that no single incident could have alerted relevant agencies to the impending shooting However the report also found failings in the police gun licensing system and said the countrys counterterrorism and security agencies showed disproportionate scrutiny toward the threat of terrorism committed by Muslim extremists and did not address the risks of rightwing extremism Speaking at a press conference Ardern said the government has in principle accepted all  of the recommendations contained in the report On behalf of the government I apologize she said Among the initiatives Ardern said the government will introduce are placing a minister in charge of coordinating and implementing the recommendations and amending laws to strengthen counterterrorism legislation She said the government will also place greater focus on supporting and strengthening social cohesion and extend government funding to help communities at risk of hate crimes and terrorism to upgrade their security arrangements Ultimately this roughly  page report can be distilled into one simple premise Muslim New Zealanders should be safe Anyone who calls New Zealand home regardless of race religion sexual orientation or gender should be safe Ardern said At a separate press conference members of Christchurchs Muslim community expressed their gratitude that the report acknowledged their longheld concerns that intelligence services had failed to investigate threats to the community by the far right Imam Gamal Fouda of the Al Noor Mosque the location that saw the highest casualties said he had previously reported suspicious people in the vicinity of the mosque and was disappointed by the lack of action taken by police Fouda recalled the global response after the Sept   terror attacks on New York City and called on New Zealanders to respond differently The approach after  was to match an attack of hate with further attacks That approach left humanity no closer to bridging our divides he said We ask our beloved country of Aotearoa New Zealand to chart a different course This is a course that is not of division but one of unity compassion kindness and aroha love In August Tarrant became the first person in New Zealand to receive a sentence of life without parole after pleading guilty to  charges of murder  counts of attempted murder and one charge of terrorismKyodo

groups continue to operate in the northern and eastern areas of the country Insurgents have repeatedly targeted schools government offices and security checkpoints Moreover Islamist groups including Jamaat Nasr alIslam wal Muslimin JNIM and Ansarul Islam are attempting to stoke conflict between religious groups by targeting churches in rural areas several such incidents occurred in  As a result of the poor security environment a State of Emergency SoE and associated curfews remain in place in several regions of Burkina Faso The measures will likely remain through at least January  Affected regions include HautsBassins Boucle du Mouhoun Cascades North Sahel and CentreEstCurfews are also in place in the following locations for the time frames noted below Est Region  in the regional But the proposal has been strongly criticised by common people and activists
Do they want to close the schools and deprive us of knowledge and culture Do they want to take back our schools from us the channel showed Abdul Rauf a resident of Kabul as saying 
Following the criticism the ministry said that the plan was meant only for those areas which do not have school in infrastructure
The presidential office has also defended the Education Ministrys plan
Presidential spokesman Sediq Sediqqi said that plan has been misinterpreted and that it was only aimed at strengthening the curriculum the report added

By BBC Monitoring
Islamic State group IS has belatedly claimed to have killed  Chadian soldiers on  December in the southwestern Lake Chad area near the border with Nigeria
The group made the claim in a statement on  December via its channels on the messaging platform RocketChat 
The statement said that IS militants had attacked two military boats with improvised explosives near the villages of Kaiga and Ngouboua on the shore of Lake Chad
It claimed that the attack killed all  troops who were on board the vessels
No mainstream media reports matching the IS claim have been observed
The claim comes after the group claimed two major attacks last month on military vessels in the same area
On  November IS claimed to have killed four Canadian and dozens of Chadian forces travelling by boat in the same area 
Mainstream media at the time reported that four Chadian soldiers were killed after a bomb that was planted under their boat detonated No reports of Canadian casualties were reported
On  November the group claimed another deadly boat bomb attack on Chadian forces near Ngouboua
ISs selfproclaimed West Africa Province branch is active in the Lake Chad basin area mainly in northwestern Nigeria and southwestern Niger Rival group Boko Haram also operates in the same area
Source RocketChat messaging service in Arabic  gmt  Dec

AFRICA
Kenyan troops alShabab clash in southern Somalia
Somali alShabab militants have attacked Kenyan troops from the African Union Mission to Somalia Amisom contingent in Lower Jubba Region privatelyowned Somali station Radio Risala reported The clash in which both sides exchanged heavy fire took place in Hosingow village on  December Radio Risala website in Somali  Dec 
AlShabab attacks army base in Somali capital
According to the proAlShabab news website Somali Memo the groups militants attacked an army base in Yaqshid district Banadir Region on  December The militants also attacked a base housing government troops trained by the US in the village of Sabiid near Afgoye town in Lower Shabelle Region the report said No further details about the attacks were provided Somali Memo website in Somali   Dec 
Grenade attack wounds eight in South Sudan capital
At least eight people have been injured in a bomb explosion in a bar in the South Sudan capital Juba privatelyowned Eye Radio website reported  The incident happened on  December when an unidentified person on a motorcycle reportedly threw the grenade into the bar during the evening hours Police said the motive for the attack was unclear Eye Radio Juba  Dec 
AlQaeda group says it seized village from Islamic State in Mali
AlQaedas branch in West Africa has killed and wounded more than  members of the rival jihadist group Islamic State group IS in eastern Mali according to a proalQaeda media outfit
In the seventh edition of its weekly magazine published on  December Thabat new agency reported that Jamaat Nusrat alIslam walMuslimin JNIM had repelled several attacks by IS and taken control of Indelimane village
The publication did not specify when the supposed clashes occurred but it indicated that they took place around  November when JNIM claimed to have targeted French military bases in Malis northern Kidal region The magazine said IS took control of the village after forces loyal to the Tuareg Movement for the Salvation of Azawad forces withdrew from it Telegram messaging service in Arabic  Dec 
SOUTH ASIA
Afghan security body says Taliban still maintain links with alQaeda
Afghanistans top security body the National Security Council NSC has said that the Taliban have not yet cut their ties with alQaeda private Channel One TV TV reported
The NSC spokesman said that alQaeda militants continue to carry out activities in Talibanheld areas They Taliban deny having ties with the alQaeda due to foreign pressure only the channel showed Andar as saying
Reports have suggested that over  alQaeda militants were secretly present in  provinces of Afghanistan the channel added Afghan Channel One in Dari  Dec 
Blasts reported in north Afghan city
Three consecutive explosions took place in Mazare Sharif city the capital of Afghanistans northern Balkh province on  December The spokesman for the provincial police said there were no reports of casualties Arzu Arezo TV in Dari  Dec 
Carbomber kills soldier in south Afghan district
A car bomb explosion in which one government soldiers was reportedly killed took place in the district of Zheray in Afghanistans southern Kandahar province on  December
The spokesman for Kandahar police said that the police attempted to stop an explosiveladen vehicle which was heading towards its reported target in Zheray adding that the vehicle exploded after the police opened fire on it He said that noone was injured in the incident but an unnamed source told the Pakistanbased Afghan Islamic Press AIP that one soldier had been killed in the blast
In another incident on the same day a suicide car bomber blew up his vehicle in the provinces Daman district Over  people including the district police chief soldiers and civilians were injured in the explosion the report said Afghan Islamic Press news agency in Pashto  Dec 
MIDDLE EAST
Islamic State militants kill Iraqi policeman in Kirkuk
At least one Iraqi policeman was killed and two others wounded in a night attack by Islamic State IS militants in Iraqs province of Kirkuk on  December Iraqi Kurdish Bas News reported The spokesman for Kirkuk police said the militants targeted a federal police force in the town of Rashad some  km south of the city of Kirkuk before fleeing the scene
According to the report IS has recently regrouped and resumed attacks on government forces in the area Bas website in Sorani Kurdish  Dec 
Syria jihadist group claims attack on Turkish troops
A recently emerged jihadist group in northern Syria claimed an attack on a Turkish military base in Idlib province on  December The claim was released via its account on the messaging app Telegram and shared by supporters of alQaeda on the platform In an infographic issued the same day the group which calls itself Sariyat Ansar Abi Bakr alSiddiq Ansar Abu Bakr alSiddiq Squadron said it bombarded the Turkish base in Ram Hamdan village in Idlib without giving information about casualties
The group first emerged on  August when it claimed responsibility for a suicide attack on a Turkish army observation post in Idlib three days earlier On  October the group claimed an attack on a Turkish military convoy in Idlib saying it was to avenge a woman killed by Turkish forces in the same province in September Telegram messaging service in Arabic  Dec

Colombia Gunmen kidnap Spanish head of international research centre
Colombian authorities confirmed that a Spanish national who heads a foreignfunded agricultural research centre was kidnapped by gunmen on  December near the town of Toribio in the southwestern department of Cauca Colombian daily El Pais reported His name was given as Jesus Quintana Garcia head of the International Centre for Tropical Agriculture CIAT
Authorities said that the scientist who enjoys diplomatic status in Colombia was held hostage for ransom No mention was made of any specific armed group suspected of being behind the abduction El Pais website Cali in Spanish  Dec

Russias antiterror forces kill  terrorists in 
Russias National Antiterrorism Committee NAC has released its annual statistics for  according to which the security forces killed  armed militants and uncovered  terror cells over the last year

Thirtysix commanders of armed groups  gunmen and  accomplices were detained About  firearms  improvised explosive devices and more than  bullets as well as  mines grenades and other ammunition were confiscated it added Fifty workshops for the making and alteration of weapons were liquidated

The following is compiled from a selection of reports and headlines in lunchtime bulletins newspapers websites and news agencies on  December
Afghan peace process
The latest developments in the Afghan peace process and the negotiations in Qatar were prominently reported in the afternoon bulletins of the countrys three main news channels  Tolo News TV Ariana News TV and Channel One TV TV
Tolo News TV for instance led its bulletin with a report on a meeting between the Chairman of the High Council for National Reconciliation HCNR Abdullah Abdullah US Charge dAffaires to Kabul Ross Wilson and Scott Miller  the commander of NATOled troops in Afghanistan
Citing a statement by the HCNR the news channel reported that Abdullah Wilson and Miller had held discussions on the ongoing peace talks in Doha negotiations the start of work by HCNRs Leadership Committee and recent political and security developments in Afghanistan
Wilson reportedly said that the Taliban wanted the release of  of their members from the Afghan governments custody within two weeks
Channel One TV on its part reported that a spokesman for the Afghan National Security Council had said that the release of more Taliban prisoners will not accelerate the peace process
The spokesman Rahmatullah Andar said that even though the government has so far freed  Taliban prisoners it has not only not had any positive impact on the peace process but has led to an escalation of the violence in the country
It is when the US embassy in Kabul has said that the Taliban have recently requested the release of  more prisoners
Several newspapers also published editorials this morning on aspects of the peace process
After a week the Doha talks will enter their third month During this period of talks the government delegation and the Taliban have not had any achievements there is direct link between the deadlock in Doha and soaring violence in the country Afghanistan the independent and secular Hashte Sobh daily wrote
The private Daily Afghanistan denounced the Taliban for refusing to reduce violence
The other side of the Afghan conflict is the Taliban and other terrorist groups allied with the Taliban who are fighting against the Afghan government under the name of Islam jihad and against occupiers These groups do not honour international laws and sometimes even call it at odds with Islamic laws With the beginning of the talks in Qatar the systematic and target killing of people from some ethnic and religious groups have increased it remarked
The private Weesa meanwhile commented on the first meeting of the HCNR held in Kabul on  December
The first meeting of the council was convened at a time when the USA has expedited the Afghan peace process Fresh authority will be given to Dr Abdullah since the US has shown the green light He should implement the authority given to him during the political agreement with Ashraf Ghani Ghani has so far held the peace process hostage it said in an editorial titled High Council for National Reconciliation main mission begins now
UN report on violence against women
Tolo News TV and TV gave prominent coverage in their afternoon bulletins to a new UN report on violence against women and girls in Afghanistan
The report  released yesterday  December by the UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan UNAMA and the UN Human Rights Office  assessed redressal provided to survivors in reported cases of violence against women and girls between September  and February 
It found that while the Afghan justice systems response continues to improve progress had been limited since only half of reported crimes reached a primary court with perpetrators being convicted in only about  per cent of the cases
One in every five women in cases documented by UNAMA decided not to pursue their case through justice channels by either not filing a complaint or later withdrawing it The failure by State authorities to pursue crimes in such cases is particularly disturbing in cases of child marriage as victims are unlikely to be able to independently seek recourse from the system UNAMA monitoring underscores how many women resort to selfimmolation or suicide due to violence suggesting they feel that the justice system does not offer a realistic path to escape the UN said in a statement accompany the report
The report raises multiple concerns about the justice systems treatment of women and girls such as low rates of conviction for socalled honour killings  just  per cent as compared to a conviction rate of  per cent for murders unrelated to honour the statement added
Security incidents and civilian deaths in Afghanistan
In its afternoon bulletin Tolo News TV reported that Kabul police had thwarted an attempted mine explosion in the Afghan capital yesterday
Police personnel detected and defused a magnetic mine planted by militants in the Cinema Pamir area of Kabuls Precinct No  the news channel reported adding that mine had since been defused
Meanwhile Ariana News TV reported in its afternoon bulletin that civilian deaths in US air strikes in Afghanistan had dramatically increased since   when the Pentagon relaxed the rules of engagement for air strikes
Citing a new study from the Brown Universitys Costs of War Project the news channel reported that in  alone air strikes killed  civilians  higher than in any other year since the start of the US war in Afghanistan in  and 
After the US and Taliban reached a peace agreement in late February  US and other international air strikes declined  and so did the harm to civilians caused by those strikes The Afghan government is now negotiating with the Taliban and as part of a broader offensive perhaps aimed at increasing Afghan government leverage in the talks air strikes by the Afghan Air Force AAF have increased As a consequence the AAF is harming more Afghan civilians than at any time in its history the study said

The Public Health Ministry also reported  deaths and  recoveries from Covid in the same period the news channel reported
The new cases were reported in Kabul  Herat  Kandahar  Nangarhar  Takhar  Parwan  Nimruz  Badghis  Ghazni  Wardak  Helmand  Laghman  Kapisa  Panjshir  Zabul  and Uruzgan  provinces The deaths were reported in Kabul  Herat  Balkh  Nimruz  and Helmand  provinces according to data provided by the Ministry of Public Health it added

The fighting between the Kurdishled Syrian Democratic Forces SDF and Turkeybacked Syrian armed opposition groups took place in the villages of Kafr Kalbin and Kafr Hasir in the southern and western outskirts of the Turkishcontrolled Syrian town of Azaz in Aleppo Province reported the Rudaw TV website affiliated to the Iraqi Kurdistan Democratic Party KDP
It said that the two sides had also clashed near the village of AlIremah in the southwestern outskirts of the SDFheld town of Manbij Aleppo Province
It added that both sides have yet to issue official statements on the outcome of the fighting
Russian troops are known to have been stationed in the AlIremah area alongside SDFaffiliated local forces since October last year At that time Russian troops moved into the area following the withdrawal of USled coalition forces ahead of a Turkish offensive against the SDF
Serious possibility of attack
Russian military officials recently asked the SDF to hand over the town of Ain Isa Ayn Issa in Raqqa Province to Syrian government forces to avoid an imminent Turkish attack Kurdish media reports said on  December citing a report in the Saudiowned Londonbased Sharq alAwsat newspaper
KDPaffiliated Kurdistan TV website said on  December that the Russians had made it clear to the SDF at a recent meeting held in the area that the threat of a Turkish offensive to take control of Ain Isa was serious
It said that four civilians have been killed and  others injured in bombardments carried out by Turkishbacked armed groups on the SDFheld Ain Isa area since  November It added that the region has been under sporadic shelling by the Turkishled groups for over  days
The rebels shelled the area on  December and hit a checkpoint manned by SDFaffiliated internal security forces according to a Kurdistan reporter based in the nearby city of Kobane There were no reports of casualties that day
No official SDF reaction has yet been observed on its website or in Kurdish outlets regarding the reported Russian warning at the meeting said to have been held in Ain Isa
Russias Syria strategy
Syrian Kurdish political commentator Walid Coli told Kurdistan late on  December that Russia was using the Turkish threat to put pressure on the SDF to hand over Ain Isa to the Syrian government adding that this was part of a wider Russian strategy in defence of Damascuss interests in that area
He said Russia uses this card to tell the SDF If you do not give them to us then we have no choice but to give those areas to the Turks or we would withdraw our forces so that the Turks take our place
He said that this Russian scenario was first implemented in the Afrin region of Aleppo Province ahead of the first major Turkish offensive against the Kurdishled forces in early 
He added that Moscow was using the same method to take over other SDFheld areas as part of its Syria strategy to protect Damascus and expand the territorial presence of Syrian government troops in the north
He pointed to the fact that Moscow and Ankara had concluded several agreements on the fate of many areas throughout the Syrian civil war saying Ain Isa could be the next in line as part of a new deal between the two
He added that Russia and Turkey might also feel the time was ripe for such a move since Washington is currently busy with domestic politics given the presidential handover from Donald Trump to Joe Biden He added that Ankara was perhaps aware that making such attacks against the Kurdishled forces would come up against obstacles in the near future under a Biden presidency
Syrian Kurds accused Russia of betrayal when Turkey and its allied Syrian armed opposition groups attacked and captured the Afrin region from Kurdishled forces in northwestern Syria in March  after two months of fighting
Last October when Turkey initiated its second offensive against the SDF this time in the northeast the SDF struck a military agreement with the Syrian government at Russianmediated talks to have the Syrian army and Russian military police deployed in areas abandoned by the USled coalition so as to limit the scope of the Turkish incursion

Text of report in English by Myanmar news website The Irrawaddy on  December
Three abductions have been carried out by armed groups in Mogoke Township Mandalay Township in the last two months
On Sunday a yearold woman from Kyauktalone village in Mogoke Township was seized by an armed group Mogoke is a former ruby town about km north of Mandalay city
The Shan State Army  North the armed wing of the Shan State Progress Party SSPP claimed responsibility for the abduction of a villager alleging she was a drug dealer
An SSPP representative told the Tachileik News Agency that it detained the woman after she refused to stop selling drugs
The SSPP which refuses to sign the Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement with the government said it will only detain her temporarily
The group has agreed to a statelevel ceasefire with Myanmars military
Sanpya Bakery owner and gems merchant U Kyaw Win a prominent Mogoke figure was abducted by an armed group on Dec  while he driving near the towns market
The Taang National Liberation Army TNLA claimed responsibility for U Kyaw Wins kidnapping last Friday but has not revealed the reason behind the abduction
The TNLA based in northern Shan State is actively fighting Myanmars army and is a member of the Northern Alliance which has engaged in peace negotiations with the government
The TNLA has been recruiting and taking a grip on the area since  It has not signed a ceasefire with Myanmars authorities
In October the TNLA was accused of abducting a Mogoke resident Daw Khin Myint Htay from her home and demanding a ransom of  million kyats US the victim recently told The Irrawaddy
Daw Khin Myint Htay said she was detained by the TNLA for  days until Oct  and suffered repeated beatings
U Aung Naing the National League for Democracys Lower House lawmaker for the township told The Irrawaddy that since  the town has seen increasing activity by armed groups Since  extortion cases by the armed groups in the township had become more frequent
U Aung Naing said It is because of the curse of treasures Many people envy our towns rubies and they think a lot of residents are rich But no rubies are left because they were dug up by outsiders years ago
On Dec  the City Elders Society of Mogoke Township asked armed groups to stop their extortion and abductions
Its statement said the town is trying to develop as a tourist attraction but extortion and abductions by armed groups scared off investors
U Win Naing of the society told The Irrawaddy on Monday residents are frightened of being kidnapped despite military patrols at night
We want to live peacefully he said
Clashes between Myanmars military and TNLA occurred about km north of Mogoke on Nov  and  prompting nearly  villagers to flee their homes and take shelter at Mogokes monasteries churches and community halls and with relatives
Some soldiers were killed and injured in the clashes according to Myanmars military
The Mogoke Townships administrator TNLA and SSPP could not be reached for comment on Monday
Source Irrawaddy website Chiang Mai in English  Dec

Afghan Security Forces Hit By Surge Of Taliban Suicide Car Bombings The Taliban is employing a fightandtalk strategy in Afghanistan seeking to gain leverage in peace talks through gains on the battlefield The militant group carries out targeted killings and assassinations against civilian targets in major urban areas In rural areas where the Taliban holds sway the militants are also staging mass casualty attacks against Afghan government military targets In its attacks against Afghan military bases and outposts the Taliban is increasingly utilizing a deadly and effective terror tactic suicide car bombings or what military experts call suicide vehicleborne improvised explosive devices SVBIEDs The Taliban has carried out suicide car bombings for years But in recent months there has been a major escalation with dozens of the attacks staged across Afghanistan The surge in the use of the tactic has coincided with peace talks that started in September in Doha Qatar between Afghan government representatives and the Taliban The aftermath of a SVBIED attack in Kandahar Province on December  The intraAfghan negotiations are a key part of a USTaliban deal signed in February Under that agreement foreign forces are to leave Afghanistan by May  In exchange the Taliban has vowed security guarantees to prevent future terrorist attacks out of Afghanistan and to negotiate with Kabul on a permanent ceasefire and a powersharing arrangement Fragile and deeply divided the Afghan government has come to the negotiating table in a position of relative weakness With about half of the territory in the country controlled or contested by the Taliban Kabul lacks the military advantage to drive a hard bargain The Taliban is attempting to pressure the Afghan government into concessions at the negotiating table by continuously conducting these attacks on a regular basis says Hugo Kaaman an independent researcher focused on SVBIED design and tactics by militants and terrorist groups Kaaman has documented at least  Taliban SVBIED attacks in Afghanistan since August  That on average is about three SVBIED attack every week The Taliban is showcasing that they have the capability to conduct these attacks far more often than they have actually done previously and that it will continue like this until they give up Kaaman says Talibans Most Powerful Weapon Experts say SVBIEDs are effective at causing mass casualties and are notoriously difficult to stop The vehicles used often are either flatbed trucks and USbuilt Humvees  lightarmored vehicles given to Kabul by the US military vehicles that have been captured from Afghan government forces by the Taliban The trucks usually are equipped with armor plating to protect the vehicle for as long as possible Once a vehicle is driven into its intended target the driver detonates explosives packed inside to trigger a powerful blast Experts say the explosives are being carried by the vehicle rather than the driver Although a driver may also wear a suicide bombers vest in addition to the vehicles explosive cargo suicide vests are never the main charge Afghan forces patrol the highway between Kandahar and Helmand file photo Kaaman says the Talibans use of Humvees as SVBIEDs is particularly scary given that the vehicles are sometimes able to pass through security checkpoints and gain access to government military facilities before they are detonated Taliban suicide drivers often prepare for the attacks by shaving off their long beards and wear captured uniforms from the Afghan National Army he says Its the Talibans most powerful weapon Kaaman says Its a force multiplier that allows them to knock out hardened positions despite a technological disadvantage Besides SVBIEDs the Talibans usual arsenal also includes rockets mortars small arms and the groups signature weapon  improvised explosives devices IEDs Kaaman says the main reason the Taliban has been increasing its use of SVBIEDs is to expand the territory under its control Theyre trying to seize land and using SVBIEDs to knock out crucial Afghan Army bases and outposts in their way using one of the more effective ways to do so he says The Taliban has carried out most of its SVBIEDs against military targets in its traditional strongholds in the countrys south and east where the militants retain larger resource bases and operational capabilities In the most recent attack the Taliban rammed a captured military vehicle packed with explosives into an Afghan Army post in the southeastern province of Ghazni on December  killing at least three Afghan soldiers and wounding five others A week earlier on November  a Taliban SVBIED attack killed at least  Afghan security personnel at the entrance to an Afghan Army base in Ghazni The pace of such attacks seems likely to continue both because of the large numbers of casualties they cause and the demoralizing effect they have upon the Afghan security forces says Ted Callahan a security expert on Afghanistan Ceaseless Violence The Talibans growing use of suicide vehicle bombs comes as part of its intensified wave of attacks across Afghanistan In recent months the Taliban has launched major offensives aimed at seizing control of two provincial capitals in southern Afghanistan Lashkar Gah and Kandahar City Involving hundreds of Taliban fighters and lasting for weeks the onslaughts were eventually quelled by US air strikes The Taliban has also been behind a surge of targeted killings and assassinations in Afghan cities that have targeted government workers as well as journalists rights activists cultural figures moderate religious leaders and women in public roles The attacks are a violation of the USTaliban deal which is thought to include a Taliban pledge to reduce violence Afghan security officials inspect the scene of an IED blast in Lashkar Gah the provincial capital of Helmand which killed RFERL correspondent Mohammad Ilyas Dayee on November  US forces have retaliated by increasing air strikes against the Taliban That has provoked a war of words between the US military and the Taliban which alleges that the air strikes violate the USTaliban deal The US military said it reserves the right under the deal to defend Afghan security forces who come under Taliban attack Observers say the Taliban is likely to continue its attacks because violence is the groups main leverage in the Doha peace talks The militants analysts say will resist a ceasefire because violence is a source of new recruits and motivates its fighters But the Talibans relentless violence has sapped a fragile trust between the two sides Afghan and Taliban negotiators had been deadlocked since the Doha peace talks started in September In a small breakthrough on Johnny Roman Garza a member of the neoNazi group Atomwaffen received a month prison sentence for his role in a plot to threaten and intimidate journalists and advocates who work to expose antiSemitism Justice Department officials announced on Wednesday
A federal judge in the Western District of Washington state said Garza conspired with other members of Atomwaffen to commit offenses against federally protected activities because of religion according to a statement from the US Department of Justice
Garza admitted in a plea agreement to conspiring with other defendants to identify journalists and advocates and then threaten them for their work in exposing antiSemitism
The group focused primarily on journalists and advocates who were Jewish or people of color In a message to the other codefendants Garza explained the plot was designed to have them all wake up one morning and find themselves terrorized by targeted propaganda Justice Department officials said in a written statement
On the night of Jan   Garza placed a poster on the bedroom window of a prominent Jewish journalist that depicted a figure in a skull mask holding a Molotov cocktail in front of a burning home the statement continues The poster contained the victims name and address and warned Your actions have consequences Our patience has its limits    You have been visited by your local Nazis
In February Breitbart Texas reported the intimidation tactics included the mailing of threatening posters to the houses of journalists and making SWAT calls to send a large law enforcement response to their homes or places of worship the complaint states
Swatting is an intimidation tactic where the attacker calls emergency dispatchers and claims people at an address are in imminent danger The law enforcement agency typically responds with an overwhelming show of force
Officials said the conspirators included two Texas men  Kaleb Cole a yearold resident of Montgomery and John Cameron Denton a yearold man who also lives in Montgomery along with two other men
While this defendant did not hatch this disturbing plot he enthusiastically embraced it researching addresses for journalists and those who oppose hate in our communities Brian T Moran US Attorney for the Western District of Washington said in the December  written statement Ultimately in the dark of night he delivered a hateful threatening poster  spreading fear and anxiety Such conduct has no place in our community

MOSCOW December  TASSDEFENSE Each military district will have peacekeeping units in  The organizational matrix and the strength will be approved by the end of the year General parameters have been determined and details are streamlined More units of the Russian army will be trained for humanitarian missions Experts believe the units can be deployed in conflict zones more rapidly than UN forces It was demonstrated in NagornoKarabakh the Izvestia daily writesDefense Ministry sources said the new matrix of peacekeeping units had been defined It is to come into force from  Some technical details remain to be agreedEach of the current four military districts the Northern fleet will acquire the status in  will train one motorized infantry battalion an air squadron an engineering company and a medical detachment for peacekeeping operations One marine battalion in the Western Southern Eastern districts will become peacekeeping The Northern fleet will have an air assault battalionAt present the peacekeeping forces comprise fully contracted th motorized rifle brigade of the Ground Forces and the st air assault brigade two military police battalions of the Southern district and a medical detachment of the Burdenko military hospital They are permanent readiness units which can be deployed in the necessary place in few daysThe force is trained for the specific missions The military study the English language international humanitarian law resolution of conflicts interaction with the locals and setting up checkpointsThe new peacekeeping units will keep the combat functions and arms but will undergo additional training Their new missions are regularly trained at exercises Thus the Unbreakable Brotherhood drills of the CSTO in Tajikistan deployed a refugee camp and trained delivering food water and medicines by air and land The military also interacted with combat jets to repel a militant attack and trained rescuing the crew of an airlifter which was conditionally downed by terrorists and freeing a residential settlement seized by militantsRussian troops actively participated in UN missions in s former Deputy Secretary General of the organization the conflict and stop it Ordzhonikidze saidRussian peacekeepers deploy much faster than UN forces expert Viktor Murakhovsky said It took a day for them to arrive after the decision on Karabakh was competitors he saidSince s Russian peacekeepers have been engaged in all conflicts in the postSoviet space after the collapse of the country This year they engaged in a new mission The decision to send them to NagornoKarabakh was agreed by the leaders of Russia Armenia and Azerbaijan on November  the Izvestia said

ASABA There was pandemonium yesterday in Uvwie Local Government Area of Delta State as unidentified gunmen dressed in army uniform kidnapped three teachers of Ohorhe Secondary school
Daily Independent gathered that the bandits made a shocking appearance in the school in a gold coloured Toyota Highlander and held both the teachers and students hostage for hours before they were able to get their victims
An eyewitness who spoke under anonymity disclosed that the gunmen drove into the school and headed to the staff room where the teachers were relaxing and abducted three teachers while others and students who were equally in the staff room escaped through other exits
I was in the village I was sitting with my two brothers I am not living here I came for a visit The next minute what we heard was kidnappers kidnappers
So we ran down to the school Before getting there the kidnappers have already gone
Then we went to meet the teachers and they started explaining that some gunmen came into the school in army uniform that they drove in one gold coloured Highlander
When they came they parked After some time they came down They entered the staff room wielding guns and abducted three teachers
When our community boys heard the shout of kidnappers they started running towards the direction of the school They met the Highlander coming out of the school premises and they pointed gun at the boys
The boys ran down there with their empty hands no cutlass no wood and nothing so they had to back off as there was nothing they could do in that situation
They started shouting to draw attention as the school is close to the road Before others came the kidnappers are already gone the eyewitness said

 When contacted the spoke man to the commissioner for Basic Secondary school Mr Sam Ijeh said  Im just hearing it but I need to confirm from the Chief Inspector of Education he is the one to give reports of such incident
When contacted Police Public Relations Officer PPRO DSP Onome Onovwakpoyeya confirmed the story
