Ethiopia  At least ten people killed in Benishangul Gumuz region Western Part of Ethiopia still facing security crisis and victims are innocent civilians  borkena December    As central government carries on law enforcement operation in the Tigray region of Ethiopia in the north Benishangul Gumuz region continues to be a place where innocent civilians are slaughtered According to a report by DW Amharic on Tuesday unidentified gunmen killed at least ten people in the Debate district of the region The incident happened on Sunday starting  am local time Many of the victims are said to be daily laborers who were  in their workplace  The source added that they were killed when the gunmen opened fire Residents of the kebele where the incident happened in Debate district reportedly said that there are missing people whose numbers are unspecified Some are believed to be kidnapped while others disappeared from the district fearing for their lives  Meanwhile The Command Post of Emergency measure in the Metekel zone of the region claims that it has eliminated at least  antipeace forces  as it called them  There have been recurring incidents of killing innocent civilians in Benishangul Gumuz region at least for the past two years However it has been happening more frequently since September of this year Based on reports so far most of the victims are ethnic Amhara who depend on subsistence agriculture or daily labor jobs for their livelihoods  In the past two days there has been rage and anger as seen from social media among many Ethiopians that the regions president Ashadly Hassan is not doing enough to stop the attacks Some go to the extent of seeing possibilities that the regions president himself is a party to the perpetrators of the attack  whom the government describe as unidentified gunmen And there is a call for the government to take decisive action to enforce law in the Benishangul Gumuz region of Ethiopia too   Amhara regional state police commissioner Abere Adamu told  journalists this week that the region has been asking the Federal government for permission to dispatch law enforcement forces to the region to decisively deal with the security crisis in the region  The Ethiopian government has admitted in October that some region and zone level government officials had involvement in the massacre in the form of facilitating it Srinagar Dec  Three militants of AlBadr outfit were killed in an encounter at Tiken village of South Kashmirs Pulwama district today while six civilians were injured in a grenade attack in Baramulla district of North KashmirClick here to watch video
Security forces including Police Armys  RR and CRPF launched an operation in Tiken village of Pulwama in the wee hours today
As the security forces approached towards the suspected spot the hiding militants fired upon them leading to an encounter
Inspector General of Police Kashmir Vijay Kumar said that after initial exchange of fire when it was found that the trapped militants are locals they were repeatedly asked to surrender by the security forces However they turned down repeated surrender offers and fired upon security forces who retaliated and in the ensuing gunfight three militants were killed he said
Kumar identified the three militants as Mehrajud Din Lone son of Bashir Ahmad Lone resident of Arigam Pulwama Umar Ali son of Ali Muhammad Mir resident of Dadsara Awantipora and Owais Farooq son of Farooq Ahmad Allaie resident of Kadlabal Chersoo Awantipora
All three were missing since August this year Umar Ali was brother of Shahnawaz Ahmad Mir who was also a militant and was killed in an encounter on st July  in North Kashmir
The encounter took place in South Kashmir after a gap of one month as earlier on th November two local militants were killed in Kutpora in district Shopian
Army in a tweet said that three militants were killed in Pulwama encounter
Recoveries include AK rifle  magazines  with  rounds  pistol  magazines  with  rounds and joint operation over the tweet read
A police spokesman in a statement issued that one Zamir Sadiq Lone in whose house the militants were hiding also received gunshot injuries and was evacuated to hospital for the treatment of his injuries wherehis condition is stated to be stable
As per police records the killed militants were part of groups involved in many crime cases including planning and executing several major attacks on security forces the statement said
Keeping in view the prevailing pandemic and to ensure the safety of people from inherent risk of contracting the infection the dead bodies of the killed militants shall be sent to Baramulla for their burial and last rites after completion of medicolegal formalities The nearest family members of the killed militants shall be allowed to participate in the last rites at Baramulla the statement said
In the meantime a woman was among six persons injured in a grenade attack in the main market of Singhpora area of Pattan in North Kashmirs Baramulla district
Militants hurled a grenade on a security force vehicle in the main market of Singhpora which missed the intended target resulting in injuries to six civilians including a nonlocal resident from Uttar Pradesh and a woman from Handwara
The injured were shifted to a nearby hospital for treatment from where they were referred to SMHS hospital Srinagar for advanced treatment
The injured were identified the as Ghulam Mohammad Parray son of Mohammad Ramzan Parray Gulzar Ahmad Khan son Ghulam Mohiuddin Manzoor Ahmad Bhat son of Ghulam Mohammad Bhat Zubair Ahmad Dar son of Ashiq Darall residents of Singhpora Tabasum daughter of Abdul Rehman Bhat a resident of Doodipora Handwara and Farman Ali of Uttar Pradesh
The IGP said that one militant of JeM Tariq Ahmed Bhat son of Bashir Ahmed Bhat of Hanjigund Chadoora in district Budgam was arrested during naka checking
He said one pistol and ammunition have been recovered from his possession

before Salman returned to the UK on May  four days before the bombingHe was arrested in Libya shortly after and extradited to Britain last summerRamadan Abedi and Samia Tabbal remain in Libya but contained a very small number of posts but there were likes for different armed groups on opposing sides of the Libyan conflict including militia group the February th Martyrs Brigade  which the inquiry has heard her son Salman may have fought or trained with aged There was also a like for Libya Shield Force which is reported to have links to al Qaida the inquiry heardThe hearing was previously told images from devices recovered at the home of the bombers older brother Ismail  following his arrest on May   indicated he was sympathetic to the ideals of IsisHe was later released without charge and denied any involvement with the bombingOn Wednesday the inquiry learned similar images of an extremist mindset were analysed when he was subject to a port stop by officials when returning from his honeymoon in September His Facebook account was also examined at the same time and showed images of Ismail variously holding a firearm a rocket launcher a machine gun and in camouflage clothing with what appeared to be an Islamic State logo in flames behind himHe was also pictured holding a rifle with the February th Martyrs Brigade flags in the background and captured sitting beside the son of Anas alLibi who was holding a pistolThe inquiry has heard Libyan national alLibi had close links with al Qaida and its leader Osama bin LadenHe died of natural causes before Islamist terrorism hasnt gone away As president Biden will have to confront it  Opinion As a string of brutal attacks in France in recent weeks reminds us Islamist terrorism is far from dead Because the pathology largely spared the United States during the past couple years it won little attention in our election And yet it surely will rise  sooner or later  to the top of Presidentelect Bidens agenda Anyone who thinks the end of the socalled Islamic State in  destroyed the threat has only to look at France and across Africa The Tunisian who shouted Allahu akbar after knifing three people to death in Nice on Oct  may have been inspired by the decapitation of a history teacher near Paris on Oct  by a Chechen refugee Or perhaps the knifing of two people three weeks earlier in Paris near the former offices of the Charlie Hebdo magazine drove them both The publication may have infuriated them by republishing caricatures of the Prophet Muhammad as those accused of aiding the  attack against its staff stood trial But the root cause was Islamist terrorism a virus barely slowed by COVID even as the world has looked elsewhere The French attacks should remind Westerners of the ugliness rampant on the African continent Consider the gory examples The Islamic State in the Greater Sahara murdered six French aid workers and two others in a Niger safari park attack in August A week before Boko Haram killed  and wounded six in Cameroon In March Boko Haram killed at least  people and razed a village in Nigeria A couple months before an alShabab suicide bomber in Somalia killed four people The toxin that is terrorism has not abated just moved In its  Country Report on Terrorism the US State Department warned that surviving ISIS leaders welcomed affiliates throughout Africa Such ISIS supporters launched attacks in Asia including the killing of more than  people on Easter Sunday in  in Sri Lanka In the United States a Saudi killed three people and wounded eight at the Naval Air Station in Pensacola Florida in December  For Americans and others who escaped such horrors in the past couple of years its easy to think the problem has been solved The indictment in October of two British jihadis in the murders of American aid workers Peter Kassig and Kayla Mueller and journalists Steven Sotloff and James Foley seem like moppingup operations So too does the recent transfer of four ISIS supporters including Moroccanborn Minnesotan Abdelhamid AlMadioum to the United States to stand trial AlMadioum  when he joined ISIS mid was among more than  Americans  many from Minnesotas SomaliAmerican community  who joined tried to join or supported terrorist groups beginning in  History tells us that Islamist doctrine can be contained for a time but soon springs up anew Until the World Trade Center towers fell in  most Americans had dim memories of the  bombing there that killed six people and hurt over  Many were likely oblivious to attacks on transit systems in France in  And many likely forgot that bombers killed  and wounded over  in  at US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania Americans paid close attention after  But terrorists largely laid low until  when Islamists  led partly by an American  killed more than  in Mumbai Five years later terrorists killed  in a Nairobi shopping mall in early October two men were convicted in Kenya Attacks climbed after ISIS set up the Caliphate in  attracting more than  fighters from nearly  countries Terrorists moved into the United States with the  spree by a married couple in San Bernardino who killed  and hurt  The following year an ISIS supporter killed  and hurt  in a nightclub in Florida And in  a jihadi bomber hurt  in New York and New Jersey Then a Somali American hurt  in a bizarre carramming and stabbing spree at Ohio State University In  an Uzbek Islamist killed eight people and hurt a dozen in New York City followed two weeks before Christmas by an attempted suicide bombing at New Yorks Port Authority Bus Terminal President Trump declared ISIS defeated in December  although the real end of ISISs territorial hold in Syria came on March   when Syrian Democratic Forces SDF took over Baghouz Still ISIS inspired attacks in Kenya Syria Somalia France Lebanon Afghanistan and the Philippines COVID will be vanquished But if the French attacks and recent history prove anything its that Islamist fanaticism will endure And the West especially President Biden must remain awake to its threats Joseph Weber author of Divided Loyalties Young Somali Americans and the Lure of Extremism teaches journalism at the University of NebraskaLincoln

Mozambique LNG security in spotlight again as insurgency creeps closer London  Militants have attacked a village in northern Mozambique just  km from the site of two major LNG project developments according to local media reports highlighting the continued security issues facing the southeast African country and its fledgling LNG industry More than  million mtyear of LNG production capacity is under development in Mozambique as the country looks to join the ranks of the worlds biggest LNG exporters It emerged Dec  that militants had attacked the village of Mute in the Palma district which lies in a buffer zone between the Afungi peninsula  where Frances Total and US major ExxonMobil are developing LNG export facilities  and the militantcontrolled port of Mocimboa da Praia The port has been occupied since midAugust as part of the growing Islamist insurgency that began in October  Total plans to produce first LNG from its  million mtyear Mozambique LNG project in  with FID on the project taken in  Total had no immediate comment Dec  in response to a request for reaction to the latest attack ExxonMobil meanwhile has deferred a final investment decision on its  million mtyear Rovuma LNG facility until at least  Italys Eni though remains on track to start up its  million mtyear capacity Coral South floating LNG production facility offshore Mozambique in  Total security pact The insurgency  which also spread to offshore tourist islands in the autumn  prompted Total in late August to agree a pact with the Mozambique government to provide security for its LNG activities in the country The deal provides for the establishment of a joint task force in a bid to bolster security measures and create a safe operating environment A number of groups are now part of the insurgency including the Ahlu Sunnah WaJamo ASWJ group and the Islamic States Central Africa Province ISCAP which has declared Mocimboa da Praia as the capital of its province The Mozambique government has called on the EU and US for assistance in combatting the insurgency Ed HobeyHamsher Senior Africa Analyst at global risk consultancy Verisk Maplecroft said the LNG developers would not need to amend their security protocols in light of the latest attack They are already bypassing the road between Mocimboa da Praia and Palma moving freight and personnel by air or sea HobeyHamsher said The attack did not demonstrate an escalation in the capabilities of ASWJ that would signal the group now poses a direct threat to the already heavily protected LNG project site he said However there are question marks around the governments priorities in light of the continued insurgency The failure of the significant deployment of Defence and Security Forces FDS to successfully repel the attack will increase popular skepticism that their primary interest is the protection of the LNG companies at the expense of local communities HobeyHamsher said Public distrust of the FDS will prolong the insurgency as successful counterinsurgency depends on popular confidence for intelligence and information operations he said

Ethiopias government is rejecting calls for independent investigations into the deadly conflict in its Tigray region saying it doesnt need a babysitter
The declaration by senior government official Redwan Hussein came amid international calls for more transparency into the monthlong fighting between Ethiopian forces and those of the fugitive Tigray regional government that is thought to have killed thousands including civilians
At least one largescale massacre has been documented and others are feared
Hussein told reporters on Tuesday evening that Ethiopia will invite others for assistance only if it feels that it failed to investigate
To assume the government cannot carry out such probes is belittling the government he said
Ethiopias government has pushed back against what it calls outside interference from efforts at dialogue to delivering aid drawing on its history as the rare African country never colonised a source of deep national pride
But frustration is growing as the northern Tigray region remains largely cut off from the outside world with food and medicines desperately needed by the population of six million  nearly a million of them now thought to be displaced
The lack of transparency as most communications and transport links remain severed has complicated efforts to verify the warring sides claims
It also hurts efforts to understand the extent of atrocities that have been committed since Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on November  announced that fighting had begun with the Tigray Peoples Liberation Front TPLF which dominated Ethiopias government and military for nearly three decades before he came to power and sidelined it
The federal and the regional governments regard each other as illegal as the TPLF objects to the postponement of national elections until next year because of the COVID pandemic and sees Abiys mandate as expired
Meanwhile UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Michelle Bachelet said the situation in Ethiopia is worrying and volatile amid reports of ethnic profiling of Tigrayans including in Addis Ababa
We have reports that particularly areas surrounding towns like Mekelle Sherero Axum Abiy Addi and the borders between the Amhara and Tigray regions fighting continues between federal forces and the TPLF and affiliated militias on both sides Bachelet told a news conference in Geneva on Wednesday
There is an urgent need for independent monitoring of the human rights situation in the Tigray region all necessary measures to protect civilians and accountability for violations
UN staffers shot at
Abiys government has made it clear it wants to manage aid delivery On Tuesday it said its forces had shot at and detained United Nations staffers who allegedly broke through two checkpoints while trying to reach areas where they were not supposed to go

was the detonation of an explosive device at about  am on Agnew Street in Amherst near the Col James Layton Ralston Armoury It was the second consecutive night an explosive device had been detonated near downtown Amherst Hopes home on Clarence Street isnt far from either of the explosions On Monday she was in her living room when the first device exploded just up the street from the second explosion It was so loud it literally shook the house she said It sounded like a car crash right outside my house It felt like it was on my front lawn Hope said I went around the house checking all the doors and windows and went outside to check the shed A third device was located by police in the Rotary Centennial Park soon after the explosion early Wednesday morning It was destroyed just before  am in a controlled detonation by the RCMP Explosives Disposal Unit This is scary said Hope whose daughters school is a couple of blocks away from the explosions This sort of thing doesnt happen in Amherst Can you imagine if my daughter was nearby when this person explodes one of those things Amherst Mayor David Kogon heard Mondays explosion as it was near his Rupert Street residence but he did not hear Wednesdays I heard it in my sleep but must have thought I was dreaming the mayor said It was only a house away from me The mayor said its very concerning for incidents like this to streets Police cordoned off streets around the park and just before  am the third device was detonated by the RCMPs explosives unit For safety reasons the decision was made by the explosives disposal unit to detonate the device in a controlled way Pike said Pike said the departments major crimes unit is continuing its investigation with assistance from the RCMP and the Cumberland County Integrated Street Crime Enforcement Unit The chief said he cant comment on the devices or who may be responsible We dont want to comment on that because were still in the early stages of the investigation Pike Situation Overview
In the past two months September and October  and especially following school resumption on  October  there has been an increase in the number of attacks on education The month of October saw the most violent and bloody attacks on education experienced since the beginning of the crisis in  Incidents reported this month include cases of killing torture and abduction of students and teachers as well as arson of education facilities Major incidents were recorded in Bui and Mezam divisions in the NorthWest region NW Meme Fako and Boyo divisions in the SouthWest SW with the Kumba massacre on  October being the deadliest and most violent attack At least eight children were killed and more than a dozen were wounded after unidentified gunmen stormed the Mother Francisca International Bilingual Academy in Kumba Meme division on that day On  October the day before  students of the Progressive Comprehensive College of Bamenda were reportedly abducted by nonstate armed group NSAG fighters while returning from school They were taken to an unknown destination and tortured Six of them were released on the same day and the others on a later date Both NSAGs and Government security forces accused each other of the massacre in Kumba as well as of other attacks against education Between  and  October women and children marched on the streets of many towns in the NWSW demanding an end to the crisis The Humanitarian Coordinator in Cameroon released a statement on  October condemning the killing of students in Kumba
Separatist have remained divided on their position with regards to education While some separatists called openly on social media for a resumption of schooling pupils students and teachers continue to be physically attacked and to receive threats from other separatists through audio messages No NSAG group has issued any public statement to reflect that orders have been given to the fighters under their influence to avoid any threats or other targeting of schools as well as children teachers and parents
Incidents perpetrated by Government security forces were also reported in October This includes security forces forcibly transporting children to Government schools in military vans the occupation of nonoperational school facilities and the closing down of informal or community schools in favour of Government schools Such incidents were reported in NgoKetunjia Bui and Donga Mantung divisions all in the NW region
The month of October also saw cases of harassment of humanitarians improvised explosive devices IEDs lockdown days and roadblocks obstructing humanitarian access of aid agencies to people in need

THE FOLLOWING IS COMPILED FROM A SELECTION OF REPORTS AND HEADLINES IN AFGHAN NEWSPAPERS AND LUNCHTIME BULLETINS ON  DECEMBER 
IntraAfghan peace talks
Abdullah Abdullah  the head of Afghanistans top peace body High Council for National Reconciliation  has said that very serious discussions will begin between the governments and the Talibans negotiators in Qatar today independent Tolo News and private Channel One TV TV news channels have reported
Today the two teams held some internal discussions From tomorrow they will have very serious talks Abdullah had said yesterday
According to sources cited by Tolo News TV the Talibans working group in Doha has now slightly softened its stance by offering to remove both republic and emirate from its proposal
While the Afghan government has long held that the countrys Islamic republic system is nonnegotiable the Taliban have repeatedly called for establishing an Islamic emirate in the country
Today is the fifth day of discussions between the negotiating teams of the Afghan government and the Taliban to finalize the agenda of the peace negotiations the private Ariana News TV channel noted
Though none of the sides have officially announced the issues raised by them in the talks it has been said that the government has set ceasefire as its main priority in the talks the channel added
The State Ministry of Peace Affairs had previously said that the current meetings are preliminary and both teams are busy holding internal discussions with their members the channel added
Private daily Maseer has urged both sides to hold the negotiations with patience
Both sides should be ready to discuss all the contentious issues and should have patience They should start from the common and less contentious issues And they should also admit that there is no other way except reconciliation and peace It is the basic demand of the people the paper said
Taliban prisoner release issue
Some newspapers have commented on the recent debate on the issue of releasing  Taliban fighters held in Afghan  prisons Few days ago the US Charge dAffaires to Afghanistan Ross Wilson said that the Taliban expect these fighters to be freed simultaneous with the ongoing peace talks in Doha
But unconfirmed reports say that the Taliban have not included it in their proposed agenda points for the main negotiations and aim to get it addressed through the US
Independent Hashte Sobh newspaper said that there should be a proper guarantee that the militants would not return to the battlefield after they are freed
There should be a strong and sufficient guarantee which can prevent the released Taliban prisoners from returning to battlefields Otherwise the release of the remaining Taliban prisoners will become a poisoned chalice for the government the paper said in an analytical report The report is captioned Taliban prisoners will be released under US pressure   
Staterun Hewad has warned about the adverse consequences of releasing the militants without any guarantee
As peace has not been ensured yet the Taliban do not declare a ceasefire and even run away from peace talks so releasing these prisoners will turn into a major disaster and lead to intensification of the war the paper said in its editorial
Armane Melli a private daily has carried an article by Abdul Matin Ferahmand headlined Unending consequences of a deal  Taliban prisoners awaiting freedom
As Kabul authorities had no determination or power to take decision regarding the release of  dangerous Taliban prisoners before of the start of intraAfghan talks the same situation will prevail in the release of the remaining  prisoners the author said
Civilian casualties
Today also a section of Afghan media has discussed the USs reaction to Brown Universitys report on Afghan civilian casualties
The US has dismissed the study on civilian casualties calling it a onesided analysis based on disputed data Tolo News reported today
According to the study  published on Monday  December by Brown Universitys Costs of War project  the number of Afghan civilians killed in US and coalition air strikes rose by  per cent between  and 
While the report attributed this rise to the easing up of the rules of engagement for air strikes by the Pentagon in  US military spokesman Col Sonny Leggett rejected the findings
The report relies on disputed data and ignores civilian casualties caused by Taliban and ISIS attacks This includes ongoing Taliban use of car bombs IEDs rockets and targeted killings to intimidate harass and instil fear across Afghanistan he said yesterday
Talibans income
The Afghan Taliban have grown richer and more powerful since the regime was toppled by US forces in  TV has said citing a report by the Radio Free EuropeRadio Liberty
According to the findings of a confidential project commissioned by NATO and later obtained by Radio Free EuropeRadio Liberty  Mullah Yaqoob son of the late Taliban spiritual leader Mullah Mohammad Omar revealed that the Taliban brought in bn US dollars in the fiscal year that ended in March  the report said
In comparison the Afghan government earned bn US dollars during the same period the report added
Afghanistan accounted for approximately  per cent of global opium production over the past five years according to the UNs World Drug Report  the report said
According to a  report by the Afghanistan Research and Evaluation Unit a major part of the profits earned from the illicit drugs go to the Taliban which manage opium in areas under their control the report added
Security incidents
An overnight Taliban attack in the eastern province of Ghazni has caused several casualties among Afghan forces the Pakistanbased Afghan Islamic Press news agency AIP Tolo News and Ariana News have reported
According to AIP Wahidullah Jumazada  a spokesman for the Ghazni governor  said The Taliban had planned to attack two military bases in the Mullah Nooh Baba area of Andar district last night But one of the bomber was identified and targeted by security forces and his vehicle blown up
He added that another vehicle which was being prepared for a suicide attack was identified and seized by soldiers but the suicide bomber managed to flee
AIP reported that three Afghan soldiers were killed and two others were wounded in the attack but according to Tolo News and Ariana News the Defence Ministry said that two soldiers had been killed and three others wounded in the attack
A statement released by the ministry said that after the blast the assailants engaged in fighting against army soldiers in the town as a result of which the militants also suffered heavy casualties the TV channels said
In another incident three mines have been defused in Mirbachakot district of the eastern Kabul province Tolo News reported separately
One person has been killed in a dispute over a land in Paghman district of Kabul Ariana News added Police have said that the fighting took place between three brothers last night in which one of them got killed His two brothers have been arrested in connection with the case according to the TV channel
Coronavirus vaccine
President Mohammad Ashraf Ghani has announced that the World Bank and other partners have pledged to provide m dollars to Afghanistan to help the country in buying Covid vaccines Tolo News reported
The president added that the Asian Development Bank has pledged another m dollar of funds for the vaccine the website of Tolo News added
The Ministry of Public Health as cited by the TV channel said that it has received pledges under which  percent of the Afghan population will get Covid vaccination in the first phase
Quoting the ministry the channel added that the Afghan government is making preparations to get the vaccines for another  percent of the population as well
Source BBC Monitoring in Dari and Pashto  gmt  Dec

Staterun Hewad has warned about the adverse consequences of releasing the militants without any guarantee

As Kabul authorities had no determination or power to take decision regarding the release of  dangerous Taliban prisoners before of the start of intraAfghan talks the same situation will prevail in the release of the remaining  prisoners the author said
Civilian casualties
Today also a section of Afghan media has discussed the USs reaction to Brown Universitys report on Afghan civilian casualties
The US has dismissed the study on civilian casualties calling it a onesided analysis based on disputed data Tolo News reported today
According to the study  published on Monday  December by Brown Universitys Costs of War project  the number of Afghan civilians killed in US and coalition air strikes rose by  per cent between  and 
While the report attributed this rise to the easing up of the rules of engagement for air strikes by the Pentagon in  US military spokesman Col Sonny Leggett rejected the findings
The report relies on disputed data and ignores civilian casualties caused by Taliban and ISIS attacks This includes ongoing Taliban use of car bombs IEDs rockets and targeted killings to intimidate harass and instil fear across Afghanistan he said yesterday
Talibans income
The Afghan Taliban have grown richer and more powerful since the regime was toppled by US forces in  TV has said citing a report by the Radio Free EuropeRadio Liberty
According to the findings of a confidential project commissioned by NATO and later obtained by Radio Free EuropeRadio Liberty  Mullah Yaqoob son of the late Taliban spiritual leader Mullah Mohammad Omar revealed that the Taliban brought in bn US dollars in the fiscal year that ended in March  the report said
In comparison the Afghan government earned bn US dollars during the same period the report added
Afghanistan accounted for approximately  per cent of global opium production over the past five years according to the UNs World Drug Report  the report said
According to a  report by the Afghanistan Research and Evaluation Unit a major part of the profits earned from the illicit drugs go to the Taliban which manage opium in areas under their control the report added
Security incidents
An overnight Taliban attack in the eastern province of Ghazni has caused several casualties among Afghan forces the Pakistanbased Afghan Islamic Press news agency AIP Tolo News and Ariana News have reported
According to AIP Wahidullah Jumazada  a spokesman for the Ghazni governor  said The Taliban had planned to attack two military bases in the Mullah Nooh Baba area of Andar district last night But one of the bomber was identified and targeted by security forces and his vehicle blown up
He added that another vehicle which was being prepared for a suicide attack was identified and seized by soldiers but the suicide bomber managed to flee
AIP reported that three Afghan soldiers were killed and two others were wounded in the attack but according to Tolo News and Ariana News the Defence Ministry said that two soldiers had been killed and three others wounded in the attack
A statement released by the ministry said that after the blast the assailants engaged in fighting against army soldiers in the town as a result of which the militants also suffered heavy casualties the TV channels said
In another incident three mines have been defused in Mirbachakot district of the eastern Kabul province Tolo News reported separately
One person has been killed in a dispute over a land in Paghman district of Kabul Ariana News added Police have said that the fighting took place between three brothers last night in which one of them got killed His two brothers have been arrested in connection with the case according to the TV channel
Coronavirus vaccine
President Mohammad Ashraf Ghani has announced that the World Bank and other partners have pledged to provide m dollars to Afghanistan to help the country in buying Covid vaccines Tolo News reported
The president added that the Asian Development Bank has pledged another m dollar of funds for the vaccine the website of Tolo News added
The Ministry of Public Health as cited by the TV channel said that it has received pledges under which  percent of the Afghan population will get Covid vaccination in the first phase
Quoting the ministry the channel added that the Afghan government is making preparations to get the vaccines for another  percent of the population as well

Islamic State group IS has claimed three separate attacks on the Nigerian army in the restive northeastern state of Borno on  December
On  December the group said in a statement that its militants had killed seven troops captured one soldier and wounded others in clashes in Alagarno forest
The militants also seized vehicles and ammunition after the fighting which reportedly occurred when the army attempted to advance on IS positions in the area
IS subsequently released images purporting to show the captured soldier the corpse of another and army vehicles that were supposedly seized by its militants
AFP news agency reported that  Nigerian soldiers were killed and one was taken hostage following clashes with IS militants in Alagarno village in Damboa district
Also on  December IS claimed two other attacks on the Nigerian army in Borno
In one of the attacks IS militants reportedly ambushed troops on the road between Gamboru and Dikwa killing four soldiers and wounding others
The group said the other attack targeted an army checkpoint in the town of Gajibo killing two soldiers and wounding others According to IS its militants burnt down the checkpoint
IS claimed the three attacks in the name of its West Africa Province branch which operates mainly in Nigerias Borno state but also carries out attacks in neighbouring countries
The claims were released via IS channels on the messaging platform RocketChat

By BBC Monitoring

Saudi Arabia has announced it had intercepted a bombladen drone launched by Yemens Houthi rebels according to media outlets
The drone was fired in the direction of Saudi Arabias southern region that borders territories controlled by the Houthis according to the spokesman for the Saudiled Arab military coalition which has been engaged in Yemens war on the side of the internationally recognised government
Coalition Spokesman BrigGen Turki alMaliki said in a statement on  December that the drone was intercepted and destroyed earlier in the morning the official Saudi SPA news agency reported
The drone was deliberately aimed at civilian targets the report quoted AlMaliki as saying
Covering the incident the Saudifunded panArab Al Arabiya TV recalled that the rebels had launched another drone towards Saudi Arabia the previous day
Prorebel media outlets have not been observed to report these latest launches of drones which are part of a series of attacks against Saudi Arabia in recent months including one on a facility of the Saudi oil company Aramco in Jeddah which was promptly claimed by the Houthi rebel group
AlMasirah TV instead focused on the latest attacks by the coalition on the rebelheld territories including seven air raids which it said in a breakingnews post on its website the Saudi warplanes had launched at the Nihm district on the evening of  December
In July  the rebelrun media showcased their newly unveiled weapons and military capabilities including the Sammad  drone saying that they have a strategic stockpile enough to sustain them in their fight for years 
According to the rebels their new weapons were domestically manufactured However the USA and the Saudiled coalition say Iran arms the Houthis
Yemens conflict escalated in March  when the coalition backing the internationallyrecognised government launched a military campaign against the Houthi rebel movement which had seized control of the capital Sanaa in September the previous year  
Source BBC Monitoring in Arabic  gmt  Dec

By BBC Monitoring

Syriabased jihadist group Ansar alTawhid has released a video showing off combat footage and its militants taking part in military training
The hardline group released the fiveminute production on  December via its channel on the messaging app Telegram
The video was shared by supporters of alQaeda as well as Shimali alHurr  a channel aligned to dominant the jihadist group in northwestern Syria Hayat Tahrir alSham HTS
The video comes as Ansar alTawhids relationship with jihadist groups in the oppositionheld region remains unclear
Earlier this year alQaeda supporters denied reports that Ansar alTawhid had joined HTSled alliance alFatah alMubin after a crackdown on a rival grouping that was spearheaded by the suspected local alQaeda branch Hurras alDin
Ansar alTawhid which once forged an alliance with Hurras alDin issued a statement in May that stressed it was an independent organisation Its propaganda and military efforts were not effected by the HTS clampdown on its rivals
Proceed
The latest video titled We Proceed flaunts footage of fighting against government forces and military training efforts
Scenes of militants engaged in frontline fighting are interspersed with shots of missile and mortar attacks
A masked militant stresses that the groups fighters remain steadfast in the war against the Syrian government and its Russian backers
He emphasises that militants continue to take part in physical and military training and urges fighters to have the patience to outlast their enemies
The video ends with shots of militants undergoing target practice and battle simulations
The production was billed by the group as part of a series titled If You Return We Will Too
The motivational combat video appears to be aimed at boosting the morale of the groups supporters and fighters 
Source Telegram messaging service in Arabic  gmt  Dec

ETHIOPIAS TIGRAY CRISIS
Website says UN seeks to use Eritrea port to deliver Tigray aid
Proopposition Eritrean website Radio Erena has cited diplomatic sources as saying that the UN is negotiating with Eritrean authorities to use its port to deliver aid to neighbouring Ethiopias northern Tigray region
According to the diplomatic sources the Eritrean port of Massawa has been taken as main option for transporting the humanitarian aid to Tigray because of its proximity to the areas controlled by the Ethiopian federal forces However the sources said talks are underway between the governments of Eritrea Ethiopia and the UN the website reported yesterday
Yesterday Ethiopian authorities said government forces shot at a UN convoy for attempting to breach a checkpoint in Tigray Humanitarian agencies have said they are still not able to deliver aid to various parts of Tigray due to government restrictions
Hundreds of thousands of Ethiopians as well as Eritrea refugees are in dire need of food and medical supplies following the armed conflict
Website says hundreds of Ethiopian troops evacuated from Eritrea
Parisbased proopposition Eritrean website Radio Erena has reported that more than  Ethiopian troops who were receiving treatment in hospitals in Eritrea were yesterday evacuated by bus through the Humera border point
Last week the website said some  wounded Ethiopian soldiers were evacuated from hospitals in Senafe and Asmara in Eritrea
The US has said it believes Eritrean soldiers crossed into Ethiopia to support Prime Minister Abiy Ahmeds government in fighting forces loyal to the rebel Tigray Peoples Liberation Front TPLF according to a report by Reuters yesterday
The TPLF has accused Eritrea of being involved in the conflict and Tigray forces have fired rockets into the Eritrean capital Asmara three times during the monthlong conflict Radio Erena had reported on  December the alleged involvement of Eritrean troops in the Tigray conflict
Prime Minister Abiy was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in  for a peace pact between Ethiopia and Eritrea that ended nearly twodecades of military hostilities between the two countries
Ethiopia prime minister expected in Kenya today
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed will visit neighbouring Kenya today his first foreign visit since he announced a military operation to oust the authorities in the northern Tigray province
A spokesperson for the Kenyan presidency said Abiy will arrive in the country through the Moyale border post in Kenyas northern Marsabit County
The prime minister and Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta will visit Moyales one stop border stop then proceed to the southeastern region of Lamu to tour the port currently under construction The Lamu port is an anchor project of the Lamu PortSouth SudanEthiopiaTransport LAPSSET Corridor
Ethiopian officials have visited neighbouring countries as part of efforts to calm concerns over the monthlong conflict in Tigray
See Explainer Ethiopias Tigray conflict threatens regional stability
Ethiopian general says TPLF forces fully destroyed
An Ethiopian army general has said TPLF forces have been fully destroyed and fighting has ended in Tigray according to a report by Ethiopian Satellite TV ESAT
Major General Muhammed Tessema the federal armys directorgeneral of indoctrination also said that federal forces were in control of TPLF hideouts in the Tigray region He said TPLF officials are believed to have used a bunker to flee from the regional capital Mekele to Workamba and no one knows where the TPLF leaders are now
The interim administration of the Tigray region held talks with residents in Mekele earlier this week and said it has embarked on reconstructing the region as normalcy slowly returns
OTHER DEVELOPMENTS
Ghanaians urged to remain calm as opposition claims victory
The African Union AU and the west African regional bloc Ecowas have urged for calm after a delay in the announcement of presidential election results
The Electoral Commission EC had projected that it would announce results within  hours of polls closing at  GMT on  December It said in a statement yesterday that is has so far received results from  of the  regions but had only certified results from seven regions
Opposition candidate John Mahama in a press conference yesterday claimed victory and accused the authorities of attempting to use the military to overturn poll results The government has accused him of breaching a peace pact stipulating that the candidates would use legal means to challenge election results
The incumbent Nana AkufoAddo is currently leading with  of votes against Mahamas 
See Explainer Perennial rivals contest Ghana presidential election
DR Congo MPs violently clash amid political standoff
Clashes took place outside the National Assembly in DR Congo yesterday after MPs were summoned to the House amid a standoff over the dissolution of the coalition between President Felix Tshisekedi and his predecessor Joseph Kabila
According to Actualite website security around the National Assembly building was beefed up after the clashes between ruling party and opposition supporters
The MPs are expected back in parliament tomorrow to debate a petition seeking the dismissal of the Speaker
Kabilas Common Front for Congo FCC has a majority in parliament holding  out of  seats
Tshisekedi said that an advisor will soon be appointed to oversee the formation of a new majority a move that was dubbed unconstitutional by the FCC
Liberians await referendum senatorial poll results after low turnout
Vote counting following the senatorial election and constitutional referendum is underway in Liberia amid reports of a low turnout according to Daily Observer website
The pace of voting is not quick as voters anticipated and many are finding it difficult to understand the referendum ballot paper Most voters spoken to seem to be frustrated when issued a referendum ballot paper as most of them dont understand what they are voting for and the impact it would have on them the website reported
It added that the opposition is leading in early senatorial poll results from key counties
The controversial referendum is seeking to reduce the terms of the president and MPs from six to five years decide when elections should be held and allow dual citizenship The opposition fears it will be exploited by President George Weah to extend his stay in power by contesting a third term
Somalia to begin training electoral commission team
The Somali federal government will begin training members of the regional electoral commissions in Mogadishu despite some regional administrations not submitting their representatives to the poll body
According to privatelyowned Radio Kulmiye representatives from the federal government will be trained alongside those from Hirshabelle and Southwest regions
Jubbaland and Puntland states have not yet submitted the names of their representatives in the electoral commission The two regions have opposed the electoral body appointed by the federal government and demanded the withdrawal of government forces from the southwestern Gedo Region
Parliamentary elections that were scheduled for  December have been delayed
Sudans Darfur UN mission urged to remain amid rebel clashes
Amnesty International has urged the UN to extend the mandate of its peacekeeping mission in Sudans Darfur UNAMID by at least six months citing failure by the countrys national security forces to protect civilians from attacks in recent months
A report by UNAMID to the UN Security Council early this month said infighting between holdout rebel groups over control of gold mines in Darfur has displaced more than  people within two months It also cited  cases of human rights violations and  cases of sexual violence
UNAMID is scheduled to leave Darfur on  December It has been deployed in the region since  
In October Sudan started implementing a plan to replace UN troops in Darfur with national forces Sudans paramilitary Rapid Support Forces RSF said it is ready to secure volatile Darfur However IDPS have expressed mistrust in the RSF which has previously been linked to atrocities in the region
IS claims killing  Chadian soldiers in boat bomb attack
Islamic State group IS has belatedly claimed to have killed  Chadian soldiers on  December in the southwestern Lake Chad area near the border with Nigeria
The group made the claim in a statement on  December via its channels on the messaging platform RocketChat
The statement said that IS militants had attacked two military boats with improvised explosives near the villages of Kaiga and Ngouboua on the shores of Lake Chad killing all  soldiers aboard the vessels
No mainstream media reports matching the IS claim have been observed IS previously claimed two major attacks on Chadian military vessels in the same area
Nigeria denies US accusations of religious freedom violations
The Nigerian government has denied accusations by the US that it violates religious freedoms amid rising concern over attacks targeting Christians in northeastern states devastated by terror attacks
On  December the US blacklisted Nigeria for engaging in systematic ongoing egregious religious freedom violations US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo who announced the measure said his country will continue to act when religious freedom is attacked
But in a statement cited by The Cable website Nigerias Information Minister Lai Mohammed described the allegation as a case of honest disagreement between the two nations on the causes of violence in Nigeria 
Victims of insecurity and terrorism in the country are adherents of Christianity Islam and other religions the minister said adding that the country jealously protects religious freedom
Islamist militants operating in the northeast have frequently called for attacks against Christians fuelling fears of sectarianism
Spain Portugal to support Mozambique as insurgents threaten gas projects
Mozambique Defence Minister Jaime Bessa Neto is scheduled to meet his Portuguese counterpart Joo Gomes Cravinho today after the latter pledged to support the southern African nations fight against insurgents privatelyowned Carta de Mocambique has reported
Spain has also pledged to provide all necessary support as militant attacks increasingly threaten the exploration of Mozambiques multimillion dollar gas project in Palma District in the volatile northern province of Cabo Delgado
Yesterday security forces repelled two suspected militant attacks in Palma and Nangade districts In Palma the insurgents occupied a village  kilometres from Afungi the home of the natural liquefied gas project
Mozambique has been battling an escalating Islamist insurgency since October  The government recently updated the number of people displaced by the violence to

Uganda has reportedly allowed Chinese nationals living in the country to import Covid vaccines on compassionate grounds

The Chinese nationals are said to have requested Uganda to help them import the vaccines from China

According to privatelyowned Radio Kulmiye representatives from the federal government will be trained alongside those from Hirshabelle and Southwest regions
Jubbaland and Puntland states have not yet submitted the names of their representatives in the electoral commission The two regions have opposed the electoral body appointed by the federal government and demanded the withdrawal of government forces from the southwestern Gedo Region
Parliamentary elections that were scheduled for  December have been delayed
Sudans Darfur UN mission urged to remain amid rebel clashes
Amnesty International has urged the UN to extend the mandate of its peacekeeping mission in Sudans Darfur UNAMID by at least six months citing failure by the countrys national security forces to protect civilians from attacks in recent months
A report by UNAMID to the UN Security Council early this month said infighting between holdout rebel groups over control of gold mines in Darfur has displaced more than  people within two months It also cited  cases of human rights violations and  cases of sexual violence
UNAMID is scheduled to leave Darfur on  December It has been deployed in the region since  
In October Sudan started implementing a plan to replace UN troops in Darfur with national forces Sudans paramilitary Rapid Support Forces RSF said it is ready to secure volatile Darfur However IDPS have expressed mistrust in the RSF which has previously been linked to atrocities in the region
IS claims killing  Chadian soldiers in boat bomb attack
Islamic State group IS has belatedly claimed to have killed  Chadian soldiers on  December in the southwestern Lake Chad area near the border with Nigeria
The group made the claim in a statement on  December via its channels on the messaging platform RocketChat
The statement said that IS militants had attacked two military boats with improvised explosives near the villages of Kaiga and Ngouboua on the shores of Lake Chad killing all  soldiers aboard the vessels
No mainstream media reports matching the IS claim have been observed IS previously claimed two major attacks on Chadian military vessels in the same area
Nigeria denies US accusations of religious freedom violations
The Nigerian government has denied accusations by the US that it violates religious freedoms amid rising concern over attacks targeting Christians in northeastern states devastated by terror attacks
On  December the US blacklisted Nigeria for engaging in systematic ongoing egregious religious freedom violations US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo who announced the measure said his country will continue to act when religious freedom is attacked
But in a statement cited by The Cable website Nigerias Information Minister Lai Mohammed described the allegation as a case of honest disagreement between the two nations on the causes of violence in Nigeria 
Victims of insecurity and terrorism in the country are adherents of Christianity Islam and other religions the minister said adding that the country jealously protects religious freedom
Islamist militants operating in the northeast have frequently called for attacks against Christians fuelling fears of sectarianism
Spain Portugal to support Mozambique as insurgents threaten gas projects
Mozambique Defence Minister Jaime Bessa Neto is scheduled to meet his Portuguese counterpart Joo Gomes Cravinho today after the latter pledged to support the southern African nations fight against insurgents privatelyowned Carta de Mocambique has reported
Spain has also pledged to provide all necessary support as militant attacks increasingly threaten the exploration of Mozambiques multimillion dollar gas project in Palma District in the volatile northern province of Cabo Delgado
Yesterday security forces repelled two suspected militant attacks in Palma and Nangade districts In Palma the insurgents occupied a village  kilometres from Afungi the home of the natural liquefied gas project

Nepal Dec   History repeats itself first as a tragedy then as a farce said Karl Marx the reigning deity of many of Nepali communists and leftists In  cadres of the Communist Party of Nepal Maoists which organised the year insurgency brutally murdered Muktinath Adhikari a Lamjungbased high school headmaster for refusing to kowtow to the partys demands Eighteen years later on Tuesday cadres of the Communist Party of Nepal a splinter of the erstwhile Maoists killed Rajendra Kumar Shrestha  the principal of Saraswati Basic School in Ramite of Miklajung Rural Municipality in Morang district The MechiKoshi bureau of the outfit had abducted Shrestha from his home before killing him purportedly for working as an informant for the policeThe latest killing is a chilling reminder that the Maoist insurgency did not get over in its entirety as the political parties and the state did not care much to tie up its loose ends The insurgency left over  dead  disappeared and hundreds of thousands displaced in the decade beginning in  The country has remained considerable peaceful after the Maoists came to mainstream politics following the Peoples Movement II in  and the signing of the Comprehensive Peace Agreement in  However the political upheavals in the years that followed left enough space for hardliners in the Maoist party including the likes of Netra Bikram Chand as well as various other outfits to see violence as the gateway to political power Now the Chandled organisation has begun to kill people it considers counterrevolutionary after organising a series of bomb blasts extortions and other kinds of violence across the country It looks like we are back to square one with regard to political violenceAs if it were an unprecedented occurrence the Nepal Police has sent a fresh directive to its units across the country to increase security vigilance claiming that there is a risk of an increase in criminal activities although it has claimed the directive is for forceful implementation of the security plans that are already in place The Maoist insurgency and the peace process that followed have enough lessons for us on the successful management of political violence the preeminent one being that no amount of brute power is able to contain insurgent voice and violence There is no doubt that the state must use its resources to stop incidents of violence and extortion in the short run But in the long run there is no other place where the state and the insurgents must meet other than at the dialogue tableAll major parties in the country today have a history of violence and what they have all learntor should learn if they havent alreadyis that violence is hardly the catalyst for political change If the exMaoist combatants who came to power riding on the insurgency believe they can contain violence by any means sans dialogue they are in for a rude shock If the Chandled violent campaign is not nipped in the bud it is more likely than not to grow bigger sooner than later The political parties and the ruling government must sit together immediately to chart out a comprehensive plan to bring the Chandled outfit to the dialogue table immediately and help restore peace They cant repeat the mistake they committed in  when they ignored the possibility of dialogue only to see an endless series of violence in the years that followedPublished by HT The District Head of Yakila community in Rafi Local Government Area of Niger state Alhaji Ibrahim Abdulhamid has been kidnapped by suspected armed bandits
The kidnappers also invaded a neighbouring community GarinGabbas and kidnapped a staff Nurse whose name was given as Halima and two of her children during the encounter which took place at about am Thursday
The armed bandits numbering about twenty riding on motorcycles and armed with sophisticated weapons including AK riffles Daily Independent learnt raided both Yakila and GarinGabbas the two adjoining villages in the district in the early hours yesterday unchallenged
Eye witness account said The bandits shot sporadically into the air to instill fears and scare away possible interferences from members of the communities before disappearing into the darkness with their victims
Though no life was lost the eye witness said the armed bandits operated without restrictions in the two communities adding that Some of the bandits had entered the district heads room and forced him out and took him along with them
While the gunshots were fired by the armed bandits the source said many of the villagers who were rattled by the sporadic gun shots scampered for safety and some ran into nearby bushes for their safety while the bandits had field day selecting choice products from their food stuff
Both the local vigilante and conventional police men in the areas were caught unawares by the attackers as such they could not repel the armed men who spent quality time ransacking the homes of their victims and taking along with them food and materials
The Director General Niger State Emergency Management Agency NSEMA Alhaji Ibrahim Tanko Inga when contacted on phone confirmed receiving report about the attacks early Thursday yesterday morning saying We will get the details and get back to you
Rafi local government area of the state has come under series of attacks by bandits in the last couple of days Just last Monday the palace of the village head of Pangu in the Gunna district of the same local government area was set ablaze by suspected bandits
Also burnt during raid last week Monday are the only existing rural hospital in the area built and donated to the community by the World Bank while several houses and freshly harvested agricultural products were destroyed as well and many of the villagers rendered homeless

 Our correspondent also gathered that the bandits who carried out the earlier attack also rode on about  motorcycles and armed with sophisticated weapons
Niger State Police Command has not issued any statement on the two incidents And efforts to get the Police Public Relations Officer PPRO ASP Wasiu Abiodun confirm the incidents proved abortive
The PPRO declined several calls and also did not respond to text messages sent to him as at the time of this report

North Sinai plunged into darkness following suspected electrical tower attack Israel gas pipeline targeted by militants for second time On the evening of November  some  residents of North Sinai were thrown into total darkness until the early hours of the following morning after three high voltage electrical towers collapsed near the city of Bir alAbd in the west of the governorate Residents from North Sinais six main cities found themselves cut off from the world as telephone networks and internet services went down While what caused the towers to collapse is yet to be confirmed local sources in the Bir alAbd area told Mada Masr that the city went dark immediately after residents clearly heard a series of loud explosions coming from the west of the city in the vicinity of the Nagah and Kharba villages  the same area in which the towers that fell down were located Clashes between the Egyptian Armed Forces and militants have caused damage to electrical towers in the past leading to blackouts in cities across the governorate For the entire governorate to be plunged into the dark unprecedented as is the alleged targeting of electrical towers in the west of Bir alAbd A source inside North Sinais public electricity sector told Mada Masr that a domino effect followed the collapse of the three towers as an electrical grid on Egypts mainland west of the Suez Canal went out of service and the main transformer station in the city of Bir alAbd went down as well leading to a capacity overload at the steam plant in Arish  the secondlargest source of electricity in the governorate  which also went offline Another source in North Sinais electricity sector described the blackout as orchestrated in comments to Mada Masr saying that the three towers were brought down to cut the electricity off to the entire area The source noted that three towers are not situated next to each other and that they are responsible for mainstreaming six high voltage circuits from three networks into the transformer station in Bir alAbd two from Port Said two from East Qantara and another two from a small power plant in the area of Baluza   Until November the biggest blackout to have affected the governorate came in September  when the cities of Arish Sheikh Zuwayed and Rafah as well as parts of central Sinai went dark for nearly a week after three electrical towers collapsed west of Arish Residents have faced frequent electricity cuts  sometimes for hours in Arish or days in Sheikh Zuwayed  while authorities have failed to propose any concrete solutions to avoid the recurrent crises For example following the September  blackout authorities attempted to address the problem by bringing a dieselpowered electrical station from Sharm elSheikh The source inside the electricity sector described the station as rundown explaining that it first operated in Arish in the eighties before being moved south According to the source the plant was brought from Sharm elSheikh in  to serve as a backup electrical source to restart Arishs steam power plant when power is cut off as a result of damage to the main electrical line coming from mainland Egypt  However when the governorate was hit with a blackout on November  the backup dieselpowered stations operational teams were surprised to learn that one of their units was so run down as to be unresponsive In spite of the best efforts of the maintenance teams power was only restored to the city when an emergency line extending from Sharq alTafria was used to start up the grid  The threat of governoratewide blackouts continuing as a knockon effect of the collapse will persist until a concrete base can be constructed for the three towers according to the source in the electricity sector One week prior to the blackout on November  an explosion hit a gas line west of Arish on November  Residents of the city of Arish  kilometers away from the explosion site could see the flames as could the residents of the city of Bir alAbd some  kilometers away Just two hours after the November  explosion the spokesperson for the Armed Forces issued a statement describing the blast as limited and identifying its location at Sebeika west of the city of Arish The militarys statement was followed by another from the governorate  which stated that the Egyptian Natural Gas Company was able to respond to the explosion quickly and switch off the control valve adding that the explosion would not affect the supply of gas to peoples homes in Arish the gas power plant or the only natural gas station for vehicles in the area While both statements said that concerned agencies would investigate the cause of the explosion the Province of Sinai got there before them to claim responsibility for bombing the gas pipeline using explosive devices This is the second time the Islamic State affiliate in the peninsula has claimed to have attacked the pipeline passing through North Sinai since it was announced that natural gas would be imported from Israel in January with officials announcing that a February explosion on the same pipeline had been caused by militants The Province of Sinai also claimed responsibility for the February attack announcing it had targeted a pipeline connecting Israel and Egypt Two additional attacks took place in North Sinai in November without any official statements issued in response or any party claiming responsibility The first was the killing of a resident in late October in front of his farm in the village of Galbana an area on the Sinai side of the Suez Canal that falls under Ismailas administrative control MP Gazy alOwaida said the attack came in retaliation to the mans cooperation with the Armed Forces and the police The second incident occurred on November  when Nabil Habashy Salama  a Coptic resident of the Ghazlan neighborhood in downtown Bir alAbd was abducted in front of his house by three militants riding a private car who then stole a pickup truck then retreated from the area Even with the abduction and explosions at the gas pipeline and suspected explosion that felled the electrical towers there has been a relative lull in the Province of Sinais militant activity in areas in the vicinity of villages in Bir alAbd in recent weeks Though the group had previously been very active in these villages to the far west of the peninsula militants have instead reemerged in the areas of Sheikh Zuwayed and Rafah in the far east where the group originally formed and developed In November the Province of Sinai targeted multiple military targets in Sheikh Zuwayed particularly in the coastal area It claimed responsibility for IED attacks on several military vehicles  as well as targeting soldiers in their bases The group released photos of these operations as well as video footage of another firearms attack that targeted a border guard at a checkpoint in the city of Rafah Aside from attacks on the Armed Forces the group has also continued to target civilians After Sheikh Zuwayed resident Mohamed Abdel Salam Abou Iskanadar was abducted in October the group released photos of militants executing the fisherman by firing squad days later The Province of Sinai justified its actions by claiming that Iskandar was among a group of fishermen charged with transporting food supplies and fuel to military checkpoints along the coast of Sheikh Zuwayed in exchange for permission to fish in the sea The group claimed through the Islamic Stateaffiliated AlNaba newsletter that its militants had forced the Armed Forces to stop using military vehicles to transport supplies to these checkpoints after targeting them several times According to the newsletter this drove the military to use the fishermen to transport the supplies in their boats in exchange for permission to fish Armed civilians who fight alongside the Armed Forces have also recently been engaged as the combat once again moved to areas in Sheikh Zuwayed and Rafah where these civilian groups are concentrated The Province of Sinai has recently declared itself responsible for two attacks The first was on November  when an explosive device hit a joint patrol of armed civilians and military units in the village of Zaheer The second was on November  which saw Province of Sinai elements set a trap for members of the Union of Sinai Tribes near the village of Barth south of Rafah The group claimed that it injured two people and destroyed a car and released photos of heavy automatic weapons that it claimed it had captured from UST fighters following the attack For its part the UST did not announce any of the November attacks against its fighters on its official Facebook page As for the Egyptian Armed Forces a December post on the official spokespersons Facebook page claimed that  militants had been killed in military operations taking place between September  and December  adding that in the same period two officers four noncommissioned officers and a soldier were killed and injured The UST meanwhile released a photo in October of a lieutenant colonel in the Armed Forces expressing wishes for his recovery and that he was injured after being shot in the head by a sniper during a raid in North Sinai A few days later the UST published photos of four bodies on its website with automatic weapons and ammunition laid next to them claiming they were among the militants who had been killed by the Armed Forces in the village of Qasrawit in Bir alAbd Amid the clashes that have extended across all of North Sinai authorities have been trying to restore a semblance of normal life to the governorates towns and cities In Bir alAbd the governorate reopened schools in the villages of Qatiya Iqtiya Merih and Ganayin after a lull in Province of Sinai activity in the area following the end of a twomonth occupation of the villages  and as the threat of explosive devices left by the group receded after the Armed Forces discovered and detonated dozens of them with the assistance of residents Even though the governorate decided in midNovember to extend its suspension of schools in these villages for two weeks it reopened them last week without issuing an official statement A total of  schools in these four villages welcomed their students starting last Saturday In Sheikh Zuwayed decisions issued recently by security agencies and other government bodies once again gave hope to the remaining families in the city who are considered the most affected by the ongoing armed clashes in the governorate The most important of these decisions was the opening of a number of roads that have been closed for years and paving a number of others MP Ibrahim Abu Shaira released photos of sand barriers being removed and the opening of roads leading to several village communities in the lead up to their residents returning In downtown Sheikh Zuwayed security agencies allowed the Sheikh Zuwayed Middle School for Girls to reopen after six years of closure since the Province of Sinai tried to take over the city in  The school which is located right next to the citys main police station was immediately closed following the  attack The city of Arish has also witnessed some relief from a raft of stringent security measures In October a number of squares in the city were opened after five years of closure helping to revitalize commercial traffic within the city after years of stagnation The governorate also announced last Sunday that on April  next year  the governorates national day  the industrial area to the south of Arish would be reopened The statement said that LE million was allocated to rehabilitate the areas roads and infrastructure as well as to provide it with six new electrical transformers While North Sinai has been cautiously coming back to life amid an ongoing insurgency militant attacks have cropped up in South Sinai On November  an officer and a policeman were killed and a conscript was injured in an attack carried out by militants in an offroad vehicle without license plates on a traffic police vehicle as it traveled on the Abu RudeisAlTor section of the New International Road according to local news websites  While no official statements have been made about the attack and no group took responsibility for it security at checkpoints on roads in the area has been tightened with residents being arrested as suspects The post first appeared on Mada Masr

political elitesJudge Fadi Sawwan the prosecutor responsible for the investigation filed the charges against Hassan Diab and former Finance Minister Ali Hassan Khalil as well as Ghazi Zoaiter and Youssef Fenianos both former ministers of public works All four were charged with carelessness and negligence leading to death over the Aug  explosion at Beiruts port which killed more than  people and injured thousandsThe explosion was caused by the ignition of a large stockpile of explosive material that had been stored at the port for six years with the knowledge of top security officials and politicians who did nothing about itAnger has been building up over the slow investigation lack of answers and the fact that no senior officials have been indicted About  other security officials and port and customs officials have been detained in the probe so farDiab is a former professor at the American University of Beirut who became prime minister late last year Although he served as minister of education from  he is considered to be an outsider to the political ruling class that has run Lebanon since the end of the  civil warSince the shipment of ammonium nitrates arrived in Lebanon in goes beyond the person to the position per se and Hassan Diab will not allow the premiership to be targeted by any party a statement issued by his office saidIt was not clear whether his comments meant he would not accept to be questioned again Judge Sawwan said he would interrogate Diab and the three ministers as defendants next weekThe move by Sawwan to exercise his jurisdiction came after he sent a letter and documents to parliament last month informing lawmakers of serious suspicions relating to government officials The Lawmakers responded by saying that the material they received did not point to any professional wrongdoingThis is an important and brave decision and requires a lot of courage said attorney Diane Assaf The question now is how far will the judge go she said adding that Sawwan could either stop after questioning them as defendants issue a temporary travel ban or arrest warrant or issue an indictment meaning they would go on trialA conviction in a crime of negligence that causes deaths can carry a prison term of up to three yearsYoussef Lahoud a lawyer representing families affected by the blast described Sawwans move as essential step toward revealing
