As Jersey City Police Chief Michael Kelly deployed officers and assessed how to dislodge two heavily armed killers from a kosher grocery in last Decembers deadly mass shooting he faced a major problemOne of Kellys officers managed to peek inside the shooters UHaul van which was parked on Martin Luther King Drive across from the grocery and in front of the Sacred Heart Catholic elementary school Inside a backpack that had been strapped between the drivers and passengers seats the officer spotted a large pipe bombThe officer took the bomb from the backpack and laid it on the passenger seat of the van police said But the officer could not disarm the bomb That delicate job fell to a team of bomb experts  a task made all the more difficult because it had to be done amid a raging gunbattleThe presence of the bomb later determined to be fully operational added heightened danger to the scene on Dec   when David Anderson and Francine Graham  both wearing body armor and armed with militarygrade weapons  burst into the grocery and killed three people in a torrent of bulletsThe two killers reportedly had studied antiSemitic writings of the radical group known as the Black Hebrew Israelites Their target was the JC Kosher Supermarket on Martin Luther King Drive and its Jewish customersThe attack on the market was just minutes after Anderson and Graham killed Jersey City police Detective Joseph Seals as he tried to check out their UHaul van in a remote corner of a cemetery Anderson and Graham have also been linked to the killing of an Uber driver in Bayonne several days earlierPolice now believe Anderson and Graham may have been putting finishing touches on their bomb when Seals approached their van After killing him they quickly drove to the kosher grocery and opened fireAs Kelly who is not related to this columnist recounted his thought process that day in a recent interview with NorthJerseycom and the USA TODAY Network New Jersey he said that after learning of the bomb in the van he did not feel he could move armored BearCat vehicles onto the street to confront the shooters in the groceryThe street was narrow with cars parked on both sides There was barely enough room for cars to pass by It would be even more difficult for the BearCats to maneuverWe had trouble positioning our BearCats with the bomb there Kelly said How do we get that device out of there so we can have free run at the front of the groceryHe also feared that the bomb might explode either from a remote device or from gunfire FBI bomb technicians later said the bomb turned out to be so powerful that it could have damaged buildings  and killed or injured residents  up to  yards awayOne of those rifle rounds could have hit the bomb and taken out the whole block Kelly saidFirst he had to figure out what to do about the bomb in the vanThere were not a lot of good plans Kelly said Twenty feet away we were being shot at by highpowered weaponsOne option he said was to sneak an officer into the van and drive it away Another was to disarm the bomb inside the van A third choice was to find a way to remove the bombKelly chose the third optionMeanwhile Kelly said he was facing mounting pressure to launch some sort of attack on the grocery The gunbattle had lasted nearly an hour at that point With the killers holed up in the grocery with plenty of ammunition he feared that the firefight would continue indefinitely unless he did somethingMeanwhile scores of cops  many in SWAT gear  descended on the scene and engaged Graham and Anderson in a wild gunfight that turned the streets of Jersey City into a war zone and left buildings and cars riddled with bullet holesIn the weeks and months after the shooting lawmakers as well as state Attorney General Gurbir Grewal condemned the attack on the grocery by Anderson and Graham as a vicious hate crime and an example of domestic terrorismThe duo had planned the attack for months honing their skills with firearms and living inside the van that later was the center of the bomb threatMuch of the neighborhood around the van had been evacuated as the gunfight escalated that day The exception was Sacred Heart School where many of its students were hunkered down in the basementBut how to disarm the bombFirst Kelly ordered two BearCats to position themselves sideways on the street between the van and the kosher grocery  effectively forming an armored wall between the shooters and the van with the bombWhat happened next seemed more like an excerpt from The Hurt Locker the  Academy Award winning film that depicted the dangers  physical and psychological  faced by a US Army bomb disposal unit that was assigned to discharge boobytrap roadside bombs in IraqKelly turned to three officers  all members of the elite Jersey City Police Department Bomb Squad The squad which includes eight specialists handles  calls a year not just in Jersey City but all over Hudson CountyThe three who rushed to the shooting scene at the kosher grocery Capt Vincent Glenn the bomb squad leader and two officers John Traynor and Anthony Moschella didnt even have time to put on special bomb disposal suitsThere was no time for that Glenn said in a recent interviewAfter driving to the scene in the units command truck the officers donned helmets and flak jackets and took cover behind a car about  feet from the van on Martin Luther King DriveRifle in hand Traynor provided cover as Moschella crept to the van Glenn followed a few steps behind Sitting on the passenger seat was the bomb which Glenn said consisted of explosive powder that had been packed in a inchbyinch pipeGlenn and Moschella placed the bomb on the vans back seat Then they fetched a special blastproof bag  about the size of a duffel bag Glenn saidThe officers put the bomb in the bag then carried it back to their command truck and drove it to an open area near Caven Point where they used a robotic device to disarm itWere they nervousNot really said Glenn  who has been a bomb technician for  of his  years on the Jersey City police force He said his extensive training which included studies at the FBIs Hazardous Devices School in Huntsville Ala helped allay any fearsIm glad we were there that day to do the job Glenn said adding that the bomb squad was summoned later that day to other locations in Jersey City to check on two suspicious packages that turned out not to be bombsThe bomb squad followed the initial response of three other Jersey City officers Raymond Sanchez Mariela Fernandez and Kendric Jackson The trio were on walking patrols not far from the scene when they heard the shotsThey ran to the scene and opened fire pinning down the killers in the grocery and stopping them from making their way to an adjoining Jewish school where police now believe they planned to kill childrenSanchez and Hernandez were both wounded in the gunfightThey were credited by Jersey City Mayor Steve Fulop and their superiors in the Jersey City Police Department after the shooting for trapping the killers in the grocery and preventing more bloodshed All three were promoted to detective in JanuaryBoth Fulop and Public Safety Director James Shea credited the quick Jersey City police response that day to increased training since  for possible active shooter situations as well as upgraded equipment and restructured police unitsAnd it was not just Jersey Citys police who distinguished themselves that dayNewark police Detective Joseph Kerik a member of the FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force and the son of former New York City Police Commissioner Bernard Kerik of Franklin Lakes volunteered to attack the store in an armored vehicle along with two Jersey City detectives after the bomb was removed Kerik and the two Jersey City officers in the armored vehicle killed the shootersThere was also police backup from surrounding counties and from the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey as well as agents from the FBI and ATFI think Jersey City residents have a lot to be proud of in regard to the police response that day Fulop said in a recent interview As you review the camera footage of the response in the minutes hours days weeks and months after the event it only emphasized more and reinforced the fact the JCPDs response was amazingEmail kellymnorthjerseycomTwitter mikekellycolumn

A PROMINENT activist from Davao City who rose to become the spokesperson of the National Democratic Front in Mindanao and his companion were killed by a joint team of Army Special Forces and police when they allegedly tried to resist arrest in Tandag City Surigao del Sur Thursday dawn
Army st Brigade commander Brig Gen Allan Hambala said Alvin Luque aka Joaquin Jacinto spokesperson of the National Democratic Front in Mindanao and his companion opened fire at the arresting forces prompting the police and Army to return fire
Hambala said Luque and his companion identified as Rodel Macana of Sitio Sangay Barangay Libas in San Miguel town Surigao del Sur were killed in the exchange of gunfire
In a statement sent to journalists in Mindanao the National Democratic Front refuted the Army story saying that Luque and Macana were allegedly murdered by the Armed Forces
The rebels said Luque or Ka Joaquin was unarmed and recuperating from partial paralysis from the wounds he sustained during the fighting with government troops
He was detached a few months ago from the main office of the NDFMindanao to undergo medical checkups and to recuperate from partial paralysis A few months ago he was physically debilitated and could not walk the NDF said
The NDF demanded for a full investigation and said they are outraged over the killing of Luque who was allegedly unarmed
There were three bullet marks found on the door and ceiling indicating they fired their guns Hambala told the Gold Star Daily by phone
Hambala said they knew Luque was wounded during a series of encounters between government troops and NPA rebels in Andap Valley Surigao del Sur on May  to May 
He said the rebels first brought Luque to the town of Marihatag and then transferred him from one place to another
Hambala said the police officers and Army soldiers found Hambala and his companion staying at Herminias Resort Purok Milion Barangay San Agustin Sur Tandag city Wednesday
He said the operation to arrest Luque was hatched at around  pm Wednesday after a local intelligence operative confirmed that Luque was indeed staying in the concrete semidetached cottage at the resort
But Luque and his companion fired at the arresting police officers before they can enter the cottage We did not know if he was severely wounded Hambala said
Hambala said the team of police officers was trying to serve five arrest warrants for criminal cases against Luque for frustrated murder and kidnapping with serious detention
He said the arresting officers found inside the cottage a Cal  Remington pistol with a magazine containing live bullets a fragmentation grenade IED components a blasting cap and cartons containing  rounds of brand new AK Cal  ammunition
Hambala said the police also impounded an Isuzu Dmax pickup found parked beside the cottage
He said the body of Macana was released to his parents Thursday while they are waiting for the relatives of Lugue who is reportedly from Koronadal City South Cotabato to claim his remains
The death of Luque removes one of the most senior and durable leaders of the communists operating in the Caraga region Hambala said
Elements of the rd Special Forces Battalion also killed Jevilyn Cullamat the yearold daughter of Bayan Muna partylist Rep Eufemia Cullamat in an encounter in Marihatag Surigao del Sur on Nov 
Luque was a prominent member of the Bagong Alyansa Makabayan or Bayan in Davao and Cagayan de Oro before he joined the communist rebels in 
During the celebration of the st anniversary of the Communist Party of the Phillipines Luque said he had sought refuge with the revolutionary forces to escape harassments by the military and cases filed against him by the police
Luque had said Bayan or any other progressive organization had nothing to do with his decision to go underground adding that it was his personal decision

By BBC Monitoring
Islamic State group IS has claimed responsibility for the killing of a female journalist in eastern Afghanistan on  December
The jihadist group made the claim in a brief statement the same day via its channels on the massaging platform RocketChat
The statement said its militants had shot dead progovernment reporter Malala Maiwand in Jalalabad
Mainstream media reported that Maiwand was killed when gunmen opened fire on her vehicle as she was on the way to work Her driver was also reportedly killed in the attack
Maiwand  a journalist at Enikass TV and Radio and civil society activist  was the latest victim of a spate of assassinations that have targeted activists and political figures
ISs selfproclaimed Khorasan Province branch which operates in Afghanistan has lost much of the territory it once held in the east of the country but retains the ability to carry out deadly attacks
It has recently claimed a series of major attacks in the capital Kabul including a rocket attack on the citys green zone and two assaults on educational institutions that killed over  people
Source RocketChat messaging service in Arabic  gmt  Dec

Death of Afghan journalist
Tolo News TV and Channel One TV TV have reported that the anchor of Afghan TV channel Inekas Reflection has been killed in Nangarhar province
Citing some eyewitnesses the channel reported that Inekas anchor Malalai Maiwand was killed along with her driver in a gun attack by unidentified men in Jalalabad city this morning
Maiwand is the third journalist to have been killed in Afghanistan in the past month the channel reported
Meanwhile Ariana News has reported that the Afghan presidential palace has condemned Maiwands killing
The palace said that the incident does not mean that freedom of speech and press are constrained in Afghanistan

Ghana president reelected as opposition rejects results
President Nana AkufoAddo has narrowly been reelected into office the electoral commission announced last night following a closely contested election that was marred by violence The main opposition candidate John Mahama has rejected the poll outcome and warned that Ghanas democracy was under attack
Official results showed AkufoAddo won by  votes representing  while his closest challenger Mahama polled a total of  votes representing

Ghana presidentelect urges peace after close contest
Presidentelect Nana AkufoAddo addressed NPP supporters and the nation last night just after the electoral commission declared him the winner of the  December general election
I will continue to work very hard to build a prosperous and progressive Ghana for which we yearn he said in a broadcast carried by the local media
Now is the time for each and every one of us irrespective of political affiliations to unite join hands and stand shoulder to shoulder he said
He condemned electionrelated violence which led to the killing of five people
Since returning to civilian rule in  the west African nation has earned praise as a model democracy in a region beset by political instability Election disputes are often pursued through the courts
See Explainer Perennial rivals contest Ghana presidential election

DR Congo parliament considers petition to remove Speaker
A petition by supporters of President Felix Tshisekedi to remove the Speaker of parliament Jeanine Mabunda is to be heard in a plenary session of the National Assembly in the capital Kinshasa a development that is expected to further heighten political tensions in the country
MPs from Tshisekedis Cap for Change Cach alliance clashed in parliament with allies of former President Joseph Kabilas Common Front for Congo FCC coalition over Mabundas removal Mabunda is from the FCC
On  December following months of powersharing tussle Tshisekedi ended a political alliance between the Cach and the FCC and threatened to dissolve parliament if he is not successful in finding a new coalition to govern The FCC has more than  seats in the seat parliament
A leading website Actualite has reported that President Tshisekedi is still waiting for the resignation of Prime Minister Sylvestre Ilunga Ilunkamba an ally of Kabila
Tshisekedi took over from Kabila in January  Kabila was in power for  years until he stepped down after longdelayed elections in December 
State media say Ethiopia rescues  army officers in Tigray
Ethiopian forces have rescued about  military officers who had been kidnapped in the northern Tigray state two governmentaffiliated news outlets have reported
The director general of the National Defence Force Indoctrination Major General Mohammed Tessem said the soldiers were being held by the Tigray Peoples Liberation Front TPLF the former Tigrays regions governing party according to the staterun Ethiopian News Agency ENA
The progovernment Fana website reported that Brigadier General Adamneh Mengiste the deputy commander of the armys Northern Command was among those who were freed
Ethiopia is hunting down TPLF officials after they were removed from power in the Tigray state On  November Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced that a military operation to oust the TPLF had been completed after the national forces entered Mekele the regional capital
Mozambique denies seeking help to fight jihadists
The spokesman of Mozambiques cabinet has said the government has not asked for foreign military support to fight insurgents behind ongoing violence in the northern Cabo Delgado Province Filimao Suazi who is also the junior minister of justice said any requests for military aid will depend on the limits of the countrys sovereignty O Pais and Club of Mozambique websites quoted him as saying
There have been media reports that Mozambique had sought the support of the Southern African Development Community SADC to fight the jihadists
Meanwhile Suazi said the number of people displaced in the violence had risen to 
This week the French major Total suspended work on a construction of a camp in Afungi Peninsula Palma District following a militant attack in a neighbouring village Total and US Exxon Mobil are among the major investors in Mozambique gas industry
See Explainer Mozambiques militant violence enters year four
Nigeria rejects parliaments summon of president
The attorneygeneral Abubakar Malami has said the National Assembly has no constitutional power  to summon President Muhammadu Buhari
Buhari was scheduled to appear before parliament today to answer questions on the security situation in the country but local media say he has cancelled the appearance
On  December parliament said it had summoned the president over the rising insecurity in the country especially after the killing of dozens of farmers in Borno State by Boko Haram militants on  November
Angolan youths call for antigovernment protests
Civil society organisations and youth movements have called for antigovernment protests today the private Novo Jornal website has reported Past protests focused on state corruption unemployment rising cost of living and political freedoms 
A group of young protesters have ruled out dialogue with President Joao Lourenco and promised to demonstrate again on  December the date of the foundation of the MPLA the governing party Novo Jornal reported
The protests are scheduled to take place days after Amnesty International published a report accusing Angolan authorities of escalating a crackdown on dissent in recent months and of using disproportionate force and unlawful killings to disperse protesters
Angolan authorities had declared a state of public calamity and issued a ban on public gatherings as one of the measures to contain the spread of Covid
GuineaBissau MPs to debate alleged plans to dissolve parliament
MPs are expected to discuss reported plans by President Umaro Sissoco Embalo to dissolve parliament and call early legislative elections the local Capital FM website reported
On  December Embalo met Jose Pedro Sambu the president of the National Election Commission CNE to discuss the possibility of dissolving parliament Sambu said he told the president that before early elections can be called the electoral map and electoral register must be updated
Entrenched political divisions have continue to cause tensions in the west African nation with a history of political upheaval
The election of Embalo which was hoped will bring an end to political divisions has not eased tensions
Nigerias Katsina state bans WhatsApp in schools
Nigerias northern Katsina State has banned the use of WhatsApp as means of disseminating information in schools and ordered civil servants to avoid commenting on government activities on social media
In a circular cited by Sahara Reporters website the states Ministry of Education ordered principals of government schools to abolish all existing WhatsApp groups in their respective schools
The development comes weeks after the inspectorgeneral of police Mohammed Abubakar Adamu called for control of social media  and blamed it for the recent escalation of antipolice protests in the country 
President Muhammadu Buhari has also said that he was disgusted by international media coverage of the protests
Researcher links GuineaBissau vulture deaths to rituals
A leading Guinean researcher has linked superstitious rituals to the death of more than  hooded vultures in GuineaBissau this year
Mohammed Henriques told the French public radio RFI that heads legs and claws of the vultures are often used in west African for superstitious rituals He said many of the birds found dead in the country from February this year were beheaded and suggested that they may have been killed for ritual purposes
Toxicology reports had indicated that the birds had been poisoned by methiocarb a pesticide banned in Europe 
Since the initial death of hundreds of hooded vultures in February  there have been other reported fatalities of the scavengers in the Bafata and Gabu regions in eastern GuineaBissau and in the Bissagos archipelago western GuineaBissau
Birdlife International an NGO says GuineaBissau is home to around  per cent of the critically endangered hooded vultures

The director general of the National Health Safety Agency ANSS Dr Sakoba Keita has said Guinea does not want to be the first country to use the Covid vaccines
We are waiting for the vaccines to be effective in countries that initiated them before acquiring them This is the reason why we are not rushing into this The vaccine has to be in phase  Dr Keita told Africaguinee website

POLITICS
Kurdish media mark human rights day
ProKurdish bodies and media marked the Human Rights Day observed every year on  December with a focus on reported rights abuses targeting Kurds in Turkey  
In a report titled Rights Violations in  proKurdish Peoples Democratic Party HDP reviewed the political operations targeting the party the violations of prisoners rights and the impunity policy in favour of perpetrators 
A joint report by the Human Rights Association IHD and the Human Rights Foundation of Turkey TIHV similarly found the Kurdish issue to be main cause of violations in the country womenfocussed Jin News agency reported  
They threw human rights off a helicopter proKurdish Yeni Yasam newspapers headline read referring to the alleged lynching of two Kurdish villagers by soldiers in the eastern Van province 
One of the villagers died after they were allegedly thrown off a military helicopter and tortured the paper said adding that four reporters covering the story had been arrested 
A large group of intellectuals writers academics artists retirees students former MPs and mayors calling themselves the  Citizens published a statement on the Human Rights Week proKurdish Arti Gercek website reported 
They called on the opposition to take responsibility for the right to a peaceful and safe life the report said 
Reaction to Erdogans remarks on jailed leader 
President Recep Tayyip Erdogans instructions to the judiciary not to release HDPs imprisoned former cochair Selahattin Demirtas remained high on the agenda 
It is not for me to intervene in the work of the judiciary Everyone should know that we are not going to protect the socalled rights of a terrorist like Selahattin Demirtas at this point Erdogan said on  December His remarks were interpreted by the Kurdish media as instructing the judiciary 
He once again declared that the trial against us was based on political motives Jin News cited Demirtas imprisoned colleague Figen Yuksekdag as telling the court  
The reason for this is obvious The HDP Selahattin Demirtas Figen Yuksekdag are the strongest opponents of Erdogan and his government They are seen as adversaries objects of hate not only as rivals she added

HDP Youth Assembly member Ercan Oguz detained earlier in the southeastern Sirnak province has been arrested the agency said

EU urged not to ignore Turkeys crimes against Kurds 
Fortyone Kurdish parties and institutions in Europe have urged the EU not to ignore the Turkish states crimes against Kurds outlawed Kurdistan Workers Party PKK affiliated ANF reported

European Council summit to weigh up possible sanctions on Turkey over East Med

Israeli news TV UAE state broadcaster sign partnership deal
Israeli network iNews TV and stateowned Abu Dhabi Media have signed a cooperation agreement official Emirati news agency WAM reported on  December It allows them to create frameworks for bilateral cooperation in the field of news reports and content production the agency said The move follows a USbrokered deal to normalise relations between the two countries The UAE and Israel have since signed a number of other agreements including on aviation and visa waivers

Putin hails RT on th anniversary
President Vladimir Putin and other Russian leadership figures have congratulated the staterun international TV broadcaster RT on its th anniversary In a video message on the Kremlin website on  December Putin hailed RT as the voice of truth
He said Today tens of millions of people in many countries in the world watch and read you every day This is the voice that is trusted and respected And lets put it bluntly this is the voice  the voice of truth  that some are afraid of and would like to silence In reality the channels success is explained by the fact that it follows universal laws of fair professional and free journalism
Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov described RT as a recognised leader in international broadcasting which has won the respect and trust of millions of viewers He said his ministry values its partnership with RT in the interests of promoting an objective image of Russia on the global arena BBC Monitoring  Dec

Reilly is the first permanent VOA director to be appointed by USAGM head Michael Pack who said His respect for and profound knowledge of the legacy and traditions of VOA combined with a clear understanding of the networks charter will ensure that Americas exceptional experience is shared effectively with the world
Reilly has publicly spoken and written extensively on gay rights and Islamist extremism VOA News said It said Eliot Engle a Democrat and head of the House Foreign Affairs Committee referenced Reillys apparent antiLGBTQ views and described his appointment as a disgrace and an embarrassment

The drones reportedly belonged to private Turkish company Baykar Defence Baykar drones are said to have been used against outlawed Kurdistan Workers Party PKK targets in southeastern Turkey Iraq and Syria as well as in Turkish operations in Libya where Moscow and Ankara support opposing sides Milliyet website Istanbul  Dec 
Russian website sues prosecutor media regulator
Russian human rights news outlet Mediazona has launched legal action against the ProsecutorGenerals office and state media regulator Roskomnadzor over alleged censorship after it was forced to remove an online investigative article about Covid in Russian prisons Prominent rights lawyer Pavel Chikov said Mediazonas chief editor Sergei Smirnov had requested that the ruling be recognised as unlawful

Mediazona said Roskomnadzor had asked it to remove content it said contained inaccurate information of social importance spread under the guise of accurate information which threatens to harm the life andor health of citizens Mediazona said it was forced to delete the entire text of the investigation under the threat of being blocked and edit the headlines and introduction beyond recognition

The trial of  people charged over the November   jihadist attacks in Paris that were Frances deadliest peacetime atrocity will get underway in late  sources close to the case said on Friday
The night of carnage on November   saw  people killed and  wounded when Islamist suicide bombers and gunmen attacked the Stade de France stadium bars and restaurants in central Paris and the Bataclan concert hall
The sheer horror of the attacks which were claimed by extremists from the Islamic State IS group left scars that have still not healed Modern Frances attitude towards Islam remains an issue of burning controversy
And the security threat to France has not diminished security sources say even if the nature of the risk has changed with attackers more likely to be lone extremists inspired by a deadly ideology than part of an organised group
Jihadist propaganda
In the last five years  attacks have been carried out on French soil  plots failed and  were foiled
There has been an increasing trend of attacks being carried out by isolated individuals previously unknown to the intelligence services who are inspired by jihadist propaganda and carry out attacks with cold weapons needing little preparation
But the threat of an attack planned from outside France  as was the case on November    remains serious 
Just because IS has suffered a military defeat does not mean its military capacities have been annihilated said a French official involved in the fight against terror who asked not to be named
Between  and  French jihadists are still believed to be in former IS strongholds in northern Iraq and Syria and it would be an illusion to think they were not capable of clandestinely coming back to France added the official
Repeated attacks
In January  Islamist gunmen massacred staff at the Charlie Hebdo satirical weekly claiming they were avenging its publication of cartoons of the prophet Mohammed
True to its defiant reputation the magazine republished the cartoons to mark the start in September of the trial of suspected accomplices in the killings
In the wake of that move a Pakistanborn man wounded two people with a meat cleaver on September  outside Charlie Hebdos former offices
Teacher Samuel Paty who had shown his class the cartoons was beheaded outside his school on October  by an Islamist radical from Chechnya And on October  a man recently arrived from Tunisia killed three people with a knife in a Nice church
The attacks reopened painful debates in France about the integration of Muslim minorites and also prompted tougher rhetoric from President Emmanuel Macron against radical Islam
Background noise 
The security source said the risks were higher in the context of the current Charlie Hebdo trial and another trial over the Paris attacks which is due to open early next year
These hearings keep up a kind of background noise with the risk of actions of support to those who are on trial said the security source
The  trial into the Paris attacks will see just one of the suspecter perpetrators in the dock  FrenchBelgian Salah Abdeslam
Nineteen other suspects accused of providing various logistical support will be on trial with him though five are presumed dead in Iraq or Syria will be tried in absentia
The suspected coordinator of the attacks  Belgian Abdelhamid Abaaoud who shot indiscriminately at packed cafe terraces that night  was killed five days later in a police assault on the Paris suburb of Saint Denis

out of  Burkina Faso  Mali and Somalia rank alongside Syria and Afghanistan for the highest riskCameroon Mozambique Niger and the Democratic Republic of Congo all facing sustained violence from various jihadist groups allied to Al Qaeda or Islamic State also rank among the worst affected countries in the world Jihadism in Africa is not new but since rebels and allied jihadists invaded northern Mali in  the security situation has worsened and groups have spread across porous borders overwhelming local forces In west Africa the situation is particularly bad An array of jihadist groups such as Boko Haram Jamaa Nusrat ulIslam wa alMuslimin JNIM and Islamic State in the Greater Sahara ISGS wreak havoc over vast stretches of landIn the Central Sahelian nations of Burkina Faso Mali and Niger jihadists from the AlQaedaallied JNIM and ISGS have played ethnic groups off against each other creating a cycle of deadly tit for tat communal attacks Around the Lake Chad BasinBoko regional factors The instrumentalisation of a range of grievances such as a lack of public services ineffective absent or corrupt government authority or a sentiment of exclusion by certain segments November access to Tigray has been severely restricted due to ongoing military action a communications blackout and the suspension of civilian flights to airports in the region Amnesty International is also calling for the protection of tens of thousands of Eritrean refugees in several camps across Tigray as well as unfettered access for human rights monitors as the security situation continues to deteriorate We are on the brink of a humanitarian crisis in northern Ethiopia and the federal authorities there are making the situation worse said Deprose Muchena Amnesty Internationals Regional government must also restore phone and internet communication across the whole region to allow for the coordination of aid to help people in desperate need There are an estimated  refugees from the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa According to the UN  there are also an estimated  internally displaced people in the region since the conflict began as well as  people who were already in need of humanitarian assistance before the conflict began In recent weeks more than  people have fled from Tigray into neighbouring Sudan with many recounting horrific stories of violence to media In recent weeks the International Committee of the Red Cross warned of medical supplies running out at hospitals in the region and the UN Human Rights Commissioner has described an exceedingly worrying and clearance from the Ethiopian government and also claimed the vehicle had failed to stop at two security checkpoints These attacks are abhorrent Aid workers must be respected and protected by all UN free press is essential for justice and peace in the world UN SecretaryGeneral and UNESCO DirectorGeneral have issued messages for International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists observed on  November By Vatican News staff writer The United Nations chief is calling for a free press and the protection of journalists against death violence and threats saying when reporters are not safe people can become vulnerable to misinformation and disinformation  As the world fights the COVID pandemic I reiterate my call for a free press that can play its essential role in peace justice sustainable development and human rights said UN SecretaryGeneral Antonio Guterres in a message for International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists being marked on Monday The November  observance was adopted by the UN General Assembly on December  urging Member States to implement definite measures aimed at countering the present culture of impunity regarding crimes against journalists   It also urges the promotion of a safe and enabling environment for journalists to work independently and without undue interference  The date was chosen in commemoration of the assassination of two French journalists in Mali on  November  Pandemic and journalism In his message Guterres noted that the pandemic has highlighted new perils for journalists and media workers even as the number of attacks on their physical safety has grown There were at least  attacks on journalists covering protests in the first half of   equal to the number of such attacks in the whole of  According to the UN Educational Scientific and Cultural Organization UNESCO nearly  journalists were killed between  and  for trying to keep the public informed Society pays a price when journalists are unsafe Journalists have also been subject to constraints such as threats of prosecution arrest imprisonment denial of journalistic access and failure to investigate and prosecute crimes against them  The UN SecretaryGeneral argued when journalists are targeted societies as a whole pay a price  If we do not protect journalists he said our ability to remain informed and make evidencebased decisions is severely hampered  When journalists cannot do their jobs in safety we lose an important defence against the pandemic of misinformation and disinformation that has spread online Factbased news and analysis Guterres said depend on the protection and safety of journalists who carry out independent reporting rooted in the fundamental tenet of journalism without fear or favour Speak truth to power UNESCO DirectorGeneral Audrey Azoulay also issued a similar message for International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists saying one of the most important roles of journalists is to bring truth to light ie speak truth to power  However she regretted  that for too many journalists truth and power do not always see eye to eye  Between  and  close to  journalists were killed while doing their job more than  in the last two years alone Azoulay noted that most journalists are being killed outside conflict situations for investigating issues such as corruption trafficking political wrongdoing human rights violations and environmental issues  In seven out of eight killings she regretted the perpetrators of these crimes go unpunished  Journalists also face threats kidnappings arrests imprisonments or harassment  offline and online and targeting women in particular  This year UNESCOs  EndImpunity campaign is highlighting some of the specific risks that journalists face in their duty to uncover the truth   The UNESCO chief called on everyone to join the campaign and urged all Member States and international and nongovernmental organizations to join forces to guarantee the safety of journalists and root out impunity  Only by investigating and prosecuting crimes against media professionals Azoulay said can we  guarantee access to information and freedom of expression Only by speaking truth to power can we advance peace justice and sustainable development in our societies

Kathmandu Dec   When the government in March last year branded the Communist Party of Nepal a criminal outfit Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli told his fellow leaders that all the activities of the Netra Bikram Chandled party would be controlled within six monthsHundreds of leaders and cadres of the Chandled party were arrested in subsequent months just as it continued to carry out extortions arson and other violent activitiesBut on Tuesday one action by the Chand outfit shook the nation It killed a school principal in Morang in what came as a chilling reminder of the decadelong Maoist insurgency which left over  dead  disappeared and hundreds of thousands displacedBack in January  the Pushpa Kamal Dahalled Maoist party too had slain a schoolteacher Muktinath Adhikari of Panini Sanskrit Secondary School in Duradanda LamjungSince its inception in  the Chandled party has been involved in violent activities as it has clearly said that it wanted a unified peoples revolution Chand who was a firebrand leader in the Maoist party has argued that Dahal left the peoples war halfway and abandoned the revolutionThe party had long been accused of carrying out arson and extortions The government decided to call it a criminal outfit after a blast in February last year in Nakkhu of Lalitpur resulted in the death of a personImmediately after it was declared a criminal outfit Chand in a statement had warned of retaliationBut authorities observers say seem to have taken its warnings too lightlyAccording to them the brutal killing of the schoolteacher by the Chand party seems to have emanated from its desperation of being noticed and such a cowardly act could have been prevented had the government taken a proper approach to deal with itIt the killing is a heinous crime by an entity that says it is striving to bring about a change But the government too has not acted responsibly said Devendra Raj Pandey who was actively engaged in bringing the former Maoists to the peace process How this government has dealt with the situation is not worth commenting onIn August  the Oli government had formed a dialogue committee led by Nepal Communist Party NCP leader Som Prasad Pandey to hold talks with various disgruntled groups including the Chandled partyBut after the Chandled party refused to join the talks the Oli administration failed to take any initiatives to bring it to the negotiating table Instead it took a highhanded approach Several Chand party cadres were arrested Some of them were killed by security forces after arrest Even the National Human Rights Commission had raised concerns over the killing of Kumar Poudel the Sarlahi district incharge of the Chand party after he was taken into custodyThe killing of the schoolteacher comes at a time when some forces are calling for scrapping the countrys current political system The Chand party too has been calling the present regime fascistThe regime led by the Nepal Communist Party NCP is a combination of Prime Minister Olis CPNUML and Dahals Maoist CentreChand was a loyal soldier of Dahal when the Maoist party led the decadelong insurgency But Chand along with Mohan Baidya and Ram Bahadur Thapa had deserted Dahals party in Chand however decided to part ways with Baidya and Thapa in  to form his own Communist Party of Nepal Thapa returned to Dahals Maoist party in  and is currently the home ministerOnce comrades in arms Chand and Thapa today however are pitted against each other Thapa as the home minister has always maintained a tough stance against ChandShyam Shrestha a political commentator who has followed Nepals leftist politics including the Maoist insurgency said the more the government fails the wider space it will create for forces like ChandsAccording to him the government has taken the approach of suppressing forces like those led by ChandThis strategy wont work said Shrestha If the government worked for the people ensured good governance and controlled corruption forces led by Chand and others that are calling for reinstatement of the monarchy would never get a chanceMany say the governments failure to realise how the Chand party could unleash terror also had to do with Tuesdays incident On top of that the longdrawn transitional justice process too has prompted impunity according to themConflict experts around the world say delay in implementing peace accords leads to violence said Daman Nath Dhungana a former Speaker and a civil society leader For the delayed justice all successive governments are responsibleAccording to Dhungana the government seems to be failing to assess the threat the Chand outfit could pose to the societyIt must decide now how to deal with the Chand party so as to stop it from committing further violence said DhunganaObservers say there should be no place for violence in the society and that since Nepal has already faced a bloody war the government of the day must make prudent decisions to not let another cycle of violence repeat in the countryAccording to Hari Roka a political scientist who has closely watched the Maoist conflict the governments approach to dealing with the Chand outfit has been wrong since its early daysTheir activities seem to be increasing but the situation is not in their favour said Roka The party itself is not clear what it wants to achieve and how So The Day Boko Haram Executed Dozens of Nigerian Farmers More than  agricultural workers were killed by militants who accused them of telling the authorities that the extremist group was in the area ZABARMARI Nigeria  For years the farmers had an agreement with Boko Haram militants They could tend their fields in peace as long as they did not report the fighters presence to the Nigerian Army But just over a week ago that deal was broken The Islamist group killed more than  farmers from Zabarmari a village in northeastern Nigeria residents say The militants accused the farmers of betraying them Everything is shattered now said Ibrahim Abubakar  Four of his friends were beheaded he said People in rural areas of northeast Nigeria Africas most populous country have largely been left at the mercy of Boko Haram by a government whose security forces have mainly retreated from the countryside to protected garrison towns Villagers are caught in a deadly Catch If they report the militants to the Nigerian authorities they risk gruesome reprisals by Boko Haram a group known for abducting schoolgirls and killing tens of thousands of people If they stay silent they risk the wrath of the Nigerian military which has been accused of routinely shooting villagers dead and burning their houses down during raids as well as detaining people for years in inhumane conditions In Zabarmari villagers struggle to eke out a living through subsistence farming and fishing We are accused of being collaborators by both the security operatives and the insurgents when all we did was look for peace said Garbati Sani a village elder What do we do to stay safe Militants came to the farmers as they were working in rice fields on Nov  and told the workers that they needed their help with something several residents said in interviews Thinking that they were protected by the peace deal around  farmers went with the militants to the nearby village of Koshebe But when they arrived more militants appeared and took most of them into a building where they slit their throats Later other bodies were found nearby bringing the total number of dead to more than  villagers said In addition the militants abducted about a dozen women from the village Boko Haram and its offshoots have terrorized northeastern Nigeria as well as parts of Cameroon Chad and Niger for more than a decade When Muhammadu Buhari was elected president in  it was partly on a promise to use his expertise as an army general to resolve the crisis Mr Buhari has claimed repeatedly that Boko Haram has been defeated or greatly weakened and the government has encouraged displaced people to return to their home areas But in fact the militarys strategy of retreating to highly militarized garrison towns  or supercamps  has left over a million people in rural areas to fend for themselves And the situation has deteriorated in recent months so much so that the governor of Borno which includes Zabarmari and is the countrys worstaffected state last week called for the federal government to send in mercenaries Boko Harams leader Abubakar Shekau pledged allegiance to the Islamic State in  a year after the abduction of hundreds of schoolgirls from the village of Chibok in Borno State But when in  several Boko Haram commanders split off to form their own faction Islamic State West Africa Province ISIS backed them It was the Shekau faction widely considered to be more bloodthirsty than the other group that claimed the Zabarmari attack in a video circulated on social media We are the ones that carried out that job said the spokesman in the clip slung with ammunition his face wrapped in a scarf You thought you can arrest one of us and hand him over to soldiers and expect to stay in peace Residents had alternate theories about what had motivated Boko Haram to carry out the massacre One said a member of Boko Haram had come to the village and asked a local woman to cook him some food She told her neighbors who tipped off the authorities and the militant was arrested Another said that the military had raided Boko Harams camp confiscating a gun and some motorcycles Yet another said that soldiers had caught a militant on a motorcycle when they were on patrol Surviving farmers said that they would return to their fields because there was no way they could eat otherwise Conflict and other conditions in northeastern Nigeria have made the people there desperately hungry and the region could face a famine in the next few months if nothing is done according to the United Nations World Food Program Villagers in Zabarmari said that those killed were mostly young men many of them the breadwinners in their families The elderly were not killed because according to the insurgents they dont have enough blood said Idi Musa a fisherman who sat near the mosque clutching his prayer beads But older people in areas controlled by Boko Haram have suffered abuses torture and killing that amount to war crimes and possibly crimes against humanity according to a report released by Amnesty International this week Many have also had to watch their children and grandchildren die On the morning he was killed one of the farmers Zakariyau Mohammed  told his father to rest up while he went to the farm I didnt know it was the last smile I would ever see on his face said his father Saadu Mohammed a tall slim man in his late s standing outside his modest home of unplastered bricks Zakariyau had been a dedicated son spending all the money he could earn on looking after his family his father said He had been planning to get married He was everything I felt proud of Mr Mohammed said Ismail Alfa reported from Zabarmari Nigeria and Ruth Maclean from Dakar Senegal

BEIRUT  The Lebanese prosecutor probing last summers port explosion in Beirut filed charges on Thursday against the caretaker prime minister and three former ministers accusing them of negligence that led to the death of hundreds of people Lebanons official news agency said The four are the most senior individuals to be indicted so far in the investigation which is being conducted in secrecy And though it is too early to predict whether any of the four would end up on trial the development was significant in Lebanon where a culture of impunity has prevailed for decades including among the entrenched political elites Judge Fadi Sawwan the prosecutor responsible for the investigation filed the charges against Hassan Diab and former Finance Minister Ali Hassan Khalil as well as Ghazi Zeiter and Youssef Fenianos both former ministers of public works All four were charged with carelessness and negligence leading to death over the Aug  explosion at Beiruts port which killed more than  people and injured thousands The explosion was caused by the ignition of a large stockpile of explosive material that had been stored at the port for six years with the knowledge of top security officials and politicians who did nothing about it Anger has been building up over the slow investigation lack of answers and the fact that no senior officials have been indicted About  other security officials and port and customs officials have been detained in the probe so far Diab is a former professor at the American University of Beirut who became prime minister late last year Although he served as minister of education from  he is considered to be an outsider to the political ruling class that has run Lebanon since the end of the  civil war Since the shipment of ammonium nitrates arrived in Lebanon in late  four prime ministers have been in office It was not clear why Sawwan has singled out Diab who was prime minister for less than a year among the expremiers who have held the post while the nitrates were improperly stored at a port warehouse a ticking bomb Diab received the backing of the Hezbollah group and its allies after Prime Minister Saad Hariri resigned in the wake of mass antigovernment protests late last year Diab himself resigned a few days after the blast which leveled the countrys main port and destroyed large parts of the city He has continued to function in caretaker capacity while efforts to form a new government have floundered amid political disputes Commenting on Thursdays development Diab said his conscience is clear and he is confident that his hands are clean and that he handled the Beirut port blast file in a responsible and transparent manner A statement issued by his office accused Judge Sawwan of violating the constitution and bypassing parliament adding that Diab has already provided all the information he had to Sawwan The judge first questioned Diab over the blast in September This surprising targeting goes beyond the person to the position per se and Hassan Diab will not allow the premiership to be targeted by any party a statement issued by his office said It was not clear whether his comments meant he would not accept to be questioned again Judge Sawwan said he would interrogate Diab and the three ministers as defendants next week The move by Sawwan to exercise his jurisdiction came after he sent a letter and documents to parliament last month informing lawmakers of serious suspicions relating to government officials The Lawmakers responded by saying that the material they received did not point to any professional wrongdoing This is an important and brave decision and requires a lot of courage said attorney Diane Assaf The question now is how far will the judge go she said adding that Sawwan could either stop after questioning them as defendants issue a temporary travel ban or arrest warrant or issue an indictment meaning they would go on trial A conviction in a crime of negligence that causes deaths can carry a prison term of up to three years Youssef Lahoud a lawyer representing families affected by the blast described Sawwans move as essential step toward revealing the complete truth He said Sawwan is charging the four based on a criminal investigation The Aug  blast is considered to be among the largest nonnuclear explosions ever to be recorded Zeitar was transport and public works minister in  followed by Fenianos in  who held the job until the beginning of  Khalil was finance minister in  and from  until  Documents surfaced soon after the explosion showing that at least  times over the past six years authorities from Lebanons customs military security agencies and judiciary raised the alarm that a massive stockpile of potentially dangerous chemicals was being kept with almost no safeguard at the port in the heart of Beirut President Michel Aoun in office since  said he was first told of the stockpile nearly three weeks before the explosion and immediately ordered military and security agencies to do what was needed But he suggested his responsibility ended there saying he had no authority over the port and that previous governments had been told of its presence Former Prime Ministers Najib Mikati Tammam Salam and Saad Hariri have reportedly said that they were not aware of the existence of the material Diab has said he was only informed about the presence of the explosives days before the blast and had planned to visit the port Later he told reporters he canceled the visit after being told the stored chemicals were fertilizers There is a list to be made of all those who knew and should all be held responsible said Elie Hasrouty whose father died in the port explosion Their job is not to refer the matter to others but to stop that bomb from going off and to protect people Investigators probing the blast had so far focused on personnel at the Port of Beirut Both Khalil and Fenanios were sanctioned by the US in September this year the first two officials to be subjected to those outside of the militant Hezbollah group Associated Press writer Sarah El Deeb and Dalal Mawad in Beirut contributed reporting

Moroccan outlets largely focused on the Western Sahara component of the announcement though the countrys foreign minister denied that there had been a quid pro quo He said ties between the two countries went back many years and that there had been talks for more than two years leading up to the announcement on Western Sahara
Similarly some media outlets in the region fronted the recognition of Moroccan sovereignty over the disputed territory while others focused on the deal with Israel For more read here

Morocco Drunk driver in Laayoune injures four policemen
Four Moroccan policemen were injured in Laayoune after a driver caused an intentional accident in the town the Moroccan staterun MAP news agency reported on  December
It said the incident had occurred on the previous evening and said the driver was drunk and had had previous runins with the authorities He crashed into a police van because of his state of inebriation MAP said This caused material damage and in his attempt to flee the scene four police officers were injured it continued
Police were forced to respond firing at the vehicles tyres MAP added The man was arrested and is being investigated
The incident came on the same day that the US announced that Morocco and Israel had agreed to establish ties apparently in exchange for US recognition of Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara Laayoune is situated in the north of the Moroccancontrolled part of Western Sahara
LEBANON
Lebanons Hariri lends support to caretaker prime minister
Lebanese Sunni politician Saad Hariri who is trying to form a government has expressed support for caretaker prime minister Hassan Diab who has been indicted over the massive  August explosion at the Beirut Port the official Lebanese National News Agency reported on  December
I came here to express my utter rejection of the clear and obvious constitutional breach that the prosecuting judge made by indicting the prime minister Prime ministers only stand before a special tribunal formed by parliament The office is not to be blackmailed This is inadmissible Hariri said in defence of the caretaker prime minister
Yesterday Diab issued a defiant statement saying he was confident of his integrity and surprised by the attack not only against the person but against the office A host of politicians have come out in his support
We reject the absence of set standards which led to what we believe is a political targeting of some people and not others with no objective scale the Lebanese Hezbollah group said in a statement earlier carried by its AlManar news network
WEST AFRICA
IS claims capturing Red Cross workers in Nigeria
Islamic State group IS has claimed to have kidnapped two Red Cross employees in Nigerias northeastern Borno State on  December
In a brief statement on  December via its channels on the messaging app Telegram IS said it kidnapped the individuals after setting up a fake checkpoint on the road linking the towns of Maiduguri and Mainok in Borno
The group said the workers it allegedly abducted were Christians but did not offer any further details or evidence to back up its claim
On  December IS said it kidnapped a Red Cross employee in Borno
In August and September the group claimed attacks on Red Cross vehicles in the same area and using a similar tactic setting up fake checkpoints That same month IS declared war on humanitarian agencies with focus on aid workers in Africa accusing them of implementing antiIslam agendas
EUROPE
Six injured in reported suicide bombing in Russias North Caucasus
Six people are reported to have been injured in a suspected suicide bombing in the KarachayCherkess republic in Russias North Caucasus the Interfax news agency has reported citing informed sources The incident took place on  December outside the Federal Security Service FSB building in the village of Uchkeken 
The source told Interfax that there was an initial explosion in which no one was injured Some five hours later a group of lawenforcement officers working at the scene were approached by a man who shouting Allahu Akbar blew himself up 
After the explosion six people including lawenforcement personnel and passersby who happened to be near the scene sought medical assistance Interfax quoted the source as saying 
The suspected assailant was killed in the explosion he set off the report said According to preliminary findings the man shared the views of extremist groups and the militant underground the source told Interfax 
Ukraine busts alleged terror financing group
Two Ukrainian citizens of Syrian origin are suspected of setting up a mechanism to illegally transfer money between individuals in Ukraine and countries with increased terrorist activity like Syria and Iraq the InterfaxUkraine news agency reported on  December citing the Kharkiv regional prosecutors office and the Security Service of Ukraine SBU   
The head of the press service of the SBU directorate in Kharkiv Region Vladyslav Abdula said on Facebook that the homes of both suspects had been searched and financial documents had been seized there 
New Lithuanian government sworn in
The new government of Lithuania led by Prime Minister Ingrida Simonyte has been sworn in and received the mandate to act from parliament the ELTA news agency has reported
This afternoon Simonyte and the new ministers will participate in a remote expert meeting on the management of the Covid pandemic followed by a press conference The first sitting of the new Cabinet is expected to follow afterwards 
Turkeys Erdogan says potential US sanctions would be disrespect
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has said potential US sanctions on Ankara over its purchase of Russian S air defence systems would amount to disrespect to its Nato partner privatelyowned NTV reports
The fact that the US subjects Turkey to a thing called CAATSA sanctions is disrespect to its very important partner in Nato This is how I see it Erdogan was quoted as saying while returning from a visit to Azerbaijan
He added that developments on the issue would become clearer after US Presidentelect Joe Biden enters office and Ankara would remain patient until that time
Washington is poised to impose sanctions on Ankara over the procurement of the Ss as early as Friday international news outlets reported on  December
Explainer How will Turkey use Russian S defence missiles
TurkeyUS ties face daunting challenges as Biden prepares for presidency
CORONAVIRUS
European press hails Covid recovery fund compromise
Media in Western European countries have welcomed a compromise reached by EU leaders with Hungary and Poland to avoid their veto of the blocs  trillioneuro budget and Covid recovery fund
The sides agreed on  December that the contested clause tying funding with adherence to the rule of law in those two countries would not apply to the stimulus package while Budapest and Warsaw can contest the application of the clause to future spending in court
German and Austrian papers described the compromise as painful and difficult but necessary while a Spanish daily downplayed the concessions as not substantial A French website warned of more legislative hurdles to come
Progovernment media in Hungary and Poland presented the compromise as their governments victory but opposition outlets agreed to differ For more read here
Covid Vaccines What measures are Asian countries taking
As vaccination drives proceed in countries such as the UK and Russia efforts have picked up across Asia to develop or procure a vaccine for Covid
China and India have promised to make vaccines available to other countries though there is some concern about the safety of Chinese vaccines
In Muslimmajority nations Indonesia and Malaysia the halal status of the vaccine has become a talking point For rest read here

Islamic State group IS has claimed fresh attacks targeting electricity pylons in the Iraqi western province of Anbar as part of the groups socalled economic war in the country 
The jihadist group made the claims on  December in its weekly newspaper alNaba which was released via ISs channel on the decentralised platform RocketChat 
IS said its militants on  December targeted three electricity pylons using improvised explosive devices IED in alQaim allegedly destroying them and causing power shortage in the town
The group said the latest claim is part of IS attacks on vital economic targets in Iraq The aim it explained is to pressure the government to deploy the army and police to protect these sites and consequently deplete government forces   
Media reports said citing a local official that eight electricity pylons on the outskirts of alQaim were destroyed following attacks by IS The electricity was completely cut off in alQaim on  December following the IS attacks the reports said citing the official
The pylons are reportedly located between the city of Haditha and alQaim in Anbar
IS has in the past strongly recommended sabotage attacks targeting the economic interests and infrastructure of its enemies with focus on oil gas and energy installations 
On  December the group claimed responsibility for an attack on oil wells in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk saying its militants had detonated bombs at two wells at the Khabbaz oil field
In November the group claimed multiple attacks on electricity pylons in Iraqi northern provinces of Kirkuk and Nineveh
In May the jihadist group boasted about its economic war against the government of Iraq claiming attacks on the countrys electricity infrastructure a gas plant an oil pipeline and agricultural crops
Source RocketChat messaging service in Arabic  gmt  Dec

The following is a selection of major news items from select Urdu and Kashmirilanguage press and online media outlets in Indianadministered Kashmir on  December 
Daily Chattan
Police arrest militant accomplice from Budgam Tral
The Jammu and Kashmir Police on  November claimed that they had arrested a Pakistanbased militant group JaisheMuhammad JeM militant and an accomplice of JeM militants in separate operations from central Kashmirs Budgam district and Tral in south Kashmir Pulwama district Police claimed to have arrested JeM militant identified as Tariq Ahmed Bhat at a check post in Budgam district They claimed to have seized a pistol and some incriminating material from his possession Tariq had become a militant in September Police said that they also arrested an accomplice of JeM militants from Tral Police identified the arrested person as Irshad Ahmed Reshi a resident of Tral Payeen and claimed to have seized eight detonators and a walkietalkie set from him Online Approximate Words 
 per cent voter turnout in phaseV of local polls
The fifth phase of the ongoing District Development Council DDC elections in Jammu and Kashmir on  November recorded the voter turnout of  per cent Addressing a press conference in Jammu Chief Election Commissioner Kewal Kumar Sharma said that polling for  seats in the region ended peacefully without any untoward incident being reported from anywhere He said that the Jammu division recorded  per cent polling with Poonch reporting the maximum voter turnout at  per cent Sharma said that in Kashmir region the polling percentage was at  per cent with Bandipora recording the maximum voter turnout at  per cent Online Approximate Words 
Urdulanguage Daily Chattan is proKashmir separatist promilitant daily that is popular in the northern part of Indianadministered Kashmir The daily favours talks with Pakistan for the resolution of the Kashmir dispute
Sangarmal
Senior superintendent of police beats journalists in Anantnag
Sandeep Choudhary senior superintendent of police SSP Anantnag on  December allegedly thrashed three journalists when they were covering the ongoing District Development Council polls in the Srigufwara area of south Kashmirs Anantnag district The journalists Mudasir Qadri from News  Fayaz Lolu from ETV Bharat and Junaid Rafiq from TV  alleged that the SSP assaulted them without any reason in full public glare leading to hospitalisation of one of them They said on his directions they were detained in police station Srigufwara for some time Meanwhile the Kashmir Press Club has criticised the assault on the working journalists who were discharging their professional duties and taken up the matter with the higher authorities Online Approximate Words 
Kashmirilanguage newspaper daily Sangarmal is a proseparatist daily It is the sister publications of Englishlanguage daily Rising Kashmir The daily focuses of local issues and favours IndiaPakistan talks for resolution of Kashmir issue
Daily Aftab
Indian firing along de facto border kills two Pakistani soldiers
The Indian Army on  November said it had killed two Pakistani soldiers in the retaliatory action against Pakistans ceasefire violations along the Line of Control de facto border between India and Pakistan in Kashmir Pakistani Army admitted that its two soldiers Lance Naik Tariq and Zaroof were killed in the Indian firing in Khui Ratta sector Meanwhile Indias paramilitary Border Security Force BSF on  November spotted a Pakistani drone flying over the international border in Jammus Ranbir Singh Pura sector According to an unnamed BSF officer the troops at a border outpost fired on the drone forcing it to return back to the Pakistani territory Earlier in June the Indian troops had shot down a Pakistani drone that had entered the Indian territory Online Approximate Words

Covid deaths in Jammu and Kashmir rise to 
Jammu and Kashmir on  December recorded eight more deaths due to Covid taking the total number of the virusrelated deaths in the union federallyruled territory to  Out of the eight deaths on  December five took place in Kashmir while Jammu also reported three deaths Out of the total  deaths in the union territory  have been reported from Kashmir and  from the Jammu division Meanwhile the health authorities in Jammu and Kashmir on  December detected  fresh cases of Covid infection taking the total number of cases in the union territory to  Out of the  fresh cases  were reported from Kashmir while  were from Jammu Out of the total  cases  were reported from Kashmir and   in Jammu Online Approximate Words

IS claims responsibility for assassination of Afghan journalist in Jalalabad

Eight soldiers killed in Taliban attack in west Afghanistan

Afghan journalist killed in mysterious attack in Kabul
A journalist with the private Afghan news channel Ariana News TV was killed in a mysterious attack in Kabul on  December Fardin Aminis murder comes just a day after another journalist Malala Maiwand was killed in Nangarhar province No further details were provided Amini is the fourth journalist to have been killed recently in  Afghanistan Tolo News in Dari  Dec 
IS claims responsibility for assassination of Afghan journalist in Jalalabad
Islamic State group IS claimed responsibility for the killing of a female journalist in eastern Afghanistan on  December In a brief statement via its channels on the massaging platform RocketChat the group said that its militants shot dead progovernment reporter Malala Maiwand in Jalalabad Islamic State channels on RocketChat in Arabic  Dec 
Report says Afghan security forces arrested Jalalabad journalists killers
A news agency has reported that the security forces detained the suspected killers of the journalist Quoting the governor of the Jalalabad the agency said that the arrests were made the same day Afghan Islamic Press news agency in Pashto  Dec 
Eight soldiers killed in Taliban attack in west Afghanistan
At least eight Afghan soldiers have been killed in a Taliban attack in the western province of Nimroz the Pakistanbased Afghan Islamic Press news agency AIP reported Quoting a spokesman for the Nimroz governor the news agency said that the attack targeted an army outpost in the Palwashe area of Delaram district on the night of  December The Shahab outpost located along the ZaranjDelaram road fell to the Taliban the spokesman said adding that the Taliban also suffered casualties without providing further details Afghan Islamic Press news agency in Pashto  Dec 
AFRICA
AlShabab abducts miners in northeastern Somalia
AlShabab militants kidnapped three gold miners from the village of Milho in Sanaag region in northeastern Somalia on  December Radio Risala in Somali on  Dec 
Somali militants kill man accused of sorcery
ProAlShabab news website Somali Memo reported that a sorcerer who practised witchcraft for  years and harmed many Muslims in the process was publicly executed on  December in Tiyeglow district Bakool region southwestern Somalia The website gave his name as Issack Hassan Daud An alShabab court sentenced Daud for sowing discord between husbands and their wives using magic Somali Memo website in Somali on  Dec 
AlShabab says six Ethiopian soldiers killed in Somalia
The alShabab group said its militants have killed six Ethiopian in the southwestern Gedo region of Somalia the proShabab Calamada website reported quoting the alShababs Radio Andalus The Ethiopian soldiers which are part of the African Union peacekeepers in Somalia were reportedly killed on the night of  December in the district of Burdubo Calamada website in Somali  Dec 
Ten militants killed in US air strikes in southern Somalia 
AlShabab explosives experts have been killed in two air strikes conducted by the US Africa Command Africom in the southern Somali town of Jilib The air strikes were conducted in coordination with Somalias government forces on  December Africom said in a statement on Twitter The statement said that the killed militants were known to play important roles in producing explosives for alShabab to include vehicleborne improvised explosive devices Africom did not specify the number of militants killed in the air strikes but the Somali Ministry of Information said that  militants were killed in the strikes Africom on Twitter  Dec 
Somali militants kill four soldiers in south
Unidentified militants have killed four government soldiers in the district of Wanlaweyn in the southern Lower Shabelle region Radio Dalsan reported The killed soldiers were members of the South West State regional force Two more soldiers were injured when the militants attacked a security checkpoint on  December No further details were provided Radio Dalsan in Somali on  Dec 
Somali forces lunch hunt for killers of government soldiers
The Somali National Army and Galmudug regional forces have launched a hunt for gunmen who killed government soldiers in an area between the towns of Guriel and Balanbale in central Somalia Radio Dalsan reported The troops have already captured one of the killers the report said On  December armed men ambushed members of the military who were heading to Balanbale town Radio Dalsan  and  Dec 
MIDDLE EAST
Blast reportedly targets USled coalition convoy in Iraq
An explosion has targeted a convoy belonging to the USled international coalition against Islamic State in the southern province of Muthanna The Beirutbased Iraqfocused AlSumaria TV reported that an explosive device went off as two trucks affiliated to the US forces were driving on the motorway in Samawa city south of Baghdad on  December No further details about eventual causalities or damage to the vehicles were given AlSumaria TV website Beirut in Arabic  Dec 
Car bomb kills at least  in Turkishcontrolled northern Syria
At least  people were killed in a car bomb attack in the Turkishcontrolled town of Ras alAin Kurdish Sari Kani in Syrias northeastern Hasaka province The car bomb went off at a checkpoint to the south of the town Two of the victims were Turkish soldiers seven proTurkish Syrian policemen and three civilians the proopposition Step news agency reported The UKbased Syrian Observatory for Human Rights put the death toll at  dead and over  injured BBC Monitoring in Arabic  Dec 
IS says attacks on Iraq electricity pylons part of economic war
Islamic State group IS has said recent attacks targeting electricity pylons in the western province of Anbar were part of the groups economic war in the country The group made the claims on  December in its weekly newspaper alNaba The group said its militants targeted on  December three electricity pylons using improvised explosive devices in alQaim allegedly destroying them and causing power shortage in the town The attacks on economic targets are part of the groups strategy to pressurise the government to deploy the army and police to protect these sites and consequently weaken government forces Islamic State said Islamic State channels on RocketChat in Arabic  Dec 
EUROPE
Six injured in suspected suicide bombing in Russias North Caucasus
Six people have been injured in a suspected suicide bombing in the KarachayCherkess republic the Interfax news agency reported citing informed sources The incident took place on  December outside the Federal Security Service building in the village of Uchkeken The source told Interfax that there was an initial explosion in which no one was injured About five hours later police officers working at the scene were approached by a man who shouting Allahu Akbar blew himself up The suspected bomber was killed in the explosion he set off the report said Interfax news agency Moscow in Russian  Dec  
Source BBC Monitoring  Dec
