The United Nations UN says it has not been able yet to reach the people who are in desperate need of humanitarian assistance in Ethiopias restive region of Tigray where an armed conflict triggered a refugee crisis and a humanitarian disaster
The UN has finalized an agreement with Ethiopian authorities on humanitarian access and assessment missions but has yet to see concrete progress UN spokesman Stephane Dujarric said on Monday
Its somewhat frustrating to say that we have not been able to go in we have not been able to reach people that we know are in need he added Days wasted by a lack of agreement or a lack of green light for us is just one more day of suffering for the people who need help
Tigray with a population of six million  some one million of them now thought to have been displaced  has remained cut off from the world since an armed conflict erupted between Ethiopian troops and local rebels there last month
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed ordered an army offensive in the restive region on November  in response to a deadly attack on an army base that killed at least  people
Abiy accused the Tigray Peoples Liberation Front TPLF the regions ruling party of having staged the attack
His government which had restricted access to the region said last week that it had defeated forces loyal to the TPLF and struck a deal with the UN to allow aid
Aid agencies however said the agreement was too restrictive and security remained a problem
Mekelle the regional capital and home to  people on Saturday received the first humanitarian aid convoy since the war broke out
The UN Security Council held an informal closeddoor video conference on the situation in Tigray on Monday at the request of the United States and European members
We need full safe unhindered access for humanitarian workers  said Germanys UN Ambassador to Christoph Heusgen after the meeting We have information that refugee camps will run out of food by the end of this week
We have information that refugees are prevented from fleeing to Sudan There are also reports that Eritrean soldiers appear to control some movement of refugees in the Eritrean border region Again all this must stop he said

The Ethiopian government is meanwhile trying to restore normalcy to Tigray The government on Monday ordered civil servants to go back to work and gun owners to disarm
Some power and telephone links were also restored in Mekelle after a virtual communications blackout according to Abiys government
Accounts of hunger and harassment however emerged from refugees along with reports of big fuel and food price hikes as well as water shortages
Citing three refugees in the Adi Harush camp Reuters said there was no food and little water and they were being mistreated by armed men without uniforms The men had raped two women one of the refugees said
The UN High Commissioner for Refugees Filippo Grandi had said formerly that the UNHCR had received an overwhelming number of disturbing reports of refugees being killed or kidnapped and forcibly returned to Eritrea which borders Tigray to the north
Thousands of people have so far been killed in Tigray according to the International Crisis Group think tank and around  Ethiopians have fled to refugee camps across the border in Sudan
Human rights groups say they have documented at least one largescale massacre in the region and that others are feared

Several Afghan newspapers also published editorials on aspects of the peace process
The independent and secular Hashte Sobh analysed recent remarks by Afghan NSA Hamdullah Mohib who said that the next round of intraAfghan talks should be held in Afghanistan
Based on three clear reasons the government opposes peace talks outside the country First the government intends to bring the Taliban directly under public pressure inside Afghanistan Second the government wants to reduce costs of peace talks  however it is so far paid by Qatar Third it wants to curtail foreign countries involvement in the peace process the newspaper wrote

When there is day delay in ensuring peace in the country its result is killing of thousands of innocent Afghan civilians Also tens of thousands of children become orphans tens of thousands of women lose their guardians and public properly is destroyed in the country it said

It seems that the USA is implementing the agreement it signed with the Taliban and it has reduced the number of its troops in Afghanistan based on the agreement If the remaining US forces also do not withdraw from Afghanistan on the time mentioned in the agreement that would mean a violation of the agreement and then it would be natural that the Taliban will also resort to violating the agreement it wrote in its editorial

No group including the Taliban has immediately claimed responsibility for the blast it added
In an earlier report  also published on its website  the news channel said that at least one policeman was killed and two others were wounded in an attack by gunmen in Kabuls Bagrami district this morning

However Kabul police in a statement said that one policeman was killed in the attack and only one other was wounded the report added
Separately the news channel also reported that Abdul Rahman  the deputy head of the provincial council of the western province of Ghor  had been killed in a magnetic mine explosion today
The explosion took place near the provincial council office in Ghors capital Feroz Koh
No group has so far claimed responsibility for this either

In a report on its website earlier today Tolo News TV said  citing Health Ministry figures  that  new cases of Covid had been recorded over the past  hours in  samples tested countrywide

By BBC Monitoring
Islamic State group IS has claimed killing  members of its rival alQaeda in clashes in central Mali 
IS issued a statement on  December saying its militants clashed with alQaeda militants on  December between the villages of Ndaki and Beli in central Mali close to the border with Burkina Faso allegedly killing  fighters and injuring dozens others
The group said it had seized four vehicles and motorbikes as well as weapons and ammunition in the clashes  
IS is most likely referring to alQaedas Sahel branch Jamaat Nusrat alIslam walMuslimin JNIM which is active in the region and has clashed with IS before 
Analysis Africas Sahel becomes latest alQaedaIS battleground
AlQaeda has not yet made a comment on the latest IS claim 
IS and alQaedas local branches have been at war for months in the border areas between Mali Burkina Faso and Niger
In its weekly newspaper alNaba released on  November IS said it had killed around  alQaeda militants between late August and early November during scores of attacks in central Mali and northern Burkina Faso
IS claimed the latest attack in the name of its West Africa Province branch which operates mainly in Nigerias Borno state but also carries out attacks in neighbouring countries including Mali and Burkina Faso
It published the statement via its channel on the decentralised online platform RocketChat
Source RocketChat messaging service in Arabic  gmt  Dec

By BBC Monitoring
The prime minister of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq Masrour Barzani has strongly condemned what he described as a fatal attack on Peshmerga forces by Turkeys rebel Kurdistan Workers Party PKK fighters in the region
On  December he tweeted of the incident which had taken place near Amedi in Duhok Province the previous day The group has martyred three security personnel in recent months Their behaviour including efforts to exploit peaceful protests threatens regional stability
He was reiterating an indirect accusation that he levelled during recent antigovernment demonstrations in the regions Sulaymaniyah and Halabja provinces
In a statement published on the Kurdistan Regional Government KRG website on  December after days of protests he said that some had taken advantage of the protests and infiltrated them
He did not specify to whom he was referring but it was understood to be a reference to the PKK
UK accusation
British ConsulGeneral in Erbil James Thornton also tweeted on the latest incident in which he said that a Peshmerga was killed by the PKK describing it as a terrorist organisation that should not be present in the KRI Kurdistan Region of Iraq
The PKK has been on the UKs list of proscribed terrorist organisations since March 
There were conflicting reports about the incident on local media the following day
There has been increasing tension between the regions ruling Kurdistan Democratic Party KDP and the PKK in recent months A Peshmerga was killed in clashes in November and the PKK claimed responsibility for an attack on the Kurdistan Regions oil pipeline in southeastern Turkey in late October
The PKK has accused the KDP of participating in military operations against its fighters in border areas including recently deploying forces near PKK bases For their part the KDP and the KRG have accused the PKK of using the regions territory to carry out crossborder operations against Turkey
The PKK seeks autonomy for the Kurds in southeastern Turkey and has been involved in conflict with Turkish authorities for  years both on its own territory and from inside the border areas of the Kurdistan Region Ankara for its part considers the PKK a terrorist organisation
Source Twittercom in Sorani Kurdish  gmt  Dec

By BBC Monitoring
Boko Haram has claimed responsibility for the kidnapping of hundreds of schoolboys in Nigerias northwestern Katsina State hinting at the groups continued expansive and deadly reach in recent weeks the private Daily Nigerian website has reported
The Boko Haram terrorists have claimed responsibility for the abduction of hundreds of schoolboys of Government Science Secondary School Kankara in Katsina state on Friday  December night In the wake of the attack at least  out of over  schoolboys were declared missing the website said
According to Daily Nigerian Boko Haram leader Abubakar Shekau said in a fourminute audio message that his group carried out the attack because Western education is against the tenets of Islam
What happened in Katsina was done to promote Islam and discourage unIslamic practices as Western education is not the type of education permitted by Allah and his holy Prophet the website quoted Shekau as saying
The site said that Shekau did not give details about the attack the number of schoolboys abducted or confirm reports of negotiations with the government
Katsina governor Aminu Masari has said at least  students are unaccounted for and that the abductors made contact with the authorities for negotiations Premium Times website reported yesterday
The attack took place as President Muhammadu Buhari began a oneweek private visit to the state where he hails from
Kidnapping and bandit attacks have been on the rise in northwestern and central Nigeria in recent months
Reports say Boko Haram  which largely operates in the northeast  is expanding its activities by coordinating with bandits and other criminal groups
In July a Boko Haram video claimed to show members in the southcentral state of Niger suggesting links with bandits
The claim of the abduction in Katsina comes hours after Boko Haram claimed killing  people in the neighbouring Republic of Niger as local elections were underway
In  Boko Haram kidnapped more than  girls from a boarding school in Chibok town in Nigerias northeastern Borno state
Lengthy negotiations between the government and militants saw the release of around  girls between  and 
However dozens of others are yet to return to their families
Source BBC Monitoring on  Dec

By BBC Monitoring

The jihadist group Boko Haram has released an audio message from its leader Abubakar Shekau in which he claimed his groups responsibility for the  December abduction of hundreds of schoolboys in Nigerias northwestern state of Katsina where Boko Haram is not known to be active
The minute audio message which was packaged as a video was released late on  December via Boko Harams media outlet on the messaging app Telegram alTibyan While the introduction was in Arabic the key message was in Hausa
In it Shekau said his group targeted the boarding school in the town of Kankara for its Westernstyle education that is against Islamic values
Boko Haram whose name translates from the local Hausa as Western education is forbidden has repeatedly stated its opposition to Westernstyle education
Shekau did not provide details about the attack including the number of children abducted nor made any demands for their release
According to a local news outlet the attack on the school is Boko Harams first significant operation in northwestern Nigeria
The attack is reminiscent of Boko Harams  abduction of  girls from a government school in Chibok in northeastern Borno State
The video
The video titled in Arabic Letter from the imam leader of Jamaat Ahl alSunnah lilDawah walJihad Boko Harams official name features a still image of Shekau in military fatigues clutching an automatic rifle 
In the message Shekau takes responsibility for the schoolboys abduction but he does not provide any details about the attack such as the number of children who had been taken
There have been conflicting reports on the number of students taken hostage On  December the Katsina state governor said  students were unaccounted for
The Boko Haram leader does not make demands for the release of the students either
Shekau starts speaking in Arabic addressing Muslim brothers 
Oddly he gives the date of the recording as Tuesday  Rabi alThani  in the Islamic Hijri calendar which is equivalent to  December 
He identifies himself as the leader of Boko Haram
He says he will start addressing brothers in Hausa about this operation that took place in Katsina He adds God willing we carried it out
Shekau then continues his message in Hausa
He explains that his group abducted the schoolboys to promote the religion Islam and pull down disbelief
Shekau says the group took action because Boko western education is not Allahs way nor conforms to Prophet Muhammads teachings In fact they are teaching them students how to destroy Islam even if they hide it
In a video message last year Shekau voiced his groups absolute rejection of democracy and Westernstyle education He also condemned the education system in Nigeria suggesting that it was a remnant of Western colonialism and Christian missionary work He said children were learning from books that taught secularism women rights nationalism atheism freedom of thinking and individualism which are all reviled by Boko Haram and other jihadist groups
First major attack in northwest Nigeria
According to the Abujabased website HumAngle run by Nigerian journalist Ahmad Salkida the schoolboys abduction is Boko Harams first major attack in northwestern Nigeria
According to the site the groups attacks in the region were often limited to ambushes of security operatives and smallerscale kidnappings for ransom
Boko Haram primarily operates in the northeastern Nigeria states of Borno Adamawa and Yobe as well as parts of southeastern Niger northern Cameroon and western Chad surrounding the Lake Chad basin Lake Chad straddles Chad Nigeria Niger and Cameroon
In June Boko Haram released a video that signalled an alliance with militants in northwestern Nigeria The video message in four languages addressed brothers in northwestern Nigeria urging them to remain committed to the jihadist cause  
A month later the group released another video claiming to show its presence in Niger and Zamfara states in northwestern Nigeria where the group was not previously known to have an active presence
Shekaus faction of Boko Haram split from Islamic State IS groups West Africa Province ISWAP in  after IS replaced Shekau with another leader Shekaus faction then reverted to its earlier name Jamaat Ahl alSunnah lilDawah walJihad although it has continued to use IS names and branding
Source Telegram messaging service in Hausa  gmt  Dec

By BBC Monitoring
The Afghan Talibans fighters consisting of foreign citizens have warned about their intention to attack Tajikistan the heavyweight Russian newspaper Nezavisimaya Gazetas website reported on  December
At least  Afghan security personnel including the districts police chief and its intelligence head were killed and a number of others were wounded reportedly by the Talibans Tajik fighters during clashes in Maimay District of Afghanistans northeastern Badakhshan Province on  November
Commander vows to attack Tajikistan
The website said that right after the massacre of Afghan policemen in Maimay District the Taliban commander of Tajiks said standing on the River Panjs bank and addressing Tajikistans authorities security and lawenforcement bodies that they did it on the other side of the river in Afghanistan and threatened that we will reach you and do the same with you
The film caused quite a nervous reaction since up to  citizens of Tajikistan took part in the Maimay attack and they did not even try to hide their faces said sources of Nezavisimaya Gazeta in Tajikistans security and lawenforcement bodies
The promise by the Taliban commander of Tajik fighters from Afghanistans Badakhshan to come to Tajikistan is the first public acknowledgement of Taliban representatives on a possible aggression in the postSoviet Central Asian region the report said Until now it was believed that only Islamic State supporters had such expansionist plans but the Taliban militants limit their ambitions exclusively to Afghanistans territory the website noted
The website mentioned that the Taliban had plans to attack Central Asia in s but they changed their rhetoric after the fall of the Taliban regime Recently Taliban leaders reiterated in Qatar that they would not interfere in other countries affairs The website stressed that the Talibans political leaders either do not control their local militants or they are simply lying to their neighbours
Threat taken seriously
Radio Libertys Tajik Service Radio Ozodi website reported on  December that the incident increased the concern of the Tajik and Afghan authorities after a video of the killing of Afghan servicemen by militants speaking in Tajik was circulated three days earlier
Tajik intelligence officers identified at least  Tajik militants in the video and disclosed their names later
A Tajik Interior Ministry official told Radio Ozodi that the issue was taken seriously after the video of the attack near the border of Tajikistan was circulated It is really a threat They mostly fight for the Talibans interests in Afghanistan but it is unpredictable what they will do in the future the website quoted the source as saying
The Tajik and Afghan authorities believe that the Tajik militants are from the Ansarullah group affiliated to the Taliban and fighting in northern Afghanistan the report said The provincial police spokesman in Badakhshan told Radio Ozodi that most of the fighters in the Maimay attack were Tajikistans citizens accompanied by Pakistanis and Afghans
Afghanistans authorities say that over  foreign militants from Tajikistan Uighurs of China Uzbekistan and Caucasians have gathered in Badakhshan Province bordering Tajikistan and are fighting on the side of the Taliban the website said
Unprecedented attack
Afghan MP Latif Pidram told Radio Ozodi that the Tajikistani Talibans attack was unprecedented He said that the groups threat to Afghanistan was known before but their dangerous activeness was also a threat to Tajikistan Naturally when there is a conflict on a border area it is also dangerous for a neighbouring country the Afghan MP was quoted as saying
The website said that the Taliban had intensified its activities near Tajikistans border over the past six years and took some districts under their control The Ansarullah group which is mostly comprised of Tajik citizens was set up by Amriddin Tabarov a resident of the Tajik district of Nurobod According to the Tajik Interior Ministry Tabarov was killed during an operation in Afghanistan in 
Source BBC Monitoring in Russian and Tajik  gmt  Dec

Suspected Boko Haram militants have killed an estimated  Nigerian refugees living in the neighbouring Niger Republic privately owned Daily Trust website has reported

Tajikborn fighters in Afghan Taliban ranks have warned that they intend to attack Tajikistan the Russian newspaper Nezavisimaya Gazeta reported on its website
At least  members of the Afghan security were killed and many others wounded by the Talibans Tajik fighters during clashes in Maimay District of Afghanistans northeastern Badakhshan Province on  November the report said
It added that after the Maimay massacre the Tajiks commander addressed Tajikistans authorities saying We will reach you and do the same with you Several days later a video of the clashes was circulated online showing militants speaking in Tajik Tajik intelligence officers identified at least  Tajik militants in the video This reportedly caused quite a nervous reaction since they did not even try to hide their faces a source within Tajikistans security bodies was quoted as saying by Nezavisimaya Gazeta
The promise by the Tajik fighters commander to come to Tajikistan was the first public acknowledgement by Taliban representatives of possible aggression in the postSoviet Central Asian region the report said Until now it was believed that only Islamic State supporters had such expansionist plans but Taliban militants limit their ambitions exclusively to Afghanistans territory it added BBC Monitoring in Russian and Tajik  Dec 
MIDDLE EAST
Saudi Arabia announces terrorist attack on oil tanker in Jedda
Saudi Arabia has said that a terrorist attack took place in the port of Jedda in the early morning hours on  December when a boat loaded with explosives targeted an oil tanker A spokesman for the Saudi Ministry of Energy said that the attack resulted in a small fire that was successfully extinguished by local emergency units the official SPA news agency reported He did not name the ship adding that there were no casualties and no damage to the port facilities
On the same day a Yemeni website said that an oil tanker belonging to an international shipping company collided with a vessel The report referred to a statement by the Hafnia shipping company that one of its tankers had been hit by an unidentified external source SPA news agency Riyadh in Arabic  Dec 
Blasts target several liquor shops in Iraqi capital
Four explosions went off near liquor shops in the Iraqi capital Baghdad leaving no casualties on  December The explosive devices went off near offlicence shops in the districts of Police Tunnel alDawrah alAdl and alAmeriyah in Baghdad The police succeeded in defusing a fifth device the Kurdish privatelyowned Shafaq News website reported The blasts caused damage to the shops but there were no casualties Shafaq News website Baghdad in Arabic  Dec 
IS claims activity in Syrias Hama after lengthy absence
The Islamic State group IS has claimed to have repelled an attack by the Syrian army in the northwestern province of Hama where IS rarely claims any activity Apart from a lowprofile attack on an army vehicle in Hama on  December the group has not claimed activity in the province since 
In a statement IS said its militants killed three soldiers and injured  others during clashes with a large Syrian army unit on  December It said that the army unit included tanks trucks and x vehicles It added that the group prevented reinforcements from reaching the embattled unit allegedly forcing the air force to intervene and help pull out the trapped troops
Local media reports said IS militants attacked military posts in alSaan area in the eastern parts of Hama province killing and injuring soldiers RocketChat messaging service in Arabic  Dec 
Source BBC Monitoring  Dec

AFRICA
Boko Haram says holding  Nigerian students
The Nigerian militant group Boko Haram has claimed that it is holding  students who were abducted from a school in the northwestern Katsina State on  December a website associated with prominent journalist Ahmad Salkida reported
There have been conflicting figures in the Nigerian media concerning the actual number of students who are still missing after the kidnapping at the Government Science School in Kankara
Earlier Boko Haram claimed responsibility for the abduction of students saying they kidnapped them because Western education is against the tenets of Islam  BBC Monitoring  Dec 
Suspected Boko Haram militants kill  Nigerian refugees in Niger
Suspected Boko Haram militants have killed an estimated  Nigerian refugees living in the neighbouring Niger privatelyowned Daily Trust website reported The incident took place in the Niger town of Tumuk on  December
Over  Nigerian refugees reportedly live in Tumuk after fleeing deadly jihadist attacks in Nigerias northeastern Borno state the report added Daily Trust website in English  Dec 
Militants abduct humanitarian staff in northeast Nigeria
A report by Dandal Kura Radio International has said that unidentified terrorists kidnapped two humanitarian workers in Borno on  December One of the victims was identified as UN staff and his counterpart worked for the Red Cross Members of ISWAP Islamic State West Africa Province were suspected of carrying out the kidnapping which took place at Shengen village Maiduguri the report said Dandal Kura International Radio in Hausa Maiduguri  Dec 
Militants kill  in northern Mozambique
According to the privatelyowned Mozambican Carta de Mocambique website militants killed  civilians and carried out several attacks in the northern Cabo Delgado Province on  December
Four civilians were killed when they attacked the Chai Administrative Post in the Macomia District They also attacked Litingina village in Nangade District killing  residents the report added On the same day the terrorists attacked villages of Namuine  Setembro Naleke ChicuaiaNove and Lukuamba in Nangade Carta de Mocambique in Portuguese  Dec 
AlShabab militants destroy police station in northeastern Kenya
Suspected alShabab militants have attacked a newlybuilt police station on the KenyaSomali border in northeastern Mandera County The Star newspaper website said there were no casualties but the attackers caused extensive damage to the police station known as Borehole  AlShabab militants operating in the area near the KenyaSomalia border are said to have been behind the latest attack the website reported BBC Monitoring in English  Dec 
SOUTH ASIA
Afghanistan Kabuls deputy governor killed in blast
The deputy governor of Kabul was killed in an explosion in the city on  December the independent Tolo News TV reported on Twitter Mohibullah Mohammadis secretary was also killed when an improvised explosive device attached to their vehicle went off Two of Mohammadis bodyguards suffered injuries Twittercom  Dec 
Senior provincial official killed in blast in west Afghanistan
The deputy head of the provincial council of the western Afghan province of Ghor has been killed in a magnetic mine explosion the Pakistanbased Afghan Islamic Press news agency AIP reported The news agency said that a magnetic mine attached to Abdul Rahman Atshans vehicle exploded near the provincial council building in Ghors capital Feroz Koh on  December Afghan Islamic Press news agency Peshawar in Pashto  Dec 
Civilians killed injured in mortar attack in east Afghanistan
At least  people including women and children have been killed and wounded when a mortar grenade hit a house during a clash between the Taliban and Afghan forces in Alisheng district of eastern Laghman province the Pakistanbased Afghan Islamic Press AIP reported
The provincial governors spokesman said the clash erupted after the Taliban attacked Afghan security forces posts in Islamabad and Shakarman areas of Alisheng on  December He said that the Afghan forces repulsed the attack killing a key Taliban commander who was identified as Abdol Malik Afghan Islamic Press news agency in Pashto  Dec 
At least six soldiers killed three injured in north Afghan attack
At least six Afghan soldiers have been killed and three others injured in a Taliban attack in Emam Saheb district in the northern Kunduz province the Pakistanbased Afghan Islamic Press AIP reported The Taliban claimed responsibility for the  December attack saying that they killed  soldiers Afghan Islamic Press news agency in Pashto  Dec 
Mine blast kills four civilians in east Afghanistan
At least four civilians have been killed in a roadside mine blast in the eastern Afghan province of Nangarhar the Pakistanbased Afghan Islamic Press AIP news agency reported Nangarhar governors spokesman said that the four were killed when their vehicle hit a roadside mine in the Zawe area of Khogiani district on  December He attributed the mine blast to the Taliban Afghan Islamic Press news agency Peshawar in Pashto  Dec 
Local police commander killed in south Afghanistan
A commander of the Afghan Local Police ALP has been killed in an insider attack in the southern province of Kandahar the Pakistanbased private Afghan Islamic Press AIP news agency reported An informed source said that the ALP commander of the Zherai district was killed by a Taliban infiltrator in the district on the afternoon of  December the report added The Taliban claimed responsibility for the commanders death Afghan Islamic Press news agency in Pashto  Dec 
Three soldiers killed in Taliban attack in south Afghanistan
At least three Afghan security personnel have been killed in Taliban attack in Helmand province Quoting an informed source Afghan Islamic Press AIP news agency reported that three Afghan border soldiers were killed and two others wounded after the Taliban hit their vehicle with a rocket in the Bolan area of Lashkar Gahs Police District  on  December Afghan Islamic Press news agency Peshawar in Pashto  Dec 
Pakistan arrests three militants in Rawalpindi
Pakistans Counterterrorism Department CTD has arrested three people suspected of involvement in four bomb attacks in the city if Rawalpindi Pindi carried out between January and December  Pakistan newspaper The News reported on its website The suspects were reportedly also planning to attack the Islamabad Stock Exchange and other key installations
One of the arrested reportedly admitted that his instructions explosives and his financial reward came from a mastermind in Afghanistan The attacks took place on  January  March  June and  December the report said The News website Islamabad in English  Dec

Text of report published by Pakistan newspaper The News website on  December
Lahore Tedious investigations helped the Counterterrorism Department CTD arrest three terrorists involved in four bomb blasts in Rawalpindi in  who were also planning to attack the Islamabad Stock Exchange and other key installations
In preliminary investigations a terrorist revealed that he got orders from his handler A name not disclosed who had been in contact with the masterminds based in Afghanistan He got money for every bomb blast He used to send video of the incident to hishandler on which the handler sent him funds He received explosives through his accomplices just a couple of days before the planned blast According to him his handler got funds from Afghanistan
The terrorist disclosed he had committed three blasts in Rawalpindi He had used two hand grenades in the first incident of Adyala Road Similarly he used two hand grenades in the second incident of Kabarri Bazaar He used explosive landmines in the third incident
He made a startling disclosure that he had plans for making terrorist attacks in Rawalpindi and Islamabad in the near future His next target was the Islamabad Stock Exchange He had completed recce of the building and saved its video in his cell phone An attack on the Hamza Camp Rawalpindi was also on his list The Quba Mosque I Islamabad was also included in the targets
The videos of all future targets were saved in his cell phone he disclosed It was only a matter of time If he had not been caught he would have committed his next bomb blast in the next couple of days It was easy for him to make attacks in Rawalpindi because he had lived in Rawalpindi from  to  A hideout was also available to him
A case has been registered at the Police Station CTD Rawalpindi Recoveries include explosives detonators safety fuse wire cell phones and other articles A detailed report of the CTD available with The News shows that on December  at about pm a bomb blast ripped through the Usman General Store near Crystal Line Bus Stand Pir Wadhai Rawalpindi The shop was gutted A rickshaw parked in front of the general store caught fire An innocent victim Afzal Khan lost his life and seven citizens were injured One of them are still in a critical condition
A senior CTD officer said it was not the first blast of its kind in Rawalpindi It was the fourth since January  On January  two hand grenades were lobbed on the Adyala Road which killed one innocent citizen Asif Ali and injured more than a dozen others The CTD Rawalpindi had registered an FIR but the perpetrator could not be arrested even after protracted investigations
The second incident occurred in Kabarri Bazaar Sadar Rawalpindi on March  when two grenades were lobbed in front of a shop One person Nadeem lost his life and six persons were injured
The third blast took place in Koila Centre Saddar Rawalpindi on June  killing a fruit vendor Arifeen and injuring another eight persons Terrorists were lucky every time in the first three incidents They did not leave any traces Even sustained and longterm investigations could not catch them Thousands of CCTV cameras had been analyzed but to no avail A doortodoor survey was conducted to see if any selfradicalized lone actor might be involved But this proposition also did not bear any fruit the CTD spokesman said
Terrorist organizations were analyzed to trace their involvement but no clues were found But the CTD officers did not give up Investigations continued uninterrupted The CTD officer said luck ran out for the terrorists on December  The crime left behind a trail this time The perpetrator was caught on the camera of the Usman General Store while placing the bomb The CCTV Camera DVR was retrieved from the gutted shop and it was analyzed by CTD officers The terrorist was clearly recognizable in the CCTV footage He was seen placing the bomb
Tedious process of tracking him through analysis of hundreds of private CCTV cameras took several days Finally on December  the camera trail led the CTD officers to AdyalaKharakan Road along the Swan River hideout of the main terrorist He was arrested on December  exactly after  months after his first blast and ten days after the last blast of Pir Wadhai on December  He was in possession of more explosives at the time of his arrest His two accomplices have also been arrested along with explosives
Source The News website Islamabad in English  Dec

Factional Boko Haram leader Abubakar Shekau issued an audio message early on  December claiming that his Jamaat Ahl alSunnah liDawa walJihad JAS group was behind the abduction of hundreds of students in Nigerias Katsina state on  December Hundreds of students from the allboys Government Science Secondary School north of Kankara town are still missing after more than  gunmen on motorcycles targeted the rural premises Many students were able to escape as they were forced into the bush but Katsina state governor Aminu Masari said on  December that  were still missing while reports in the Nigerian media suggest an even higher number The army claims it has located the hideout of the bandits and that a military rescue operation is under way 
Significance If JAS or affiliates carried out the abductions as is likely this would be Boko Harams first major operation in the NorthWest geopolitical zone of Nigeria Despite claims by Nigerian authorities that the kidnapping of the students is the work of bandits the scale and targeted nature of the attack supports the claim by Shekau The incident echoes the abduction of  girls from Chibok in Borno state in   of whom remain missing Successful retention of the large majority of captives would reinforce the view that this is an operation with JAS involvement The incident also underlines the inability of Nigerias security forces to keep Islamist operations confined to the northeastern states of Borno Yobe and Adamawa It gives more credibility to a propaganda video released in July by a NorthWest based group of Islamist fighters pledging loyalty to Shekau who is trying to rival the generally more effective Islamic State West Africa Province faction These fighters are most likely to have carried out the operation on behalf of JAS A westward expansion also makes further kidnapforransom incidents likely in Nigerias NorthWest and renders more credible the possibility of strengthened operational ties and an exchange of manpower and technical resources between Boko Haram and Islamist groups located in western Niger and eastern Burkina Faso

The Boko Haram faction Jamaat Ahl alSunnah liDawa walJihad JAS led by Abubakar Shekau on  December claimed responsibility for a raid on Toumour town in Nigers southeastern Diffa region in which at least  people were killed and  wounded Local officials said the  December attack lasted three hours and destroyed  of the town comprising a population of about  They said some  attackers arrived on foot having swum across Lake Chad and burned hundreds of houses as well as the central market The attack came hours before municipal and regional elections in Niger which did not go ahead in Toumour 
Significance The raid was very likely aimed at disrupting the local elections and its success in preventing the Toumour vote is likely to encourage further largescale jihadist attacks in the runup to presidential and parliamentary elections on  December Local politicians in Diffa region unsuccessfully attempted to block the candidacy of the presidential frontrunner Mohamed Bazoum of the ruling Nigerien Party for Democracy and Socialism Parti nigerin pour la dmocratie et le socialisme PNDS questioning his nationality and thus eligibility to run Islamic Stateaffiliated groups are likely to attempt to capitalise on local antipathy towards the PNDS for further disruption in Diffa as well as the regions of Tahoua and Tillaberi where Islamic State in the Greater Sahara is also active Smallarms attacks occasionally preceded by a suicidevehicleborne improvised explosive device are likely to target local and foreign military bases local airports churches and villages In addition foreign aid workers in these regions will face a high risk of kidnap and murder In September Islamic States West Africa Province claimed responsibility for an ambush and smallarms attack killing six French aid workers and their local guides at the Kour giraffe reserve in Tillaberi region Attacks have continued despite the operationalisation in December  of a US military facility including armed drones in Nigers Agadez desert indicating its limited potential to track jihadists In the event that Bazoum is elected Nigers counterterrorism cooperation with and proinvestment attitude towards the West are likely to continue driving a persistent terrorism threat for at least the next  months

Azerbaijans Ministry of Defence and State Security Service issued a joint press release on  December  describing an antiterror operation near Hadrut in Khojavend region which abuts the breakaway enclave of NagornoKarabakh This was in response to two alleged attacks carried out by Armenian fighters who remained in the wooded areas near Hadrut even though they were required to withdraw in accordance with the Russianbacked trilateral ceasefire see Armenia  Azerbaijan  Russia  November  Trilateral ceasefire agreement backed by deployment of Russian peacekeepers safeguards cessation of hostilities in NagornoKarabakh conflict zone The first attack was an ambush in the village of Sur on  November in which three Azeri soldiers were killed and two wounded The second took place on  December when an Azeri soldier died and a technician from the Azeri telecoms company Azercell was wounded near Hadrut The Azeri operation took place on  December after Russian peacekeepers had registered a ceasefire violation near the villages of aylaqqala Armenian designation Khtsaberd and Khn Taglar Hin Tagher and entered the area in an unsuccessful attempt to persuade the Armenian fighters to leave their hiding places under safe escort The Armenian separatists claimed that their positions in these villages were attacked by Azeri forces resulting in the wounding of three Armenian soldiers 
Significance Hadrut is outside the area where the Russian peacekeeping forces have a mandate to monitor the ceasefire The fact that they deployed there in an attempt to defuse the situation drew an angry reaction from Azeri MP Tahir Karimli who accused them of exceeding their mandate While the Hadrut incident is unlikely to cause the Russianbacked trilateral ceasefire to break down if similar ceasefire violations occur in and around the NagornoKarabakh enclave it is unlikely that the Azeri government will extend the Russian peacekeeping forces mandate before it expires in November  Given Armenias concessions under the ceasefire terms the presence of irreconcilable Armenian fighters in and around the NagornoKarabakh enclave is likely to result in skirmishes with the Azeri forces which the Russian peacekeepers will struggle to prevent and contain but these are unlikely to lead to resumption of fullscale hostilities Nevertheless they increase the likelihood of death and injury from hitandrun attacks to civilians on the Azeri side as they go about restoring infrastructure along the new Line of Contact LoC and in the newly regained territories adjacent to the NagornoKarabakh enclave As the ethnic landscape becomes more stable due to the finalisation of partition and the Armenian population resettles in the separatistcontrolled territory the Armenian fighters will be deprived of support in the areas ceded to Azerbaijan reducing their overall capacity to carry out insurgent activities

KYOTOProsecutors here on Dec  indicted an unemployed man on multiple charges of murder and attempted murder over the arson attack against Kyoto Animation Co last year that killed  workers
Shinji Aoba  will be tried under the lay judge system
Aoba from Saitama city has admitted to setting fire to the studio and trying to kill as many people as possible investigative sources said His arrest and indictment were delayed until after he recovered from serious burns he suffered in the attack and underwent a psychiatric evaluation
Based on the evaluation investigators at the Kyoto District Public Prosecutors Office concluded that Aoba can be held criminally responsible for his actions His detention period for those tests expired on Dec 
Aoba said he attacked the threestory studio in Kyotos Fushimi Ward because Kyoto Animation stole novels that he had entered in a contest the sources said
But police found no evidence that the popular animation company known as Kyoani used any ideas of the suspect according to the sources
Aoba was taken into custody by police on July   near the site of the blaze At the time  employees and executives were inside the building
Aoba is suspected of killing  of them and injuring the  others by setting fire to the studio with gasoline he brought He told investigators that he used gasoline in the attack because he believed it would lead to a high death toll the sources said
He also had six kitchen knives in his possession in the attack a violation of the swords and firearms control law according to the sources
Aoba was also badly burned in the attack and required about  months of hospitalization His formal arrest by Kyoto police came on May  after authorities determined that he had recovered enough for detention
He was transported to the Osaka Detention House on a stretcher for police questioning The facility was selected because it can provide good medical services
Investigators interrogated Aoba while he lay on his bed in his room Precautionary measures were in place to ensure that he would not contract a virus the sources said
Prosecutors had experts conduct a sixmonth psychiatric evaluation of Aoba from June  to determine if he was mentally fit to face charges and stand trial

NEW EYEWITNESS REPORTS OF ETHNIC KILLINGS IN ETHIOPIAS TIGRAY REGION
Despite Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed declaring an official end to the fighting in Ethiopias northern Tigray region on  November there has been continued violence around Mekelle Sherero Axum and Abiy Addi as well as along the regional border between Amhara and Tigray Since  November the conflict has displaced more than one million people at least  of whom have fled to neighboring Sudan
On  December the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Michelle Bachelet issued a statement calling for urgent monitoring of the human rights situation in Tigray and accountability for alleged violations The statement corroborated reports of ethnic profiling of Tigrayans including harassment and hate speech High Commissioner Bachelet also stated that such discriminatory actions are deeply unjust but are also fostering divisiveness and sowing the seeds for further instability and conflict
On  December the UN High Commissioner for Refugees Filippo Grandi expressed alarm about the situation facing almost  Eritrean refugees trapped in Tigray High Commissioner Grandi highlighted an overwhelming number of reports that refugees had been killed or forcibly returned to Eritrea where they could face persecution The refugees have also been cut off from lifesaving assistance since the fighting in Tigray first began in early November Although the federal government and the UN signed an agreement to allow the resumption of humanitarian aid on  December the government claims insecurity has hampered access with the Tigrayan capital of Mekelle only receiving its first convoy of medical supplies on  December
As the communications blackout in the region has slowly been lifted fresh reports have emerged of war crimes and other violations and abuses of human rights including eyewitness accounts of the massacre of hundreds of people in MaiKadra on  November Survivors recount a systematic planned attack against ethnic Amhara civilians by Tigrayan youth groups local police and militias Meanwhile in Sudan ethnically Tigrayan refugees from MaiKadra reported attacks on ethnic Tigrayans perpetrated by Ethiopian government forces and an allied Amhara militia in MaiKadra at the same time as the massacre of Amhara civilians Amnesty Internationals Ethiopia Researcher Fisseha Tekle has stated that MaiKadra may only be the tip of the iceberg with details emerging of ethnic targeting and other attacks on civilians in Humera Dansha and Mekelle
The Ethiopian government must ensure unfettered humanitarian access to all vulnerable populations in Tigray Refugees and other displaced persons must also be protected in keeping with international law All reports of war crimes and other violations and abuses of human rights should be properly investigated and the perpetrators held accountable regardless of their position or affiliation
 YEARS SINCE STOCKHOLM AGREEMENT YEMENI CIVILIANS CONTINUE TO SUFFER
Sunday  December marked two years since parties to the conflict in Yemen signed the Stockholm Agreement At the time the agreement was hailed as a diplomatic breakthrough that prevented a military escalation in Hodeidah governorate and helped alleviate the suffering of Yemeni civilians In addition to prisoner exchanges and steps towards deescalation in Taizz parties committed to a ceasefire in Hodeidah governorate enabling the return of thousands of displaced civilians and the resumption of critical humanitarian aid deliveries across the country
However despite initial signs of promise civilians have continued to endure widespread violations of international law According to the Norwegian Refugee Council at least  civilians have been killed or maimed in Yemen since December  with  casualties in Hodeidah alone Indiscriminate attacks have escalated during  causing civilian casualties to almost triple since May
In recent weeks hostilities in both Hodeidah and Taizz governorates have continued to increase forcing hundreds of families to flee as residential areas are shelled and the delivery of humanitarian aid is systematically obstructed At least  civilians including  children were killed or maimed during October due to renewed fighting  the highest monthly casualty count since September  Eleven children and dozens of other civilians have been killed or maimed by indiscriminate shelling so far during December
In a press statement on  December the UN Security Council UNSC condemned increased fighting in Marib Hodeidah and Taizz governorates and called for implementation of the global ceasefire call detailed in UNSC resolution 
Jahaan Pittalwala Research Analyst at the Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect emphasized that recent violence in Hodeidah not only threatens the viability of the ceasefire but also the delivery of lifesaving aid to millions of vulnerable Yemenis Preserving the ceasefire and the delivery of humanitarian goods is more crucial than ever given that at least  people in Yemen are already living in faminelike conditions All parties to the conflict should fully implement the Stockholm Agreement and must end ongoing attacks on civilians
 STUDENTS STILL MISSING AFTER GUNMEN ATTACK SCHOOL IN NIGERIA
An estimated  boys remain missing after gunmen attacked a school in the town of Kankara in Nigerias northwestern Katsina State on  December A group of men on motorcycles armed with AKs stormed the Government Science Secondary School and marched hundreds of students into the surrounding woods It is unclear how many of the missing boys are hiding in the remote forest or are still being held by the armed group On Sunday  December UN SecretaryGeneral Antnio Guterres called for the immediate and unconditional release of the abducted children and urged the Nigerian authorities to bring those responsible to justice
The armed extremist group Boko Haram has reportedly claimed responsibility for the attack If true it would mark their first major operation in northwest Nigeria The attack took place in a state where criminal armed groups known locally as bandits are active Since early  armed banditry in Zamfara Kaduna Katsina Sokoto and Niger states has displaced more than  people Despite efforts by the security forces bandits have killed more than  people in rural areas during  While bandits in Katsina State are known to carry out kidnappings for ransom they have not previously perpetrated an attack on this scale
The Regional Director for West and Central Africa of the UN Childrens Fund Pierre Poirier said that last Fridays attack is a grim reminder that abductions of children and widespread grave violations of childrens rights continue to take place in northern Nigeria Kidnappings have become increasingly common with children often being the target of armed groups In the most notorious incidents during  Boko Haram abducted more than  girls in the town of Chibok and more than  girls in the town of Dapchi in 
While the Minister of Defense has indicated that a rescue operation is underway President Muhammadu Buhari has faced criticism for the security forces inability to provide civilians with adequate protection from armed groups On Monday the parents of some of the missing boys took to the streets to pressure the government to increase their efforts to rescue the boys The campaign hashtag BringBackOurBoys has also been trending on social media
Nigeria is currently facing multiple security threats that leave civilians at risk of atrocity crimes but armed groups  including bandits and Boko Haram  are unlikely to be defeated by counterterrorism operations alone The government needs to comprehensively address structural issues of poverty corruption youth unemployment and environmental degradation that are exploited by armed groups to recruit and grow

A Nigerian state has shut down ten schools as of Wednesday in response to the jihadist terror group Boko Haram abducting hundreds of boys from a school this weekend the nations Daily Trust newspaper reported
In audio surfacing Tuesday a voice claiming to be that of Boko Haram leader Abubakar Shekau took responsibility for the attack and asserted its message was to discourage Nigerians from educating their children instead pressuring them to embrace radical Islam
The attack occurred in Katsina state significantly west of where Boko Haram typically operates the countrys most northwestern state of Borno It follows several waves of deadly jihadist attacks against Christians in the region and is the third mass abduction of children this decade by Boko Haram following the  Chibok Borno kidnappings and the mass abduction of girls from Dapchi Yobe in 
The government of Nigerian President Muhammadu Buhari has repeatedly claimed that Boko Haram is defeated and no longer a national security threat Buhari first made the claim shortly after taking office in  When confronted by the continued vigor of Boko Haram jihadist attacks on civilians Buhari officials have insisted that those attacking are not Boko Haram but the Islamic State West Africa Province the name that Boko Haram adopted after swearing allegiance to slain ISIS chief Abu Bakr alBaghdadi in 
The Daily Trust listed ten schools in Zamfara state which borders Katsina to its west that have chosen to shut down in response to the Boko Haram attack all on the borders of either Katsina or Kaduna state
The affected schools are at a location sharing boundaries with Katsina and Kaduna states and given the current situation in the neighbouring Katsina state we felt compelled to close these schools even though the term is ending in one weeks time Ibrahim Gusau Zamfaras education commissioner told reporters The closings the newspaper noted were in addition to the shutdown of all boarding schools in Katsina which authorities consider more vulnerable to attack since children sleep together in one easily identifiable dormitory allowing for overnight attacks
The school attack this weekend which targeted Katsinas Government Science Secondary School resulted in the disappearance of  boys that may remain missing Authorities initially claimed less than half of that number  had been abducted They then said they had found hundreds of boys but were struggling to contact parents so confirmation of whether the boys were safe had not yet occurred Other boys are believed to be hiding in the densely wooded bush areas surrounding the school and have yet to come out fearing abduction
Gov Aminu Masari confirmed Wednesday that authorities had reunited at least  children with their families
Parents of the missing children believed to be between ten and  years old began demanding on Wednesday that Nigerian officials pay Boko Haram a ransom to free the boys asserting that Nigerian police and military are too incompetent to rescue the children
I support government paying ransom to secure release of our children whatever amount since the government cant rescue them Had it be that the government can rescue them we wouldnt have supported paying of ransom one parent identified as Aminu Dayyabu told Nigerias Vanguard newspaper
In my presence about  vehicles of the soldiers came to Kankara entered the bush and came out Dayyabu narrated to the newspaper One of the soldiers I engaged in little discussion with told me their vehicle was attacked as their tyre and glass were shot at I saw the damages on the vehicle With that he told me that government has to sit up if it must defeat the bandits because they are well armed
So whatever amount they demand as ransom the government should pay and secure the release of our children he concluded
No party including Boko Haram has demanded a ransom for the boys In the audio surfacing this week the man alleging to be Shekau insists that the objective of the attack is simply to stop Nigerians from going to school
What happened in Katsina was done to promote Islam and discourage unIslamic practices as Western education is not the type of education permitted by Allah and his Holy Prophet the voice claimed They are also not teaching what Allah and his Holy Prophet commanded They are rather destroying Islam
It may be subtle but Allah the lord of the skies and earths knows whatever is hidden May Allah promote Islam May we die as Muslims the audio concludes
Buhari the president prompted a national uproar after video showed him to be visiting his farm this weekend in his native Katsina state not far from the scene of the attack but failing to meet with parents or even issue remarks on the incident Buharis spokesperson Garba Shehu told the Premium Times that Buhari did not know the attack had happened when he chose to visit his home
We arrived on Friday evening to Daura President went to his farm  am or thereabouts when the report has had not broken out Shehu alleged  So for anyone to now say he has chosen to visit his cow instead of the parents of students is mischief Let me tell you we are being careful about one thing We dont want politics to divert attention from rescuing these boys
Buhari and his officials have claimed repeatedly that Boko Haram is no longer a threat
I think technically we have won the war Buhari told the BBC in December  Boko Haram is an organized fighting force I assure you but we have dealt with them
A month later the Nigerian armys chief of staff Lt General Tukur Buratai asserted the terrorists have been defeated these criminals may rear their ugly heads through other means We will continue to maintain vigilance
The position of the Nigerian government is that the Boko Haram terrorism has been degraded and defeated The real Boko Haram we know is defeated Shehu Buharis spokesman said in  again following a wave of significant Boko Haram attacks
In contrast to statements from Abuja the governor of Ekiti state another region besieged by Boko Haram admitted last week the government was overwhelmed by the jihadist group it had defeated five years ago
The reality we can all say and I personally as security scholar the reality I can see is that our military is overwhelmed Our military is no longer in a position to singlehandedly tackle this menace effectively Gov Kayode Fayemi said

years as security forces combed a vast forest on Wednesday for armed captors possibly from the jihadist Boko Haram movement According to an unverified audio clip the Islamist group  whose name means Western education is forbidden  was responsible for last weeks raid on an allboys school in the town of Kankara in northwestern Katsina state Parents fear time may be running out Boko Haram has a history of turning captives into jihadist fighters They will radicalise our children if the government does not act fast to help us rescue them said trader Shuaibu Kankara crying as he spoke from home His yearold son Annas was among those abducted from the Government Science school on Friday night Two other sons managed to escape he added when men on motorbikes with AK assault rifles stormed the school and marched the boys into a forest Though the military said it had them roughly located some experts feared the boys could be taken over the porous border with Niger about an hours drive north or at least split into small groups to make finding them harder Boko Haram and its offshoot Islamic State West Africa Province have waged a decadelong insurgency estimated to have displaced about  million people and killed more than  They want to create states based on their extreme interpretation of sharia Islamic law If Boko Haram carried out the kidnapping in an area where it had not previously claimed attacks that would mark an alarming expansion beyond its northeastern base security experts say But it may alternatively have purchased the boys from criminal gangs in the northwest with whom it has been building ties CHIBOK GIRLS REMEMBERED Nigerian soldiers and intelligence officers were combing the Rugu forest on Friday in search of the roughly  missing schoolboys Abdu Labaran an aide to Katsinas state governor told Reuters Planes have also been deployed One of the largest forests in Nigeria Rugu straddles three states and includes woodland near the school Labaran said earlier in the week that a bandit had called a parent demanding a ransom and an end to helicopter flyovers The mass abduction echoes Boko Harams  kidnapping of more than  girls from a school in the northeastern town of Chibok The attack stunned Nigerians and gave rise to a global BringBackOurGirls campaign Six years on only about half the schoolgirls have been found or freed Others were married off to fighters while some are assumed to be dead We pray its not going to be another situation of the Chibok girls abduction said Ahmed Bakori a farmer whose yearold son Abubakar was among those taken About two dozen parents came to the Government Science compound on Wednesday and prayed in the school mosque The compound comprised of white singlestorey buildings built on dusty red soil was quiet Abubakar Lawal who has two children among the captives said he did not believe Boko Harams claim and would wait with patience and prayers The government has to do diplomacy in a way to rescue these people he said outside the school building The attack is awkward for President Muhammadu Buhari who comes from Katsina and arrived on a private visit hours before the kidnapping occurred Buhari has repeatedly said that Boko Haram has been technically defeated A retired general and former military ruler Buhari was elected to office in  in large part due to his pledge to crush the insurgency Under his predecessor Goodluck Jonathan Boko Haram grew in strength and controlled a large tract of territory in northeast Nigeria around the size of Belgium Around the nation anger and anxiety were building over the abductions with BringBackOurBoys trending on Twitter Armed forces spokesman John Enenche said on Wednesday that troops were determined to rescue the boys alive and had no evidence any were dead He gave new details of the school attack and subsequent firefight with guards Soldiers arrived but could only shoot in the air as the assailants used the boys as shields It is the characteristics of terrorists he said Reporting by Afolabi Sotunde in Kankara Additonal reporting by Garba Muhammad in Kaduna Ardo Hazzad in Bauchi Alexis Akwagyiram in Lagos Camillus Eboh in Abuja are doing their best to limit IS activity with Russian support through intense airstrikes According to SOHR since the Syrian Democratic Forces SDF announced their control of Baghouz village IS last stronghold on March   the human losses amounted to  deaths from the regime forces and the militants loyal to it of both Syrian and nonSyrian nationalities two of whom were Russians in addition to  deaths from nonSyrian proIranian militias all of whom were killed during IS attacks bombings and ambushes in the west of the Euphrates the desert of Deir ezZor Raqqa Homs and Suwayda The report also mentioned  deaths in IS ranks during the same period Khalil alMuqdad a researcher on jihadist groups affairs currently residing in Qatar told AlMonitor After  losing its last stronghold  in Baghouz IS changed its strategy and reorganized its ranks relying instead on ambushes and guerrilla warfare to eliminate its opponents The group quickly started activating its cells and members that have redeployed in several areas It targeted members and headquarters of the SDF which led the campaign against IS with air and logistical support from the USled international coalition The group seems keen on pursuing this process and accelerating its pace by targeting regime convoys and Iranian militias as well as allied militias such as Liwa alQuds Jerusalem Brigade and the National Defense Forces It managed to inflict heavy losses in their ranks then moved to attack detachments fixed barracks and guard posts especially in the vicinity of oil fields  This escalation coincided with an increase in the pace  of operations in Iraq as well as the group there also activated its guerrilla strategy Muqdad noted that IS guerrilla strategy was the most prominent factor that allowed it to choose its targets accurately and attack them in a destructive and deadly manner He said that the group would hit the regime convoys before their arrival which incurred great losses and confused the regimes offensive plans as it deprived it of the advantage of regrouping and repositioning IS then moved to the strategy of attacking convoys of oil tanks burning and destroying dozens of them and even killing the drivers There is no doubt that the groups reliance on the strategy of ambushes and the element of surprise were two important factors in giving it an advantage especially in a vast and sprawling area The regime and Iranian militias convoys travel long distances which enable IS to monitor them and allow it to choose the best way to target them IS laid minefields that caused the regime and Iranian militias heavy losses and even led to the death of a prominent Russian general  Such ambushes are carried out by small groups that know the terrain of the area well and cannot be detected even by drones Muqdad added He believes that IS took advantage of the US election crisis which coincided with the speech of the groups spokesman Abu Hamza alQurashi on Oct  in which he called on IS cells to accelerate the pace of operations The cells immediately responded and we started hearing about operations stretching from Deir ezZor in the east to the countryside of Aleppo in the north to the vicinity of Salamiyah in the eastern countryside of Hama in western Syria as well as the countryside of Homs and Palmyra Speaking about IS expected operations in the coming days Muqdad said I think that IS will try to find a foothold and strengthen its presence near Damascus and even on the border with Lebanon especially in Wadi Barada The group has effectively controlled the main roads that connect eastern and northern Syria with its west which allows it the freedom to move in small groups with light and medium weapons and set up ambushes and seize weapons from its enemy IS operations are not only limited to what it claims responsibility for they vary between direct attacks laying mines and ambushes and intercepting convoys  not to mention directly eliminating opponents Hamam Issa a media activist in Idlib following up on IS operations told AlMonitor IS is highly active in Palmyra and alSukhnah desert in the eastern countryside of Homs in addition to the AthriaKhanasser area near the eastern Hama countryside and the eastern Deir ezZor countryside which are vast areas in the desert that no party has been able to fully control The Syrian desert is not a flat sandy land as some people imagine it to be it has many hills valleys and rugged areas that provide protection and camouflage for those holed up in it Issa added After the Syrian regime forces failed to sweep the desert and expel IS and because of the great losses they endured in addition to fighting the opposition in Idlib the regime had to deploy the Iranbacked Baqir Brigade as well as By Nan Lwin Hnin Pwint  December  
Yangon  The Arakan Army AA released an ethnic Chin man on Monday after detaining him for more than four months in Paletwa in southern Chin State
Salai Aung Soe had been missing since July  and the Rakhine ethnic armed group has repeatedly denied allegations of his arrest
On Dec  the armed group told his family in Paletwa to collect him
I could not relax until I arrived back in Paletwa Anything could happen on the way home But I have really arrived back in Paletwa now It is not a dream said Salai Aung Soe
He was released on Monday and arrived in Paletwa on Tuesday after walking through the forest
I was held in their cell for all four months In the first eight days I was shackled They accused me of working for media agencies and having ties to Myanmars Tatmadaw military I denied the allegations said Salai Aung Soe
The AA seized him along with three other Chin men Salai Benjamin Salai Khin Maung Tun and Salai Aung Tun on July  on their return from Rakhine States Kyauktaw to Paletwa
AA troops arrived by motorboat near Nga Tha Yine village in Paletwa and the four were taken away blindfolded
The three others were freed on Aug  Though the three stated that Salai Aung Soe was still under detention the AA denied it
Salai Aung Soe said it is unacceptable to detain someone for more than four months without strong evidence He asked the armed group not to kidnap other Chin civilians
Mai Nan Wai spokeswoman for the Khumi Affairs Coordination Council which demanded Salai Aung Soes release said she views the armed groups continuous denials over his kidnapping to be disrespectful to the Chin community
As an ethnic Chin I support the cause of establishing an Arakan state This is their right We accept it But in so doing they seize people of other ethnic groups who coexist with them and that they dont even admit is disrespectful to us If they keep on it will create conflict between the two ethnic groups she said
Since clashes erupted between the military and AA in November  until October this year  Chin men have gone missing Some of them were detained by the AA at their homes according to their relatives The AA dismissed the allegations
Myanmars government declared the AA a terrorist organization on March 
Tensions have eased since the Nov  general election
Japans special peace envoy Yohei Sasakawa mediated in two rounds of talks between the military and AA first online and then in person to sign a ceasefire agreement

security experts say Following are details about Boko Haram BOKO HARAMS ORIGINS The groups name means Western education is forbidden in the Hausa language spoken across northern Nigeria Its original members were followers of militant preacher Mohammed Yusuf who was based in the northeastern state of Borno and wanted a wider adoption of Islamic sharia law across Africas most populous nation He died in police custody in  The following year his deputy Abubakar Shekau said in a video he was the groups new leader TACTICS Under Shekaus leadership Boko Haram has carried out suicide bombings in churches and markets and abducted thousands of people in northeastern Nigeria In  Boko Haram began overrunning northeastern towns to try to create an Islamic state adhering to sharia law By early  Boko Haram controlled a swathe of land around the size of Belgium near Lake Chad before being driven from most of it by troops from Nigeria Chad Cameroon and Niger Bomb attacks looting and shootings in villages and cities continued More than  people have been killed and  million displaced from their homes since the insurgency began in  according to the United Nations refugee agency and the New Yorkbased Council on Foreign Relations CFR think tank KIDNAPPING Boko Haram kidnapped more than  girls from a school in the northeastern town of Chibok in April  an attack that sparked outrage and gave rise to a global BringBackOurGirls campaign About half the girls have since been found or freed but many never returned home and some are thought to have died in captivity Boko Haram has kidnapped thousands of other people to raise ransom money and recruits and provide wives for its fighters regional security experts say SPLIT Shekau pledged allegiance to global jihadist group Islamic State in  But the following year it named another figure Abu Musab alBarnawi as its leader in West Africa Shekau rejected the move and the groups split in  The regional security analysts say the split was over Shekaus refusal to adhere to Islamic States instructions to target the Nigerian military rather than civilians AREAS OF OPERATION Boko Harams roots are in northeastern Nigeria but it has Accessing Information Sources in Niger Conflict Zones Journalists Share Experiences Of the eight regions in Niger four namely Tillabery Tahoua Diffa and Maradi are affected by insecurity linked to attacks by terrorist groups in Niger since the invasion by armed groups from northern Mali Working as a journalist in this context is a real challenge as mobility and access to information are restricted due to the security measures taken by the government The state of emergency that was declared as part of efforts to tackle the security crisis gives special powers to the security forces in their zones of operations Notable among them is the power to order house searches or decide on the movement of the population in the affected areas The enforcement of these special powers militates against the research collection processing and dissemination of information especially since the populations are reluctant to express themselves on the security issue out of fear The fear of offending the defense and security forces and on the other hand of becoming the target of armed groups who carry out targeted attacks against populations who denounce them Quest for information in the context of insecurity According to Ismael Saloua an expert on security and media issues  journalists must have credible local sources in dangerous areas which they cannot access for security reasons to give them information Still according to Saloua the journalist must have a contact list in the affected regions which can provide him with information if necessary When the journalist decides to go out into the field he or she must do so under protection or adopt some basic security skills For Lawan Boukar correspondent for DW in Niger collecting and processing information in a security crisis situation is very complex Journalists are faced with problems accessing sources of information The defense and security forces do not give information Often we have to resort to local sources that is to say information that comes to us from the populations Boukar stressed Difficulty verifying information Another difficulty often encountered by journalists working in conflict zones is the confirmation of certain information After the attacks the local assessment can sometimes be different from that given by official sources I can cite as an example an attack carried out by Boko Haram in  in Bosso which resulted in a hundred terrorists being killed and injuries on the side of the defense and security forces according to local sources The official statement from the authorities however reported  terrorists killed recalled journalist L Boukar In  after the attack on Karamga Island an attack that claimed many lives in the national army it took more than  hours for the government to establish the death toll Meanwhile  hours after the attack we had the toll from local sources  he added What does it take to report in conflict zones Journalists deployed in these areas are sometimes tagged as accomplices of the security forces and sometimes as conspiring with armed terrorist groups You have to be very seasoned and have a lot of patience to work as a journalist in insecure areas In conflict zones you should never move or be transported by the Defense and Security Forces in search of information always use private vehicles to travel outside the villages It is a way of having the confidence of the people advises Boukar the correspondent of the Kalangou studio He adds that one must use anonymity during interviews in order to reassure those being interviewed especially when one knows that even the population is not immune from the abuses of Boko Haram and other terrorists In addition to this journalists working on insecurity issues related to terrorist attacks face several cases of denial of information from some authorities False Information Journalists and security forces collaboration In Niger despite the difficulties in accessing information sources the authorities in charge of the defense ministry have shown their readiness to work with all the actors to facilitate the work of the media Several meetings brought together security forces civil society and the media to facilitate communication in times of crisis These initiatives were aimed at finding a suitable mechanism that could lessen the persistence of attitudes of mistrust Journalists and the media are seen in this context as active and strategic players Niger and the West African subregion have been facing multiple security challenges for several years In this context the media are strategic players and their role is decisive in handling security information noted Ibrahim Harouna Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Maison de la Presse However in the face of a multifaceted security crisis several obstacles hinder collaboration between the Defense and Security Forces FDS and media actors The persistence of attitudes of mistrust between the SDF and media players calls for a reflexion on how to collaborate in order to benefit from the interface and complementarity of the two institutions so that the population can be informed with professionalism and responsibility on issues of security and defense noted Abdoulrazack Idrissa president of the Association of Journalists for Security and Migration To this end the association recognises the facilitation of exchanges between the Defense and Security Forces FDS and media actors as key to finding means of collaboration For Abdoulrazack Idrissa who cites the results of a recent survey notable among the factors that make this collaboration difficult is the mutual ignorance of the roles and responsibilities of the actors and the low level of understanding of the factors of insecurity that have become very complex and varied However the two players now more than before have common issues that they must resolve together fakesnews and information on social networks Conclusion and recommendations The Defense Forces are very wary of journalists and the media who for them are in a rush for information and indulge in sensationalism just for the scoop For the security forces these attitudes are especially detrimental to the efforts of defense and security actors and do not always correspond to their principles and operating rules Here are some recommendations To journalists and the media Prioritize security measures in reporting on conflicts Make sure you are clearly identified by the security forces when reporting to have the protection of the security forces Deal professionally with the victims of terrorist attacks while preserving the sensitivity of the public and the victims To the authorities and security forces Facilitate access to information through the media to get the population informed and enabled to contribute to security efforts Involve the media in briefings on security measures and public awareness Set up psychological support units for conflict reporters To development partners Continue to support journalists and the media on journalistic capacity building on issues of security and asymmetric conflicts Support media organizations in the collection processing and dissemination of information
