ISIS steps up Sinai fight with bombs in civilian homes in Egypt CAIRO AFP  Residents of Egypts restive North Sinai region ran for their lives when an Islamic State group affiliate occupied their villages Now they are returning to find their homes boobytrapped I lost my sisterinlaw and her ninemonthold baby when an explosive device planted in their home went off said a young resident of Aqtiya village who asked not to be named for fear of repercussions Around  people have been killed by improvised explosive devices IEDs since midOctober in villages around Bir alAbd in the northwest of the troubled province say Egyptian security sources The IED attacks that have multiplied in the vast remote and sparsely populated region which authorities have declared offlimits to journalists recall those the ISIS launched to sow terror in Iraq and Syria The recent deaths have badly shaken the  or so residents who returned in October after seeking refuge elsewhere in Egypt for three months as the army continued its grinding battle to crush ISIS Another resident speaking to AFP by phone said locals found ISIS had taken over their homes used them as hideouts and then boobytrapped them They even stole our livestock he added Egyptian security forces have been battling a longrunning Islamist insurgency in the Sinai Peninsula spearheaded by a local ISIS affiliate The fighting intensified after the militarys  ouster of Islamist president Mohamed Morsi In February  security forces launched a nationwide operation against militants focused on the sparsely populated North Sinai The Egyptian army said Tuesday that since September it had killed  suspected jihadist militants in air and ground operations in the Sinai region and that seven of its own personnel had been either wounded or killed In a slickly produced video set to rousing military music the army showed panning shots of its troops tanks and air strikes along with blurred bloody pictures of what it said were dead militants Reflecting the militants significant fire power the army said it had also destroyed  weapons caches defused  improvised explosive devices and confiscated dozens of other types of weapons Rigging childrens toys The coastal town of Bir alAbd lies on the edge of the barren desert In  it saw modern Egypts deadliest attack when  worshippers were killed in a gun and bomb assault at the Rawda mosque during Friday prayers The attack was carried out by armed men carrying flags similar to those of ISIS although the jihadist group never formally claimed the attack In recent months attacks have spiked The US State Department estimates that ISIS conducted  IED attacks last year centred on north and central Sinai along with nearweekly complex assaults on governmentfortified positions The booby traps in north Sinai directly follow the precedent set by ISIS operations in Iraq and Syria said Nadia alDayel a Washingtonbased ISIS expert and head of Critica a think tank She said the militants have honed their techniques investing considerable time and resources rigging doors household furniture appliances and even childrens toys Such tactics mirror those found in Syria and northern Iraq where three years ago retreating and encircled ISIS militants would rig explosives to fridges toys and even copies of the Koran Civilians in northern Iraq told AFP last year that they were still afraid of returning to their homes because of the bombs planted in unsuspecting places It is likely that the tactic of targeting civilian life will not only continue but will be taken up by other violent groups warned Dayel regarding ISIS in Sinai Not going away Human Rights Watch last year accused both Egyptian security forces and insurgents of committing war crimes in North Sinai a report rejected by Egyptian authorities Some  suspected militants and dozens of security personnel have been killed in North Sinai since February  according to official figures No independently verified death toll is available and the region is largely cut off to journalists Residents told AFP the main threat remained ISIS and its indiscriminate attacks Neither Egypts military spokesperson nor North Sinais governor responded to requests for comments on IEDs killing residents But the civilian death toll has continued to rise with locals caught between the army operations and a hardening insurgency One resident who also declined to be identified told AFP that the governors office had provided schools as shelters for those displaced after ISIS razed five villages around Bir alAbd That offensive followed a deadly counterterrorism operation in July Dayel said that even though the militant group had been largely crushed in Iraq and Syria North Sinai provided a fertile ground for its expansion Even with limited resources ISIS has proven to be a constant threat in Sinai she said They are not going away anytime soon

Pakistan Dec   Earlier this year the Doha accord signed between US and Taliban in an effort to bid farewell to the year old war bounds Taliban to disassociate from AlQaeda on every forum a condition the Taliban has committed to fulfill More precisely the agreement demands that the Afghani soil will not be used as a breeding ground for terrorists against US and its western alliesIn the last few years attacks by AlQaeda on the western targets have significantly diminished Many policy makers and practitioners hold that regardless of their commitment to US Taliban are still very actively associated with AlQaedaBut the question is Are Taliban in touch with the version of AlQaeda that carried out deadly attacks in the west and also how much say does AlQaeda have in Talibans policy and decision makingAlQaeda while still holding some power have in the recent decade reduced more to the ranks of insurgents that participates alongside the people against weaker governments eg Yemen than a hardcore terrorist organization Afghani Taliban in Doha on the other hand seem to limit their influence only to AfghanistanMr Edmund Fitton brown coordinator of UNs Islamic state AlQaeda and Taliban monitory team told BBC that he had noted some reports that Taliban required some foreign fighters for Afghanistan to register with them and adhere to a code of conduct forbidding attacks outside Afghanistan He said it wasnt yet clear whether the same conditions applied to AlQaedaAlQaeda leaders pledge allegiance to Taliban commanders and when asked how could Taliban carry crackdown on a group that pledges loyalty to its leaders the Taliban official told BBC that they have not formally accepted the oath and the pledge of allegiance remains invalid if AlQaeda disobeyed Talibans orders to refrain from plotting attacks abroadAt present Taliban have availabletofight force of between  people contesting  percent of Afghan territory with full control over  districts An additional force of a few hundred that AlQaeda has to offer wouldnt make a significant difference anywayAlQaeda is more of a rugged liability than a durable partner TalibanAl Qaeda partnership has survived BinLadens death and two Emirs of Taliban But that doesnt necessarily indicate deeper personal relationship at the top level The thread that has bound them has been more at a foundational level than an ideological one The current relationship between the two resonates with the one in s when Taliban were in power and frustrated with Bin Ladens blatant attacks shifted him to Kandahar to keep him under observation In  Mullah Omer the Emir of Taliban went as far as to promise chief of Saudi intelligence that the Taliban will not shelter Bin Laden after he had threatened the Saudi Royal family However after US air strikes on AlQaeda they got Talibans support again But circumstances have dramatically shifted ever since Back then both the parties had a common enemy The United States But now as the agreement states after the US withdraw its troops from Afghanistan they will not interfere with the internal affairs of the countryBut that doesnt mean Taliban can or will disassociate from AlQaeda so easily If Taliban cut ties with AlQaeda abruptly it will have a domino effect Young lot from the Taliban that operates in far off lands of Afghanistan and usually out of touch with the top leadership can come out of Talibans influence and further their support to AlQaeda that they share their beliefs with on foundational level Many people within Taliban show resentment towards USTaliban deal Also many of these members can also join Talibans rivals as ISKP as happened in the pastPossibility of coordination between the two groups cannot be ruled out altogether Under extraordinary circumstances both the parties may collide under different framework A former Taliban governor Abdus Salam Hanafi who left the group back in  but remains in contact with the senior leadership alleges that AlQaeda trained Taliban for the talks The group may not cut ties abruptly when it comes to Afghanistan but the possibility of AlQaeda being a ferocious threat to the west has decreased over the yearsNaila Mahsud is a The factional Boko Haram will most likely ask for ransom or prisoner swap to release the hundreds of schoolboys abducted in a school in Katsina State credible sources and security experts told the Daily Trust on Tuesday
In an audio message a man who claimed to be Abubakar Shekau the leader of the factional group claimed that they were responsible for the abduction of over  students at Government Science Secondary School Kankara Katsina State on Friday
The man said a total of  students were taken away Governor Aminu Bello Masari had said that  were still missing The school register seen by our reporter had shown that  students were missing but some of the students have resurfaced in the last two days
Based on their findings security experts and those with knowledge of Boko Haram operations confirmed that the abduction was carried out by the Boko Haram loyal to Abubakar Shekau
They however expressed doubts as to whether the man in the audio was Shekau considering the manner he spoke the way he called himself Abubakar Shekau instead Abu Muhammad  Asshakawi the way he normally addresses himself in most of his messages both audio and video
One of the experts also wondered why the man slipped in pronouncing the name of the group Jamatu AhlisSunnah Liddaawati Wal Jihad
He said But setting the inconsistencies aside the message is clear that Boko Haram is responsible for the mass abduction
Of course we have been saying it for a long time that the terrorists have infiltrated the North West and North CentralA lot of atrocities being committed could be attributed to them but the message they sent yesterday has put everything to rest the source a retired military officer said
Daily Trust reports that after the group was checkmated by the intelligence community and fighting forces between  and  two factions of the Boko Haram Shekau and ISWAP restricted their activities mostly along the shores of the Lake Chad parts of Borno South Yobe and Adamawa states
The Kankara incident is therefore the biggest and visible onslaught by the group of recent outside their enclave
In the audio message the man behind the microphone said the attack was carried out to promote Islam and discourage unIslamic practices
According to him What happened in Katsina was done to promote Islam and discourage unIslamic practices as western education is not the type of education permitted by Allah and his Holy Prophet
They are also not teaching what Allah and his Holy Prophet commanded They are rather destroying Islam he said
Boko Haram will soon roll out conditions
Security expert Salihu Bakhari said on Tuesday that the Shekau faction will soon give their conditions for the release of the Kankara schoolboys
According to him They Boko Haram dont have the luxury of time to keep the boys for long I learnt that they are keeping the boys in clusters around Zamfara Katsina and Kaduna for now but the federal government must act very fast to avert the Chibok saga
I can confidently tell you that the location of the abduction is not favourable for Boko HaramIt is extremely far from the North East and therefore free movement with such a huge number of people might be problematic for them in the coming days
I have the conviction that they would soon ask the government to pay a ransom on each of the boys to be released and they may release them in batches In the alternative they would ask the federal government to release some of their high profile members being kept in various prisons across the country
These boys are highly treasured captives just like the Chibok girls  After the  episode the government used different options including payment of ransom and prisoner swap to get back some of the Chibok girls he said
Another source said the government should not use force It will be a disaster if they deploy force to release the boys because the Boko Haram can do anything I think the advantage at the disposal of government is the location of the abduction
But if they give space in terms of gathering intelligence the terrorist would find their way to Sambisa Forest or Alagarno Forest in Yobe And once they achieve this they would start conscription the children God forbid he said
Parents wait to hear news about their abducted children outside the Government Science in Kankara Katsina State yesterday where gunmen abducted students of the school on Friday night
No word from FG army
The Presidency on Tuesday kept mum over the claim by the Boko Haram group that it was responsible for the kidnap of schoolboys in Katsina State
The Senior Special Adviser to the President on Media and Publicity Garba Shehu didnt reply to inquiries sent to him by our correspondent over the matter as of the time of filing this report
The Defence headquarters and the Nigerian Army have also kept mum over the claim
Several calls to the mobile phone of the Coordinator Defence Media Operations Maj Gen John Enenche were not picked neither did he respond to a text message sent by our correspondent The Nigerian Army spokesman Brig Gen Sagir Musa did not also pick his calls
A former DirectorGeneral of the Department of State Services DSS Mike Ejiofor in a telephone interview with one of our correspondents noted that the public proclamation by Governor Aminu Bello Masari was not necessary
Soldiers comb the surroundings of the school yesterday
I dont even know why the government would come out openly to say they are in talks or they are negotiating with bandits Ejiofor said

Srinagar Dec   Militancy in Jammu and Kashmir has entered a crucial transitional phase In the last five years it kept surging its lethality increasing year after yearin terms of recruitment infiltration and violent attacks The year  marked a remarkable shift in the trends of militancy indicating a downgrading in lethality despite high recruitmentThe recruitment numbers for the year  do not show a big change compared to last year As per news reports the number of local recruits for this year till October end stood at the second highest in a decade The spate of recruitment suggests that the counteroffensive of security forces is proving to be a zerosum game as for every militant killed a new one is being recruited or infiltratedHowever there is another data point which depicts a significant downgrade in militant operations Data suggests that militants in Kashmir are witnessing a dearth of weaponry and logistics which is severely denting their capacity to carry out big lethal attacksData accessed by ORF shows that  countermilitancy operations were conducted by the security forces till October end Out of  weapons recovered  were pistol or handguns and  were various types of assault riflesAK AK M Insas etc Many operations in which militants were killedarrestedsurrender had no major weapon recoveryRecovery of ammunitions showed that the militants possessing pistols carried on an average  rounds for each weapon In the case of assault rifles an average of  rounds per weapon was recorded A pistol is primarily a selfdefence weapon and can only be used to carry out targeted assassinations at pointblank rangeThe above data clearly shows that the pistolwielding members posed a lesser threat as they are not capable of carrying out big attacks against the military establishment This also explains why there werent any major militant attacks in the year  barring a few The nature of attacks carried out in  were mostly targeted killings of civilians and standoff attacks on cornered solders Data shows that this year only one improvised explosive device or IED was recovered compared to the  recovered last yearThe critical metric to judge the state of militancy is not the disruption in supply of weapons but the surge in demand for weapons In other words the continuous flow of recruits suggests that the demand for weapons is much more than it has been in the last few years Perhaps the weapon supply chain has primarily been interrupted by shutting down of the crossLoC trade and crackdown on the overground networks of the militant outfits In the past trucks involved in cross LoC trade have been caught by the security forces carrying weapons into the Indian side of the LoC In April  India shut down cross LoC trade after investigative agencies found out the route was used for smugglings weapons drugs and fake currencyIt is an open secret that militants also procured weapons through trade with rogue members of security forces DySP Davinder Singh currently being investigated by the NIA brought this reality into the public glare when a former sarpanch was arrested for supplying arms to Hizbul Mujahideen The arrest of DySP Davinder Singh and subsequent investigation has perhaps acted as a deterrent against this network and created further problems in the procurement of weaponryOfficials of the Indian Army and JK Police have publicly stated that the militants in Kashmir were facing a shortage of weapons This deficit in weaponry has provoked desperate attempts by Pakistan to find new routes and modes of weapon delivery to militants in KashmirOn June  Border Security Forces BSF shot down a Chinamade drone carrying arms and explosives that had crossed the international border from the Pakistani side near Kathua district of Jammu and Kashmir The hexacopter was carrying an M Carbine rifle and seven grenades Similarly on September  two AK  rifles  two pistols and four grenades were recovered from three arrested militants who claimed that arms and ammunition were received via drones The incidents of weapon drops through drones has not been limited to Jammu and Kashmir Reports of drone drops have taken place in Punjab as well along the international border between India and Pakistan It is possible that weapons dropped in Punjab are then transported up north to Jammu and KashmirThese incidents of airdrops of weapons have added a new dimension to militancy in Kashmir Most importantly they are an indicator of the evolution of militant groups in Kashmir The shortage of weapons is affecting the traditional militant outfits like Hizbul Mujahideen HM more than the newly created ones like The Resistance Front TRF and Peoples AntiFascist Front PAPF The new recruits in HM and LeT have to make do with the handguns thereby limiting their activitiesAfter statements by Indian Army officials regarding the shortage of weapons faced by militants TRF sought to counter the claims of security forces by issuing a propaganda video on social media In the video which appears to have been hurriedly recorded in a residential house a militant of TRF is seen counting eight assault rifles of AK  model seven pistols and some hand grenades put on display against a wall The video put out a statement which read there is no scarcity of weaponsEven as Kashmir witnessed a less lethal and downgraded militancy in the year  the trends suggest trouble is far from over The rising recruitment in militant ranks remains a point of concern and all efforts by security forces to stop new recruits from joining militant groups have had no positive outcome This will remain a cause for worry in the coming months too The incidents of airdrops suggest that militant outfits and their managers are utilising new methods and tactics to keep the pot boiling Perhaps these shifting tactics by militant outfits are just a part of a bigger plan which is yet to come in motion They may even be planning to launch a big assault in the future much like the wave of militancy that emerged after the killing of Burhan Wani in Khalid Shah is an Associate Fellow at Observer Research Foundation ORF Khalid was previously associated with leading news channels of India and did a brief stint as a Correspondent in Srinagar with WION News reporting extensively on conflict in Kashmir The article first appeared on the Observer Research On Tuesday Boko Haram which had kidnapped hundreds of schoolgirls in the countrys Chibok region in  claimed responsibility
The majority of the kidnapped students are in the Zamfara forest in the neighbouring province Efforts are under way to save them he said
Katsina states police spokesman Gambo Isah said a security guard was injured during the operation and additional security forces would be dispatched to the area for search and rescue operations

Boy who survived the abduction
For Umar Ahmed the nightmare began in confusion Gunmen arrived late on Friday at his school just as he and his classmates were about to go to bed
Their first thought was that the men were vigilantes  civilians who take on a policing role  so we were not scared the yearold told AFP
But then he says heavy firing started We became terrified Some of us ran to the perimeter fence trying to escape while others hid inside
They kept shouting we should come back that they were in the school to rescue us And most of us came back he added
Lanky and softspoken Ahmad explained how the students were rounded up under a tree split into three groups and led through the forest
We had no footwear he said his feet swathed in black socks after they became riddled with thorns
The teenager said the group trekked for hours heading towards neighbouring Zamfara state They flogged us with tree branches and the flat side of their machetes he said
But then came a stroke of luck
He and a friend were able to hide behind a bush They waited for complete silence to prevail before they retraced their steps back home to safety

The kidnapping of several hundred college students last Friday in Katsina state was therefore claimed on Tuesday December  by Boko Haram 
  In a fourminute audio message received by the Daily Sun yesterday the same newspaper points out  the insurgents claimed that they had carried out this kidnapping for Allah and for Islam   
Indeed specifies Le Monde Afrique    for the Nigerian jihadist Abubakar Shekau the leader of one of the Boko Haram factions attending public school is worse than a crime Its a sin Abubakar Shekau considers any student as a disbeliever to whom he promises suffering death by bullets or by slitting  President Muhammadu Buhari denounced cowardly bandits and UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres strongly condemned this attack calling for the immediate and unconditional release of the children Schoolchildren were able to escape but to date more than  remain missing according to the Nigerian authorities who are continuing their research This is the first time still specifyLe Monde Afrique which Shekau claims to have orchestrated a largescale operation in this part of northern Nigeria The state of Katsina is far from its traditional stronghold of Borno in the NorthEast where was born this Salafist sect which became on the death of its founder Mohamed Yusuf shot dead by the police in  an armed jihadist group among the deadliest on the planet   
Boko Haram is recovering
For Le Pays au Burkina this kidnapping of high school students is   a real snub to President Buhari    Because the kidnapping occurred   at the very moment when the latter was taking it easy in this state of Katsina his native region President Buhari would benefit from having these high school students released as quickly as possible continues the Burkinab daily  before some are brainwashed and end up being used as suicide bombers  This sting of reminder of the filthy beast reflects the urgency to better secure high schools and other education centers  It is true Le Pays reminds us  that the combined action with neighboring countries such as Idriss Deby Itnos Chad and Paul Biyas Cameroon has contributed to considerably reducing the wings of this vermin But everything suggests that Boko Haram has recovered Because despite the dissent within it this Islamist movement still has a great capacity for nuisance In any case concludes the Ouagadougou daily  it is an understatement to say that it gives the Nigerian and Nigerian armies a hard time Because we are witnessing an incessant pingpong between helplessness and fierce battles  
Ivory Coast KKB the reconciler
Also on the front page Cte dIvoire with the appointment by President Ouattara of a Minister of National Reconciliation   Kouadio Konan Bertin Minister of National Reconciliation for relentless challenges exclaims LIntelligent  Abidjan on the front page The task will indeed be tough for KKB as he is nicknamed a PDCI dissident  
  Its roadmap remains to be specified points out  Jeune Afrique  Will KKB be associated with the relaunch of negotiations with the opposition the leadership of which has been entrusted to the Prime Minister Hamed Bakayoko   Jeune Afrique  recalls that  Kouadio Konan Bertin was the only one to campaign against the outgoing president during the presidential election refusing the call for a boycott of the ballot and civil disobedience launched by Bdi of the PDCI and Affi N  Guessan of the FPI A position which had provoked the ire of the opposition and which had earned the former member of PortBout to be temporarily excluded from the PDCI his party of origin   
Reward 
And finally points Today in Ouagadougou   by agreeing to row against the tide of the opposition from which he came Kouadio Konan Bertin has rendered service to Alassane Ouattara who would have found himself as a lone rider on his way to a mandate illegitimate and controversial It is therefore a mark of recognition that has just been given to KKB But what is akin to a reward is at the same time a heavy load on his shoulders still falls today In the coming days the brand new Minister in charge of National Reconciliation will therefore be tasked with bringing the protagonists back to the dialogue table a real challenge after the waves of violence that have marked the electoral process

A blast was reported in the interim Yemeni capital Aden early on  December amid an operation to redeploy government and UAEbacked separatist Southern Transitional Council STC forces as part of a peace agreement between the two sides
An explosive device detonated as a vehicle belonging to the commander of the Facilities Protection Force FPF drove by a security source told privatelyowned AlMasdar Online news website
According to the source the blast occurred as BrigGen Ahmed bin Afifs vehicle was heading to the forces Sawlaban military base in the Khormakser district east of Aden It added that none of the soldiers on board were injured
The FPF is tasked with guarding government offices and hospitals and is affiliated with the UAEbacked Security Belt forces AlMasdar said But said the report it has been engaged with disputes with the Security Belt and other security forces in Aden after it refused to hand over the airport and port earlier this year
The Security Belt is loyal to the STC which seized control of Aden amid deadly clashes with the government forces in the summer of 
A Saudi military committee has been overseeing the redeployment of STC and government forces in Aden and neighbouring Abyan over the past few days in line with the military terms of an agreement brokered by Riyadh over a year ago
The operation aims at paving the way for the announcement of a new powersharing government made up of representatives from the countrys north and south

The power struggle between the government and the STC has opened up a new front in the Yemen conflict which escalated in March  with the launch of a military campaign led by Saudi Arabia backing the government against the Houthi rebel movement

Stories being covered today by BBC Monitoring from African broadcast press and social media sources
Boko Haram says holding  Nigerian schoolboys
The Nigerian militant group Boko Haram has claimed that it is holding  students abducted from a school in the northwestern Katsina State on  December
The incident has evoked memories of an April  attack in which Boko Haram abducted  girls from a government secondary school in Chibok northeastern Borno State
Reacting to the lack of clarity concerning the number of schoolboys abducted from a Katsina secondary school last Friday Boko Haram has disclosed that it currently has  children in captivity HumAngle website which is associated with prominent journalist Ahmad Salkida reported yesterday
Salkida has gained a reputation for frequently publishing exclusive reports on Boko Haram activities in northeastern Nigeria and the greater Lake Chad basin region
Boko Haram said it kidnapped the schoolboys because Western education is against the tenets of Islam The government had earlier blamed bandits for the kidnapping
Nigeria making progress in negotiating release of abducted boys
Katsina State Governor Aminu Masari has said that the authorities are making progress in efforts to free the kidnapped schoolboys He added that the gunmen responsible for the attack had made contact with the government
The authorities have said that they believe the students are being held in a forest in the neighbouring state of Zamfara
The incident has prompted the neighbouring states of Kano and Jigawa to close all schools before the end of the school term Zamfara has closed  schools along its border with Katsina and Kaduna
Niger mourns dozens killed in Boko Haram attack
Niger has declared three days of national mourning for  people killed by militants in the southeastern Diffa Region which borders Nigeria
A government statement said the  December attack targeted the village of Toumour which hosts thousands of Nigerian refugees
Ten of the victims were shot  were burned while four died after drowning said the statement
About  others were injured in the attack claimed by Nigerias Boko Haram jihadist group
Kenya deepens ties with Somaliland amid Somalia spat
Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta and Somaliland President Muse Bihi have agreed to deepen bilateral relations amid a worsening diplomatic spat between Kenya and Somalia
In a joint statement cited by local media Kenya is expected to open a consulate in Hargeisa by March  while Somaliland will upgrade its liaison office in Nairobi to a consulate within the same timeframe
Kenya Airways and other Kenyan airlines are expected to commence direct flights between Nairobi and Hargeisa by next year
Kenyan exPM and African Union special envoy on infrastructure Raila Odinga has challenged the continental bloc to expedite the process of recognising Somaliland as a fully independent state Odinga who met Bihi in Nairobi yesterday said that it is impossible to reunite Somalia and Somaliland
Bihis threevisit to Nairobi upset Somalia which announced on  December that it was severing diplomatic ties with Kenya Somalia cited Kenyas constant violation of its sovereignty and territorial integrity Somalia has since heavily deployed troops along its border with Kenya
Somali police and army clash over opposition protest
Somali media outlets have reported tensions in the capital Mogadishu over antigovernment protests organised by an alliance of opposition parties The opposition is demanding the disbandment of the national electoral commission which it accuses of bias
Security forces were heavily deployed in Mogadishu yesterday while soldiers blocked access routes leading to the presidency privatelyowned Radio Risala reported
Radio Dalsan reported that at least four people were wounded after police clashed with soldiers supporting protesters in Mogadishus Yaqshid District Some reports said that armed antigovernment militia were involved in the clashes
In a related development the opposition has urged Turkey to delay a planned delivery of weapons to the Haramaad unit of the Somali Police Radio Dalsan has reported The opposition claims that the Haramaad forces and the weapons could be used to hijack the upcoming elections
Ethiopian Airlines resumes flights to Tigray capital
The stateowned Ethiopian Airlines has resumed flights to Mekele Mekelle a day after most essential services were restored in the capital of the restive northern Tigray region
An Ethiopian Airlines plane landed at Mekele Alula AbaNega International Airport yesterday with passengers from Addis Ababa the first commercial flight since the federal government launched a military operation in Tigray on  November
The operation culminated in seizure of Mekele from the rebel Tigray Peoples Liberation Front TPLF on  November
Sudan receives Kuwaiti aid for Ethiopian refugees
The Sudanese Red Crescent Society SRCS yesterday received a planeload of relief aid from the Kuwaiti Red Crescent Society KRCS meant for Ethiopian refugees staterun Sudanese news agency Suna reported
The aid consists of  tonnes of foodstuff and nonfoodstuff including food baskets blankets mosquito nets face masks clothes soaps walking canes for the disabled as well as water purification tablets
The UNHCR said on  December that it had registered nearly  Ethiopian refugees who had crossed into eastern Sudan since the fighting erupted between federal troops and rebel forces on  November
Sudan has warned that the influx of Ethiopian refugees has put a huge strain on its resources at a time when it is struggling due to deteriorating economic conditions political instability and recurrent ethnic conflicts
See Explainer Ethiopias Tigray conflict threatens regional stability
Uganda seeks closure of YouTube channels linked to protests
We are watching for reaction to reports that the Uganda Communications Commission UCC has asked Google to close at least  YouTube channels allegedly linked to last months riots that left more than  people dead
The UCC said that it wrote to Google after receiving complaints from stakeholders including the minister of internal affairs who chairs the National Security Council and the Uganda Police Force
In the letter cited by Daily Monitor website UCC wants Google to immediately stop aiding and abetting any further breach of the regulatory and penal laws of Uganda
The  riots broke out in the capital Kampala and other major towns following the arrest of opposition presidential candidate Robert Kyagulanyi popularly known as Bobi Wine
Uganda will hold a general election on  January President Yoweri Museveni who has been in power since  will be seeking reelection

The following is compiled from a selection of reports and headlines in lunchtime bulletins newspapers websites and news agencies on  December
IntraAfghan peace talks
Abdullah Abdullah  chairman of Afghanistans High Council for National Reconciliation HCNR  has said that the governments negotiating teams will resume the talks with the Taliban as scheduled Channel One TV TV reported in their afternoon bulletin today
The next round of peace talks will begin on  January 
Tolo News TV have reported that Abdullah will meet the members of the negotiating team who returned to Kabul last night
Meanwhile several Afghan newspapers have discussed the intraAfghan talks
An editorial in the independent Hashte Sobh said that the most crucial issue to be discussed in the next phase of the talks is the nature of the future system adding that the Taliban should specify what they mean by an Islamic system
The private Maseer daily has criticised the threeweek break in the dialogue saying The first concern is that during this period of halt violence continues as usual Secondly there are some circles who try to create some obstacle and challenges against resumption of the talks The government of Afghanistan has demanded that the second phase of the talks should be held inside Afghanistan although it is a good suggestion it is not practical
Dispute over location of peace talks
The High Council for National Reconciliation has said that the outcome of the peace talks is more important than the location
It is one of the options that the next round of talks should be held inside the country We hope the peace talks go well The result of the peace talks is important for the Afghans HCNR spokesman Fraidun Khwazoon said
Earlier Afghan President Ashraf Ghani had suggested that the next phase of intraAfghan be held in Afghanistan but the Taliban rejected his call
Afghan Foreign Ministrys spokesman Geran Hewad said Holding the next phase of the talks inside Afghanistan will give a chance to the Talibans negotiating team to get acquainted with the reality on the ground the level of violence pain and agony faced by the people of Afghanistan 
But Taliban spokesman Mohammad Naeem said that there are contradictions in the statement of the president as the Afghan government had earlier asked the UN to include members of the Taliban in a blacklist
Meanwhile an editorial in the private Armane Melli discussed the appropriate location of the talks The Taliban and the Afghan government could choose a place in Afghanistan with consensus Even the security measures of the place for the talks could be given to foreign forces or the UN
However Etilaate Roz said in an editorial today that changing the location of the talks from Qatar to Afghanistan is not practical
Taliban delegation in Pakistan
TV has reported that a highranking Taliban delegation from the groups political office in Qatar has travelled to Pakistan
Taliban spokesman Mohammad Naeem said that the delegation has travelled to Islamabad at the invitation of Pakistan where the delegates will meet Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan and Foreign Minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi
He added that the delegation is headed by Mullah Baradar  the groups deputy head for political affairs and leader of its political office
Naeem further said that issues of mutual interest like problems of refugees easing the process of Afghans travel to Pakistan and problems faced by Afghan traders will be discussed during the visit
The Taliban delegations visit to Pakistan comes just a day after US Special Representative for Afghanistan Reconciliation Zalmay Khalilzad visited Islamabad
It has been reported that Khalilzad met Pakistani Army Chief General Javed Qamar Bajwa and discussed the Afghan peace and intraAfghan negotiations with him
Security incidents
Ariana News TV have reported that Uruzgan provinces Dehrawud district may have been captured by the Taliban
The channel reported while citing a security official that commanders of the district police headquarters an army battalion and some other personnel were killed in a Taliban attack
However the Afghan Defence Ministry has said in a statement that the attack was thwarted by the Afghan forces and at least eight Taliban militants were killed adding that the district has not been captured by the militant group
Meanwhile Tolo News reported in their afternoon bulletin today that five policemen were killed and three others were wounded in the Taliban attack in Dehrawud
Moreover Tolo News and Ariana News have reported that  Afghan soldiers were killed in a Taliban attack in Baghlan province after militants targeted a checkpoint in Pole Khumri city
Furthermore a sticky mine explosion in Kabuls Precinct  has wounded two people today Ariana News reported
Source BBC Monitoring in Dari and Pashto  Dec

Report by Michael Fitzpatrick Five suspected radical left activists held by French police on terror charges
Five of the seven people arrested earlier this week by police investigating plans for violent activity by members of the French radical left have been charged with associating with terrorist criminals and detained in custody Two others have been conditionally released
The seven arrested earlier this week in raids in Paris Toulouse and the Dordogne are suspected of planning violent activity No details of the sort of action allegedly planned have been released
The six men and one woman are said to be aged between  and  years
Weapons and material which could be used to produce explosives were discovered at the time of the arrests according to the Internal Security branch DGSI of the French national police
The French AFP news agency reports that one of those arrested identified as Florian D and allegedly the leader of a group of activists is known to have fought alongside Kurdish forces in Rojava northeastern Syria
The rightwing politician Eric Ciotti is sure that all seven are guilty No sooner had they been arrested than Ciotti issued a Twitter message saying these radical left wing terrorists were planning to attack the police They attack the uniform of the Republic because its the only barrier to their hunger for chaos
Attack on HighSpeed Train Service
Before this weeks arrests the last police move against suspected radical left activists was in  in the southern French town of Tarnac
On that occasion several members of the radical left were charged in connection with damage caused to the power lines supplying highspeed trains
Those charged successfully objected to being accused of terrorism and were all eventually freed without charge
Since  a number of firebomb attacks against police stations have been associated with the radical left There have been no arrests
Earlier this year Eric Vaillant the chief investigating judge in the eastern city of Grenoble called for a police investigation of possible radical left implication in more than  fires in the region around the city targeting police stations public buildings and churches No investigation was undertaken

By BBC Monitoring
Nigeria has ordered the closure of schools in three northwestern states bordering Katsina State where Boko Haram claimed the kidnapping of hundreds of students on  December Jigawa and Kano states have closed all schools with immediate effect and advised parents to evacuate students by today according to Premium Times website
The announcement comes three days to the end of the third term Schools in Kano were expected to close on Friday  December the website reported
In Zamfara the state government announced the closure of  schools along its border with Katsina and Kaduna The states commissioner for education Ibrahim Gusau said the closure was to forestall any breakdown of law and order
Boko Haram denies negotiations
Boko Haram said it was holding  students from Government Science Secondary School Kankara in Katsina The Katsina government however said  students were abducted
The Punch website citing an audio released on  December said Boko Haram claimed it had not entered into negotiations with the government contrary to claims by the authorities Katsina State Governor Aminu Masari had earlier said that the gunmen responsible for the attack had made contact with the government
The Vanguard newspaper quoted some parents urging the government to pay ransom to secure the release of their children
I support the government paying ransom to secure the release of our children whatever amount since the government cant rescue them a parent of the kidnapped schoolboy was quoted as saying
Teachers threaten strike
The Nigeria Union of Teachers has threatened to go on strike if the government does not secure schools with Amnesty International saying education was under attack in northern Nigeria
The opposition Peoples Democratic Party PDP has condemned President Muhammadu Buhari for making a private visit to his Daura hometown in Katsina instead of visiting Kankara where the schoolboys were kidnapped
The pannorthern organisation the Arewa Consultative Forum ACF has said Nigeria as a country was no longer safe under President Buhari
Both the police and the army seem to have been overwhelmed It is really a distressful situation ACF said in a statement cited by the Punch website
The kidnap of schoolboys in Katsina has evoked memories of an April  attack in which Boko Haram abducted  girls from a government secondary school in Chibok northeastern Borno State
About  girls were released after negotiations between the government and militants but dozens of others are yet to return to their families

After the Kumba massacre Schools in Cameroons Anglophone crisis Until recently activists in the diaspora and separatists had insisted that schools remain closed and used violence to ensure it  On  October armed men attacked a school in Kumba in the Southwest region of Cameroon They killed seven students and injured others several more In the aftermath of the assault the Cameroonian government was quick to blame separatist fighters who have been locked in war for independence since  The secessionist groups rejected the claim They said the attack was conducted by agents of the Cameroonian military in an attempt to tarnish the separatists reputation Regardless of who was responsible for it the Kumba attack underscored the fact that educational institutions have been a target throughout the crisis that has engulfed the two Anglophone regions of Cameroon Since its start teachers and students have played a key role whether as players or pawns Many schools had only just reopened following years of enforced closures and Kumba is just the latest school in the Anglophone regions to have been attacked in the last few years Calling for a school boycott Schools and teachers have been central to the Anglophone crisis since protests against the regions decades of marginalisation began in  That October teachers and lawyers trade unions organised demonstrations demanding an end to Francophone domination in their institutions By the end of November students had joined in leaving schools empty As the Cameroonian government brutally suppressed these demonstrations the Anglophone Civil Society Consortium which was spearheading the movement at the time called for civil disobedience in the form boycotting businesses and schools The day after this action commenced the protest leaders were arrested Soon after several teachers trade unions and members of the consortium called for schools to resume but the consortium leaders refused to change their stance Activists in the diaspora also spread disinformation by saying UNESCO would not recognise any educational certificates issued in Cameroon that year The boycott largely held The few schools that reopened faced reprisals The first attack on a school occurred in February  near Kumba In May a government primary school in Bamenda that was preparing to host exams was burnt down It is not clear who carried out these attacks as separatist fighters had not yet mobilised but it is likely they were motivated by activists in the diaspora who had begun to advocate for a violent approach The boycott was further solidified in the summer of  when members of the diaspora formed the Interim Government of Ambazonia The new group which advocated for the creation of an independent state said it would not permit the resumption of schooling until independence was granted Matters turn more violent When conflict then broke out in January  separatist fighters added the threat of violence and attacked schools that defied the boycott In April  high school staff member Thomas Nkongho was killed by secessionist fighters Days later primary school teacher Sophie Maloba was executed Some other teachers were kidnapped This use of violence was encouraged by activists in the diaspora USbased activists such as Eric Tataw and Tapang Ivo Tanku for instance issued threats of violence that were later carried out or openly celebrated the executions of students These attacks continued at the start of the academic year in  That August Ayeah Ngam Emmanuel a teachers trade unionist calling for school resumption was abducted Then on the first day of the term fighters attacked the Presbyterian School in Bafut kidnapping teachers and students By the end of  at least  schools had been attacked or burned This pattern has continued up to now with the vast majority of children in the two Anglophone regions unable to attend school The official reason separatists have given for opposing the resumption of schooling is that it is not safe for students due to the conflict It is widely assumed that the real reason for the policy however is so that they can use it as leverage in negotiations with the Cameroonian government When a delegation of female leaders travelled to the US to discuss reopening schools with separatist leaders for instance they were told that the issue could only be addressed as part of official negotiations A change in policy At the beginning of the academic year in  segments of the divided separatist movement began to change their stance The Interim Government of Sisiku AyukTabe who remains in prison in Yaound announced that parents may send their children to school if they determine it to be safe Fighters on the ground announced their support for limited forms of schooling Activists who had vociferously opposed school resumption in the past including Eric Tataw and Mark Bareta changed their positions And some other separatist groups such as the Ambazonbia Governing Council AGOVC stated that while it did not support government schools resuming it supported community schools Others retained their previous stance such as the Interim Government of Samuel Sako which said that school resumption would not be allowed unless accompanied by international negotiations to end the conflict Following these changes many students began attending school for the first time in years and felt secure doing so However this all changed with the killing of students in Kumba While it is too early to know the full impact that attack will have on the resumption of schooling it is clear that many children will continue not to receive an education as long as the conflict continues

its use of magnetic bombs to demonstrate the extent of its reach into the capital as well as the governments vulnerability as it seeks leverage at the next round of peace talks that are scheduled to reconvene in Qatar in January Magnetic bombs have been used in Afghanistan since the early years of the insurgency around  as well as in Iraq But the intensified pace of such attacks this year has shifted the security equation in Kabul forcing anyone connected to the government to reassess how and when they use their vehicles Kabuls chaotic traffic works to bombers advantage Vehicles are often pinned in traffic jams where attackers on motorbikes or passing pedestrians can ease past and furtively attach a magnetic bomb The capital now feels like a city under siege with something as prosaic as a commute to work a source of dread and every car on the street a potential deathtrap The situation is so unpredictable  you dont know what will happen tomorrow when you get into your car said Aiman Mayar  whose father a Ministry of Education official was killed by a magnetic bomb in Kabul three months ago The official Dr Abdul Baqi Amin was riding in a ministry vehicle that had been parked in a ministry parking lot the night before his son said Like the loved ones of so many other bombing victims Mr Mayar was left wondering why his father was targeted  and how someone managed to attach an explosive device to his vehicle despite government bodyguards and security precautions I want to know how its possible that a car with a governmental number plate gets blown up with a magnetic bomb and the government doesnt even know who did it or how Mr Mayar said Its been three months since they promised an investigation but theres been nothing The Taliban has claimed responsibility for some magnetic bomb blasts but others go unclaimed such as the attacks on Mr Mayars father and Mr Mohibi exacerbating public fears that anyone could be targeted at any time for reasons that will never be explained The brazen attacks leave an enduring impression that the militants can operate in the governments capital with near impunity said Atiqullah Amarkhel a retired Afghan general who watched an insurgency slowly strangle Kabul in the early s until Afghanistans Russianbacked government collapsed Kabul is an open city  these Taliban live here and make their bombs here Mr Amarkhel said After each one of the magnetic bomb explosions the government gets more discredited The magnetic bombs are typically assembled using plastic high explosives and powerful magnets a government intelligence official said speaking on condition of anonymity The official said insurgents smuggle explosives into Kabul using an underground courier system known as belti Attackers try to attach the bombs as close as possible to a cars fuel tank to ensure that the vehicle is engulfed in flames The devices can be detonated remotely with radio signals or with a timedelay fuse At the same time the Taliban have stepped up widespread attacks against government forces in rural provinces and remote district centers Afghan civilians are frequently killed in the crossfire At least  civilians were killed in October the deadliest month for civilians since September  according to data compiled by The New York Times Even lowlevel functionaries affiliated with the government have been targeted by magnetic bombs In October Yousaf Jan an Afghan contractor hired to deliver fuel for police vehicles was killed by a bomb attached to his delivery vehicle in Khost Province in eastern Afghanistan Gul Nawaz the contractors cousin said he had no idea who had attacked Mr Jan or why I just know that nobody has investigated his case and nobody has helped his family Mr Nawaz said The magnetic bomb attacks are likely to persist The device is a brutally effective weapon  cheap precise and lethal It doesnt cost much and requires little in the way of facilities said Mr Rahmani the Parliament security member But it has a very high impact Fatima Faizi contributed reporting from Kabul and Farooq Jan Mangal from KhostFatima Faizi contributed reporting from Kabul and Farooq Jan Mangal from Khost

the figure of  as those unaccounted for Where are the remaining  At home Or still in the bush where they ran to when the insurgents arrived Kankara has like the other incidents exposed the underbelly of the porous security arrangements in schools susceptible to Boko Haram attacks Boko Haram chooses schools to invade carefully and carries out its mission with deadly precision It goes without saying that a government which cares about the welfare and security of its citizens especially children in schools in the line of Boko Harams attack will do everything within its power to protect them Boko Haram insurgents are not spirits that can operate stealthily without trace as they have been doing Something must be wrong somewhere for the group to always catch troops prosecuting the insurgency war on the wrong foot Is it possible for a soldier who is ready to lay down his life for his country to engage in a war whether conventional or otherwise like this It appears the soldiers believe that there is nothing at stake in this their socalled asymmetrical warfare and as such Boko Haram is being to run riot all over the place Are the soldiers war weary What about their commanders Are they motorcycles move about in that community that night without attracting suspicion What happened was again the failure of intelligence and the seeming reluctance to pursue the insurgency war aggressively Must the military acquire  Super Tucanoes as we are being told at billions of naira before it defeats Boko Haram The public keeps hearing of air strikes against Boko Haram in some places with the killing of some of the insurgents and the destruction of their weapons  Are these reports backed up with aerial pictures of those sorties real If they are where then does Boko Haram get the strength with which to unleash the kind of  attacks it carried out in Zabarmari  Borno State where  rice farmers were killed on November  and in Kankara the relatively unknown community shot into limelight by the abduction of innocent kids six days ago The casualty figure will always remain a thorny issue Masari has given  Presidential spokesman Garba Shehu gave  and the lie in this number was seen with the reported escape of  of the boys from their captors A media report on Monday put the figure at over  quoting the school register The families affected feel the heat Only God knows the hostels If things were this way when many of us were growing up our parents would not have sent us to boarding schools It is a big shame that due to no fault of parents and their children  schools have become unsafe What is the government doing about this As usual it is just to condemn the development as if that will bring back the abducted kids The  purpose of government is to guarantee the The following information was released by the Bureau of Alcohol Tobacco Firearms and ExplosivesCharges Include Destruction of Property Conspiracy Possessing Destructive DevicesLITTLE ROCK A federal investigation resulted in charges against four people for their alleged involvement in fire bombings of police vehicles in Little Rock and North Little Rock in August  Cody Hiland United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas and Bureau of Alcohol Tobacco Firearms and Explosives New Orleans Field Division Special Agent in Charge Kurt Thielhorn announced todays arrests of Brittany Dawn Jeffrey  Emily Nowlin  Renea Goddard  and Aline EspinosaVillegas  all of Little RockAccording to the Criminal Complaint filed on December   numerous incidents of vandalism occurred after protests were held at local police stations earlier this year On August   a large group of protestors held a demonstration at the Little Rock Police Department th Street Substation The following morning officers arriving for duty noticed that several police vehicles in their parking lot had punctured tires Officers also saw two green glass bottles with fluid inside that smelled like gasoline The bottles were examined and found to be consistent with improvised incendiary devices commonly referred to as Molotov cocktailsThe Complaint explains that a Molotov cocktail is typically made by using a container filled with an ignitable liquid and placing a wick in the opening of the container If the Molotov cocktail functions as designed the container will break spreading ignitable liquid which will be lit by the flaming wickAccording to the Complaint surveillance footage reflected that two individuals were moving near the parking lot after the protests and a flaming object can be observed being launched into the parking lot area Cooperating witnesses stated that the Molotov cocktails were assembled at Brittany Dawn Jeffreys residenceThe Complaint states that on August   an Arkansas State Police vehicle was vandalized and burned while stored in a fenced parking lot at Arkansas State Police Headquarters in Little Rock One vehicle had been set on fire one had been vandalized with spray paint and several others had punctured tires Investigators discovered a detonated Molotov cocktail made from a bottle of brandySurveillance video from that incident shows three people entering the vehicle storage area wearing dark clothing and backpacks The video shows them bending down in a motion consistent with slashing vehicle tires as well as throwing a lighted object into a police vehicle The Complaint states that witnesses informed law enforcement that Renea Goddard Emily Nowlin and Aline EspinosaVillegas were responsible for the incident Federal search warrants were executed to obtain the locations of their cell phones and cell site data confirmed that their cell phones were in the location of Arkansas State Police Headquarters on August  Todays arrests send a message that violence targeted toward law enforcement will not be tolerated stated US Attorney Hiland Breaking into a police compound and fire bombing a police vehicle with a homemade explosive device is clearly not a peaceful protest Those who would target law enforcement with violent acts will not do so in the Eastern District of Arkansas without the full resources of the federal government being deployed to assist our state and local partners in bringing those responsible to justice They will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the lawWe worked methodically on each of the scenes collecting evidence interviewing witnesses and following leads to help us solve these cases said ATF New Orleans Field Division Special Agent in Charge Kurt Thielhorn We were able to narrow in on particular individuals who we identified responsible for the law enforcement vehicle fires in the Little Rock area We appreciate the assistance the public was able to provide in order to bring these individuals to justiceThe charges in todays unsealed Complaint include malicious destruction of property belonging to an entity receiving federal funding conspiracy to commit those acts and possession of a destructive deviceThe defendants arrested today will appear before US Magistrate Judge Joe J Volpe at  pm this afternoon for their initial appearance The investigation was conducted by ATF Arkansas State Police North Little Rock Police Department and Little Rock Police Department The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Stacy WilliamsA complaint contains only allegations Defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty

A round up of media stories about violence by terrorist groups and other terror related activity available to BBC Monitoring in the period  December  
AFRICA
Nearly  students missing after DR Congo clashes
A DR Congo radio station has reported that nearly  students went missing following clashes between rival militia groups in the eastern Babuyu sector Kabambare territory in Maniema Province Several villages including Kulewa and Kahoya in Kabambare territory were also burnt down during the clashes the website of Radio Okapi added According to a source the fighting began on  December and went on until  December resulting in massive displacement of people Radio Okapi website Kinshasa in French  Dec 
Radio says Mali in talks with militants over besieged Segou village
Mediation efforts are taking place to end a twomonth blockade of the Malian village of Farabougou in Niono District in the central Segou region where local media say a jihadist siege continues Radio France Internationale reported All actors including the jihadists were involved in the mediation led by the influential High Islamic Council the report said  It added that three direct meetings with the jihadists had already been held Generally speaking the whole area is under the control of jihadists the report said
Talks are also focusing on relations between the Fulani livestock herders and the Bambara farmers in Niono District over longrunning mistrust and clashes Radio France Internationale in French  Dec 
Somali militants claim attacks on African Union forces
The proAlShabab news website Somali Memo reported on  December that the groups militants attacked a military base in a village in Middle Shabelle Region At least six Burundian soldiers were injured in the attack in the village of Biya Adde Mahaday District the report said Somali Memo website in Somali  Dec 
Islamic State video belittles rival alShabab in Somalia
The Islamic State group IS has released a lengthy documentarystyle video aimed at discrediting its jihadist rival in Somalia the alQaedaaffiliated alShabab group The video  produced by the groups Somalia branch wilayat alSomal Somalia Province was released on  December
The propaganda film is presented as the third instalment in an IS video series called To be absolved before your Lord The first episode in April sought to discredit alQaedas branch in Yemen AQAP and the second in September attacked the Taliban in Afghanistan All episodes present IS as the only righteous jihadist group worthy of following
The third video tries to undermine alShabab largely by referring to its loyalty through alQaeda to the Afghan Taliban IS and its supporters online have increasingly been using the Taliban and its foreign policies to discredit alQaeda branches
Although the video flaunts ISs presence in Somalia its complaints about alShabab persecution and attacks on the one hand and the scarcity of IS activity in the country on the other indicate the groups weakness in Somalia BBC Monitoring said
IS first announced receiving pledges of allegiance from Somalia in October  Despite claiming sporadic lowprofile activity in the country since then it only named Somalia a wilayah official branch in July  Apart from a rise in attacks in the country in  the groups activity there has been very limited likely a result of the more powerful rival alShabab
AlShabab openly declared war against IS in December  calling the group a deadly disease that must be uprooted At the time both groups exchanged threats to wipe out each other Telegram messaging service in Arabic  Dec 
SOUTH ASIA
Four Afghan soldiers said killed in Taliban attack
Four soldiers of Afghanistans National Security Directorate NDS the countrys top intelligence body have been killed and five others injured in a Taliban attack in northern Baghlan province the Pakistanbased Afghan Islamic Press AIP reported The provincial polices spokesman said that the Taliban attacked a security post in the Chashma Shir area on the BaghlanSamangan highway on the morning of  December He did not gave any casualties figure but a source told AIP that four soldiers lost their lives and five others were wounded in the attack Afghan Islamic Press news agency in Pashto  Dec 
Taliban kidnap five Afghan civilians in west
The Taliban have kidnapped five civilians in Ferozkoh the capital of the western Afghan province of Ghor the Pakistanbased Afghan Islamic Press AIP reported The civilians were abducted in the Ahangaran area on the night of  December According to the provincial governors spokesman the Taliban were the abductors but it was unclear why they kidnapped the civilians Afghan Islamic Press news agency in Pashto  Dec 
IS claims responsibility for beheading sorcerer in west Afghanistan
The Islamic State group IS has claimed it beheaded a sorcerer in the western Afghan city of Herat The jihadist group made the claim in a short statement on  December saying that its militants captured a man named Sayed Kamal Agha and beheaded him for allegedly practising sorcery No other media reports matching the description of the incident were seen
IS has a history of claiming to have killed alleged practitioners of black magic but such claims were more common when the group controlled large swathes of Syria and Iraq ISs selfstyled Khorasan Province which operates in Afghanistan has previously claimed several attacks on Shia Muslims in Herat RocketChat messaging service in Arabic  Dec 
Human rights body concerned over targeted killings in Afghanistan
The Afghan Independent Human Rights Commission AIHRC has expressed its concern about targeted killings in the country calling them obvious examples of war crimes The targeted killings accounted for  per cent of all civilian casualties in the first six months of  the AIHRC said in a statement released on Twitter on  December adding that  civilians including journalists human rights activists and civil servants were killed in that period Twittercom in Dari and Pashto  Dec 
MIDDLE EAST
Bahrain welcomes US terrorist designation of Iranbacked group
Bahrain has welcomed the US designation of the Iranbacked group Saraya alMukhtar AlMukhtar Brigades as a terrorist organisation the stateowned Bahrain News Agency BNA reported
The US designated Saraya alMukhtar as a terrorist organisation backed by Iran on  December accusing it of plotting attacks against US personnel in Bahrain Saraya alMukhtar is a relatively lowprofile group that operates in Bahrain It has previously claimed cyberattacks targeting the Bahraini government Bahrain News Agency Manama in Arabic  Dec

ProalQaeda outlet advertises Bitcoin online course
The proalQaeda media outfit Jaysh alMalahim alElectroni The alMalahim Electronic Army has advertised a course on Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies In a message on  December via its channel on the decentralised platform RocketChat alMalahim Electronic Army described the course as the first of its kind in the world of jihadist electronic armies The advert said the course will start in the next few days
AlMalahim Electronic Army has been active since at least June Its content including the latest publication is often shared by alQaeda supporters on the platform The outlet frequently publishes original proalQaeda posters and reposts official alQaeda content RocketChat messaging service in Arabic  Dec

Two suspected militants killed in Russias Chechnya
Two suspected militants were killed in Chechnyas Kurchaloyevskiy District on  December the regional Interior Ministry reported The incident took place in the early hours of the day when local traffic policemen tried to stop a car for a preventive check the ministrys press service said The men tried to flee opening fire and throwing an improvised explosive device at the police They were killed by return fire the ministry said The police officers were not injured Interfax news agency Moscow in Russian  Dec

Ten years since start of the Arab Spring
Today marks  years since street vendor Mohamed Bouazizi set himself on fire in the Tunisian province of Sidi Bouzid in protest against repression and police harassment
That incident sparked nationwide unrest that toppled Tunisias longserving President Zine El Abidine Ben Ali and triggered uprisings across the region  known as the Arab Spring
The uprisings brought previously inconceivable changes in countries ruled by entrenched authoritarian leaders but even in Tunisia hailed as the only success story of the Arab Spring challenges remain
Ten years to the month after Bouazizis death another young Tunisian died after setting himself on fire in the very same province over continuing economic hardship
In the first of a series of articles examining the countries involved in the Arab Spring BBC Monitoring provides a snapshot of how the protests transformed political and media landscapes
Analysis  years on from the Arab Spring
Tunisia marks Bouazizi anniversary
Today Tunisian figures and media are marking the anniversary of Bouazizis death
Locals from his province of Sidi Bouzid said yesterday that the cradle of the Tunisian uprising is still suffering from deep social and economic problems
Though they lamented a lack of progress it is nonetheless telling that they made these remarks to state news agency TAP which regularly publishes criticism of the government  a trait unheard of at the time of Ben Ali or in other Arab Spring countries state media
In its report on the anniversary of the first spark of the revolution TAP aired the locals grievances on successive governments inability to tackle problems
The former postuprising president Moncef Marzouki has meanwhile said that the revolution achieved half of its goals but issues around corruption and social justice remain unresolved
We will publish today an analysis of Tunisias media scene contrasting its milestones with growing concerns over freedoms

Text of editorial titled Magnetic mines a dangerous killer not yet taken seriously by Afghan Daily Afghanistan newspaper on  December 
Magnetic and sticky bomb blasts have been going on in capital Kabul for several years now Magnetic explosives have targeted dozens of government vehicles police rangers pick up vehicles and even civilian vehicles
In the beginning the destructive power of the magnetic bombs was insignificant and limited and that is why they were not taken seriously Even ordinary people did not take these mines seriously However things are different this year The enemies of the people of Afghanistan have included escalating violence and targeted assassinations in their strategy leading to an increase in the use of sticky bombs with stronger destructive power Therefore this dangerous killer cannot be overlooked anymore
The death toll from magnetic mines this year alone highlights how serious the issue is The deputy governor of Kabul and a member of Ghor provincial council were killed in magnetic bombs yesterday A few days ago a member of parliament fortunately survived a magnetic bomb blast in Kabul Some journalists were also killed in magnetic bomb blasts some time ago
Sticky bombs are dangerous for a number of reasons
 The bomb is light and portable and can easily be transferred around the city
 These bombs are affordable and it is not difficult for terrorists and other groups to acquire them
 This type of mines were first used in Kabul but are now also used in the provinces to kill people The increasing use of sticky bombs in more places can in the future create serious problems for the people and the government
 These mines can be easily planted and blown up There is no need for professional training as anyone can easily stick it under or on the side of a vehicle or other places
 It is not only the terrorists that use these types of mines Some of those planting these mines are ordinary people Therefore ordinary peoples access to these mines can bring about dangerous consequences for both society and government
 The perpetrators behind these attacks have not yet been identified Not all these explosions may have terrorist motives Some people may use these mines for personal hostilities and revenge
 It is difficult to identify those behind distribution and plantation of these mines for the reason that terrorist groups use ordinary people drug addicts criminals and even the children for planting these mines Members of criminal networks smugglers land usurpers bullies and hire ordinary people for killing their rivals and opponents
The widespread use of sticky bombs and the rising number of victims of these explosions has raised serious concern in the society No one feels safe now An explosion may occur and kill people anywhere In such a situation members of society lose trust in one another and suspect each other It is the most dangerous situation that society members experience in their life
The life threats as well as the psychological impacts of the sticky bombs are quite deep and unfortunate This is an issue that has unfortunately been ignored among the horrible news and no individual or official has paid attention to
The security and operation institutions should respond to some questions about the magnetic mines
First where are the sticky bombs made in such a high quantity or which country are they imported from
Second why have security and intelligence agencies failed to discover and seize these mines and why have they failed to prevent the transfer of these mines
Third why has the widespread network involved in the distribution of these mines across the country particularly in the capital not yet been identified
Fourth who are the perpetrators behind planting sticky bombs and what is their motive for such attacks
Fifth is it only the Taliban and other terrorist groups carrying out these attacks or there are personal hostilities and other personal issues behind these explosions and killings
Sixth why do the security bodies ignore the danger of sticky mines and its psychological consequences in society Why do they never speak about the arrest and prosecution of those behind such attacks
It is the first and main responsibility of security institutions to answer the questions above If these institutions pay no attention to this issue now the use of the sticky mines will turn into a common practice in the society in the future It will then be difficult and costly for these agencies to prevent it The negligence of the security bodies in this regard is not justifiable at all The government is responsible to ensure the security of citizens and the people have the right to expect the same from the government Therefore take the threats of sticky bombs seriously
