More mass abductions reported in northern Nigeria
Boko Haram abducted around  road travellers in northeastern Nigeria on  December and police rescued  schoolchildren who were kidnapped on the same day reports say
The local Guardian newspaper reported that militants dressed in military uniforms waylaid nine commercial vehicles and whisked away the passengers into the bush on a road linking the town of Damaturu in Yobe state and Maiduguri the capital of Borno state
Many of the passengers fled the scene but about  of them were abducted 
Separately Nigerian police said they rescued  students abducted from an Islamic school in the northwestern Katsina state
A spokesman for the local police Gambo Isah said the students were accosted by bandits on their way home from a religious ceremony
He said the children were freed after security forces engaged the bandits in a fierce gun duel
It was the third mass abduction in Nigeria in a week
On  December  schoolboys abducted from a school six days earlier were released by their abductors
Channels Television reported that kidnappers have recently been targeting schools in northern Nigeria raising fears about the safety of students
CAR opposition calls for election delay due to unrest
An opposition coalition in the Central African Republic has demanded the postponement of  Decembers general election due to violence by rebel groups and the inability of the government to protect candidates
The  Democratic Opposition Coalition Cod said it is impossible to hold the vote as scheduled due to robbery theft and confiscation of campaign materials vehicles motorcycles and funds of several candidates
It called for the postponement of the grouped elections of  December  until the restoration of peace and security in the country
Fighting took place at the weekend in several towns including the city of Mbaiki km from Bangui the capital
The local media reported that Mbaiki and a number of other towns including Grimari in the centre have fallen into rebel hands
Government forces backed by United Nations peacekeepers and Russian mercenaries  are trying to stop the rebels marching on the capital
Rwanda deploys more peacekeepers to violencehit CAR
Rwanda has said it deployed force protection troops to the Central African Republic where government forces are battling a coalition of rebel groups
In a statement Rwandas defence ministry said the deployment is in response to the targeting of the Rwanda Defence Force RDF contingent under the UN peacekeeping force by rebels supported by Franois Bozize former CAR president
The statement said the Rwandan soldiers will also contribute to ensure a peaceful and secure general election scheduled on Sunday  December 
CARs government has accused Bozize a member of the Cod opposition coalition of plotting a coup after the countrys highest court rejected his candidacy for the election
Bozize was ousted by a Muslim rebel coalition in  ten years after he came to power in a coup
His removal plunged the country into a civil war as Muslim Seleka rebels and Christian antiBalaka fighters battle for control
Tensions between Kenya and Somalia serious concern for AU
Ongoing tensions between Somalia and Kenya and the breakdown in their diplomatic relations remain a serious concern for the African Union head of the African Union Commission Moussa Faki Mahamat has said
He spoke on Sunday in Djibouti as member states of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development Igad regional bloc met to discuss the spat between Kenya and Somalia
Faki called on the two countries to open dialogue with a view to the resumption of these relations
The meeting in Djibouti was called after Somalia wrote a letter to the bloc accusing Kenya of interfering in its internal affairs
Somalia severed diplomatic ties with Kenya on  December accusing it of violating its sovereignty and meddling in its internal affairs
Kenya has repeatedly rejected these accusations
The two countrys presidents met on the sidelines of the Igad summit but gave no details of what they discussed
Ethiopias staterun ETV channel reported that they agreed to reestablish diplomatic relations
Meanwhile tensions are high in the border towns of Beled Hawo Somalia and Mandera Kenya amid reports of troop buildup
See Timeline SomaliaKenya row threatens fight against militants
Turkish troops to replace departing US forces
Turkish soldiers will take over the training of Somalias Danab special forces and carry out air strikes against alShabab militants once US forces withdraw from the country next month privatelyowned Radio Kulmiye has reported
Kulmiye based in Mogadishu cited Turkeys staterun TRT Arabic channel as reporting that Ankara will take over the command and training of the Danab forces who were previously under the US government
The Turkish government also said that it will conduct air strikes against the terrorists The Turkish government said it will send its warplanes especially F fighter jets to fight alShabab and Islamic State militants in Somalia Radio Kulmiye reported
On  December President Donald Trump ordered the withdrawal of most American military personnel and assets from Somalia by  January
The US has about  military personnel in the wartorn nation who have been assisting local troops in their fight against alShabab
Bomb blast kills three in Ethiopias capital
Three people died on Sunday and five others were wounded when a bomb abandoned by unknown people exploded in Ethiopias capital Addis Ababa state media and officials said
Police official Alemayehu Ayalqie said the authorities were investigating the incident and would make their findings public
The stateowned Ethiopian News Agency reported that the blast took place in a place earmarked for development
It said three homeless people were killed
Meanwhile the chairman of the African Union Commission Moussa Faki Mahamat has commended Ethiopia for its bold steps to preserve the integrity of the country an apparent reference to a military offensive in the northern Tigray region
Faki made the remarks at an extraordinary summit of the InterGovernmental Authority on Development Igad regional grouping in Djibouti on Sunday
Ethiopian federal troops have forced the leaders of the Tigray Peoples Liberation Front TPLF from power in Tigray in a law enforcement operation which started on  November
Ugandas military denies supporting opposition candidate
The Ugandan army has dismissed claims that it is supporting opposition presidential candidate Robert Kyagulanyi who is challenging President Yoweri Museveni in next months election
Kyagulanyi also known as Bobi Wine said on  December that the Uganda Peoples Defence Forces UPDF would help him end Musevenis year stranglehold on power in the  January election 
He said Ugandan soldiers and police were supporting him because they were yearning for change 
However army spokesperson Brig Gen Flavia Byekwaso said Bobi Wines claims were baseless and reckless according to the stateowned New Vision website 
Meanwhile a privatelyowned radio based in the western town of Fort Portal went off the air over the weekend after it interviewed independent presidential candidate Joseph Kabuleta 
KRC FM was switched off one hour into the interview the Observer website reported
Separately the Facebook pages of two online TVs affiliated to Bobi Wine have reportedly been hacked into and deleted
The government last week asked Google to close more than a dozen YouTube channels allegedly linked to deadly preelection protests
Ethiopia and Sudan to hold border talks after attack
Sudan and Ethiopia will hold talks on  December in a bid to contain crossborder tensions a week after Ethiopian gunmen  killed at least four Sudanese soldiers in an attack
Sudanese Prime Minister Abdalla Hamdok and his Ethiopian counterpart Abiy Ahmed met on the sidelines of a regional summit in Djibouti yesterday to discuss tensions along the two countries shared border
They agreed to form a joint committee to coordinate tomorrows talks in Sudans capital Khartoum
Meanwhile Sudans military said it reclaimed a strategic area from Ethiopian militias in the eastern alQadarif state along the border
It said it captured Abu Tuyur where Ethiopian gunmen killed four Sudanese soldiers on  December
The private Sudan Tribune website  said that the army retook control of new border areas from Ethiopian Amhara militias
The two countries have a longrunning border dispute with both sides claiming alQadarifs fertile Fashqa triangle

Islamic State group IS has claimed an attack on a commander with Turkeybacked Syrian rebels in Afrin a town located in the northern Syrian province of Aleppo
IS rarely ventures into Afrin which is currently controlled by armed factions backed by Turkey
In a statement on  December via its channel on the decentralised platform RocketChat IS said its militants used an improvised explosive device IED to target a vehicle belonging to a leader in the sahwat allegedly injuring him and his bodyguard on  December 
Sahwat is a term used by IS and its supporters to refer to Sunni armed groups opposed to the group
The statement did not give any further details 
IS rarely carries out attacks in Aleppo province from which it was driven out in  at the hands of Turkishbacked Syrian rebel groups and rival Kurdish forces
Turkish forces and allied rebel groups have controlled parts of northern Aleppo province including Afrin since pushing out Kurdishled Syrian Democratic Forces SDF in March 
In recent months Afrin has been the scene of frequent explosions and attacks targeting opposition military commanders
The Turkishbacked rebel group Syrian National Army has blamed the attacks on Damascus loyalists IS and the Kurdish militia group YPG

By BBC Monitoring
A proalQaeda news outlet has claimed that Islamic State group IS has halted attacks against French and Malian forces to focus its efforts on rival alQaedas affiliate in the Sahel Jamaat Nusrat alIslam walMuslimin JNIM
Thabat new agency  made the comments in the latest edition of its weekly newspaper which was shared by prominent alQaeda supporters on the messaging app Telegram  August
JNIM and IS have been at war for months in the border areas between Mali Burkina Faso and Niger
In a report Thabat newspaper said that IS had fully stopped its operations against French forces in Mali for months and hinted at collusion between the French and IS against JNIM
The Thabat report said that while JNIM had continued to target French troops and apostate lackeys Malian security forces IS had been attacking JNIM and harassing local Muslim populations
The newspaper said that JNIM had lost  fighters after IS militants ambushed them in Gao in northern Mali The JNIM fighters were allegedly attacked while they were returning from battle with French forces in the area
Thabat did not say when the IS attack on JNIM militants had taken place
Las week IS claimed killing  JNIM fighters in clashes in central Mali  
In its report Thabat newspaper also accused French forces in Mali for seeking to strengthen IS in Mali in order to stop JNIM attacks on them
It claimed that French war planes on several occasions targeted JNIM fighters while they were on their way to fend off attacks by IS
Nevertheless the newspaper stopped short of explicitly accusing IS of collusion with the French forces against JNIM
JNIM has so far not made any such accusations against IS via its official outlet on the decentralised platform RocketChat
However IS has previously accused JNIM of secretly collaborating with national and possibly even foreign forces as well as local militias and rebel groups in its fight against IS
In November ISs regional leader in Africas Sahel Adnan Abu alWalid alSahrawi accused JNIM in an interview published by IS weekly newspaper alNaba of forging alliances with a number of apostate nationalist movements in northern Mali
IS has also repeatedly used JNIMs agreement in March to hold talks with the Malian government as a means to undermine the jihadist credentials of its rival and prompt defections 
Source Telegram messaging service in Arabic  gmt  Dec

He said the Afghan security and defence forces had sacrificed a lot to ensure the populstions security in the Afghan capital and provinces
When asked what should be done to improve the situation in Kabul Mr Arian replied The Afghan government and the security forces are committed to ending violence in the country The terrorist groups particularly the Taliban have violated their commitments by carrying out attacks in the cities We have made good progress when it comes to fighting terrorist groups and criminals in Afghanistan
He went on to say that the Taliban had been defeated on the battlefields and carrying out such attacks on major cities was their only option

You know that the Taliban after signing the peace deal with the USA planned to seize a number of districts in Kabul Province but the security forces prevented them from achieving their goal We have weakened the enemy said Mr Arian
Elsewhere in his remarks he said the terrorist groups were resorting to targeted killings planting mines attaching magnetic bombs and suicide attacks because they had failed to advance on the battlefield
In the meantime a former member of the lower house of parliament Homayoun Homayoun slammed the security organs for giving false information to the people on the security situation
Arg or the Presidential Palace tries to appoint individuals as spokesmen to the security organs who can give false information to the people with regards to the security situation They always extend their sympathy to the people and pledge to improve the security situation Most of the government spokesmen have become liars said Mr Homayoun
He said the government does not have a strong policy for ensuring security of the population describing the government offices leanings to different countries as the reason behind this
When asked to elaborate this claim Mr Homayoun replied Most of the politicians within the government implement the plans of foreign countries Some implement plans from India Iran and Pakistan while a number of others work for Russia the USA and the UK The people blame Pakistan for  of the terror attacks in Kabul but I would like to say that India and Iran also have influence in Afghanistan
Another studio guest a current member of the lower house of parliament Abdul Sattar Hosseini also spoke about rising insecurity in the Afghan capital
How can the people expect the police chief of Kabul to ensure security when he is appointed by someone else not the interior minister The interior minister is a competent person and he is serious about wanting to ensure the populations security The situation will improve when the minister himself appoints the police chiefs for the provinces and districts said Mr Hosseini
He said the interior minister while presenting his programmes to the parliament vowed to use all his powers to ensure peoples security
In response to the question about the role of the parliament on the situation he replied We always respond We speak the truth You saw that we did not vote for incompetent ministerial nominees
Elsewhere in his remarks the MP said the interior minister was capable of ensuring security in Kabul and provinces if only certain individuals would stop meddling in his work

KABUL At least  security forces were killed in two attacks carried out by the Taliban insurgents in the provinces of Baghlan and Kunduz in the north and northeast respectively Sources in the provincial offices said on condition of anonymity that Taliban insurgents attacked two government forces checkpoints in the Arab Ha area of Char Dara district in Kunduz late Monday
According to the sources fire exchanges continued for several hours and the security forces called for reinforcement from the district center but the reinforcement faced Taliban ambush on their way

Taliban captured the two checkpoints and took six police hostage along with their weapons and munitions

Rahmani only confirmed the death of two police and said three others were wounded
Taliban claimed responsibility for the Char Dara attack on security forces
Separately the militants attacked three government outposts in the Gholam Boy neighborhood of BaghlaneMarkazi district in Baghlan province
Sources in the province said that the attackers killed five police officers while two officers went missing
All the three outposts fell to Taliban according to the sources who said government forces managed to retake the posts
One police officer was killed and two wounded in another Taliban attack in Baghlans district of Nahrin Fazluddin Moradi district governor said
Taliban claimed responsibility for all attacks in Baghlan too

MOSCOW December  Sputnik  Protests are boiling in the Central African Republic CAR as the country prepares for presidential and parliamentary elections this coming Sunday with the authorities blaming the unrest on exPresident Francois Bozize who was denied the right to run in the voteThe CAR is a landlocked underpopulated country in the very heart of the African continent neighboring Cameroon Chad Congo the Democratic Republic of the Congo DRC South Sudan and Sudan After proclaiming independence from France in  the country experienced several coups and eventually plunged into a civil war in the early  which resulted in Bozize coming to power in Bozize ruled until toppled in  when the CAR capital of Bangui was taken over by rebels and became a battlefield between a former Islamist movement known as Seleka and their Christianmajority antagonists known as AntiBalaka The armed conflict resulted in over  casualties and prompted the flight of an approximate  million people according to the United Nations In  the UN deployed a peacekeeping force MINUSCA to ensure the protection of civilians in the conflict zoneIn February  CAR President FaustinArchange Touadera and leaders of  rebel groups signed a peace agreement consenting to arrange for an inclusive general election in a bid to ensure a peaceful transfer of power The government also committed to ensure the freedom of organizing political parties and movements as well as facilitate the return of refugeesLast Saturday after three key rebel groups decided to form an antigovernment coalition to run in the elections CAR authorities accused Bozize of plotting a coup Sputnik learned from MINUSCA spokesman Vladimir Monteiro that the political situation in the country became tense as Bozize and the armed groups appeared to be seeking to disrupt the voteForeign embassies in the CAR are working to help make the elections happen Russian Ambassador in Bangui Vladimir Titorenko told Sputnik He said there was no attempt of a coup per se as rebels had failed to enter the capital but Bozize in the meantime frequented meeting with rebel leaders and stirring up the population to a mutiny The Russian diplomat believes that the purpose of these activities is to intimidate the people so that they simply do not show up at the polling stations in which case the electoral process can later be denounced void due to a low turnoutAccording to Titorenko a group of foreign embassies including those of France and the United States issued a joint statement calling on Bozize to stop inciting violence and try to disrupt the electionsThe Russian ambassador said the situation in Bangui remained relatively stable unlike in areas far from the capital not completely under the control of central CAR authorities as per the Khartoum agreement At the same time the diplomat said there were no known cases of active military confrontation in the country at the momentThe reason Bozize was not allowed to run in the elections was that he failed to provide evidence that he had resided in the CAR for at least one year before the vote The expresident fled the country in  and was indicted by the UN Security Council for war crimes against own people according to TitorenkoAfter a period of exile in neighboring countries Bozize supposedly returned to the CARs northwest under the control of loyal rebels and led a rally of supporters  including armed militia  on to Bangui The expresidents party has denied that he was planning a coup however CAR opposition in the meantime has called for a postponement of the election until the peace and security are restoredOn Monday Rwanda deployed troops to the CAR under a bilateral defense treaty and in response to attacks against Rwandan peacekeepers within MINUSCA The Rwandan military was also tasked with preventing any disruptions to the electionSome media reported that Russia too deployed troops to the CAR but Titorenko refuted this in a comment to Sputnik According to the Russian ambassador the Russian presence in the CAR is limited to five Defense Ministry employees army instructors who had arrived at the request of the CAR government and  peacekeepers within MINUSCAIn a comment to Sputnik earlier on Tuesday Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Bogdanov explained that the presence of the Russian Defense Ministry representatives in the CAR is of political nature rather than military as they are not engaged in any military action Bogdanov stressed that Moscow remained committed to all relevant UN Security Council Resolutions and was seriously concerned about the attempts to undermine CAR elections

kilometers of the city which is at the center of the  billion  billion ChinaPakistan Economic Corridor CPEC project According to local media there will be two entry points to the fenced part of the city and more than  surveillance cameras will be installed The main reason behind building the fence in Gwadar is to protect the Chinesefunded projects from Baloch separatists who oppose CPEC  Many Baloch politicians believe the fencing will force locals to relocate from the strategically important city China announced the CPEC project in  with an aim to expand its trade links and influence in pipeline links to improve connectivity between China and the Middle East Pakistan is grappling with an acute economic crisis Experts say CPEC can certainly stir the muchneeded economic activity in the country Balochistan remains Pakistans poorest and least populous province despite several development projects initiated by Islamabad Rebel groups have waged a separatist insurgency in the province for decades complaining that Islamabad and the richer Punjab province unfairly exploit their resources Islamabad reacted to the insurgency by launching a military operation in the province in  There have since been reports of grave human rights abuses committed by the military and its intelligence agencies in the province The strategically located Gwadar port is close to the Strait of Hormuz and Baloch nationalists fear that the Chinese are not only after the provinces natural resources but also want to exploit the port which is already being operated by the Chinese Armed rebels continue to attack security forces in Balochistan In November  Baloch separatists attacked the Chinese consulate in Pakistans southern Karachi city  Earlier this year four gunmen belonging to the Balochistan Liberation Army BLA attacked the Pakistan Stock Exchange building killing at least three people including two guards and one policeman while the four assailants were also killed by gunfire Pakistani officials say that Gwadar fencing which is part of the Smart Port City Project is aimed at transforming the city into a modern town with industrial zones trade centers and housing areas Authorities Pakistani security forces have previously been attacked in Balochistan We have the right to protect the city from those that dont want the country to progress Awan told DW They are against all development projects The fencing will be carried out and will be completed Awan vowed However independent analysts say the fencing will be counterproductive as it is likely to alienate the local population It fencing is an apartheid legacy It will harm the country Ammar Ali Jan a Lahorebased political analyst told DW Mohammad Aslam Bhootani a member of parliament from Gwadar last week slammed Terror outfit threatening Pulwama residents probe agencies alert forces Link to Image Link to Story umit Kumar SinghNew Delhi Dec  IANS Indian intelligence agencies have alerted the security establishments that a terror outfit  The Resistance Front TRF  has started threatening the residents of Jammu and Kashmir for siding with the security forces TRF a newly created terror outfit based in Pakistan has released names of residents from JUKs Pulwama district terming them as traitors and warned them not to side with India Indian probe agencies have alerted the security establishments about the TRF list
On February   Pakistanbased terrorist organisation JaisheMohammed chief Masood Azhar executed a terror attack in Pulwama in which  Indian troopers of the Central Reserve Police Force CRPF were killed The ghastly attack triggered action by the Indian Air Force IAF against a Jaish terror camp deep inside Pakistan  days later and resulted in a dogfight between fighter jets of the two nations on February 
In September this year social media accounts linked to TRF had released a hit list of  people mostly comprising Valleybased journalists political workers and activists whom the militant group accused of being on the payrolls of Indian security agencies
The  people named in the list have also been categorised as A A B and C This categorisation is similar to how the Jammu and Kashmir police slot militants based on the level of their involvement in militants activities Then the local police had filed an FIR against unknown people in connection with a hit list and a probe into the matter is on
Indian intelligence agencies had earlier stated that it was after the abrogation of Article  that Pakistan started a new terror front on social media and it was named as The Resistance Front
Various reports have come out on its links across the Line of Control many have corroborated that the TRF is supported and backed by the LashkareTaiba LeT Often claims have been made that the TRF even appears to be a proxy of the LeT
TRF is funded and backed by Pakistan a top counterterror official in Kashmir had said
The group is one of the several efforts often repeated in the past two decades to give terrorism in Kashmir an indigenous face and give the Pakistan deep state blamed for supporting terror an alibi the official had said
Since its appearance on social media platforms the TRF has resorted to claiming high traction acts and owned up the terrorists active in the Valley
From claiming the grenade hurling in Srinagars Hari Singh High Street on October  to the next one within a fortnight that killed one civilian TRF has been holding to every thread to associate itself with small and big terror incidents
It is also known that their social media accounts according to the internet protocol address were being operated from Islamabad and that too mostly from an iPhone
The connivance and support of Pakistan is clearly visible since Kashmir at that time was still under a lockdown and the internet had been snapped simultaneously to contain the propaganda
It is not a new tactic that the moment a group surfaces it makes a series of tall claims to set up and validate itself as the top rung among others What differentiates TRF is the sheer planning and precision of execution
From nicely printed English announcements on a letter head with serial numbering to professionally made videos or audio messages are all tools used for enhancing their image as an organised and better tanzeem organisation than others said a top officer of an antiterror unit based in Kashmir

Africa conflict series Sahel

 December  Jihane Boudiaf
This is the second in a series of three reports examining key conflicts in Africa in  The first on Ethiopia ran on  December
The Sahel region has witnessed an upward trend of jihadist attacks since  with the merger of several jihadist groups under the umbrella of Jamaat Nusrat alIslam walMuslimin JNIM which has pledged allegiance to AlQaeda in the Islamic Maghreb AQIM This is despite counterterrorism and peace building efforts engaged by Sahel countries and a number of international partners most notably France since 
JNIM attacks are very likely to expand deeper into Burkina Faso and Niger around the LiptakoGourma triborder area
The most prominent hotspot for jihadist and militia activity is triborder area between Mali Burkina Faso Niger known as the LiptakoGourma triborder area which has become the epicenter of jihadist activity in the Sahel However through  the insurgency has been spreading southwards towards Burkina Faso and to a lower extent Niger where jihadists have exploited poor intelligence and weak security forces Notable attacks have occurred in northern eastern and central Burkina Faso mainly targeting military police mining and humanitarian workers usually involving improvised explosive device IED followed up by smallarms assaults by jihadists

Deteriorating citizen safety political instability and local grievances stemming from poor governance and low economic opportunity will likely support the jihadist expansion
Local grievances over chronic and longlasting issues such as poverty political and security instability are likely to continue being key drivers of insecurity There is a correlation between the areas with intercommunal rivalries and the number of jihadist attacks Hotspots of both intercommunal violence and attacks in Mali include northern cities in and around Kidal Gao Timbuktu where the leader of the jihadist group Ansar Dine Iyad ag Ghaly has been advocating for the creation of an Azawad state Ethnic conflicts between the Dogon sedentary farmers and nomadic Fulani are likely to continue in the centre of Mali around Mopti In Burkina Faso land conflicts between the dominant Mossi and second largest group the Fulani is facilitating jihadist recruitment of Fulani Niger has been more successful at managing its ethnic conflicts compared with Mali and Burkina Faso probably because successive governments have been more inclusive Current hotspots of violence in the Tillaberi Tahoua regions in the west and Diffa in the southeast largely due to Islamic State activity
Low likelihood of dialogue between JNIM and governments resulting in a ceasefire in 
The is growing interest in dialogue from the JNIM and the governments of Mali Burkina Faso and Niger Even if these are initiated in  it very unlikely that insurgents will agree to a ceasefire More likely is an intensification of attacks to improve their negotiating position There is likely to be growing rivalry between the Islamic State in the Grand Sahara ISGS and AQIMaffiliated JNIM This will likely result in attempts to assert their respective leaderships by mounting attacks on security forces and government targets as well as kidnaping foreigners France is likely to be faced with growing regional hostility given its opposition to dialogue and its militarycentric counterinsurgency strategy
Posted  December  by Jihane Boudiaf Analyst Country Risk IHS Markit

KABUL Afghanistan  Acting Defense Secretary Christopher Miller visited Afghanistan on Wednesday the second senior defense official in a week to travel to the region amid ongoing Taliban violence against civilians and Afghan security forces
His mission he said was to make certain that Afghan President Ashraf Ghani understands we are still behind him despite the US troop drawdown there
Miller met with Army Gen Austin Scott Miller the commander of US and coalition forces in Afghanistan Ghani and US service members

The acting defense secretarys visit to the country follows a car bomb explosion Sunday in Kabul that killed nine people and wounded  others On Saturday militants fired five rockets onto Bagram Airfield in Parwan province the largest US base in Afghanistan from a small truck parked in a nearby village
Afghanistan continues to see violence against government forces and civilians by the Taliban and other terrorist groups such as the Islamic State A peace agreement in February between the United States and the Taliban laid out conditions for the Taliban to meet including reducing violence and stopping attacks on US and NATO troops The United States in return agreed to reduce the number of troops in the country
On Nov  Christopher Miller announced plans to reduce US forces in Afghanistan and Iraq by Jan  five days before Presidentelect Joe Biden is sworn into office The new administration would have  troops in Afghanistan and  in Iraq while the situation in both countries remains precarious
During the summer US troops in Afghanistan were reduced from  to  For the first time in the nearly year war there were now more NATO troops in the country than US troops according to a US military official There are now  NATO forces and  US forces
The United States as well its NATO allies have tried to get the Taliban to do more to reduce the violence according to a senior defense official who spoke on condition of anonymity
As to the levels of violence against the Afghan National Security Forces and civilians no the Taliban have not made those commitments And the violence has not been reduced he said

Army Gen Mark Milley the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff met last week with Taliban representatives in Doha Qatar where they are holding negotiations with the Afghan government For two hours he discussed the need for a reduction in violence in Afghanistan The Associated Press reported Milley has said he talks did not lead to any breakthroughs
Not only are attacks by the Taliban a concern for the Pentagon but so are alQaida and ISIS activities in the country
Zalmay Khalilzad the American special envoy for Afghan reconciliation has warned the violence is distressingly high and could threaten the peace agreement according to a recent Defense Department inspector general report on Afghanistan
Miller said he told Ghani that he was sorry for the attacks in the country and the Afghan people were paying the price for the violence

The peace negotiations between the Afghanistan government and Taliban representatives started in September after several months of delay
Its so much easier to start a war than it is to end one Miller said soon after he landed in Kabul I just think this is the real critical time in the peace process And Ghani is going to be the one to lead and have the courage to move forward on it
This is not Millers first time in Afghanistan He was among the first soldiers on the ground after the  terrorist attacks
I feel like the circle is complete This was the first time I was in combat I think I was at  years in the service and now to be here to see the contours and outlines of the war winding down and ending  Its pretty significant for me he said

The Pakistan Taliban Tehrike Taliban Pakistan TTP has released a propaganda video to showcase its attacks against Pakistani security forces in the past three months
The Urdulanguage video titled AlKarraroon which can be translated as The Persistent Attackers was released on  December by Umar Media the official media arm of the TTP It was published on the groups website and shared by alQaeda supporters on the messaging app Telegram
It is the fourth episode in a series of the same title covering TTP attacks against Pakistani government forces The first episode was released in June  the second in January  and the third in September 
The minute video features slick graphics and stunning scenes of nature and green mountains where the TTP militants are shown training or preparing for attacks
Such nature scenes could be designed to attract recruits who are looking for adventure and new places to see Jihadists often use in their propaganda a saying attributed to Prophet Muhammad indicating that jihad travelling to lands of jihad is the best tourism method
In addition to combat footage the video features mainstream clips of women protesting against enforced disappearances blamed on the state which the TTP tries to exploit in its rhetoric against the government in Pakistan
Footage of  attacks
The video contains footage of  attacks carried out by the TTP against Pakistani security forces mostly in the tribal districts of Bajaur South Waziristan and North Waziristan all of which border Afghanistan
The three areas fall under the newlyestablished tribal districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province formerly called the Federally Administered Tribal Areas FATA  the lawless tribal regions that served as the post bases of alQaeda TTP and their allies
The operations featured in the video include  improvised explosive device IED attacks eight raids and ambushes which include five crossborder attacks and one missile attack Eight of these attacks according to the video occurred in South Waziristan six in Bajaur four in North Waziristan and only one in Baluchistan province
All crossborder attacks were allegedly conducted from neighbouring Kunar province in Afghanistan Kunar has been a refuge for the TTP for over a decade The TTP militants from Swat Mohmand and Bajaur districts escaped there due to Pakistans military operations against the group
Attacks in three months
In the video the TTP claims to have conducted a total of  attacks in the past three months September October and November including the  attacks mentioned above
The listed attacks include  raids and ambushes  IED blasts  sniper attacks nine targeted killings three missile attacks and one suicide bombing
The video claims that the attacks caused  casualties with a breakdown of  deaths and  injuries It alleges that over  of the casualties  were military personnel  were police and  were paramilitary forces
The TTP says it cannot show footage of all the attacks for various reasons one of them being to ensure the safety and security of its members
Antistate propaganda
In addition to boasting about the TTPs recent attacks the video unsurprisingly features propaganda against the Pakistani government
The video criticises Pakistans role in the global war on terror and what it describes as the harm inflicted on ordinary people as a result of the armys pursuit of militants
The video features mainstream footage of Baloch women protesting against the state and demanding to know the fate of their missing family members Pakistani security forces are accused of enforced disappearances of hundreds of Baloch separatists and Islamist militants Although Baloch nationalists are ideological leftists and secular the TTP starting its video with the plight of the Baloch could be significant for two reasons
Firstly the women in the footage demanding the stop of abductions and the release of missing persons is vital for TTP The group claims that hundreds of its own members and supporters are also missing similar to the Baloch separatists Secondly the TTP has been trying for years to use the Baloch nationalists antistate grievances and sentiment in the hope of building momentum for action against the state
In connection to missing persons the video shows a mainstream religiouspolitical party leader Syed Munawar Hassan directly accusing the army of having a role in enforced disappearances Hassan was known for his controversial projihadist statements  publicly defending alQaeda and TTP  and for being a strong opponent of Pakistans post policies The propaganda videos of alQaeda and TTP often include snippets of his statements criticising the army and government
The video then features footage of action in  by police against female students of the Red Mosque seminary in Islamabad The controversial military operation against the Red Mosque in July  which continues to be exploited in jihadist propaganda resulted in open confrontation between proalQaeda Islamists and the Pakistani state eventually giving birth to the TTP in December that year
The video also blames the government for attacks on two other religious seminaries Jamia TalimulQuran in Rawalpindi in  and Jamia Zubairai in Peshawar in  However the sectarian riots targeted the first one while the Islamic State group IS remains the prime suspectin the latter
The video also shows Afia Siddiqi a Pakistani woman jailed in the US over alleged connections with alQaeda Siddiqi is frequently used in alQaeda and TTP propaganda against the state
An interesting aspect of this video is that it focuses on womens sufferings in the stateversusmilitants war blaming the state for womens plight The TTP may be trying to exploit notions of honour linked to women in the conservative Pakistani society to shame people into action against the state

By BBC Monitoring

Niger will hold presidential and parliamentary elections on  December amid political intrigues and a deepening security crisis fanned by Boko Haram and alQaeda and Islamic State militants in the Sahel
An estimated  million voters are eligible to cast their ballots
President Mahamadou Issouffou will be standing down after two fiveyear terms marking the first time Niger will be witnessing a democratic transfer of power
Issoufou has been praised for respecting presidential term limits at a time when other west African leaders are clinging to power He has handpicked exInterior Minister Mohamed Bazoum as candidate of his ruling Niger Party for Democracy and Socialism PNDS  Tarayya
Bazoum faces a weak challenge from a crowded field after the Constitutional Court rejected the candidacy of main opposition leader Hama Amadou over his conviction in relation to a  babytrafficking scandal In total the top court approved the applications of  presidential candidates
The opposition has rejected a biometric voters register audit endorsed by election observers alleging bias and exclusion from the process
Most presidential candidates have promised to address the jihadist insurgency particularly in regions bordering Nigeria Mali and Burkina Faso and tackle corruption that has hindered economic growth
Who are the main presidential candidates 
A presidential candidate wins in the first round if they secure  of all valid votes If none of the candidates wins outright the top two candidates in the first round will go to a runoff on  February 
Mohamed Bazoum

Bazoum alias the dolphin  served as interior minister from   when the country became embroiled in the current security crisis  until his nomination as PNDS flag bearer With his campaign managed by President Issoufous son Sani Mahamadou Issoufou Bazoum has vowed to consolidate the initiatives of the outgoing leader through the Renaissance Programme
On  December the high court dismissed an opposition petition seeking invalidation of his candidacy on allegations of fraudulently obtaining his birth certificate Bazoum rejected the allegations stating that he hails from the minority Arab communities that have been part of Niger for centuries
General Salou Djibo 

Gen retd Djibo  led the  coup against the late President Mamadou Tandja He will be vying under his newlyformed Peace Justice Progress PJP party
Djibo announced his retirement from the army in  after eschewing the political limelight since  when he handed over power to Issouffou following an election
Prior to joining the presidential race the former general was in charge of the Economic Community for West African States Ecowas task force on free trade
Seini Oumarou

Oumarou  has been serving as President Issoufous high representative since  That appointment has left some opposition supporters questioning his allegiance
However the former prime minister who is vying for the presidency for the third time has defended his opposition credentials saying he only cooperated with the ruling party under exceptional circumstances to forge unity in the fight against terrorism
He is vying under the National Movement for the Development of Society MNSD
What factors threaten the electoral process
There are fears that voters in border regions affected by jihadist attacks will not be able to participate in the upcoming polls due to insecurity which has affected delivery of voting equipment
In October  voter registration in parts of western Tillaberi and Tahoua regions was suspended after  people involved in the exercise in Alaba Tillaberi were killed by suspected terrorists
In the southeastern Diffa Region Boko Haram attacks are a persistent threat to the poll process On  December the group killed at least  people in Toumour village a day before local elections were held
There were reports of polling stations not opening for the local elections in parts of Diffa Tillaberi and Maradi southcentral Niger  due to delays in delivery of poll materials
The Constitutional Court has warned against criticism of its rulings adding that the recurrent attacks against the Court and its members have assumed unacceptable proportions in recent days
The National Independent Electoral Commission Ceni has been accused of favouring the ruling party allegations that it has denied The commission comprised of  commissioners has been accused of bias during auditing of the biometric voters list
Ecowas and African Union election observers have expressed concern over a climate of mistrust and called for dialogue between poll officials and political parties to guarantee a credible election
What is fuelling the security crisis
Lack of or limited state authority in marginalised border regions has enabled militants to build strong networks with locals that have facilitated attacks especially on security forces
Between December  and January  the Niger army suffered its biggest fatalities after over  soldiers were killed in Tillaberi The attacks were claimed by Islamic State IS militants
The presence of French Operation Barkhane and regional G Sahel troops has failed to cushion Niger from escalating jihadist attacks Most of the jihadist violence in Niger is a spill over of insurgencies in neighbouring Nigeria Mali and Burkina Faso
Corruption has also undermined the countrys fight against terrorism  A recent audit revealed that the military lost over m in fraudulent equipment procurement deals between  and 
Key media sources 
Niger is ranked last in the UNs Human Development Index which provides data on  countries The media scene is underdeveloped with poorlytrained journalists and underfunded private media outlets Internet penetration is among the lowest in the world
The print media publishes in French and primarily caters to the urban elites Radio broadcasts in French and Hausa and is popular in rural areas where the majority of the population lives
Office de Radiodifusion et Television du Niger ORTN company operates the state broadcaster  Tele Sahel and commercial channel Tal TV TeleSahel is the premier TV channel and most popular
ORTN also operates the state radio network La Voix du Sahel which has local stations in every province
Agence Nigerien de Presse the state news agency Niamey et les  jours a progovernment website privatelyowned Actu Niger the aNiamey news aggregator and Niamey et les Deux Jours are among the most popular online news sources
Source BBC Monitoring  Dec

Three police shot dead one wounded in central France Three police officers were shot dead and another wounded in central France on Wednesday after being called out to a domestic disturbance sources in the prosecutors office said A manhunt was under way for the suspect a yearold man who fled the scene The officers were shot as they attempted to rescue a woman in a house in an isolated hamlet near the village of SaintJust south of the city of ClermontFerrand Police had approached the house shortly after midnight and were targeted by gunfire The man initially shot and killed one officer and wounded another before setting fire to the house Two further officers responding to the scene were then fired on and killed according to the prosecutors office in ClermontFerrand The woman was safely rescued and was being questioned by police Police reinforcements were rushed to the scene and all roads leading to the house were blocked off Firefighters are also at the site attempting to control the blaze The gunman is said to be known to authorities for charges relating to child custody issues The greatest precautions are being taken with regard to the dangerousness of the individual a source close to the investigation told AFP The local prefecture said police had approached the house to deal with a domestic violence situation Aside from terror attacks shootings of police officers in France are relatively rare Last May a man fired at police from his house in the Gironde region of southwest France wounding one officer As he was about to fire again he was shot dead by police

SAINTJUST France  Three police officers were killed and a fourth wounded in central France on  Wednesday when a man opened fire as they responded to a domestic violence call the deadliest attack in years on French security forces outside of terrorism incidentsThe suspect a yearold man known to authorities for child custody disputes and identified only as Frederik L was found dead several hours after fleeing the home in an isolated hamlet near SaintJust a village of some  people south of ClermontFerrand Interior Minister Gerald Darmanin saidHe was very determined to create a massacre the prosecutor in the case Eric Maillaud told a news conferenceHe said the man had been heavily armed and police found hundreds and hundreds of cartridge cases at the sceneIt was truly like a war zone Maillaud saidDarmanin who travelled to the scene called the killing one of the most tragic events in the history of Frances Gendarmes force which often ensures law enforcement in rural areas Amateur shooter  The prosecutor said that the suspect fled the scene by car but about  kilometres  away lost control of the vehicle which veered off the road and tumbled down a slopeSome  police searched for hours for the man eventually locating the car and his body next to itHe wore a bulletproof vest and police found an arsenal of weapons including a Glock pistol an assault rifle with a silencer a flare a laserguided targeting device and four knivesEarly indications were that he killed himself with one of his weapons according to a preliminary coroners reportAt the house Frederik L had opened fire at two officers who arrived there shortly after midnight after being alerted to a reported domestic assaultOne was killed immediately and the other shot in the thigh before the man set fire to the house where a woman had climbed onto the roofPolice reinforcements and firefighters were rushed to the scene and all roads leading to the house were blocked offTwo other police who were trying to determine if rescue officers could reach their shot colleagues were then fired on and killed by the suspect who had barricaded himself in the houseHe was an amateur shooter a police source said History of violence  Darmanins deputy Marlene Schiappa told BFM television that the woman herself had called police to say she was being threatened adding that the husband appeared to have a history of violenceThe woman and her child were safely rescuedThe officers killed gendarmes from Frances military police were identified as Arno Mavel  Remi Dupuis  and Cyrille Morel They leave behind widows and a total of four children Darmanin saidOur security forces put their lives at risk to protect us These are our heroes President Emmanuel Macron said in a tweetAside from terror attacks shootings of policeThe most recent killings of officers in the line of duty excluding terrorism occurred in June  when two female officers died in Collobrieres southern France while intervening in a dispute Wednesday that  police have been killed in the line of duty this yearAmong the most highprofile incidents in recent months two undercover officers were shot during a surveillance operation in a Paris suburb in October while later that month a station outside Paris was attacked by dozens of people armed with powerful fireworks and steel bars

MADRID  EUROPA PRESS   At least one police officer has been killed and two others wounded in Kabul in the explosion of a car bomb while the head of the NGO Forum for Free and Fair Election in Afghanistan was killed on Wednesday by gunmen also in the Afghan capital   Kabul police have confirmed the detonation of a police vehicle at about  local time when an improvised explosive device has reached the car   For his part the brother of Yousuf Rashid head of the Forum for Free and Fair Election of Afghanistan has confirmed his death at the hands of unknown gunmen also on Wednesday according to local television network Tolo News   Rashid was leaving his home in police district seven for a press conference when he was attacked while his driver has also been injured in the incident   These deaths occur just one day after five other people died and two others were injured in the explosion of a mine in Kabul   In recent days the Afghan capital has once again been the scene of constant attacks such as the one that killed ten people and left more than  wounded on Monday after a strike against the convoy of a member of parliament in the capital Haji Khan Mohammad Wardak who was able to get out alive   More than  attacks have been recorded in Kabul in the past two months in the midst of a escalation of violence leaving some  people dead and nearly  injured   So far no group has claimed the authorship of the attacks   Despite the peace agreement signed on  February in Doha and talks with the Afghan government currently taking place in the Qatari capital the Taliban have maintained their campaign of attacks on Afghan security forces and refused to accept a ceasefire to facilitate the dialogue process

Gunmen have killed more than  people in a dawn attack in the western BenishangulGumuz region of Ethiopia according to the countrys human rights commission
The attack occurred on Wednesday in the village of Bekoji in Bulen county in the Metekel zone the staterun Ethiopian Human Rights Commission said in a statement an area where multiple ethnic groups are living
Africas secondmost populous nation has been grappling with regular outbreaks of deadly violence since Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed was appointed in  and accelerated democratic reforms that loosened the states iron grip on regional rivalries
Elections due next year have further inflamed simmering tensions over land power and resources
In a separate part of the country Ethiopias military has been fighting rebels in the northern Tigray region for more than six weeks in a conflict that has displaced close to  people
The deployment of federal troops there has raised fears of a security vacuum in other restive regions
Ethiopia is also experiencing unrest in the Oromia region and faces longrunning security threats from Somali fighters along its porous eastern border
Gashu Dugaz a senior regional security official told the Reuters news agency authorities were aware of the BenishangulGumuz attack and were verifying the identities of the attackers and the victims but did not give further information
The region is home to several ethnic groups including the Gumuz people
But in recent years farmers and businessmen from the neighbouring Amhara region have begun moving into the area prompting some Gumuz to complain that fertile land has been taken
 
 
Some Amhara leaders are now saying some of the lands in the region  especially in the Metekel zone  rightfully belongs to them claims that have angered Gumuz people
In previous attacks it was people who came from the forest who were involved but in this case victims said they knew the people involved in the attack the rights commission said in its statement
Bodies in a field
Belay Wajera a farmer in the western town of Bulen told Reuters he counted  dead bodies in a field near his home after Wednesdays raid
He and his family awoke to the sound of gunshots and ran out of their home as men shouted catch them he said
His wife and five of his children were shot dead he was shot in the buttocks while four other children escaped and are now missing Wajera told Reuters by phone late on Wednesday
Another resident of the town Hassen Yimama said armed men stormed the area at about am local time  GMT
He told Reuters he counted  bodies in a different location He grabbed his own weapon but attackers shot him in the stomach
A local medic said he and colleagues treated  injured people most suffering from gunshot wounds
Patients told him of relatives who were killed with knives and told him attackers set houses on fire and shot at people trying to escape he said
We werent prepared for this and we are out of medicine a nurse at the same facility told Reuters adding that a fiveyearold child died while being transferred to the clinic
The attack came a day after Abiy the military chief of staff and other senior federal officials visited the region to urge calm after several deadly incidents in recent months such as a November  assault in which attackers targeted a bus and killed  people
The desire by enemies to divide Ethiopia along ethnic and religious lines still exists This desire will remain unfulfilled Abiy tweeted on Tuesday along with photos of his meetings that day in the town of Metekel near where the November  attack occurred
He said residents wish for peace outweighs any divisive agenda

After more than a decade fighting for the Taliban and being hounded by Afghan and US forces Haji Lala thought there was little chance of ever returning home
Once a commander and senior district official for the insurgent group he says he was captured by Pakistans security services who took him across the border and detained him for two and a half years
Haji Lala said he was interrogated by the agents  longterm backers of the Taliban  for information about a spy working against the group
When he was released the yearold vowed to put his militant years behind him and look for a way to go back home
It was with the unlikely support of a police chief and the encouragement of a fellow former Taliban militant that he was given the opportunity to return home to the southern province of Kandahar





Haji Lala has vowed to put his militant years behind him after returning home
 AFP  WAKIL KOHSAR



I thought maybe they would hand me over to the US troops said Lala describing his initial trepidation at trusting a police officer
Before being captured US forces he had battled against had raided his house nearly  times
After I returned friends and villagers visited me for nearly  days as if there was a wedding party he told AFP 
I have a good reputation now in the village and the police are also not troubling me I feel absolutely safe
Haji Lalas return early this year was made possible because of the protection of the former police chief of Panjwai district Sultan Mohammad Hakimi
Despite the bloodshed he has witnessed throughout his career Hakimi has made it a personal mission to give exTaliban fighters commanders and officials the chance to reintegrate into village life





Former police chief of the Panjwai district Sultan Mohammad Hakimi has made it a personal mission to give exTaliban fighters commanders and officials the chance to reintegrate into village life
 AFP  WAKIL KOHSAR



We invited the former fighters to return assuring them that nobody would harass them said Hakimi
Those whose farms were destroyed we rebuilt them those who had no water we dug wells for them
Even in retirement Hakimi has continued an effort first launched by former Kandahar police chief General Abdul Raziq a fierce opponent of the insurgents who was assassinated in 
Raziqs brother Tadin Khan Achakzai has since joined the effort after taking over as police chief of the province





Hundreds of Taliban fighters have defected from the group but it still has tens of thousands of members
 AFP  WAKIL KOHSAR



We will continue to help them in the future they are our brothers too said Achakzai
If we have the right to live so does the Taliban  but to live in peace not to carry out suicide attacks and kill people
For Hakimi it is a way of contributing to a reconciliation process and also of weakening the leadership of the Taliban
During his time as Panjwai police chief Hakimi launched insurgentclearing operations in almost every village in the district making it one of the most secure areas in Kandahar
But with violence surging in Afghanistan the progress is fragile  with the Taliban last month retaking part of Panjwai in a major offensive
The Taliban ruled Afghanistan from  to  with an iron fist imposing a harsh version of the Islamic sharia law
Ousted by a USled invasion after the September  attacks the jihadists were able to regroup launching a deadly insurgency that continues to this day
In February the Taliban signed a deal with Washington that paved the way for the withdrawal of all foreign forces by May  and the start of peace negotiations between the insurgents and the Afghan government in Qatar 
Hundreds of Taliban fighters have defected from the group but it still has tens of thousands of members and claims to have influence over more than half of Afghanistan
Several previous efforts to help reintegrate Taliban fighters had failed as they were sporadic said Andrew Watkins of conflict think tank International Crisis Group 
They were never able to convince the higherup commanders to bring a lot of their fighters along with them Watkins told AFP
Taliban commander Mullah Rauf  had fought for more than half of his life before he returned from Pakistan to resettle in Panjwai and return to farming
He chose the same path as Haji Lala contacting Hakimi rather than surrendering to authorities in order to save himself from any problems such as a possible jail term
Haji Ahmadullah Khan  now lives in an upscale area of Kandahar after emerging from a militant lifestyle
I go everywhere to my village or in the city without any problem I have no weapons or bodyguards now said the former insurgent as he watched his son chatting and laughing with a son of Hakimi at the expolice officers house

fire at two officers who arrived at the house shortly after midnight after being alerted to a reported domestic assault One was killed immediately and the other shot in the thigh before the man set fire to the house where a woman had climbed onto the roof Police reinforcements and firefighters were rushed to the scene and all roads leading to the house were blocked off according to the prosecutors office in ClermontFerrand Two further police who were trying to determine if rescue officers could reach their shot colleagues were then fired on and killed by the suspect who had police which often ensures law enforcement in rural areas were identified as Arno Mavel  Remi Dupuis  and Cyrille Morel  Our security forces put their lives at risk to protect us These are our heroes ISLAMABAD  Officials in Afghanistan say gunmen Wednesday killed the head of an independent elections watchdog in Kabul the latest casualty in a string of mostly unclaimed recent attacks against prominent civilians
The violence has claimed the lives of dozens of people particularly in the Afghan capital The victims include civil society activists journalists politicians and government officials
Police said Mohammad Yousuf Rasheed executive director of the Free and Fair Election Forum of Afghanistan FEFA was traveling to his office in the city when unknown assailants sprayed his vehicle with bullets The attack also left his driver wounded
Elsewhere in Kabul officials said a bomb attached to a police vehicle went off killing an officer in the vehicle and injuring two others
The United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan or UNAMA condemned Rasheeds assassination and other attacks against so many outstanding citizens urging authorities to bring to justice those responsible
Targeted killings of civilians are taking place at a deeply disturbing rate in Afghanistan said a mission statement
UNAMA noted that in the last four days alone the conflicttorn country has seen the killing of a lawmaker as well as a wellknown journalist and a group of medics
Such dreadful attacks are rarely claimed and frequently focus on those working for an open society it said
The bomb blast on medics was however claimed by the Afghan branch of Islamic State terror group The attack killed three doctors and two other persons onboard a vehicle that was targeted
The United States also denounced Rasheeds assassination I am appalled by his murder another in a cacophony of senseless  endless violence My condolences to all those who knew him tweeted Ross Wilson the acting US ambassador in Kabul
Wilson hailed Rasheed as a dedicated and steadfast advocate for representative democracy in Afghanistan
He worked tirelessly for years to ensure free  transparent elections that engaged all Afghans His death is a loss for his family friends  nation the US ambassador said
Critics fear the wave of targeted killings and increased battlefield hostilities between Afghan security forces and the Taliban insurgency could derail ongoing USbrokered peace negotiations between the two adversaries
The slowmoving dialogue started September  in Qatar and a second phase is expected to resume next month after a threeweek break The recent spike in violence is seen as a threat to the Afghan peace process
The UN repeats its call for a sustained reduction in violence Lives and gains must be protected with spoilers prevented from undermining the vital peace negotiations due to resume  January UNAMA said in its statement

  We have decided to make the ability to comment only available to our  paying subscribers That way all the trolls who post abuse on our website will have to pay if they want to join the debate  and risk a permanent ban from the account that they subscribe with


  The conversation will go back to what it should be about  people who care passionately about the issues but disagree constructively on what we should do about them


  Well be monitoring this change over the first few weeks and were keen to know your thoughts Email us at lettersthenationalscot if you want to have your say

Interpol a global organization linking the worlds law enforcement entities warned in a report announced Tuesday that global terrorist organizations and nonstate actors were attempting to take advantage of the chaos surrounding the Chinese coronavirus pandemic to become more influential
Interpol noted that the full report was for law enforcement use only but in its statement on the reports completion asserted that the organization had reason to be concerned about the benefits the pandemic may have created for terrorist organizations
Early in the pandemic certain terrorist groups and other NSAs nonstate actors used the pandemic to reinforce their power and influence particularly among local populations or to expand their external financial resources Interpol warned The report also highlights how the impact of COVID Chinese coronavirus on the global economy is likely to indirectly affect funding available to terrorist organizations
Interpol stated its report also found reason to believe extreme lockdown measures implemented to prevent the spread of the virus could aid terrorist organizations by triggering civil unrest
As COVID cases subside in some regions and surge in others the report underlines the critical need to monitor the reaction and response by terrorist networks violent extremist groups and other potentially dangerous NSAs Interpol noted
The Interpol public release on the report bizarrely identified farright supporters in the West as a major cause of concern regarding terrorism exacerbated by the pandemic
Law enforcement will continue to face attempts by farright violent extremists to radicalize social movements such as clashing with farleft groups andor provoking the use of force Interpol stated
The Interpol report did not mention radical Islamic terrorist organizations which ample evidence throughout the year suggests are elevating their influence and profile as civilians lose their basic civil rights in lockdowns Atop the list of jihadist groups who have become more active during the pandemic is Boko Haram the Nigerian terrorist organization that Nigerian government officials have insisted for the past five years no longer exists Boko Harams victims have vocally disputed this assessment particularly after Boko Haram claimed responsibility for the mass kidnapping of hundreds of schoolboys in the latter half of this year
Nigeria Cameroon and Chad began documenting an increase in Boko Haram attacks in April as regional governments imposed lockdowns forcing civilians to stay home The jihadists began increasing the frequency of village raids and attacks on schools  Boko Haram which roughly translates to Western education is a sin in Hausa opposes the institution of education outside of jihadist indoctrination While those attacks mostly occurred in areas where Boko Haram is known to operate more recent attacks have occurred in states that did not previously document a significant Boko Haram presence
In December Boko Haram took responsibility for one of the largest mass abductions of children in Nigerian history  the kidnapping of nearly  boys from a school in northern Katsina state Boko Haram was founded in Borno state Nigerias most northeastern region and typically operates in Borno and Adamawa state Katsina is significantly west of Borno triggering concerns that the terrorist groups operational abilities have expanded
Nigerian officials claimed last week that they had successfully liberated the children in question Reports differ on whether Boko Haram chose to free them independently or if the jihadists received a ransom
While the Islamic Stateaffiliated Boko Haram expands its attacks the core Islamic State group has reportedly also attempted to take advantage of lockdowns to try to rebuild in the Middle East
The Islamic State group has been moving the fighting from Syria to Iraq  and is strengthening both financially and militarily Lt Col Stein Grongstad head of Norways forces in Iraq told NBC News in May
A spokesman for the Islamic State Abu Hamza alQurashi openly celebrated the pandemic in a speech published that month
We rejoice today with the great torment of God that befell you alQurashi said addressing the nonMuslim world  A greater punishment will befall you with our hands What you are seeing today is nothing but indications of major transformations that the Muslim countries will witness in the coming period
The most highprofile jihadist attack to occur this year was the beheading of Samuel Paty a French schoolteacher on October  Paty had recently used illustrations of Muhammad to teach a class on freedom of expression angering local Muslims in the suburbs of Paris French law enforcement officials had warned of increased jihadist activity during the nations strict coronavirus lockdowns as early as in April
In Asia the government of India warned the public in November that the Chinese coronavirus pandemic may allow for increased support of terrorist organizations accusing neighboring Pakistan of heightening its terrorist operations
While the world has come to a standstill due to the pandemic but sic Pakistan has only enhanced support to crossborder terrorism taking advantage of the pandemic Ashish Sharma an Indian diplomat told the United Nations General Assembly Pakistan has resorted to unbridled hate speech trying to foment violence and intolerance in our country
Pakistani officials denied the allegations and have similarly accused India of illicit activity

Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar  the Afghan Talibans deputy chief  met the groups members in Karachi yesterday and said that he had been receiving guidance from their leaders in Pakistan the private Tolo News TV has reported
When we conduct partial or general negotiations there Doha we share the whole process with the leaders and the Ulema council here Baradar reportedly said in a video being circulated on social media
Our entire leadership is present here in this place Pakistan Tolo News TV further quoted him as saying
Many Afghan officials and analysts called Baradars remark an open acknowledgement of Pakistans influence on the Taliban
They were already there but now they have confessed it For this reason the role of Pakistan has been critical in the process Haji Din Mohammad the deputy head of Afghanistans High Council for National Reconciliation said
Pakistan has not put any new pressure on the Taliban to accept the ceasefire or reduce violence said Sami Yousufzai a freelance journalist told Tolo News TV
Afghan officials have long accused Pakistan of funding and sheltering Taliban militants  an accusation that Islamabad denies
President Ghani meets acting US defence secretary
Afghan President Ashraf Ghani met the Acting US Defence Secretary Christopher Miller during the latters unannounced trip to Kabul yesterday

During the meeting  which was also attended by Afghan VicePresident Amrullah Saleh  Miller stressed on strengthening the strategic relationship between Afghanistan and the United States the Afghan presidential palace said in a statement
President Ghani articulated that the Afghan government has taken practical steps to ensure peace and now onus is on the Taliban to prove their commitments for peace it added
The US Defence Department meanwhile said that Ghani and Miller had discussed continued American support for Afghan security forces and the importance of achieving a reduction in violence to advance the peace process
The meeting comes during a threeweek pause in peace talks between the Afghan government and the Taliban in Qatar
Concerns over attacks on journalists
Several Afghan and international journalists and watchdog groups have reiterated concerns over the recent spate of attacks on media personnel in Afghanistan
Commenting on the killing of journalist Rehmatullah Nikzad  shot dead in Ghazni province on  December  Amnesty International urged the Afghan government to carry out a thorough investigation
The perpetrators must be brought to justice through fair trials without recourse to death penalty it said
Mujib Khalwatgar  the head of the Afghan advocacy group Nai  told Tolo News TV The Afghan government has failed to ensure the safety of journalists The government has not done anything to prevent violence against journalists and investigate cases involving journalists
Ross Wilson  the US Charg dAffaires to Afghanistan  also called for an end to the endless cycle of violence and attempts to silence Afghanistans courageous reporters
Over the past two months six Afghan journalists have died  four in IED blasts or gunmen attacks and two in what were reported as questionable or mysterious circumstances
See Timeline Attacks on media journalists in Afghanistan
Afghan Taliban officials criticise Irans interference
Iranian Foreign Minister Javad Zarifs remarks  made during an interview aired on Tolo News TV on Monday  December  are drawing condemnation
During the interview Zarif said that the Afghans fighting in Syria had gone there voluntarily to fight for their beliefs

See Irans foreign minister criticises US role in Afghan peace
Speaking to Tolo News TV about Zarifs remarks Gran Hewad  a spokesman for the Afghan Foreign Ministry  said Afghanistans foreign policy does not allow Afghan nationals to engage in regional wars and conflicts in countries except under the Afghan flag
The Taliban meanwhile focussed their criticism on Zarifs comments about the group being a UNdesignated terrorist outfit calling them an open interference in Afghanistans internal affairs 
The Islamic Emirate is not in any UN terror list and comments by Iranian Foreign Minister in this regard are based on faulty information Such irresponsible and misconceived remarks by Iranian officials have the potential of harming relations between two friendly and neighbouring countries the group said in a statement published on the Voice of Jihad website yesterday
Security incidents
Yousuf Rashid  the head of the Afghan electoral watchdog Free and Fair Election Forum of Afghanistan FEFA  died after being wounded in an armed attack in Kabul this morning the private Tolo News TV and Channel One TV TV are reporting
In a series of tweets the news channels reported that the FEFA chief executive was attacked by unidentified gunmen in Kabuls Police District 
No group or individual has so far claimed responsibility for the attack which is the latest in a spate of targeted killings of prominent Afghan officials journalists and media personnel
In an earlier incident  also in Kabul  at least one police officer was killed and two others were wounded in an IED explosion Tolo News TV reported citing a statement by Kabul police
The blast took place at approximately  local time  gmt this morning in the citys Police District 
No group has so far claimed responsibility for this incident either

New Covid cases
The Afghan Health Ministry announced yesterday that it had recorded  new cases of Covid in  samples tested over the past  hours
Sixteen more people died from the infection in this period Tolo News TV reported citing Health Ministry figures
So far  Covid cases  including  deaths and nearly  recoveries  have been recorded in Afghanistan
Roughly  of these cases are currently active
