By BBC Monitoring
A large number of people are said to have been killed in a series of blasts which rocked the airport in Yemens interim capital Aden as members of the newlyformed government arrived from the Saudi capital Riyadh privatelyowned Aden alGhad news website reported on  December
The report quoted sources as saying that the government members had been quickly transferred to the Maashiq presidential palace in the city
Ambulances and medical teams rushed to the scene to treat the large number of people who were injured in the explosions
Yemens new cabinet lineup was announced earlier this month as part of a Saudibrokered peace agreement between the internationallyrecognised government and the UAEbacked separatist Southern Transitional Council STC which was signed over a year ago
The government left Aden after the STC seized control of the city amid deadly clashes in the summer of  It had been based in the southern port city since  after a coalition led by Saudi Arabia launched a campaign of aerial bombardment against the Houthi rebel movement which had seized control of the capital Sanaa in September the previous year
Source Aden alGhad website Aden in Arabic  gmt  Dec

By BBC Monitoring
Turkish warplanes and artillery bombarded several areas in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq on  December for the second consecutive day according to reports
According to a report by privately owned NRT website on the same day Turkish artillery fired at areas around the village of Kist which lies in the Kani Masi Subdistrict Duhok province
The report added that Turkish warplanes also bombed the Gara mountains in the province
No casualties were mentioned in the report which said that the raids had caused panic among local residents
The previous day a local official told the Iraqi Kurdistan Democratic Partyaffiliated Rudaw website that Turkish warplanes had bombed uninhabited mountainous areas of Duhok Province earlier that day
Turkey carries out regular air and ground assaults in border areas ostensibly targeting Turkeys Kurdish rebel group the Kurdistan Workers Party PKK which Ankara considers a terrorist organisation
On  December Rudaw reported that  civilians had been killed in Amedi in the last three years in clashes between Turkey and the PKK
The PKK seeks autonomy for the Kurds in southeastern Turkey and has been involved in conflict with Turkish authorities for  years on its own territory and from inside border areas of the Kurdistan Region
Source Rudaw in Sorani Kurdish  gmt  Dec

By BBC Monitoring
Fifteen people were killed and  injured in a series of blasts targeting Aden international airport as government ministers arrived on a flight from Saudi Arabia local media reports
The latest figures were from medical sources speaking to privatelyowned Aden alGhad news website on  December
The website also quoted the deputy head of the Aden health department Dr Mohammed Rubaid as saying that the citys AlJumhouri hospital had received  injured people and the bodies of seven more He added that the Saber and Buraihi hospitals had received a total of  casualties and eight bodies
The cabinet ministers were reported to be unharmed
The blasts occurred as a plane carrying the newly sworn in cabinet arrived at the airport from the Saudi capital Riyadh The new government was announced earlier this month as part of a long delayed Saudibrokered peace agreement between the internationallyrecognised government and the UAEbacked separatist Southern Transitional Council STC
The deal aimed to resolve a power struggle between the two sides which had opened up a new front in the countrys conflict 
The STC captured Aden in summer  forcing the government to leave It had been based in the southern port city since  after a coalition led by Saudi Arabia launched a campaign of aerial bombardment against the Houthi rebel movement which had seized control of the capital Sanaa in September the previous year
Information Minister Muammar alEryani accused the Houthi rebels of being behind the attack on the airport
But one of his advisors hinted at continued underlying tensions between the government and the STC Mokhtar alRahbi asked in a tweet If the attack was carried out by missiles where is the Patriot surfacetoair missile system He said that the STC and the Saudiled coalition were responsible for Adens security adding that they were therefore to blame for any security failures
The government must take decisive action to transfer the security file from the STC militias and announce the results of the investigation into this cowardly criminal incident said Rahbi
Source BBC Monitoring in Arabic  gmt  Dec

Text of report by DR Congos UNsponsored Radio Okapi on  December
Presenter A fresh attack attributed to the Ugandan ADF Allied Democratic Forces has been reported in Nzenga a village neighbouring the town of Mutwanga capital of Ruwenzori sector Beni territory Nord Kivu province eastern DR Congo
According to local security and administrative sources the provisional toll indicates three civilians killed and some shops plundered by the assailants
Many inhabitants have abandoned the area Meanwhile the FARDC DR Congo Armed Forces have reinforced their presence
Martial Papy Mukeba reports
Mukeba The attack on Nzenga occurred last night Tuesday  December at around h local time
Local security and administrative sources in the village say the assailants killed three civilians before torching a residence and looting some shops The ADF combatants then attempted to attack Mutwanga the chief town of Ruwenzori but in vain meeting resistance from the FARDC
The assailants then headed towards the village of Mutsura where they attempted to attack the Congolese Nature Conservation Institute ICCN station They were repulsed after an exchange of fire with the Eco guards
According to military sources violent clashes continued between the FARDC and the ADF in Loselose until Tuesday evening
The army and the assailants are fighting for control of the village the breadbasket of Beni territory where there are many plantations of cacao and banana
Source Radio Okapi Goma in French  Dec

By BBC Monitoring
Iraqi security forces have killed an Islamic State IS militant who sought to carry out a suicide bomb attack in Diyala Province
The security forces seized the militants explosive belt in an operation northwest of Baqubah the provincial capital of Diyala a security source told the Kurdish website Shafaq News on  December

The source added that a force from Diyala intelligence managed to kill the wouldbe suicide bomber who had planned to blow himself up and target people celebrating the New Year in Baqubah
Meanwhile the National Security Service had announced a few days ago the arrest of a wouldbe suicide bomber and three other militants who were plotting an attack during the New Year holiday in Baghdad
Although Iraq declared victory over IS in December  the militant group has continued to carry out attacks across the country prompting security forces to occasionally launch operations to track them down
Source Shafaq News website Baghdad in Arabic  gmt  Dec

An explosive drone was shot down in the area around the presidential palace in Yemens interim capital Aden Saudifunded Al Arabiya TV has reported in a breaking news caption
It comes hours after a deadly series of blasts rocked the citys international airport as the government arrived on a plane from Saudi Arabia
A short time earlier local residents had reported a heavy blast in the vicinity of Maashiq Presidential Palace where the cabinet ministers are said to have been transferred following the airport attack
It comes amid reports that the death toll from the explosions at Aden International Airport have risen to around  with some  people reportedly injured Privatelyowned AlMasdar Online news website quoted the figures from medical and security officials adding that two officials were among the casualties
Ministry of Labour Undersecretary Yasmin alAwadhi was killed while Deputy Minister of Youth and Sport Moneer alWajeeh were and Deputy Transport Minister Nasser Sharif were among the injured AlMasdar said
It added that a Sudanese soldier had also been killed while the spokesperson for the International Committee of the Red Cross Yara Khawaja was injured Also among the casualties were travellers hoping to take a flight to the Egyptian capital Cairo following the arrival of the governments flight AlMasdar said
Al Arabiya reported that one journalist was killed and four others injured
Source BBC Monitoring in Arabic  gmt  Dec

By BBC Monitoring
The Yemeni information minister has accused the Houthi rebels of being behind a series of deadly explosions targeting Aden International Airport on  December
In tweets in Arabic and English Muammar alEryani said that all cabinet members were safe and that the cowardly terrorist attack by the Houthis would not deter the government from carrying out its duties
Prime Minister Mueen Abdulmalek Saeed also gave assurances that he and his ministers were well in a post on Twitter He said that the attack was part of the war being waged against the Yemeni state and its great people He added It only increases our determination to carry out our duties in defeating the Houthi rebels and restoring stability
The prime minister also expressed his condolences for those killed in the attack and wished a speedy recovery to the injured
Saudifunded Al Arabiya TV cited preliminary information that more than  people had been killed and injured in the blasts including a number of journalists Its sister channel AlHadath aired footage of the moment of the attack as a correspondent at the airport spoke to a presenter in the studio
The blasts occurred as a plane carrying the newly sworn in cabinet ministers arrived at the airport from the Saudi capital Riyadh The new government was announced earlier this month as part of a long delayed Saudibrokered peace agreement between the internationallyrecognised government and the UAEbacked separatist Southern Transitional Council STC
Privatelyowned AlMasdar Online news website quoted a source at the airport as saying that the first of three explosions occurred as a number of people accompanying the ministers were descending from the aircraft
The government had been based in Aden since  after a coalition led by Saudi Arabia launched a campaign of aerial bombardment against the Houthi rebel movement which had seized control of the capital Sanaa in September the previous year
Source BBC Monitoring  Dec

Algeria seizes ransom funds from jihadists
The Algerian army has said that during an operation in the northeastern province of Jijel it seized  euros paid as ransom to jihadist groups On  December the Algerian Ministry of National Defence said the seized funds turned out to be the first instalment of a ransom received by alleged terrorists following a deal last October in the Sahel region
The army carried out the operation after receiving information from a jihadist who was arrested on  December Algeria arrested two militants who were freed as part of a reported deal to free three European hostages and a Malian opposition leader in Mali in October
One of the men was quoted by the Algerian daily Liberte Algerie as saying that France allegedly paid a ransom of m euros to the alQaedaaligned Sahelbased group Jamaat Nusrat alIslam walMuslimin JNIM aka Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims  GSIM to free over  jihadists

IS video shows killing of five Nigerian Christian captives
Islamic State IS released on  December a new video showing the killing of five Christian men whom the group said it captured recently in Borno northeastern Nigeria The video produced by the jihadist groups news outlet Amaq featured a militant saying that the killing was an act of revenge and was intended as a message to Christians in Nigeria and the rest of the world RocketChat messaging service  Dec

Is Boko Haram Gaining Foothold in Nigerias NorthwestBy Sirwan KajjoDecember    PMBoko Harams claim of responsibility for a recent kidnapping of more than  students in Nigerias northwestern state of Katsina signals that the militant group is expanding its terror activities beyond its traditional stronghold in the West African countrys northeast experts warnOn December  Boko Harams leader Abubakar Shekau said in an audio recording that his group was behind the abduction of the schoolboys in the town of Kankara in Katsina The students however were released several days after being abducted by gunmenThe militant group also released a video showing some of the students before their releaseRegardless of whether Boko Haram was responsible for the kidnappings some experts say the incident represents a worrying sign for stability and security in northern NigeriaShekau has been able to claim it and that is in part because northwest Nigeria has been facing a simmering security crisis over the last year said Daniel Eizenga an expert on violent extremism at the Africa Center for Strategic Studies in WashingtonIn recent months northwestern Nigeria has witnessed growing intercommunal violence including conflict between herders and farmers violent crime from bandits and initial indications that extremist groups may be gaining ground in the areaWithin this complicated context of rising insecurity it is possible for Boko Haram to appear more dangerous and expansive than it may actually be Eizenga told VOAHe added that should the trajectory of northwest Nigeria follow a similar path as the northeast much of northern Nigeria will have become embroiled in a security crisis that has been simmering for the better part of the past decadeBoko Haram which has been fighting to create an Islamic state based in Nigeria has killed  people and displaced millions since it began its insurgency a decade agoDespite carrying out terror attacks in neighboring Cameroon Chad and Niger  mostly in the Lake Chad Basin  the groups activities inside Nigeria have largely remained limited to its stronghold in the northeastVarious hypothesesWhile the Nigerian government hasnt confirmed whether Boko Haram was responsible for kidnapping students in Katsina experts say there are several hypotheses for a possible Boko Haram presence in Nigerias northwestOne is that a faction of Boko Haram might well have contracted with a criminal gang to carry out the kidnapping without actually doing it itself said John Campbell a senior fellow for Africa policy studies at the Council on Foreign Relations in WashingtonAnother hypothesis is that Boko Haram simply claimed responsibility for the kidnapping as part of a propaganda initiative he told VOA adding that another possibility of course is that indeed Boko Haram has become active in the northwestHowever Campbell a former US ambassador to Nigeria stressed that if were going to talk about Boko Haram being active in the northwest I think we need some evidence of a political or ideological dimensionOther jihadist groups have in the past carried out attacks in northwest Nigeria For example the Ansaru a Boko Haram breakaway group has claimed responsibility for several attacks in the area in Government responseThe recent developments in the northwest should be a cause for the Nigerian security forces to redouble their efforts in the region especially with regards to intelligence said Gbenga Akinbule a Nigerian affairs analystThe fact that Boko Haram might be present in the northwest requires a serious response from the Nigerian military he saidOur security forces should go back there to clean up and see how best they can get to look at the dangerous trend that is happening Akinbule told VOAAnalyst Eizenga disagreesApproaching the growing insecurity in the northwest with heavyhanded operations that neutralize militants and destroy their camps is unlikely to resolve the main drivers of these different security threats he saidEizenga suggested that the Nigerian government needs to work closely with local communities to develop differentiated responses to the threats they are facingIn late  Nigerian President Muhammadu Buhari said his military had technically defeated Boko Haram militants in the countryVOA Hausa Services Sani Malumfashi contributed to this story from Katsina Nigeria

During the reporting period the security situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo was characterized by pockets of intense violence In this context in early October  President Flix Tshisekedi made a threeday visit to Goma holding a series of consultations and chairing a minisummit including on security issues with the Heads of States of Angola Rwanda and Uganda
In North Kivu operations of the Forces armes de la Rpublique dmocratique du Congo Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo FARDC scattered the Allied Democratic Forces ADF into several mobile groups and extended the ADF area of operations While supply chains were disrupted ADF continued to attack FARDC and civilians ADF demonstrated improved knowledge of improvised explosive device construction techniques While Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant ISIL claimed responsibility for many attacks in Beni territory the Group of Experts was unable to establish any direct link between the two groups
In Beni territory some cultivation harvest and sale of cocoa was linked to armed activity by ADF MaiMai groups unidentified armed assailants and some FARDC members Many cocoa farmers struggled to access fields due to insecurity and attacks on cocoa farmers rose during harvest periods Cocoa including from areas under armed control was smuggled into Uganda during  while many cocoa supply chains were opaque
Nduma dfense du CongoRnov NDCR split into two factions one led by former NDCR leader and sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwissa CDi and the other by his deputy Gilbert Bwira Chuo NDCR continued to benefit from the diversion of government stocks with several FARDC officers supplying them with weapons and ammunition FARDC contributed to the NDCR split its restructuring and the strengthening of the Bwira faction as a proxy to track down the Guidon faction and fight other armed groups
Criminal networks were involved in the smuggling of tin tantalum and tungsten originating from mine sites under armed group occupation Tantalum was the most confiscated of the three minerals at the Democratic Republic of the CongoRwanda border between January and September 
In Ituri the signing of ceasefire agreements beginning in midJuly  by Lendu armed groups commonly known as Cooprative pour le dveloppement du Congo or CODECO marked a relative lull in attacks in Djugu and Mahagi territories
At the time of drafting of the present report western Djugu territory and northern Irumu territory were the most affected by violence primarily due to the reluctance of some Lendu factions to adhere to the ceasefire process and activities of the recently created Force patriotique et intgrationniste du Congo armed group and the selfdefence group Zare
The Union des rvolutionnaires pour la dfense du peuple Congolais URDPCCODECO and the Arme de libration du Congo ALCCODECO used children a sanctionable act Some FARDC members deployed in Ituri committed exactions against Lendu civilians
Combatants of Lendu factions conducted an increasing number of attacks on goldtrading hubs and mining areas in goldrich Djugu and Irumu territories Zare elements were also present in goldmining areas but rarely targeted gold or gold miners Crossborder gold smuggling from Ituri into Uganda continued
In southern Irumu territory the number of attacks against civilians by armed groups coming from North Kivu including ADF increased with FARDC operatio ns leading to large population displacements and exacerbating tensions between communities A September attack in Payi targeted Hutus also referred to as Banyabwishas in particular
The process for the disarmament demobilization and reintegration of the Force de rsistance patriotique de lIturi resumed on  October  after stalling following a  September  clash with FARDC
In South Kivu the structure of MaiMai Yakutumba changed following the defection of deputy leader Alonda Bita in August  The armed group continued to finance its activities through the illegal exploitation of gold in the Misisi area and illicit logging particularly of redwood a species protected by the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora Raia Mutomboki factions of the Butachibera and Hamakombo groups were involved in the illegal taxation of local communities to access forests particularly in Kalehe territory
The Group of Experts is concerned by and continues to investigate the escalation of violence in the highlands of Fizi Uvira and Mwenga territories by armed groups and the attribution of collective responsibility to communities for their attacks as well as inflammatory speech
Members of the Rwanda Defence Force were present and conducted operations in North Kivu from late  to early October  in violation of the sanctions regime The Burundi National Defence Force and the Imbonerakure youth group launched incursions into South Kivu between November  and July  also in violation of the sanctions regime
Two seizures of weaponry in Kinshasa in October  and Gbadolite in April  showed the continued existence of internal trafficking networks sometimes with crossborder spillovers

government to manage the military and security issuesSources pointed out that a number of missiles fell in the terminal and runway of Aden International Airport moments before the members of the pure and simple of weekend elections that were badly hampered by armed groups More than a third of the troubled countrys districts did not take part in Sundays first round of voting for the presidency not fair and inclusive and are in no way the expression of the peoples will Condemning an electoral farce it claimed widespread ballot stuffing and complained of a lack of observers in remote areas of one of the worlds poorest has seen a string of coups and wars since gaining independence from France in  In  it spiralled once more into bloodshed when the then president Francois Bozize who had himself seized power a decade earlier was overturned by a mostly Muslim coalition called the Seleka The frontrunner in the crowded field of  candidates for the presidency is the incumbent Faustin Archange Touadera who was elected in  after a turbulent transition following the coup But his government controls only about onethird of the country with militia groups that emerged from the conflict in  controlling the other twothirds of the territory The government on December  accused Bozize of fomenting a coup with several armed groups that it said were advancing on the capital a charge Bozize denies Fears about the rebels swept the city in the following days although the UN peacekeeping force MINUSCA said the advance had been stopped In many areas militia groups hampered the organisation of the elections and intimidated voters according to local leaders and UN workers who asked not to be named In addition thousands of people were prevented from voting or never received their voting cards because of the lack of security The International Committee of the Red Cross said gunmen raided its office in Bouar a market town in the west on Sunday  Partelections  Voting did not take place in  of the countrys  subprefectures subdivisions of large administrative districts the minister for territorial administration Augustin YanganaYahote told journalists Monday Six other subprefectures managed only a partial vote Theophile Momokoama the general rapporteur for the National Election Authority ANE told AFP ALSO READ  Two Malian soldiers killed in ambush The UN says numerous polling stations managed to open but then swiftly closed or remained empty because of voter intimidation At a press conference on Tuesday observers from international organisations mainly the nation Economic Community of Central African States ECCAS of which the CAR is a member expressed satisfaction with the elections But Thierry Vircoulon a researcher with the French Institute of International Relations IFRI said These are partelections they are not credible and do not meet international standards The vote tally is expected to take three weeks because the ballots must be transported to Bangui in view of the insecurity Violence persisted after the vote with an attack on a bus in central Grimari killing an employee of Doctors Without Borders on Monday  Weeks before results  Provisional results are expected from January  but no final results are expected before January  A runoff will be held on February  if there is no outright winner in the first round Touaderas election victory in  was declared after a similarly long period marked by allegations of ballot disappearance and other irregularities COD had already called on December  for the elections to be cancelled Nathalia Dukhan a CAR specialist with a US NGO called The Sentry said electoral fraud in the  vote was tolerated and thus legitimised  it was deemed the price for consolidating peace after the civil war But today its the entire political opposition which is condemning massive rigging she said Government spokesman Ange Maxime Kazagui shrugged off the naysayers on Tuesday insisting that the Central African people showed their firm will to go and vote despite the dangers Voting took place in the CARs  prefectures Eight hundred polling stations out of  did not open That means that  percent of the polling stations were open to the public he said AFP Vanguard News Nigeria The post appeared first on Vanguard News

Myanmar military hopeful of peace talks in Rakhine The Tatmadaw military believes that peace negotiations in Rakhine State will improve through talks with the Arakan Army AA said General Zaw Min Tun chief of the Tatmadaw True News Information Team He was speaking at a press conference in Naypyidaw on December  After the ceasefire in Rakhine State we believe that the peace process will develop through conditions in which displaced villagers can return to their homes and make a living he said  He added that efforts were being made to prevent further clashes Whether or not the fighting resumes will depend on the vigilance of both sides U Zaw Min Tun said On November  eight months after the government declared the AA a terrorist organisation military and AA representatives held a minute online discussion A facetoface meeting was then held on December  in Panghsang which is controlled by the United Wa State Army  The Tatmadaw said the talks are aimed at paving the way for reelection in nine townships in northern Rakhine State where elections were unable to take place this year The next meeting between the Tatmadaw and the AA will involve  Tatmadaw Peace Talks Committee leaders and AA CommanderinChief General Tun Myat Naing Fighting between the Tatmadaw and the AA in northern Rakhine State which began in November  lasted for two years until October when more than  civilians were displaced and more than  homes were destroyed by fire  On November  sources said the military and AA had reached an agreement for a temporary truce in the conflict in Rakhine which resulted in the return of some of the internally displaced people to their villages A military spokesperson said that talks between the two sides are progressing and could pave the way for a political Maritime security companies said a suspicious objectpossibly a type of minewas discovered on an oil tanker off the coast of Iraq
According to Dryad Global one of the firms crew members on the Liberianflagged MT Pola identified the presence of a suspicious object attached to the MT Polas hull whilst conducting StS nm South Al Bakr Terminal offshore Iraq in the Persian Gulf
The firm said Further reporting indicates that the object is suspected to be a limpet mine The crew and vessel are understood to be safe at this time
A limpet mine is a type of naval mine that is attached to a target via magnets A diver or a swimmer may attach the mine to a vessel the limpet mines are then typically set off by a time fuse
Dryad said that its not clear where the alleged limpet mine was placed noting that another vessel the MT Nordic Freedom assisted the MT Pola in obtaining photos of the object
Similar devices have been used to target vessels in the nearby Red Sea according to Dryad which noted heightened tensions between the United States its allies and Iran
With anniversary of the death of IRGC commander Qasem Soleimani approaching the corresponding risk within the region to all vessels is assessed to be SUBSTANTIAL the security firm wrote All vessels are encouraged to operate at a heightened posture of vigilance whilst at anchor and in transit and are reminded to report all suspicious activity to UKMTO
Dryad was making reference to the targeted killing of Soleimani early in  Iran then fired a barrage of missiles at US assets in Iraq Meanwhile the United States flew B bombers around the Middle East on Wednesday in a bid to show the militarys commitment to regional security and demonstrate a unique ability to rapidly deploy overwhelming combat power on short notice US Central Command wrote
Another security firm Ambrey Intelligence wrote that an unidentified object was found affixed to the hull of a tanker near Khor Al Zubair Anchorage that prompted fears of it being a limpet mine
The United Kingdom Marine Trade Operations told The Associated Press that the agency is aware of an ongoing situation in the Persian Gulf
The US Navys th Fleet said it is monitoring the incident a spokesperson Rebecca Rebarich told AP
The Pola along with another tanker serves as floating fuel oil storage of Iraqs State Organization of Marketing of Oil said Sudharsan Sarathy a senior oil analyst at the dataanalysis firm Refinitiv Smaller vessels carry the fuel oil to the ship which then conducts shiptoship transfers in the Persian Gulf to clients AP reported

I saw a lot of bodies Ethiopians in Sudan traumatised by Tigray conflict Inside a makeshift tent in the Sudanese village of Hamdaiet near the border with Ethiopia a baby was born last week to a woman from the region of Tigray named Asiey Negosia The yearold had just fled her home country of Ethiopia arriving at the Hamdaiet reception centre in the state of Kassala following an arduous threeday journey that eventually took her across the Tekeze River  also known as Setit  into Sudan I lost two of my children thats very painful as I dont know their whereabouts  Sara Abraham  Ethiopian refugee Despite the lack of medical essentials at the tent  which was set up by the local community for newly arrived refugees  Negosia had a smooth delivery although she looked a little bit weak We thank God that my sister has delivered the baby without any health complications She had suffered a lot on the journey as we needed to move quickly due to aeroplane bombings and attacks from soldiers Negosias sister Ana told Middle East Eye Asiey and Ana are among more than  Ethiopians who have streamed into Sudan since Ethiopias Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed launched a military offensive in Ethiopias northernmost region of Tigray on  November Ahmed said his aim is to remove the ruling Tigray Peoples Liberation Front TPLF which he accuses of defying the government and seeking to destabilise it Hundreds of people are reported to have been killed in the operation  On Sunday Abiy published a statement on Twitter giving forces in the Tigray region a hour ultimatum to surrender before his military begins an offensive on the rebelheld regional capital of Mekelle  Its a miracle I made it out In Hamdaiet which is the first transit points for refugees entering Sudan thousands of ethnic Tigrayans rest under trees or inside the shelters set up by the Sudanese aid commission and Red Crescent as members from the local community provide them with some food and water  Many of them had rushed to cross the Tekeze River on the EthiopianSudanese border before nightfall when the local ferry boats were ordered to stop sailing by Sudanese authorities All they had in tow were personal belongings and not much else although some did manage to bring along a few small pieces of furniture Among the new arrivals was yearold Zulu Tikhli who said he made a miracle escape from his hometown Himora after the Ethiopia federal troops attacked and destroyed the city The army launched an aggressive attack on the civilians It was a tripartite attack by Ethiopia Eritrea and backed by the Amhara militia whose intention was to carry out revenge on the Tigrayans Tikhli told MEE On the road I saw a lot of bodies as well as wounded people but I had no time to help anyone as the bombing was nonstop  Zulu Tikhli Ethiopian refugee I feel its a miracle that I had made it out here with my family of three On the road I saw a lot of bodies as well as wounded people but I had no time to help anyone as the bombing was nonstop so I could only take care of my own family he said Residents in Hamdaiet are trying their best to look after the influx of newcomers Fatima Alhaj  has worked with her neighbours to cook food and provide blankets for the refugees to get through the cold nights We are not able to provide enough to meet the refugees needs as there are so many of them We can only provide them some food on a daily basis according to our capacity Alhaj explained The border crossing of Luqdi in the state of Gadaref has been another transit point for refugees from Ethiopia This area has witnessed similar scenes as in Hamdaiet and those who arrive via this route are taken to refugee camps set up across Sudan Last week the United Nations said it was anticipating that up to  people would flee unrest in Ethiopia over the next six months adding that around m would be needed to accommodate the thousands of refugees crossing into Sudan Massacre in MaiKadra Standing in the long queue for registration at Village  refugee camp yearold Abraha Burhami told MEE that the Ethiopian premier was committing crimes against the Tigrayans because they had voted in the regional elections in September in defiance of federal governments order to delay the vote The move infuriated Abiy who had called it unconstitutional and illegal Tigray officials as well as Abiys opponents had accused the prime minister of a power grab by using the Covid pandemic as a pretext to postpone scheduled elections until  extending the governments term by several months Burhami further claimed that the Ethiopian army and its allied militias had killed scores of farmers in his village MaiKadra in the Tigray region When the attacks began I was on my farm in MaiKadra so we ran with my family to the area of Barkat and then to Gargaf before finally crossing the border to Sudan We walked for four days under continuous bombings and attacks by both Eritrean and Ethiopian armies Burhami said Sara Abraham  was also in MaiKadra when the killings took place While running from air strikes and soldiers attacks she lost two of her three children in the chaos and arrived in Sudan with only one child  Now in UmRakoba refugee camp she told MEE about her heartache and frustration My sister and I succeeded in bringing five of our seven children to Sudan I lost two of my children thats very painful as I dont know their whereabouts she said Ethiopian refugees who fled the fighting in the Tigray receive maternity care in the Hamdaiet area of Sudans eastern Kassala state on  November  AFP I dont know why our government is targeting Tigray in this brutal way The bombings were ongoing with gunships and tanks destroying the houses while the soldiers use guns and even knives to kill in the night Earlier this month Amnesty International published a report describing the aftermath of mass killings in MaiKadra in southwestern Tigray  We have confirmed the massacre of a very large number of civilians who appear to have been day labourers in no way involved in the ongoing military offensive said Deprose Muchena Amnesty Internationals director for east and southern Africa in a statement published on  November  The report added that according to witnesses forces loyal to the TPLF were responsible for the killings apparently after they suffered defeat from the federal Ethiopian Defence Forces EDF The Ethiopian Human Rights Commission on Tuesday said the attack was perpetrated against residents of MaiKadra from the Amhara and Wolkait ethnic groups adding that a Tigrayan youth group stabbed strangled and bludgeoned to death at least  civilians with the collusion of local security forces according to Reuters Looming disaster As unrest escalates in Ethiopia Sudan has begun opening new camps and reopening old ones to accommodate the increasing number of arrivals the aid commissioner for the state of Kassala Alsir Khalid told MEE We opened new camps in the state of Gadaref state to help with the transportation of refugees but the setup is still very poor because we have no capacity he said Village  is one of the camps that opened quickly to receive the refugees transported from the border areas set up jointly by the Sudan aid commission and UN agencies  I expect a disaster before the end of this year if we dont get the help  Alsir Khalid Kassala state aid commissioner Before becoming a camp for refugees Village  was initially built by the Sudanese government as a residential compound to compensate Sudanese citizens who were affected by the ongoing building of a dam project but the affected people had rejected the accommodation  The situation in this camp is much better than at the border points At least it has proper shelters with the UNHCR aid commission on site to register the refugees and provide food and water However Sudanese officials say there arent enough supplies to meet the needs of all the refugees in the camp  UmRakoba another old refugee camp that had previously hosted Ethiopian refugees was also reopened With as many as  Ethiopians expected to cross the border in coming days Khalid urged the international community to act quickly in providing Sudan with food and shelter for the refugees  I expect a disaster before the end of this year if we dont get the help he warned This article is available in French on Middle East Eye French edition

Aftermath of Aden attack
The toll in an attack on Aden airport has risen to at least  people killed and  others injured Yemens interior minister announced yesterday afternoon
The blasts occurred minutes after the arrival of a plane carrying a newlyformed government The prime minister and cabinet ministers were reported to be safe but a number of other officials and Red Cross staff were among the casualties
A journalist for a domestic TV station was reportedly killed at the scene while speaking to the studio by phone live on air
Hours later local residents reported a blast near Maashiq Presidential Palace where the cabinet had been transferred
A drone was also shot down nearby
Yemens information minister said the Houthi rebels were behind the airport attack
President Abdrabbuh Mansour Hadi meanwhile vowed that terrorist acts by the rival Houthi rebels and extremist groups would not prevent the government from carrying out its work from the interim capital Aden
Houthi coverage
The Houthis AlMasirah TV has provided limited coverage of the blasts as part of its news reporting
It has not suggested the rebel group was responsible
A talk show host yesterday evening nonetheless called the incident a disgrace for the government The channel also dubbed the ministers mercenaries and said the airport is controlled by Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates
It also highlighted Saudiled coalition strikes on the Houthicontrolled capital Sanaa and its airport in the aftermath
Yemen had announced a new cabinet lineup as part of a Saudibrokered deal between the government and the UAEbacked separatist Southern Transitional Council STC
The government  forced to relocate after the Houthis seized Sanaa in   left Aden after the STC seized control of the city amid deadly clashes in the summer of  
Dozens of soldiers targeted in Syria attack
The UKbased Syrian Observatory for Human Rights SOHR says that  Syrian soldiers have so far died after an attack on military buses in a desert area that is suspected to have been carried out by the jihadist Islamic State IS group
SOHR director Rami Abdul Rahman has disputed in TV interviews Syrian state medias continued description of the casualties as civilian
The SOHRs latest reports said the ambush was the largest attack by IS on government forces this year in terms of casualties
It occurred on the desert road connecting the towns of Deir alZour and Palmyra in eastern Syria
Syria analyst Danny Makki tweeted that the area has seen scattered attacks but nothing of this magnitude
Egypt summons Ethiopian envoy over spokesman remarks
Egypts foreign ministry said yesterday that the Ethiopian charge daffaires was summoned to explain statements by Ethiopian foreign ministry spokesman Dina Mufti in which he interfered in Egyptian internal affairs
According to the panArab Sky News Arabia website Mufti accused Egypt of pushing Ethiopia towards a persistent danger to cover up problems at home alluding to Cairos alleged interference in fomenting unrest in the Tigray region
He also said that Egypt was using the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam GERD conflict as a pretext to evade its own internal crises
Negotiations between Egypt Sudan and Ethiopia over the GERD have been deadlocked for years
Egypt fears the dam will slash its water resources during the filling period while Addis Ababa accuses Cairo of seeking to impose its will over the dam
Timeline Nine years of EgyptEthiopia dam talks
Egypt halts criminal charges in Regeni case
Egypts Public Prosecution has ordered that no criminal charges be filed in the case of murdered Italian researcher Giulio Regeni as no perpetrator has been identified for the time being
Public Prosecutor Hamada alSawy also directed the authorities yesterday to continue investigations to identify the perpetrator Sawy excluded the accusations levelled by Italian officials against four Egyptian officers and a policeman over their alleged involvement in the incident
On  November Egypt temporarily closed investigations into the killing of Regeni after failing to identify his killer despite plans by Rome to prosecute members of the Egyptian security apparatus over his death
Regenis body was found mutilated after having been abandoned by the side of a road days after he went missing in Cairo on  January

By Hassan AbuHussein

Iraq is expected to face an abundance of challenges in  which could further exacerbate instability in the country and weaken the governments authority
Over the past years the country has endured a range of economic political security regional and communal problems that are unlikely to be resolved any time soon
The health and economic consequences of the Covid pandemic continued antigovernment protests growing tension between the government and paramilitary groups and a host of other problems have put unending pressure on the country which is set to face a tough year ahead
Fragile security
The Islamic State IS still poses a substantial threat to Iraqs security especially in the areas the extremist Sunni group had previously held
IS attacks on security forces and the paramilitary Popular Mobilisation Forces PMF and abduction of civilians have not ceased Military campaigns regularly launched by security forces and PMF units against IS remnants and pockets have not limited the threats posed by the extremist group which appears to have changed its tactics
Observers say IS found an opportunity in the spread of Covid Security forces have reportedly withdrawn from open areas to ensure security and enforce curfews inside cities This has left other areas vulnerable to IS attacks
Experts estimate that approximately  members of the group are scattered across some parts of western and northern Iraq especially in border areas and the towns and villages where displaced residents have not returned The group moreover is said to be recruiting new militants from among the children of its slain members and inside camps for the displaced
The paramilitaries

Some Iranbacked factions of the PMF have become so powerful that the government has appeared weak by comparison on many occasions and thus unable to enforce the law
After the assassination of top Iranian commander Qasem Soleimani and Iraqi militia leader Abu Mahdi alMuhandis in a US drone strike in January  rocket attacks on the US embassy in Baghdad and American military bases have become frequent Iranbacked militias are often accused of being the perpetrators behind such attacks
After a member from Asaib Ahl alHaq a key faction within the PMF was arrested in December over alleged involvement in a rocket attack on the US embassy the militia toured Baghdads streets with pickup trucks and different types of weapons as a show of force Several videos emerged on social media in which masked militants threatened Prime Minister Mustafa alKadhimi saying they are ready for the goahead signal from the groups leader Qais alKhazali
In response Kadhimi said the government is ready for a decisive confrontation if necessary
Khazali moreover urged Kadhimi in a video in June to turn a blind eye over attacks on US forces In defiant language he said that the arrest of any member of the resistance has never and will never happen in the history of Iraqs governments this is bigger than the size of your government Khazali released the video after the arrest of over a dozen members of another powerful militia group Kataib Hezbollah
Hezbollah has also been opposed to the prime minister accusing him of complicity in the assassination of Soleimani and Muhandis who were killed when Kadhimi was the intelligence chief
The groups leaders use tough defiant language when addressing Kadhimi On  December the Twitter account of Abu Ali alAskari who is identified as a Hezbollah security official threatened the prime minister by saying he would cut off his ears if he stands against the resistance
Local media say approximately  investigative committees have been formed to probe acts of violence and attacks targeting the US embassy and forces in Iraq But no results have been announced and no group has been blamed as of yet
Analysis Five years after forming Iraqi militias consolidate power
Explainer Iraqi decree to incorporate paramilitaries into army
New militant groups
New shadow militant Shia groups have emerged in recent months mostly adopting the rhetoric and ideology of the Iranbacked militias
Saraya Thawrat alEshreen alThaniya Brigades of Second Revolt of  which refers to the  Iraqi revolt against the British occupation Usbat alThaereen League of Revolutionaries Qabdat alHuda Guidance Fist which is sometimes written as Qabdat alMahdi Mahdis Fist Ashab alKahf People of the Cave whose name refers to a Koranic parable and Martyr Karim Daram Brigade have claimed rocket and roadside bomb attacks on the US embassy and military bases as well as logistics convoys which are part of the USled coalition against IS
Most of these groups adopt what is known in Iraq as Walai ideology  in reference to Irans VelayateFaqih the governance of the jurist
Their operations and activities including rocket attacks appear to have one mission in common  threatening the US forces stationed in Iraq and calling for their expulsion
Explainer Iraqi shadow militias  new Iranian strategy against US
Another group called Rabaallah which means Allahs Group in the Iraqi dialect has also emerged in recent months to defend the PMF
Group members dress in black with the Arabic name Rabaallah inscribed on the backs of their outfits They have been accused of committing acts of violence with protesters as well as storming the offices of some Iraqi and nonIraqi television channels whose coverage appeared to be supportive of the popular protests and opposing Iranian influence in the country They also mobilised protests outside the US and French embassies in Baghdad
Rabaallah members have also been involved in some other acts of violence that resulted in them appearing to try and act as a sort of religious police force Social media videos depict its members destroying a beauty centre and an alcohol shop as well as beating women said to be working at a massage salon in Baghdad
Observers liken Rabaallahs tactics to Irans Basij with some commentators describing the group as the Iraqi Basij Social media users describe it as the Shia Daesh a pejorative term used in reference to IS
Economic concerns

The Covid pandemic has aggravated Iraqs overburdened economy which is  dependant on oil exports
The decline in oil prices together with Opec crude cut plans have left Iraq unable to pay the salaries of its civil servants and pensioners
Despite the relative rise in oil prices with the start of vaccination campaigns against Covid in some countries uncertainty remains as to whether prices will fully rebound in the near future
To face this problem Iraq has resorted to internal borrowing and the devaluation of its national currency the Iraqi dinar by about  of its value resulting in price hikes and protests over delayed wages
The economic and financial crises have also resulted in delays in paying the salaries of civil servants in the semiautonomous Kurdistan Region which has seen protests and clashes with security forces over the unpaid salaries of public sector workers
Moreover relations between the Kurdistan Region and the federal government in Baghdad have remained sour since the former held a nonbinding referendum to secede from Iraq in September 
In addition to economic challenges chronic power and water shortages are also unlikely to find a solution in the near future
Explainer Iraqs environmental woes
Explainer Can Iraq avoid another turbulent summer
Political challenges

Economic woes and dilapidated public services which have spurred antigovernment protests since October  have been the biggest drive for political change in the country
In response to the protests the parliament adopted another election system replacing the partyvoting system with voting for individuals
The new system aims to end the influence of the Shia Islamist parties and groups which are blamed for rampant corruption in the country and the political quotas system in place since the USled invasion of Iraq in 
The new election system will be put to the test in June  the date set by Kadhimi for an early election  one year ahead of schedule
However officials have cited logistical financial and health due to Covid measures constraints that could impede the polls
The continuation of the antigovernment protests still represents a challenge facing the government which appears unable to introduce any tangible economic or political reforms
Not much hope is pinned on the outcome of the coming elections since current conditions do not allow the emergence of new political groups or faces
Explainer Can Iraqs new election law alter the political map
Explainer The dilemma of creating electoral constituencies in Iraq
Explainer Will Iraqs new election law end antigovernment protests
Internally displaced
The Iraqi Ministry of Migration and Displaced decided in November to close all the camps set up for internally displaced people IDPs in early 
More than three million IDPs were forced to leave their homes during the takeover by IS of large parts of Iraq and the subsequent battles to push back militants
The government has been urging the displaced to return to their homes and the ministry wants them to contribute to the rebuilding process
Given the destruction of their hometowns and the lack of infrastructure and security many IDPs prefer to stay in camps
However there is a communal problem related to the displaced Large numbers of them have links with IS and many widowed women have children from militants and residents in their hometowns are against their return
Despite the reported efforts made with some tribal leaders to allow those ISlinked families to return the issue requires short and longterm integration programmes
Officials are afraid that if these families remain displaced a new generation of IS may emerge

Text of report by Central African Republic Fondation Hirondellesponsored Radio Ndeke Luka on  December
A few days after the fighting between elements of the rebel coalition and the Central African Armed Forces FACA who were supported by Minusca United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilisation Mission in CAR life is gradually resuming in some cities affected by the violence A gradual return of people who fled the violence has been observed in some localities
According to the inhabitants of Mbaiki in Lobaye southwest and Bambari in Ouaka centre traffic is gradually resuming in these localities However there is still fear of a surprise attack by the armed men as they are still visible in some places
Although last week was punctuated by attacks launched by the coalition of armed groups in some cities of the country paralysing activities and causing the significant displacement of populations life is gradually resuming in some localities
According to several sources in Bambari the intensification of Minusca patrols has allowed a semblance of calm to return although the armed men are still present but disguised as civilians
Those who left their homes to join the IDP sites are gradually returning to their neighbourhoods The same sources indicate that activities have resumed in the citys central market with the exception of public services which were vandalised by rebel fighters
In Mbaiki and Boali southwest even if the return of the displaced is reported the markets and shops are not yet open According to local authorities the presence of national and international forces is reassuring in Mbaiki
Meanwhile in Nana Mambere in the northwest the status quo prevails In Bouar and Baboua the presence of armed men is noted and scenes of looting have been reported in these regions
At the same time the armed men who had previously occupied the towns of Beloko and Cantonnier on the border with Cameroon withdrew from these localities After talks with the Cameroonian authorities they agreed to open the border on Tuesday  December This was effected for a few hours
Obviously the armed groups are not in the locality We no longer see them in Cantonnier and Beloko as they have withdrawn from the localities They are now in the subprefecture of Baboua
The road that connects the two towns is closed There are no elements of the internal security forces in these localities which have remained at the mercy of the bandits a resident of Beloko revealed
It is in this fragile security climate that the Central African authorities and Minusca are offering reassurances about the arrangements for securing and taking over the towns controlled by the rebels
Source Radio Ndeke Luka Bangui in French  Dec

     Summary 
   


      Mueen Abdulmalek Saeed was appointed prime minister of Yemen in October  He succeeded Ahmad Ubayd BinDaghr who was dismissed by President AbdRabbuh Mansur Hadi for his governments inability to take real measures to stop the economic deterioration in the country In December  Saeed was reappointed as prime minister to lead a Saudibrokered powersharing government that includes the rival Southern Transitional Council STC Although some commentators have voiced scepticism over Saeeds relatively young age  when taking office others have welcomed his appointment as a positive development that may improve living conditions in Yemen Before his mandate as prime minister Saeed also served as minister of public works and infrastructure between May  and October  He has a PhD in Architecture and Design Theory from Cairo University

An improvised explosive device has reportedly targeted a logistics convoy for the USled international coalition against the Islamic State group in Iraq
The blast took place in AlYousefiya in southern Baghdad on  December the privatelyowned website Shafaq News quoted a security source as saying
No causalities have been reported but some vehicles have sustained damage the source said
Since the US assassinated top Iranian commander Qasem Soleimani and Iraqi militia leader Abu Mahdi alMuhandis in a drone attack on  January  attacks on US bases and embassy have increased
Such attacks are believed to be carried out by Iranbacked militias in Iraq
USled coalition convoys have recently become the target of roadsidebomb attacks

Earlier in the day local media said that the US forces set up a new counterrocket system in a military base at Baghdad airport for fear of revengeful attacks by Iran proxies in Iraq in the first anniversary of the killing of Soleimani and Muhandis

By BBC Monitoring
Yemens UAEbacked separatist Southern Transitional Council STC has strongly condemned the deadly attack on the airport of the interim capital Aden as a terrorist act blaming it on the Houthi rebels and powers that stand to lose from a Saudibacked powersharing deal 
A statement  signed by the STC spokesman Nizar Haitham and posted on its website late on  December   said that the criminal act happened as everyone was waiting for the arrival in Aden of the cabinet in which the south and the north are equally represented and for the start of a construction and building process to take the country out of its miserable condition 
The attacks on Adens airport happened as members of a newly formed government arrived in Aden from the Saudi capital Riyadh The cabinet represents Yemens northern and southern areas with equal numbers of members from each region
The cabinet formation is part of a  Riyadh deal to end the rift between the government of Yemeni President Abdrabbuh Mansour Hadi and the STC with the aim of confronting the Iranbacked Houthi rebels
The STC statement blamed the attacks on the terrorist Houthi militias and powers that stand to lose from the Riyadh agreement and seek to stop its implementation  
The statement called on the powersharing government and security bodies to assume their responsibilities and to open an immediate and urgent probe with international participation It also called on the Saudiled coalition to support the security forces and to provide them with the necessary logistic support in order to reinforce security in Aden 
The Yemeni president ordered the formation of a committee to investigate the attack which will be headed by the interior minister and will include the heads of the security and intelligence services and the local authority and carry out its work in coordination with the Saudiled coalition
The Yemeni information minister Muammar alEryani accused the Houthis of the attack But the rebels and their media distanced themselves from it 
The new cabinet ministers had taken oath in the capital Riyadh ahead of their return to Aden The government had left the southern port city in the summer of  after it was captured by the proSTC forces backed by the UAE
Aden has served as the temporary seat of the government since  after a coalition led by Saudi Arabia launched a campaign of aerial bombardment against the Houthi rebel movement which had seized control of the capital Sanaa in September the previous year
Source Southern Transitional Council website Aden in Arabic  gmt  Dec

According to reports in the US media US President Donald Trump has received information about Chinas alleged bounty offer to nonstate actors to kill American soldiers deployed in Afghanistan this month the private Afghan Channel One TV TV reported on  December

Afghan peace talks
Afghanistans negotiating team for the intraAfghan dialogue peace talks with Taliban has said that they will focus on ceasefire and protecting the existing political system of the country in the talks with the Taliban TV reported on  December
First there is the issue of security which has a major significance for the Afghan people the talks about security involve ceasefire and the protection of the people and highways and also the issue of drugs the channel showed Masoom Stanekzai  Afghan teams chief negotiator  as saying at an event in Kabul yesterday
Another member of the team Mohammad Natiqi has said that the current political system in Afghanistan needs to be defended in the talks
The intraAfghan peace talks began after a long delay on  September in Qatar and progressed intermittently till midDecember after which the two sides announced a threeweek break for discussions within their respective teams on the proposed agenda of the talks
The talks are expected to resume on  January
AfghanAzerbaijan diplomatic ties
The Azerbaijani parliament has approved the opening of the countrys embassy in Kabul Tolo News TV channel reported on  December
The Afghan Ministry of Foreign Affairs has said that the Azerbaijan took the decision as a result of efforts by the Afghan embassy in Baku  the capital of Azerbaijan
Welcoming the move the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has described the decision to open Azerbaijani embassy in Kabul as an important step towards expansion of bilateral ties between the two countries
Blast in Kabul
A magnetic mine blast in the Afghan capital of Kabul killed at least one person and injured two others today Tolo News TV and Ariana News channels reported
Government sources have confirmed that a senior official of the Afghan Presidential Office was injured and his driver killed in the blast which hit their vehicle in the Afghan capital Tolo News channel tweeted
Fazel Ahmad Fazly the head of the Presidential Offices Administrative Affairs Department has said that the vehicle of Mohammad  Jawid Wali the departments deputy director for advisory affairs was the target of today mornings blast in Chehelsetoon area of Kabul He added that Jawid Wali has been seriously injured and his driver Bahramuddin has been killed in the attack the channel tweeted
The presidential office staff and his driver are the latest victim of the recent spate of bomb blasts and attacks in Afghanistan especially capital Kabul which have been mostly aimed at soft targets such as journalists civil society activists and civilian officials
No group or individual has yet claimed responsibility for the incident
Meanwhile First VicePresident Amrullah Saleh has said that roads should not be blocked as part of security measures and termed it the worst strategy Ariana News reported on  December He also said that there are gaps in the current strategy of tracing and arresting criminals
Clashes between Taliban security forces
Over  Taliban militants and two Afghan soldiers have been killed in clashes in northern Badakhshan and southern Helmand provinces the private Pakistanbased Afghan Islamic Press AIP news agency reported on  December
At least  Taliban and two security personnel have been killed and three soldiers injured in clashes between the two sides in an area between Baharak district and Fayzabad city the capital of northern Badakhshan Province
Confirming the clashes and casualty figures the provincial governors spokesman Naik Mohammad Nazari said that the fighting was still going on and that  Taliban have also been captured alive by the security forces
In another incident at least  Taliban militants have been killed in air strikes in Helmands Nawa district the AIP added in a separate report
In a statement the Defense Ministry said that the Afghan air force carried out air strikes on a Taliban hideout in Nawa districts Zhar Saheb and Tabela areas on  December killing  Taliban militants and wounding  others including a commander
The Taliban have not commented on the incident so far
But the Taliban have accused the Afghan government of killing and injuring  civilians in the past one week
At least  civilians had been killed and wounded in the Afghan governments operation in the past week AIP quoted Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid as saying
He added that  civilians had been killed and  others including women and children injured in  ground and air strikes in  provinces of the country
Mujahid claimed that  similar attacks had taken place in the past month killing  civilians injuring  others destroying  houses two mosques one madrassa and two clinics
In Jalalabad city the capital of the eastern Nangarhar province one person has been killed in a roadside mine blast TV and Ariana News reported today A spokesman for provincial governors office has said that the explosion targeted a rickshaw in the citys Precinct  today
The Afghan Presidential Palace has said that the Taliban have been continuing their attacks with the aim of creating fear among people Ariana News reported on  December
The main reason behind the attacks is to create fears havoc disappointment and distance between the people and the government of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan the channel showed Deputy Spokeswoman for the Presidential Palace Fatima Morchal as saying

A statement released by the Ministry of Interior Affairs has said that the drug smuggler has been detained during a security forces operation in the province The statement said that the suspect was trying to smuggle about  kg heroin to Kabul from northern Takhar province

Yemens privately owned Belqees TV announced the death of its reporter Adeeb alJenani on the scene A video clip has been posted on Twitter in which alJenani was reporting to the studio by phone live on air only to be interrupted minutes later by the sound of the blast The line is lost after the incident

President Abdrabbuh Mansour Hadi meanwhile vowed that terrorist acts by the rival Houthi rebels and extremist groups would not prevent the government from carrying out its work from the interim capital Aden
Source BBC Monitoring  Dec

Yemens Prime Minister Mueen Abdulmalek Said said on  December that the Houthis backed by Iranian experts carried out the deadly attacks on the airport of the interim capital Aden with guided missiles according to the progovernment SABA news agency 
Said was speaking during the first meeting of the newly formed cabinet in Aden a day after the blasts which took place as ministers arrived in the airport from the Saudi capital Riyadh 
SABA quoted Said as saying preliminary investigations into the blasts indicate that the Houthi militias carried out the attack with guided missiles He added that there is military and intelligence information indicating that Iranian experts were present to do such acts 
He reiterated his governments accusations that the Houthis are a proxy of Iran 
The attacks he was quoted as saying are a clear message from the Houthi militia to the Yemeni people and the international community that it is just a tool in Irans hand and that it is not serious about making peace
The international community is still discussing whether to classify the Houthis s as a terrorist group when we in Yemen clearly see that their acts and crimes prove they are a terrorist group Said was quoted as saying 
He decried the attack as shocking and unprecedented targeting a civilian airport and leaving victims including Red Cross workers and journalists the report said 
The governments willingness to achieve peace and to make compromises towards this end does not mean putting itself at a disadvantage as a result of the Houthis continuous blood shedding 
The Houthi rebels and their media distanced themselves from the attack 
Even though the government has no magical solutions he was quoted as saying it would make every effort to restore normal conditions in the interim capital and provinces captured from the Houthis 
SABA reported that the cabinet pledged during the meeting to take all measures to put Adens airport back in operation at the earliest possible time   
The cabinet represents Yemens northern and southern areas with equal numbers of members from each region
The cabinet formation is part of a  Riyadh deal to end the rift between the government of Yemeni President Abdrabbuh Mansour Hadi and the separatist Southern Transitional Council STC with the aim of confronting the rebels
The new cabinet ministers had taken oath in Riyadh ahead of their return to Aden The government had left the southern port city in the summer of  after it was captured by the proSTC forces backed by the UAE
Aden has served as the temporary seat of the government since  after a coalition led by Saudi Arabia launched a campaign of aerial bombardment against the Houthi rebel movement which had seized control of the capital Sanaa in September the previous year
Source Saba news agency website in Arabic  gmt  Dec

An official from Yemens Houthi rebel movement and its media outlets have distanced the group from the deadly  December attack on Aden airport which occurred minutes after the arrival of a plane carrying Yemens newly formed government  a key Houthi foe
The rebels official said his group could have struck the airport had it wanted to but blamed the incident on infighting in Aden

The Saudiled coalition backing the internationally recognised government also said it shot down a Houthi drone targeting the palace

Yemens information minister has also said the Houthi rebels were behind the airport attack

Around three hours after the incidents in the vicinity of the palace were reported the Houthirun Saba news agency published remarks by a rebel official on the airport attack
Tareq Salam the Houthiappointed governor for Aden  where the rebel group does not have a presence  told Saba that the attack was the latest in a series of settling of scores between rival forces in the southern city
The Sanaa Houthis selfproclaimed government which has bombarded the palaces of tyrants in Riyadh and Abu Dhabi is not incapable of striking Aden Salam said but criticised attempts to point blame at the Houthis in order to cover up the failings of the internationally recognised government and its mercenaries and gain the sympathy of the international community
Todays attack was not unexpected for a government that cannot secure itself let alone the rights of its people It is unable to make any decisions without the approval of the Saudi ambassador on one side and the United Arab Emirates commanders on the other he went on 
The Houthis AlMasirah TV has provided limited coverage of the blasts as part of its routine news reporting citing other media outlets for the detail Though its  gmt bulletin on  December gave the incident more airtime the story was left until later in the running order

Three apparently drunk teens from Lebanon were arrested by Lebanese police after unsuccessfully trying to sneak over the border into Israel the Lebanese army reported Tuesday On  at approximately  pm a patrol from the Intelligence Directorate stopped three young men as they approached the technical fence in the Sahl alKhiam area while they were apparently drunk the Lebanese Army tweeted
On the Israeli side of the heavily defended international border the IDF spokespersons office issued a statement saying that IDF spotters who monitor the border spotted suspects approaching the border fence apparently near the town of Metula which sits right on the border
One of the suspects climbed the fence crossed several meters into Israeli territory and returned to Lebanon shortly after the IDF statement said IDF forces that arrived in the area immediately identified the suspects in Lebanese territory after crossing back and carried out a suspicious arrest procedure that included firing into the air The IDF observed the suspects throughout the incident IDF forces combed the area and confirmed no further intrusions
Lebanese news website The reported that an investigation into the incident was opened and the suspects were referred to a relevant judiciary in Lebanon Lebanon is home to Iranianbacked terror forces that use its territory as a staging ground for attacks against Israel
Hizbullah is in de facto control of southern Lebanon where the incident occurred and has repeatedly launched crossborder attacks sparking the war in  when Hizbullah fired dozens of rockets at Israeli towns and cities as a cover to kidnap IDF soldiers who subsequently died in Hizbullah captivity
Hizbullah refuses to comply with UN Security Council Resolution  passed after the  war which demands the disarmament of all armed groups in Lebanon so that there will be no weapons or authority in Lebanon other than that of the Lebanese state
In  the United Nations confirmed that several military attack tunnels dug by Hizbullah into Israel were both illegal and violated Security Council resolution  The IDF subsequently destroyed all the tunnels
There have been several attempts this year by Sudanese laborers in Lebanon to cross the border into Israel where it is known that working and living conditions are much better than in Arab countries In all cases the infiltrators were returned to Lebanon

More than three hundred children are reported to be still missing with many feared abducted after armed gunmen stormed the all boys Government Science Secondary School in Kankara Katsina state late Friday evening local time
In a statement issued by his spokesperson SecretaryGeneral Antnio Guterres strongly condemned the attack and called for the childrens safe return to their families
He reiterates that attacks on schools and other educational facilities constitute a grave violation of human rights He urges the Nigerian authorities to bring those responsible for this act to justice the statement added
Mr Guterres also reaffirmed the UNs solidarity and support to the Government and people of Nigeria in their fight against terrorism violent extremism and organized crime
Grim reminder
The UN Childrens Fund UNICEF also denounced the attack and called for the childrens release
In a separate statement MariePierre Poirier UNICEF Regional Director for West and Central Africa said that the violence is a grim reminder that abductions of children and widespread grave violations of childrens rights continue to take place in northern Nigeria
Children should feel safe at home in schools and in their playgrounds at all times We stand with the families of the missing children and the community affected by this horrifying event
In February  Boko Haram insurgents kidnapped over  school girls from a secondary school in the town of Dapchi in northeast Nigeria Six years ago in  the militant group abducted  girls from their school dormitory in Chibok Many of them remain missing

In a statement by his spokesperson issued on the eve of the polls SecretaryGeneral Antnio Guterres commended the Government and people of the west African nation for working to ensure timely elections despite significant security and humanitarian challenges amid the COVID pandemic
Mr Guterres also called on all stakeholders to ensure that the elections are held in a safe peaceful and inclusive manner
He urges the security forces to make every effort to protect the civilian population as they cast their vote the statement added
Complex challenges
The SecretaryGeneral also reiterated the commitment of the United Nations to accompany the countrys efforts to promote democracy and sustainable development
Situated in the Sahel region Niger faces complex security and humanitarian challenges A landlocked and least developed country it suffers from high levels of food insecurity and hunger Niger also hosts about  refugees and  internally displaced persons
The situation is complicated by Boko Haram violence On  December at least  people were killed and hundreds wounded in an attack claimed by the terrorist group on the southeastern town of Diffa near the border with Nigeria
